recipe.title: Adas Polo (Persian Lentil Rice)
recipe.description: Fluffy saffron basmati layered with brown lentils and warm cinnamon, crowned with sweet caramelized onions, dates and raisins, with a crisp golden rice crust (tahdig) underneath.

ingredients.item: saffron threads, ground with a pinch of sugar
salt, for the rice water, plus more to taste
plain yogurt or Shirazi salad, to serve

steps: Rinse the rice in cool water until it runs almost clear, then soak it in salted water for at least 30 minutes. Bloom the saffron in the hot water.
Simmer the lentils in plenty of water for 15 to 20 minutes, until just tender but still holding their shape. Drain and season with a pinch of salt.

Cook the onions in the oil over medium heat for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring often, until deep golden and sweet. Stir in the cinnamon and turmeric for 30 seconds, then lift out half the onions for the top.
Add 2 tbsp butter, the raisins and dates to the onions left in the pan and warm for 2 minutes, just until the raisins plump. Set aside.

Bring a large pot of water and 2 tbsp salt to a rolling boil. Drain the rice, add it and boil 5 to 6 minutes, until the grains are soft outside but still have a firm bite in the center. Drain and gently fold in the lentils.
Melt 2 tbsp butter in a heavy nonstick pot with 2 tbsp water and 1 tbsp of the saffron water. Spread a thin layer of rice over the bottom and press it down: this becomes the tahdig.
Pile the rest of the rice in a loose mound. Poke 4 or 5 holes down to the bottom with a spoon handle, dot with the remaining butter and drizzle with the rest of the saffron water.

Wrap the lid in a clean kitchen towel, cover tightly and cook 10 minutes on medium until you hear sizzling, then 40 to 45 minutes on low. Spoon onto a platter, scatter the fruit and onions over, and serve the crust broken into pieces.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Parboiling then steaming is the Persian method that keeps every grain separate and long. Stop boiling the moment the outside is soft and the center still resists.
The towel under the lid catches steam that would otherwise drip back and make the rice soggy.
Listen for the sizzle before turning the heat down: it means the bottom is starting to crisp into tahdig.
recipe.make_ahead: Cook the lentils and onions up to 2 days ahead. Leftover rice keeps 4 days; reheat with a splash of water, covered, so it steams.
variations: With meat: brown 1 lb ground beef or lamb with onion and turmeric and serve it alongside.
Add 1/4 cup barberries, quickly warmed in butter with a pinch of sugar, for a tart contrast.

recipe.title: Ajiaco (Colombian Chicken and Potato Soup)
recipe.description: Bogotá's comforting soup of chicken, corn and three kinds of potato, flavored with the herb guascas. The floury potatoes melt into a thick broth, served with cream, capers and avocado.

ingredients.item: russet potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
papas criollas or baby yellow potatoes
Mexican crema or heavy cream, to serve

steps: Put the chicken, water, green onions, garlic, cilantro, salt and pepper in a large pot. Bring to a boil, skim, then simmer gently, partly covered, for 30 minutes.
Lift out the chicken and set it aside to cool. Discard the green onions and cilantro.
Add the corn, russet potatoes and red potatoes to the broth. Simmer 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until the russets start to fall apart and thicken the soup.
Add the papas criollas and guascas and simmer 15 to 20 minutes more, until the small potatoes are tender and the broth is creamy. Mash a few potato slices against the pot if it needs more body.
Meanwhile, shred the chicken, discarding the skin and bones. Return it to the pot to warm through and taste for salt.
Ladle into deep bowls with a piece of corn in each. Serve the cream, capers and avocado at the table so everyone adds their own.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: The three potatoes each do a job: russets dissolve to thicken, red potatoes hold their shape, and the little yellow ones add buttery flavor.
Guascas gives ajiaco its signature taste. Look for it dried in Latin markets; dried oregano is a distant but workable stand-in.
Keep the chicken at a gentle simmer so it stays tender enough to shred.
recipe.make_ahead: Keeps 3 days in the fridge and thickens as it sits; thin it with water when reheating. Add the cream, capers and avocado only when serving.
variations: Serve with a side of white rice, the way many Bogotá families do.

papas criollas or baby yellow potatoes

Mexican crema or heavy cream, to serve

Add the corn, russet potatoes and red potatoes. Simmer 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until the russets start to fall apart and thicken the soup.
Add the papas criollas and guascas and simmer 15 to 20 minutes more, until the small potatoes are tender and the broth is creamy.
Stir in the beans or sliced hearts of palm for the last 5 minutes and taste for salt.
Ladle into deep bowls with a piece of corn in each and serve the cream, capers and avocado on the side.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

Guascas gives ajiaco its signature taste. Look for it dried in Latin markets; dried oregano is a distant but workable stand-in.
Keep the soup at a gentle simmer so the beans stay whole while the russets melt.
vegetarian.make_ahead: Keeps 3 days in the fridge and thickens as it sits; thin it with water when reheating. Add the cream, capers and avocado only when serving.

recipe.title: Amaretto Sour
recipe.description: The modern amaretto sour: a nut-free, almond-flavored amaretto balanced with fresh lemon and a splash of strong bourbon, shaken with egg white for a silky foam. Sweet, rich and bright.
steps: Shake the amaretto, bourbon, lemon juice, syrup and egg white without ice for 15 seconds to build the foam.
Add ice and shake hard for 10 seconds more.
Strain into a rocks glass over fresh ice. Garnish with an orange slice and cherry, and dot the foam with bitters.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake orgeat, lemon juice, cold black tea and aquafaba for an almond sour mocktail.

recipe.note: Uses raw egg white; use pasteurized egg white if you prefer.
tips: The splash of high-proof bourbon is what keeps this drink from tasting like candy.
The dry shake (no ice) whips the egg white into a thick, creamy head.
variations: Use regular-proof bourbon and increase it to 1 oz if you don't have cask strength.

tips: The splash of high-proof bourbon is what keeps this drink from tasting like candy.
Aquafaba foams just like aquafaba (liquid from a can of chickpeas). Dry shake it well for a thick head.

recipe.title: Amok Trey (Cambodian Fish Amok)
recipe.description: Cambodia's national dish: tender white fish in a silky coconut curry custard scented with lemongrass, galangal and lime leaf, steamed in banana-leaf cups.

ingredients.item: firm white fish (catfish, tilapia or cod), cut into bite-size pieces
lemongrass, tender parts only, thinly sliced
galangal or ginger, peeled and sliced
makrut lime leaves, stems removed (2 for garnish)
dried red chilies, soaked in hot water
coconut milk, plus 1/4 cup thick coconut cream for topping
red chili, cut in thin strips, to garnish

steps: Make the kroeung paste: pound or blend the lemongrass, galangal, turmeric, 2 lime leaves, shallots, garlic, drained chilies and shrimp paste with a splash of water until smooth.
Whisk the paste with the coconut milk, egg, fish sauce and sugar. Fold in the fish and let it sit 10 minutes.
Soften the banana leaves over a flame or in hot water and fold them into four cups, pinning the corners with toothpicks. Line each cup (or ramekin) with shredded spinach.
Spoon the fish and curry into the cups. Steam over simmering water, covered, for 20 to 25 minutes, until the custard is set but still trembles slightly and the fish flakes.
Top each with a spoon of coconut cream, finely shredded lime leaf and chili strips. Serve hot with rice.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: The egg is what turns the curry into amok's soft, mousse-like custard. Steam gently: a hard boil makes it grainy.
Fresh kroeung is the soul of the dish. Make a double batch and freeze half for next time.
Cut the fish into even pieces so every piece cooks in the same time.
recipe.make_ahead: The kroeung paste keeps 1 week in the fridge or 3 months frozen. Amok is best eaten freshly steamed.
variations: Chicken amok: use thinly sliced chicken thigh and steam 25 minutes.

vegetarian.title: Vegetarian Amok

coconut milk, plus 1/4 cup thick coconut cream for topping
red chili, cut in thin strips, to garnish

steps: Make the kroeung paste: pound or blend the lemongrass, galangal, turmeric, 2 lime leaves, shallots, garlic, drained chilies and white miso with a splash of water until smooth.
Whisk the paste with the coconut milk, egg, light soy sauce and sugar. Fold in the tofu and mushrooms and let them sit 10 minutes.
Soften the banana leaves over a flame or in hot water and fold them into four cups, pinning the corners with toothpicks. Line each cup (or ramekin) with shredded spinach.
Spoon the tofu and curry into the cups. Steam over simmering water, covered, for 20 to 25 minutes, until the custard is set but still trembles slightly.
Top each with a spoon of coconut cream, finely shredded lime leaf and chili strips. Serve hot with rice.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: The egg is what turns the curry into amok's soft, mousse-like custard. Steam gently: a hard boil makes it grainy.
Fresh kroeung is the soul of the dish. Make a double batch and freeze half for next time.
Press the tofu for 15 minutes so it soaks up the curry instead of watering it down.
vegetarian.make_ahead: The kroeung paste keeps 1 week in the fridge or 3 months frozen. Amok is best eaten freshly steamed.

vegan.title: Vegan Amok
vegan.description: Tofu and mushroom amok in a coconut curry set with a little cornstarch instead of egg.

ingredients.item: extra-firm tofu and oyster mushrooms, cut into bite-size pieces
lemongrass, tender parts only, thinly sliced
galangal or ginger, peeled and sliced
makrut lime leaves, stems removed (2 for garnish)
dried red chilies, soaked in hot water
coconut milk, plus 1/4 cup thick coconut cream for topping
red chili, cut in thin strips, to garnish

steps: Make the kroeung paste: pound or blend the lemongrass, galangal, turmeric, 2 lime leaves, shallots, garlic, drained chilies and white miso with a splash of water until smooth.
Whisk the paste with the coconut milk, cornstarch, light soy sauce and sugar. Fold in the tofu and mushrooms and let them sit 10 minutes.
Soften the banana leaves over a flame or in hot water and fold them into four cups, pinning the corners with toothpicks. Line each cup (or ramekin) with shredded spinach.
Spoon the tofu and curry into the cups. Steam over simmering water, covered, for 20 to 25 minutes, until the curry has thickened and set softly.
Top each with a spoon of coconut cream, finely shredded lime leaf and chili strips. Serve hot with rice.
vegan.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Cornstarch sets the curry softly in place of egg. Whisk it in well so it doesn't clump.
Fresh kroeung is the soul of the dish. Make a double batch and freeze half for next time.
Press the tofu for 15 minutes so it soaks up the curry instead of watering it down.
vegan.make_ahead: The kroeung paste keeps 1 week in the fridge or 3 months frozen. Amok is best eaten freshly steamed.

recipe.title: Aperol Spritz
recipe.description: The bright, bittersweet Italian aperitivo: Aperol, prosecco and a splash of soda in a big wine glass full of ice.

ingredients.item: vegan dry prosecco (such as Mionetto Organic), well chilled

steps: Fill a large wine glass to the top with ice. A full glass melts slower, so the drink stays fizzy and not watery.
Pour in the prosecco first, then the Aperol. Aperol is heavier and sinks, so it mixes as it goes down.
Add the soda, then give one gentle lift with a bar spoon from the bottom. Don't stir hard, or you'll knock out the bubbles.
Tuck the orange half-wheel into the glass and serve right away.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Use 2 oz non-alcoholic orange bitter aperitivo, top with alcohol-free sparkling wine and a splash of soda.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: The ratio is 3 parts prosecco, 2 parts Aperol, 1 part soda. Keep that ratio and scale it for a bigger glass.
Every bottle should be cold before it touches the ice. Warm prosecco foams over and goes flat fast.
Choose a prosecco labeled Brut or Extra Dry. Sweeter bottles make the drink cloying.
recipe.make_ahead: Make it to order; a spritz goes flat within about 15 minutes. For a party, chill everything ahead and set up glasses with ice and orange slices so each one takes seconds.
variations: Campari Spritz: swap in Campari for a more bitter, less sweet drink.
Hugo-style: replace the Aperol with 3/4 oz elderflower liqueur and add a few mint leaves.
Lighter: use 2 oz prosecco and 2 oz soda.

recipe.title: Apple Fennel Vodka Collins

steps: Shake vodka, apple juice, lemon and fennel-seed syrup with ice for 12 seconds.
Strain into an ice-filled Collins glass and top with soda.
Stir gently and add the apple slice.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake 3 oz apple juice, 1/2 oz lemon juice and 1/4 oz fennel syrup with ice; strain and top with 3 oz soda.

recipe.note: An original Relish home cocktail. Please drink responsibly.
tips: For fennel syrup, steep 1/2 tsp fennel seeds in 1/2 cup hot simple syrup for 10 minutes, strain and cool. Prep assumes cooled syrup is ready.
recipe.make_ahead: Prepare to order. Keep juices and brewed teas refrigerated until needed.

recipe.title: Classic Apple Pie
recipe.description: The all-American double-crust pie: a flaky butter pastry filled with thinly sliced tart apples, cinnamon and a little brown sugar, baked until golden and bubbling.

ingredients.item: firm, tart apples (such as Granny Smith, or a mix with Honeycrisp), peeled, cored and sliced 1/4 inch thick

steps: Make the crust: mix the flour, salt and sugar, then cut in the butter until some pea-size pieces remain. Sprinkle in ice water a tablespoon at a time, mixing just until the dough holds together. Divide in two, flatten into disks, wrap and chill for at least 1 hour.
Toss the apples with the lemon juice, granulated sugar, brown sugar, flour, cinnamon, nutmeg and salt.
Heat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the lower third and a baking sheet on it.
Roll one disk into a 12-inch circle and fit it into a 9-inch pie dish. Pile in the apples, mounding them in the center.

Roll the second disk into an 11-inch circle and lay it over the top. Trim, fold the edges under and crimp. Cut 4 or 5 slits in the top, brush with milk and sprinkle with coarse sugar. Chill for 15 minutes.

Bake on the hot baking sheet for 20 minutes, then lower the oven to 375°F and bake for 45 to 50 minutes more, until deep golden and the juices bubble through the slits. Cover the edges with foil if they brown too fast.
Cool for at least 3 hours before slicing, so the filling can set.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Keep the butter cold and visible in the dough. Those flecks of butter make the crust flaky.
Firm apples hold their shape. Soft apples like McIntosh turn to applesauce.
Wait for the bubbling: the juices must boil to thicken.
recipe.make_ahead: Bake up to a day ahead and keep at room temperature, loosely covered.
variations: Serve warm with vanilla ice cream or a slice of sharp cheddar.

recipe.title: Appletini

ingredients.item: sour apple schnapps (such as DeKuyper Sour Apple Pucker)
thin green apple slice, to garnish

steps: Chill a martini glass.
Add the vodka, schnapps, apple juice and lemon juice to a shaker and fill it with ice.
Shake for 15 seconds.
Strain into the chilled glass and float the apple slice on top.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake 3 oz green apple juice, 1/2 oz lemon juice and 1/2 oz simple syrup with ice and strain.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Brush the apple slice with lemon juice so it doesn't turn brown.
Too sweet? Leave out the apple juice and add 1/2 oz more vodka.

recipe.title: Apricot Black Tea Whiskey Sour
recipe.description: Bourbon, apricot preserves and strong black tea make a mellow fruit sour with a bright lemon finish.

ingredients.item: thin fresh apricot wedge, for garnish

steps: Stir the preserves with the tea in a cocktail shaker until loosened. Add bourbon and lemon juice.
Fill with ice and shake firmly for 12 to 15 seconds. Double-strain through a fine sieve into a rocks glass over a large ice cube.
Garnish with the apricot wedge and lemon twist. Serve immediately.

cocktail.garnish: thin apricot wedge and lemon twist
cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Stir 2 oz cooled black tea, 3/4 oz lemon juice and 1 tbsp apricot preserves with ice; strain over fresh ice and add 1 oz soda water.

recipe.note: An original Relish home cocktail. Alcohol strength and sweetness vary by product; please drink responsibly.
tips: Choose smooth preserves rather than chunky jam so the drink strains easily. The finished sour has no egg-white foam.
recipe.make_ahead: Brew and chill the tea up to 2 days ahead. Shake the drink only when ready to serve.

recipe.note: An original Relish home cocktail. Please drink responsibly.
tips: A small rosemary sprig is enough; fine-strain to remove needles.

recipe.title: Apricot Thyme Rum Collins

Add rum, apricot nectar, lemon juice and ice. Shake for 12 seconds and fine-strain into an ice-filled Collins glass.
Top with soda and garnish with the apricot slice and reserved thyme sprig.

cocktail.garnish: thin apricot slice and small thyme sprig
cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake 3 oz apricot nectar, 1/2 oz lemon juice, thyme and syrup with ice; strain and add 3 oz soda.

recipe.note: An original Relish home cocktail. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Use thyme sparingly so the drink stays fruity rather than medicinal.
recipe.make_ahead: Prepare to order. Keep juices and brewed teas refrigerated until needed.

Pack the rolls seam side down in a pot lined with spare leaves.
Add the broth and lemon juice, weigh down with a plate and simmer 1 hour.
Serve with garlic yogurt.

Strain into a chilled coupe.

recipe.title: Aviation
recipe.description: Gin, maraschino, crème de violette and lemon, pale lavender in color.
steps: Shake everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: B-52
recipe.description: The famous layered shot: coffee liqueur, Irish cream and orange liqueur stacked in three neat stripes.
steps: Pour the coffee liqueur into a shot glass.
Slowly pour the Irish cream over the back of a bar spoon so it floats on top.
Float the Grand Marnier the same way to make the top layer.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Layer cold coffee syrup, a little cream and orange syrup in a shot glass.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Pour very slowly over the back of a spoon held just above the last layer.
Chill the liqueurs first; cold layers stay separate more easily.
variations: Flaming B-52: light the top layer briefly, then extinguish before drinking. Be very careful.

vegan.title: Vegan B-52
vegan.description: The same layered shot made with an almond-based vegan Irish cream.

ingredients.item: vegan Irish cream (such as an almond-based one)

steps: Pour the coffee liqueur into a shot glass.
Slowly pour the vegan Irish cream over the back of a bar spoon so it floats on top.
Float the Grand Marnier the same way to make the top layer.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Layer cold coffee syrup, a little oat cream and orange syrup in a shot glass.

vegan.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Pour very slowly over the back of a spoon held just above the last layer.
Chill the liqueurs first; cold layers stay separate more easily.

recipe.title: Bacardi Cocktail
recipe.description: Bacardi rum with lime and grenadine.
steps: Shake everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Lime and grenadine topped with lemon-lime soda.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Bahama Mama
recipe.description: Tropical rum punch with coconut rum, coffee liqueur and fruit juices.
steps: Shake everything with ice.
Strain into a hurricane glass with ice.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Pineapple, orange, grenadine and a splash of coconut water.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Baked Cod with Tomato Chickpeas
recipe.description: Cod baked over garlicky tomato chickpeas with lemon and parsley.

ingredients.item: chickpeas (15 oz each), drained and rinsed
lemon, half juiced and half cut into wedges

steps: Heat oven to 400 F (200 C). Toss chickpeas, tomatoes, garlic, oil, oregano and half the salt in a baking dish. Bake for 15 minutes.
Season cod with remaining salt, pepper and lemon juice. Nestle the portions into the hot chickpeas.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes more, until each fish portion reaches 145 F (63 C).
Scatter with parsley and serve with lemon wedges.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: The tomato juices should keep the beans moist; add a splash of water if the dish looks dry.
recipe.make_ahead: Refrigerate promptly and use within 2 days. Reheat leftovers to 165 F (74 C).

recipe.title: Baked Lemon-Dill Cod
recipe.description: Tender cod baked with lemon, dill and garlic butter, alongside roasted green beans. Light and on the table in under 30 minutes.
steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Toss green beans with oil and half the salt on a sheet pan; roast 5 minutes.
Mix butter, lemon zest, dill and garlic. Add cod to pan, season with remaining salt and pepper, and spoon butter mixture over it.
Bake 12–15 minutes until fish flakes and reaches 145°F. Finish with lemon juice.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Baked Trout with Almond Green Beans
recipe.description: Lemon-baked trout with green beans, toasted almonds and parsley.

ingredients.item: lemon, half juiced and half cut into wedges

steps: Heat oven to 400 F (200 C). Put trout on a lined sheet pan. Brush with 1 tbsp oil and half the lemon juice; season with half the salt and pepper.
Bake for 12 to 16 minutes, until the thickest part reaches 145 F (63 C).
Meanwhile boil green beans for 4 to 5 minutes until just tender, then drain. Toast almonds in a dry skillet for 3 minutes; set aside.
Warm remaining oil and garlic in the skillet for 30 seconds. Toss in beans, remaining lemon juice and salt. Serve with trout, almonds, parsley and lemon wedges.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Check fillets for pin bones. Almonds are intentionally included and cannot be treated as an optional unlisted allergen.
recipe.make_ahead: Refrigerate fish and beans promptly and use within 2 days. Keep almonds separate to retain crunch.

recipe.title: Baked Ziti
recipe.description: Ziti baked in marinara with ricotta, mozzarella and Parmesan.
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Cook the ziti 2 minutes less than the package says.
Brown the sausage until cooked through (160°F) and stir in the marinara and oregano.
Toss the pasta with the sauce and dollop half into a baking dish. Add spoonfuls of ricotta and half the mozzarella.
Add the rest of the pasta and top with the remaining mozzarella and Parmesan.
Cover with foil and bake 20 minutes, uncover and bake 10 minutes more. Top with basil.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Baklava
recipe.description: Greek layered pastry: sheets of crisp, buttery phyllo filled with cinnamon-spiced walnuts and soaked in a honey and lemon syrup.
steps: Make the syrup: simmer the sugar, water, honey, lemon juice and cinnamon stick for 10 minutes. Remove the cinnamon and let the syrup cool completely.
Heat the oven to 350°F and butter a 9x13-inch baking pan. Mix the walnuts, 1/3 cup sugar, cinnamon and cloves.
Unroll the phyllo and keep it covered with a damp towel. Lay 8 sheets in the pan, brushing each one with butter.
Sprinkle a third of the walnuts over the phyllo. Add 6 more buttered sheets, then another third of the nuts, 6 more sheets, and the last of the nuts.
Finish with 8 to 10 buttered sheets, brushing the top generously.
With a sharp knife, cut all the way through into 24 diamonds or squares.
Bake for 45 to 50 minutes, until deep golden and crisp.
Pour the cooled syrup slowly over the hot baklava. Let it sit uncovered for at least 6 hours, or overnight, before serving.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Pour cool syrup over hot baklava, never hot over hot. That keeps the layers crisp instead of soggy.
Cut before baking. Baked phyllo shatters if you try to cut it afterwards.
Keep the phyllo covered while you work, or it dries out and cracks.
recipe.make_ahead: Store at room temperature, loosely covered, for up to 1 week. Don't refrigerate; it softens the pastry.
variations: Use pistachios, or a mix of walnuts and pistachios, for the filling.

recipe.title: Bamboo
recipe.description: A light, low-alcohol stir of dry sherry and dry vermouth.

ingredients.item: vegan fino sherry (such as Tio Pepe)
vegan dry vermouth (such as Dolin Dry)

steps: Stir everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Bangers and Mash with Onion Gravy
recipe.description: The great British pub supper: plump pork sausages on creamy mashed potatoes, smothered in a rich, slow-cooked onion gravy. Peas on the side.

ingredients.item: Yukon Gold or russet potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
salt and black pepper, to taste

steps: Make the gravy: melt 2 tablespoons butter in a skillet over medium-low heat. Add the onions and a pinch of salt and cook, stirring now and then, for 20 to 25 minutes, until soft and deep golden. Add the garlic and brown sugar for the last 2 minutes.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute. Gradually stir in the broth, mustard and thyme, if using, and simmer for 5 to 8 minutes, until thickened. Season with pepper.
Meanwhile, boil the potatoes in salted water for 15 to 20 minutes, until tender. Drain, then mash with the remaining 3 tablespoons butter and the warm milk. Season with salt and pepper.
While everything cooks, heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-low heat. Cook the sausages for 15 to 20 minutes, turning often, until browned all over and cooked through (160°F).
Pile the mash onto plates, top with two sausages each and spoon over plenty of onion gravy. Serve with peas.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Cook the sausages gently. High heat splits the skins, which is how "bangers" got their name.
Don't rush the onions. Their slow-cooked sweetness is what makes the gravy.
recipe.make_ahead: Make the gravy up to 3 days ahead and reheat with a splash of water.
variations: Use Cumberland, Lincolnshire or Irish-style sausages if you can find them.
Toad in the hole: bake the browned sausages in a Yorkshire pudding batter instead.

recipe.title: Pork Banh Mi
recipe.description: Vietnamese baguette with lemongrass pork, pickled vegetables, cilantro, chiles and mayo.

ingredients.item: Vietnamese baguettes or soft French rolls

steps: Toss the carrot and daikon in the sweetened vinegar and let stand 30 minutes.
Marinate the pork in the lemongrass, fish sauce, soy sauce and sugar for 20 minutes.
Sear the pork in a hot skillet until caramelized.
Split and toast the rolls, spread with mayonnaise and fill with pork, pickles, cucumber, cilantro and jalapeño.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Barracuda
recipe.description: A sunny Italian classic from the 1960s: gold rum, vanilla-herbal Galliano, pineapple and lime, shaken and topped with a splash of Prosecco.

ingredients.item: vegan prosecco (such as Mionetto Organic), chilled

steps: Shake the rum, Galliano, pineapple juice and lime with ice until very cold.
Strain into a chilled coupe or margarita glass.
Top with the Prosecco and garnish with a pineapple wedge.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake pineapple juice, lime and a little vanilla syrup, then top with sparkling white grape juice.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Galliano's vanilla and anise notes are the heart of the drink; there isn't a close substitute.
Shaking pineapple juice gives the drink a lovely frothy head.
variations: Serve it in a hollowed-out pineapple for a party.

recipe.title: Bay Breeze
recipe.description: A sweet, pink beach drink of vodka with cranberry and pineapple juice over ice.
steps: Fill a highball glass with ice.
Pour in the vodka and cranberry juice.
Top with the pineapple juice, which floats for a two-tone look, then stir if you like.
Garnish with the lime wedge.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Build 4 oz cranberry juice and 2 oz pineapple juice over ice with a squeeze of lime.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Shake the pineapple juice with ice first for a frothy top.
variations: Use coconut rum instead of vodka for a more tropical drink.

recipe.title: Oven-Baked BBQ Ribs
recipe.description: Fall-off-the-bone baby back ribs without a smoker: rubbed with smoky spices, baked low and slow in foil, then brushed with barbecue sauce and broiled until sticky.

ingredients.item: baby back pork ribs (about 5 lb total)

steps: Heat the oven to 275°F. Pull the thin, shiny membrane off the bone side of each rack, using a paper towel to grip it. Pat the ribs dry.
Mix the brown sugar, paprika, salt, garlic powder, onion powder, black pepper, chili powder and cayenne. Rub it all over both racks.
Wrap each rack tightly in heavy-duty foil, meat side up, and set them on a baking sheet.
Bake for 2 1/2 to 3 hours, until the meat is very tender and has pulled back from the ends of the bones.
Carefully open the foil, pour off the juices and turn on the broiler.

Brush the ribs thickly with barbecue sauce and broil for 3 to 5 minutes, watching closely, until sticky and lightly charred. Brush with more sauce and rest for 5 minutes before cutting between the bones.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Removing the membrane lets the rub in and makes the ribs more tender to eat.
Low heat and a tight foil seal steam the ribs until tender without drying them out.
Check the label if you need to avoid fish: some barbecue sauces contain Worcestershire sauce, which is made with anchovies.
recipe.make_ahead: Bake the ribs in foil up to 2 days ahead and refrigerate. Sauce and broil just before serving.
variations: Spare ribs or St. Louis ribs: bake for about 30 minutes longer.
Finish on a hot grill instead of under the broiler.

recipe.title: Beef Bourguignon
recipe.description: French beef braised in red wine with bacon, mushrooms and pearl onions.
steps: Heat the oven to 325°F. Cook the bacon in a Dutch oven and remove. Brown the beef in the fat in batches.
Return the beef and bacon, toss with the flour, then add the wine, broth, tomato paste, garlic and herbs.
Cover and braise 2 1/2 hours. Add the carrots for the last hour.
Brown the onions and mushrooms in the butter and stir into the stew.
Season and serve with potatoes or crusty bread.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Beef Broccoli Udon Skillet
recipe.description: Thick udon noodles with beef strips, broccoli and a glossy ginger-soy glaze.

ingredients.item: beef sirloin, thinly sliced across the grain

steps: Cook udon according to its package and drain. Whisk soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, ginger, garlic, cornstarch and water.
Heat half the neutral oil in a wide skillet over high heat. Sear beef in batches for 2 to 3 minutes, until cooked through; transfer to a plate.
Add remaining oil, broccoli and 2 tbsp water. Cover for 3 minutes, then uncover and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Return beef with udon and sauce. Toss over medium heat for 2 minutes until the glaze thickens and beef is fully cooked. Finish with sesame oil, scallions and seeds.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Use thin slices cut from a whole sirloin steak, not ground beef. Cook the meat fully; avoid crowding the skillet.
recipe.make_ahead: Refrigerate promptly in shallow containers for up to 3 days. Reheat leftovers to 165 F (74 C).

recipe.title: Beef Bulgogi
recipe.description: Thin slices of beef in a sweet soy, garlic and sesame marinade, quickly seared.
steps: Mix the soy sauce, sugar, pear, sesame oil, garlic and ginger. Marinate the beef 30 minutes or longer.
Cook in a very hot skillet in batches 2 to 3 minutes until caramelized.
Top with green onions and sesame seeds and serve with rice and lettuce leaves.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Beef Burrito
recipe.description: A big flour tortilla stuffed with seasoned ground beef, rice, beans and cheese.

ingredients.item: gluten-free taco seasoning (such as McCormick Gluten Free)

steps: Brown the beef until cooked through (160°F), drain the fat, then stir in the taco seasoning and 1/3 cup water and simmer 5 minutes.
Warm the beans and the tortillas.
Fill each tortilla with rice, beef, beans, cheese, salsa, sour cream and lettuce.
Fold in the sides and roll up tightly. Toast seam side down in a dry skillet for 1 minute if you like.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Beef Empanadas
recipe.description: Flaky baked pastries filled with spiced beef, onion, olives and egg.
steps: Cook the onion and pepper until soft, add the beef and spices and cook through (160°F). Stir in the olives and cool.
Heat the oven to 400°F.
Fill each round with beef and a little egg, fold over and crimp the edges.
Brush with beaten egg and bake 20 to 25 minutes until golden.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Beef Kofta
recipe.description: Grilled skewers of spiced ground beef and onion, served with yogurt sauce.

ingredients.item: small onion, grated and squeezed dry
plain yogurt with grated cucumber and mint

steps: Knead the meat with the onion, parsley, garlic, spices and salt until sticky.
Shape around skewers into long sausages.
Grill over medium-high heat 10 to 12 minutes, turning, until cooked through (160°F).
Serve with the yogurt sauce, flatbread and salad.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Beef Pot Roast
recipe.description: Fork-tender braised chuck roast with carrots, potatoes and rich gravy.
steps: Heat the oven to 325°F. Season the roast well and brown it on all sides in the oil.
Add the onion and garlic, then the tomato paste, wine, broth and herbs.
Cover and braise in the oven 2 1/2 hours.
Add the carrots and potatoes and cook 1 hour more until tender.
Thicken the liquid with the flour mixture on the stove to make gravy.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Beef Stew
recipe.description: Chunks of beef braised with potatoes, carrots and onions in a rich gravy.
steps: Toss the beef with salt, pepper and flour, then brown in batches in the oil.
Cook the onion and garlic, stir in the tomato paste, then add the broth, Worcestershire, bay leaves and thyme.
Return the beef, cover and simmer 1 1/2 hours.
Add the carrots and potatoes and simmer 45 minutes until tender.
Stir in the peas for the last 5 minutes and season.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Beef Stroganoff
recipe.description: Tender strips of beef and mushrooms in a creamy sour cream sauce over egg noodles.
steps: Sear the beef in the oil in batches over high heat. Remove.
Melt the butter and cook the onion and mushrooms until browned.
Stir in the flour, then the broth and mustard, and simmer until thick.
Off the heat, stir in the sour cream and the beef.
Serve over the cooked noodles with parsley.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Beef Tacos
recipe.description: Seasoned ground beef in crisp or soft shells with lettuce, cheese and salsa.
steps: Brown the beef and onion until cooked through (160°F) and drain the fat.
Add the spices, salt and tomato sauce and simmer 5 minutes.
Warm the shells and fill with beef, lettuce, cheese, salsa and sour cream.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Beef Tomato Butter Bean Stew
recipe.description: Fork-tender beef and large white beans in a tomato, carrot and thyme stew.

ingredients.item: large white lima beans (15 oz), drained and rinsed

steps: Pat beef dry and season with salt and pepper. Heat oil in a heavy pot and brown beef in batches for 8 to 10 minutes; set aside.
Soften onion for 5 minutes, then add garlic, thyme and paprika for 30 seconds. Add tomatoes and water, scraping the pot.
Return beef, cover and simmer very gently for 75 minutes. Add carrots and cook for 20 minutes more, until beef is fully cooked and easily pierced with a fork; add water if the sauce gets dry.
Stir in beans and simmer for 5 minutes. Finish with parsley.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Large white lima beans are also sold as butter beans; they are legumes, not dairy. Tenderness, not merely the minimum meat temperature, determines when the stew is ready.
recipe.make_ahead: Refrigerate promptly in shallow containers for up to 3 days. Reheat leftovers to 165 F (74 C).

recipe.title: Beef Wellington
recipe.description: Beef tenderloin wrapped in mushroom duxelles, prosciutto and golden puff pastry.
steps: Season and sear the beef on all sides in the oil. Brush with mustard and cool.
Cook the mushrooms and shallots in the butter until all the moisture is gone. Cool.
Lay the prosciutto overlapping on plastic wrap, spread with the mushrooms, set the beef on top and roll tightly. Chill 20 minutes.
Wrap in the rolled-out pastry, seal, brush with egg and chill 15 minutes.
Bake at 425°F for 35 to 40 minutes until 125°F inside for medium-rare. Rest 10 minutes before slicing.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: USDA's safe minimum for beef roasts is 145°F with a 3-minute rest. 125°F out of the oven gives medium-rare after resting.

recipe.title: Bee's Knees
recipe.description: Gin, lemon and honey, a Prohibition classic.
steps: Shake everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake lemon and honey syrup and top with ginger ale.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Belgian Waffles
recipe.description: Tall, crisp waffles with a fluffy center, served with berries and syrup.

ingredients.item: berries, whipped cream and maple syrup

steps: Heat the waffle iron.
Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt.
Mix the yolks, milk, butter and vanilla and stir into the dry ingredients.
Beat the egg whites to soft peaks and fold in.
Cook in the waffle iron until golden and crisp. Serve with the toppings.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Bellini
recipe.description: White peach puree topped with prosecco, from Harry's Bar in Venice.
steps: Pour the peach puree into a flute.
Top slowly with prosecco and stir gently.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Peach puree with alcohol-free sparkling wine.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Benton's Old Fashioned
recipe.description: A bacon fat-washed bourbon Old Fashioned sweetened with maple syrup.
steps: Stir everything with ice.
Strain over a large cube and express an orange peel over it.
recipe.note: To fat-wash, stir 1 oz warm bacon fat into a 750 ml bottle of bourbon, freeze, then strain out the solid fat.

recipe.title: Betsy Ross
recipe.description: Brandy and ruby port with orange curaçao and bitters.

ingredients.item: vegan ruby port (such as Cockburn's Special Reserve)

steps: Stir everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Between the Sheets
recipe.description: Cognac, white rum, orange liqueur and lemon.
steps: Shake everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Bibimbap
recipe.description: Korean rice bowl with seasoned vegetables, beef, a fried egg and gochujang sauce.
steps: Cook the beef with 1 tbsp soy sauce, sugar and 1 tsp sesame oil.
Season the spinach and sprouts with a little sesame oil, soy and salt. Sauté the carrot and zucchini separately.
Fry the eggs sunny side up.
Mix the gochujang with 1 tbsp sesame oil and a splash of water.
Fill bowls with rice, arrange the vegetables and beef on top, add an egg and serve with the sauce and sesame seeds.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Sunny-side-up eggs have runny yolks. For anyone pregnant, older or with a weakened immune system, cook them until firm or use pasteurized eggs.

recipe.title: Bigos (Polish Hunter's Stew)
recipe.description: Poland's slow-cooked hunter's stew: sauerkraut and fresh cabbage braised with smoked kielbasa, pork, wild mushrooms, prunes and red wine until rich, tangy and deeply savory.

ingredients.item: pork shoulder, cut into bite-size pieces
salt and plenty of black pepper
rye bread or boiled potatoes, to serve

steps: Soak the porcini in the boiling water for 20 minutes. Lift them out, chop them, and keep the soaking liquid, leaving any grit behind.
In a large heavy pot, cook the bacon until crisp. Brown the pork in the fat for 6 to 8 minutes, then the kielbasa for 3 minutes. Lift everything out.
Cook the onion in the same pot for 5 minutes. Add the cabbage and cook 10 minutes until it wilts.
Add the sauerkraut, meats, mushrooms and their liquid, prunes, wine, tomato paste and all the spices. Stir well.
Cover and simmer very gently for 2 hours, stirring now and then and adding a splash of water if it gets dry. It should be thick, glossy and brown.
Taste and balance: add a splash of sauerkraut juice if it's too sweet, or a pinch of sugar if too sour. Serve with rye bread or potatoes.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Bigos is famously better on the second and third day. Many Polish cooks reheat it for several days in a row before serving.
Taste the sauerkraut first. If it's very sour, rinse it once before using.
The dried porcini and prunes give bigos its deep, smoky-sweet flavor; don't leave them out.
recipe.make_ahead: Keeps 5 days in the fridge and freezes for 3 months; the flavor improves each time it's reheated.
variations: Add leftover roast meats such as beef, venison or duck, as hunters once did.

vegetarian.title: Vegetarian Bigos
vegetarian.description: The same tangy sauerkraut and cabbage stew, made smoky with smoked paprika and rich with plenty of fresh and dried mushrooms.

ingredients.item: smoked tofu, cubed, and 2 tsp smoked paprika
salt and plenty of black pepper
rye bread or boiled potatoes, to serve

steps: Soak the porcini in the boiling water for 20 minutes. Lift them out, chop them, and keep the soaking liquid, leaving any grit behind.
Heat the oil in a large heavy pot. Brown the fresh mushrooms for 6 to 8 minutes, then the smoked tofu for 3 minutes. Lift everything out.
Cook the onion in the same pot for 5 minutes. Add the cabbage and cook 10 minutes until it wilts.
Add the sauerkraut, browned mushrooms and tofu, the porcini and their liquid, prunes, wine, tomato paste and all the spices. Stir well.
Cover and simmer very gently for 1 hour, stirring now and then and adding a splash of water if it gets dry. It should be thick, glossy and brown.
Taste and balance: add a splash of sauerkraut juice if it's too sweet, or a pinch of sugar if too sour. Serve with rye bread or potatoes.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Bigos is famously better on the second and third day. Many Polish cooks reheat it for several days in a row before serving.
Taste the sauerkraut first. If it's very sour, rinse it once before using.
The dried porcini and prunes give bigos its deep, smoky-sweet flavor; don't leave them out.
vegetarian.make_ahead: Keeps 5 days in the fridge and freezes for 3 months; the flavor improves each time it's reheated.

rye bread or boiled potatoes, to serve

Taste and balance: add a splash of sauerkraut juice if it's too sweet, or a pinch of sugar if too sour. Serve with rye bread or potatoes.
vegan.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Bigos is famously better on the second and third day. Many Polish cooks reheat it for several days in a row before serving.
Taste the sauerkraut first. If it's very sour, rinse it once before using.
The dried porcini and prunes give bigos its deep, smoky-sweet flavor; don't leave them out.
vegan.make_ahead: Keeps 5 days in the fridge and freezes for 3 months; the flavor improves each time it's reheated.

steps: Marinate the chicken in the yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, spices and 1 tsp salt for at least 30 minutes.

recipe.title: Biscuits and Sausage Gravy
recipe.description: The Southern breakfast classic: tall, flaky buttermilk biscuits split open and smothered in creamy, peppery pork sausage gravy.

ingredients.item: all-purpose flour, plus more for the counter
cold buttermilk, plus more for brushing

steps: Heat the oven to 450°F and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Whisk the 2 1/2 cups flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt and sugar. Cut in the butter with a pastry cutter or your fingertips until it looks like coarse crumbs with some pea-size pieces.
Stir in the buttermilk just until a shaggy dough forms. Turn it out on a floured counter, pat it into a rectangle, fold it in half, and pat out again. Repeat twice, then pat to 1 inch thick.
Cut out 2 1/2-inch rounds, pressing straight down without twisting. Set them on the baking sheet, touching, and brush the tops with buttermilk.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes, until tall and golden.
Meanwhile, brown the sausage in a large skillet over medium heat, breaking it up, for 8 to 10 minutes. Don't drain the fat.

Sprinkle the 1/3 cup flour over the sausage and stir for 1 to 2 minutes. Slowly stir in the warm milk and simmer, stirring, for 5 to 8 minutes, until thick and creamy. Season with the pepper and salt.
Split the warm biscuits and spoon the gravy over.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Keep the butter and buttermilk cold, and handle the dough as little as possible. That's what makes biscuits flaky and tall.
Placing the biscuits so they touch helps them rise up instead of spreading out.
Gravy too thick? Stir in more milk. Too thin? Simmer a few minutes longer.
recipe.make_ahead: Freeze unbaked biscuits on the tray, then bag them. Bake from frozen for 2 to 3 minutes longer.

recipe.title: Blue Hawaii
recipe.description: The Waikiki classic: rum and vodka shaken with pineapple, fresh sweet-and-sour and blue curaçao, for a tropical drink that's as bright as it tastes.

steps: Fill a hurricane or tall glass with crushed or cubed ice.

Shake hard for 10 to 12 seconds. Pineapple juice foams nicely when shaken hard, giving the drink a light, frothy top.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake 4 oz pineapple juice, 1/2 oz lemon juice and 1/2 oz blue raspberry or blue curaçao-flavored syrup with ice and top with lemon-lime soda.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Fresh lemon and simple syrup replace the bottled sweet-and-sour mix used in many bars. It tastes brighter and less artificial.
Use 100% pineapple juice, not a pineapple drink or cocktail, which adds extra sugar.
The color comes only from the curaçao. Yellow pineapple juice turns it slightly greener; that's normal.
recipe.make_ahead: For a pitcher of 6: mix 4 1/2 oz rum, 4 1/2 oz vodka, 3 oz blue curaçao, 18 oz pineapple juice, 3 oz lemon juice and 3 oz syrup. Chill and pour over ice the same day.
variations: Blue Hawaiian: skip the vodka and lemon and add 1 oz cream of coconut for a creamier piña colada-style drink.
Frozen: blend everything with 1 1/2 cups ice.

recipe.title: Ukrainian Borscht
recipe.description: Ukraine's ruby-red beet soup: beef broth simmered with beets, cabbage, potatoes and carrots, made tangy with a splash of vinegar and finished with dill and sour cream.

ingredients.item: boneless beef chuck, cut into 3/4-inch cubes
kosher salt, plus more to taste
medium beets, peeled and grated or cut into thin matchsticks
white vinegar, plus more to taste
chopped fresh dill, plus more to serve

steps: Put the beef, water, bay leaf and 1 teaspoon salt in a large pot. Bring to a boil, skim off the foam, then cover partly and simmer for 1 hour, until the beef is nearly tender.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion and carrot for 5 minutes, until soft.
Add the beets, tomato paste, vinegar and sugar and cook, stirring, for 10 minutes, adding a splash of broth if it starts to stick. The vinegar keeps the beets bright red.
Add the potatoes and the rest of the salt to the broth and simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in the cabbage and the beet mixture and simmer for 10 minutes more, until all the vegetables are tender.
Turn off the heat, stir in the garlic and dill, and let the soup stand for 10 minutes. Taste and add more salt or vinegar.
Serve with a spoonful of sour cream and more dill.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Taste at the end for balance. Borscht should be both sweet from the beets and clearly tangy.
Dark rye bread is the classic side.
Wear gloves when grating beets, or rub your hands with lemon juice afterwards to remove stains.
recipe.make_ahead: Borscht tastes even better the next day. Refrigerate for up to 4 days or freeze for up to 3 months.
variations: Vegetarian borscht: skip the beef, use vegetable broth and add a can of drained white beans with the cabbage.

steps: Heat oven to 375 F (190 C). Simmer quinoa in water, covered, for 15 minutes or until tender; rest for 5 minutes.
Steam broccoli for 3 minutes until bright green but still firm. Brush a 9-inch baking dish with oil.

recipe.title: Fudgy Brownies
recipe.description: Dense, chewy, deeply chocolatey brownies with a crackly top, made in one bowl with melted butter, chocolate and cocoa.
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Line an 8-inch square pan with parchment, leaving an overhang.
Melt the butter and chopped chocolate together in a bowl in the microwave in 30-second bursts, stirring, until smooth.
Whisk in the sugar, then the eggs and vanilla, and keep whisking for 1 minute, until thick and glossy.
Stir in the cocoa, flour and salt just until combined, then fold in the chocolate chips, if using.
Spread the batter in the pan and bake for 22 to 26 minutes, until a toothpick in the center comes out with moist crumbs.

recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Check the chocolate label if you avoid soy: many brands contain soy lecithin.
Whisking the eggs and sugar hard is what gives brownies their shiny, crackly top.
Pull them out while the center still looks slightly underdone. They firm up as they cool.
recipe.make_ahead: Store airtight for up to 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months.
variations: Double the recipe in a 9x13-inch pan and bake for about 30 minutes.

recipe.title: Buffalo Wings
recipe.description: The 1964 Anchor Bar original from Buffalo, New York: crisp fried, unbreaded wings tossed in hot sauce and butter, with celery sticks and blue cheese dip.

ingredients.item: chicken wings, split into flats and drumettes, tips removed
vegetable or canola oil, for frying
Frank's RedHot Original cayenne pepper sauce

steps: Make the blue cheese dip: mix the mayonnaise, sour cream, blue cheese, lemon juice and garlic with a pinch of salt and pepper. Chill until needed.
Pat the wings very dry with paper towels and season with the salt.
Heat 2 inches of oil in a heavy pot to 375°F. Fry the wings in batches for 10 to 12 minutes, until golden, very crisp and cooked through (165°F). Drain on a rack.
Meanwhile, melt the butter with the hot sauce in a small pan, whisking to combine. Keep it warm.
Toss the hot wings in a large bowl with the sauce until well coated.
Serve right away with the celery sticks and blue cheese dip.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Dry wings fry crisper and spatter less. For extra crisp skin, leave them uncovered in the fridge for a few hours first.
More butter makes milder wings; less butter makes them hotter.
To bake instead: toss the dry wings with 1 tbsp baking powder and the salt and bake on a rack at 425°F for 45 to 50 minutes, turning once.
recipe.make_ahead: Make the blue cheese dip up to 3 days ahead.

recipe.title: Bun Cha
recipe.description: Hanoi-style grilled pork patties in a sweet-sour dipping broth with rice noodles and herbs.

ingredients.item: lettuce, mint, cilantro, Thai basil, pickled carrot and chiles

steps: Mix the pork with 1 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp sugar, shallots, half the garlic and the pepper. Shape into small patties.
Grill or broil the patties until charred and cooked through (160°F), about 4 minutes per side.
Stir the remaining fish sauce, sugar and garlic with the lime juice and warm water for the dipping broth.
Put the patties in bowls of the broth and serve with noodles, herbs and pickles to dip.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Butter Chicken
recipe.description: Tender chicken in a mild, silky tomato sauce enriched with butter and cream.

ingredients.item: boneless chicken thighs, cut into pieces

steps: Marinate the chicken in the yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, 1 tsp garam masala and the chile powder for 30 minutes.
Sear the chicken in 1 tbsp butter until browned. Set aside.
Melt the remaining butter and cook the onion until soft. Add the tomato puree and simmer 10 minutes.
Blend the sauce smooth if you like, then add the chicken and simmer 10 minutes, until it reaches 165°F.
Stir in the cream, remaining garam masala, crushed fenugreek, sugar and salt. Top with cilantro and serve with rice or naan.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Buttermilk Pancakes
recipe.description: Fluffy, golden buttermilk pancakes.

ingredients.item: butter and maple syrup, to serve

steps: Whisk the dry ingredients together.
Whisk the buttermilk, eggs and melted butter, then stir into the dry ingredients until just combined. Lumps are fine.
Cook 1/4-cup portions on a buttered griddle over medium heat until bubbles form, then flip and cook 1 to 2 minutes more.
Serve with butter and syrup.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Butternut Squash and Sage Pasta
recipe.description: Caramelized roasted butternut squash tossed with penne, crispy sage brown butter and Parmesan. Autumn in a bowl.
steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Toss squash with oil and salt; roast 25–30 minutes until tender and browned at the edges.
Cook penne in salted water until al dente; reserve 1 cup pasta water, then drain.
Melt butter in a large skillet and crisp sage briefly. Toss in squash, pasta, Parmesan and enough pasta water to make a light sauce. Season with pepper.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Stuffed Cabbage Rolls
recipe.description: Cabbage leaves rolled around beef and rice, baked in a sweet-sour tomato sauce.
steps: Core the cabbage and boil it whole, peeling off 12 leaves as they soften. Trim the thick ribs.
Mix the meats, rice, onion, garlic, paprika, salt and pepper.
Roll a portion of filling in each leaf, tucking in the sides.
Mix the tomatoes, sugar and lemon juice. Spread some in a dish, add the rolls and cover with the rest.
Cover and bake at 350°F for 1 1/2 hours.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Cable Car
recipe.description: Spiced rum, orange curaçao and lemon with a cinnamon-sugar rim.
steps: Rim a coupe with cinnamon sugar.
Shake everything with ice and strain into the glass.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Cacio e Pepe
recipe.description: Rome's three-ingredient pasta: spaghetti tossed with finely grated Pecorino Romano, starchy pasta water and lots of toasted black pepper into a creamy, peppery sauce.

ingredients.item: very finely grated Pecorino Romano, plus more to serve

steps: Bring a pot of water to a boil, using less water than usual so it gets extra starchy, and salt it lightly. Pecorino is salty.
Cook the pasta until 2 minutes short of al dente. Before draining, scoop out 2 cups of the cooking water.
While the pasta cooks, toast the pepper in a large, dry skillet over medium heat for 1 minute, until fragrant. Ladle in 1/2 cup of the pasta cooking water and let it simmer.
Put the cheese in a bowl and stir in about 1/3 cup of the warm (not boiling) pasta water to make a smooth, thick paste.
Add the drained pasta to the skillet and toss for 1 to 2 minutes, adding splashes of pasta water, until al dente.
Take the pan off the heat. Let it cool for 30 seconds, then add the cheese paste and toss quickly, adding more pasta water a little at a time, until the sauce is creamy and coats the pasta.
Serve right away with more pecorino and pepper.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: If the cheese is too hot, it clumps. Mixing it into a paste with warm water first, off the heat, keeps the sauce smooth.
Grate the cheese on the finest holes of the grater. Coarse shreds won't melt into a sauce.
Pecorino Romano is made with animal rennet, so this dish isn't vegetarian.
variations: Add 2 tablespoons of butter to the pan with the pepper for an even silkier, more forgiving sauce.

recipe.title: Caesar Salad
recipe.description: Crisp romaine with homemade croutons, Parmesan and a creamy anchovy-garlic dressing.
steps: Toss the bread with 2 tbsp oil and bake at 375°F for 10 minutes until golden.
Mash the anchovies and garlic, then whisk in the yolk, lemon and mustard.
Slowly whisk in the 1/2 cup oil until thick, then stir in half the Parmesan.
Toss the romaine with the dressing, croutons and the remaining Parmesan.
recipe.note: The dressing uses a raw egg yolk. Use a pasteurized egg if you prefer.

recipe.title: Café Brûlot
recipe.description: New Orleans' flaming coffee: brandy and orange liqueur warmed with sugar, cinnamon, cloves and citrus peel, set alight, then mixed with hot dark coffee.

ingredients.item: orange, peel cut in one long strip
hot strong coffee (New Orleans chicory coffee is traditional)

steps: Put the citrus peels, cinnamon, cloves and sugar cubes in a heatproof bowl or small saucepan.
Add the brandy and curaçao and warm gently over low heat, stirring to dissolve the sugar. Don't let it boil.
Away from anything flammable, carefully light the warm brandy with a long match. Ladle it over the orange peel for a minute as it flames.
Slowly pour in the hot coffee to put out the flames. Stir and ladle into heatproof glasses, with a strip of peel in each.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Simmer coffee with orange peel, cinnamon, cloves and sugar, and serve hot.

recipe.note: Flaming alcohol is dangerous. Work slowly, keep a lid nearby to smother the flame, and never pour spirits from the bottle near a flame.
tips: Warm the brandy only gently; if it's too hot it may flare up suddenly.
Use heatproof glasses or mugs, and keep long hair and sleeves away from the flame.
variations: Stud the orange peel with the cloves for the classic restaurant presentation.

recipe.title: Caipirinha
recipe.description: Brazil's cachaça muddled with lime and sugar.
steps: Muddle the lime and sugar in a rocks glass.
Add the cachaça and fill with crushed ice. Stir.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Muddle lime and sugar and top with guaraná soda (such as Guaraná Antarctica) or lemon-lime soda.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Caipiroska
recipe.description: A caipirinha made with vodka.
steps: Muddle the lime and sugar in a rocks glass.
Add the vodka, fill with crushed ice and stir.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Muddle lime and sugar and top with lemon-lime soda.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Cajun Shrimp and Corn Rice Skillet
recipe.description: Cajun-seasoned shrimp, sweet corn and rice cooked together in a skillet.
steps: Toss shrimp with half the oil, Cajun seasoning and half the salt. Cook in a large skillet over medium-high heat for 2–3 minutes per side, until opaque and cooked through. Transfer to a plate.
Add remaining oil, corn and rice to the skillet; cook, stirring, 4–5 minutes until piping hot. Season with remaining salt.
Return shrimp to the pan and warm through. Finish with scallions and lemon juice.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Caldo Verde (Portuguese Kale Soup)
recipe.description: Portugal's beloved green soup: a velvety potato and onion broth, finished with ribbons of collard greens or kale and slices of smoky chouriço, with a ribbon of good olive oil on top.

ingredients.item: extra-virgin olive oil, plus more to serve
Portuguese chouriço or linguiça, thinly sliced
floury potatoes (Yukon Gold or russet), peeled and cut in chunks
collard greens or lacinato kale, stems removed
black pepper and crusty cornbread (broa), to serve

steps: Warm the olive oil in a large pot and fry the chouriço for 3 to 4 minutes, until lightly browned. Lift it out, leaving the paprika-red oil behind.
Cook the onion in the same oil for 6 to 8 minutes, until soft, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the potatoes, water and salt. Bring to a boil and simmer, partly covered, for 20 minutes, until the potatoes fall apart.
Meanwhile, stack the greens, roll them up tightly like a cigar and slice as thinly as you can into fine ribbons.
Blend the soup until smooth, right in the pot with a stick blender. It should be creamy but pourable; add water if it's too thick.
Bring back to a simmer, add the greens and cook 3 to 5 minutes, until bright green and just tender. Taste for salt.
Ladle into bowls, top with the chouriço and a thin drizzle of olive oil, and serve with cornbread.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Slice the greens as thin as angel hair. That fine chiffonade is what makes caldo verde: it cooks in minutes and stays bright green.
Don't add too much water at the start. You can thin the purée later, but a watery soup is hard to fix.
Add the greens only at the end so they keep their color and a little bite.
recipe.make_ahead: The potato base keeps 3 days in the fridge or 3 months frozen. Add freshly cut greens and the sausage when reheating.
variations: Use Spanish chorizo or a smoked kielbasa if you can't find Portuguese sausage.

vegetarian.title: Vegetarian Caldo Verde
vegetarian.description: The same silky potato and greens soup with smoked paprika oil and white beans in place of the chouriço.

ingredients.item: extra-virgin olive oil, plus more to serve
floury potatoes (Yukon Gold or russet), peeled and cut in chunks
collard greens or lacinato kale, stems removed
black pepper and crusty cornbread (broa), to serve

steps: Cook the onion in the olive oil for 6 to 8 minutes, until soft, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the potatoes, water and salt. Bring to a boil and simmer, partly covered, for 20 minutes, until the potatoes fall apart.
Meanwhile, slice the greens into very fine ribbons. In a small pan, warm 3 tbsp olive oil with the smoked paprika for 1 minute and toss the beans in it.
Blend the soup until smooth, then bring back to a simmer, add the greens and cook 3 to 5 minutes until just tender. Taste for salt.
Ladle into bowls and top with the paprika beans and their red oil. Serve with cornbread.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: The smoked paprika oil brings the smoky, rosy flavor that the sausage normally gives.
vegetarian.make_ahead: The potato base keeps 3 days in the fridge or 3 months frozen. Add freshly cut greens and the white beans when reheating.

vegan.title: Vegan Caldo Verde
vegan.description: The same silky potato and greens soup with smoked paprika oil and white beans in place of the chouriço.

ingredients.item: extra-virgin olive oil, plus more to serve
floury potatoes (Yukon Gold or russet), peeled and cut in chunks
collard greens or lacinato kale, stems removed
black pepper and crusty cornbread (broa), to serve

Add the potatoes, water and salt. Bring to a boil and simmer, partly covered, for 20 minutes, until the potatoes fall apart.
Meanwhile, slice the greens into very fine ribbons. In a small pan, warm 3 tbsp olive oil with the smoked paprika for 1 minute and toss the beans in it.

Ladle into bowls and top with the paprika beans and their red oil. Serve with cornbread.

vegan.make_ahead: The potato base keeps 3 days in the fridge or 3 months frozen. Add freshly cut greens and the white beans when reheating.

recipe.title: Canchánchara
recipe.description: One of Cuba's oldest drinks, from the town of Trinidad: raw cane spirit stirred with honey, lime and a little water over ice.

ingredients.item: Cuban aguardiente (or a light Cuban-style rum)

steps: In a rocks glass or clay cup, stir the honey and lime juice together until the honey dissolves.
Add the water and stir again.
Fill the glass with cracked ice and pour in the aguardiente.
Stir well from the bottom up and garnish with the lime wedge.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Stir 1/2 oz honey and 1/2 oz lime juice with 3 oz cold water over cracked ice.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Dissolve the honey before adding ice. Cold honey turns stiff and won't mix in.
Traditionally it's served in a small clay cup that keeps the drink cold.

recipe.title: Cantaloupe Lime Gin Cooler
recipe.description: Fresh cantaloupe and lime soften a lightly sparkling gin cooler.
steps: Muddle melon cubes with syrup in a shaker until very juicy.
Add gin, lime juice and ice; shake for 15 seconds and fine-strain into an ice-filled highball.
Top with soda, stir gently and add the melon wedge.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Muddle melon with syrup, shake with 3/4 oz lime juice and ice, strain and top with 4 oz soda water.

recipe.note: An original Relish home cocktail. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Use ripe melon; hard melon produces little juice and needs more sweetener.
recipe.make_ahead: Prepare to order. Keep juices and brewed teas refrigerated until needed.

recipe.title: Cantarito
recipe.description: A Jalisco roadside favorite: tequila and fresh orange, grapefruit and lime juices with a pinch of salt, topped with grapefruit soda and served ice-cold in a clay cup.
steps: Soak a clay cantarito cup in cold water for 10 minutes, then pour out the water. Rim it with Tajín if you like.
Fill the cup with ice. Add the tequila, citrus juices and salt and stir.
Top with the grapefruit soda, stir gently and garnish with citrus wedges.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Mix the citrus juices and salt, top with grapefruit soda and serve in a chilled clay cup.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Soaking the clay cup keeps the drink extra cold as the water slowly evaporates.
A pinch of salt makes all the citrus taste brighter.
variations: Make a pitcher: multiply by 8 and add the soda just before serving.

recipe.title: Cape Codder
recipe.description: The original vodka cranberry: vodka and cranberry juice over ice with a squeeze of lime.
steps: Fill a highball glass with ice.
Pour in the vodka, cranberry juice and lime juice.
Stir gently and garnish with the lime wedge.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Build 4 oz cranberry juice and 1/2 oz lime juice over ice and top with 2 oz soda water.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Use sweetened cranberry juice cocktail. Pure cranberry juice is very sour on its own.
variations: Cape Cod Cooler: top with 2 oz soda water for a longer, lighter drink.

recipe.title: Cape Malay Tomato Bredie
recipe.description: South Africa's slow-cooked lamb and tomato stew, gently spiced with cinnamon, cloves and cardamom, until the lamb falls from the bone and the tomatoes turn jammy.

ingredients.item: lamb neck or shoulder chops, cut into large pieces
chili flakes or 1 fresh green chili, chopped
ripe tomatoes, chopped, or 2 cans (14 oz) chopped tomatoes
steamed rice and chopped parsley, to serve

steps: Season the lamb with salt and dust it lightly with flour. Brown it in the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat, in batches, for about 3 minutes a side. Set aside.
Lower the heat and cook the onions for 10 minutes until soft and golden. Add the garlic, ginger, cinnamon, cloves, cardamom, bay leaves and chili and stir for 1 minute until fragrant.

Add the tomatoes, tomato paste and sugar and return the lamb with its juices. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook gently for 1 1/2 hours, stirring now and then. Add a splash of water only if it starts to catch.
Add the potatoes and cook, covered, for 25 to 30 minutes more, until the potatoes are tender and the lamb pulls easily from the bone.
Uncover for the last 10 minutes if the sauce is thin. It should be thick and glossy. Taste for salt and sugar, then serve over rice with parsley.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: The lamb braises in the tomatoes' own juice, so add water sparingly. A thick, jammy sauce is the goal.
A spoon of sugar balances the acidity of the tomatoes. Taste and add more if your tomatoes are sharp.
Bony cuts like neck give the richest sauce; boneless shoulder works too and cooks a little faster.
recipe.make_ahead: Like most stews it tastes better the next day. Keeps 4 days in the fridge or 3 months frozen.
variations: Green bean bredie: replace the tomatoes with 1 1/2 lb green beans and a cup of stock.
Pressure cooker: after browning and adding the tomatoes, cook 35 minutes on high, then add the potatoes for 6 minutes.

vegetarian.title: Vegetarian Tomato Bredie
vegetarian.description: The same warmly spiced, jammy tomato stew made with chickpeas, butternut squash and potatoes.

ingredients.item: chili flakes or 1 fresh green chili, chopped
ripe tomatoes, chopped, or 2 cans (14 oz) chopped tomatoes
steamed rice and chopped parsley, to serve

steps: Cook the onions in the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat for 10 minutes until soft and golden. Add the garlic, ginger, cinnamon, cloves, cardamom, bay leaves and chili and stir for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, tomato paste, sugar and broth. Simmer, covered, for 20 minutes to build the sauce.
Add the potatoes and squash and simmer, covered, for 25 minutes. Stir in the chickpeas and cook 10 minutes more, until the vegetables are tender.
Uncover for the last few minutes if the sauce is thin. Taste for salt and sugar and serve over rice with parsley.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Simmering the sauce on its own first gives the spices time to soften into the tomatoes, the way the lamb's long braise would.
vegetarian.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge or 3 months frozen.

vegan.title: Vegan Tomato Bredie
vegan.description: The same warmly spiced, jammy tomato stew made with chickpeas, butternut squash and potatoes.

ingredients.item: chili flakes or 1 fresh green chili, chopped
ripe tomatoes, chopped, or 2 cans (14 oz) chopped tomatoes
steamed rice and chopped parsley, to serve

steps: Cook the onions in the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat for 10 minutes until soft and golden. Add the garlic, ginger, cinnamon, cloves, cardamom, bay leaves and chili and stir for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, tomato paste, sugar and broth. Simmer, covered, for 20 minutes to build the sauce.
Add the potatoes and squash and simmer, covered, for 25 minutes. Stir in the chickpeas and cook 10 minutes more, until the vegetables are tender.
Uncover for the last few minutes if the sauce is thin. Taste for salt and sugar and serve over rice with parsley.
vegan.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Simmering the sauce on its own first gives the spices time to soften into the tomatoes, the way the lamb's long braise would.
vegan.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge or 3 months frozen.

recipe.title: Cardinale
recipe.description: A drier, sharper cousin of the Negroni: gin and dry vermouth with just a splash of Campari, stirred cold and served up.

ingredients.item: vegan dry vermouth (such as Dolin Dry)

steps: Chill a coupe or martini glass.
Add the gin, dry vermouth and Campari to a mixing glass and fill it with ice.
Stir for about 20 seconds, until very cold.
Strain into the chilled glass, squeeze the lemon twist over the top and drop it in.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Stir 2 oz non-alcoholic gin alternative with 1/2 oz non-alcoholic bitter aperitivo and a dash of verjus over ice, then strain.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Stir, don't shake. Shaking clouds the drink and waters it down.
Keep your vermouth in the fridge once opened. It is wine and goes stale in a few weeks at room temperature.
variations: For a bolder drink, raise the Campari to 1/2 oz.

recipe.title: Caribou Lou
recipe.description: A sweet, tropical party drink made famous by a 2006 Tech N9ne song: overproof rum and coconut rum over ice, filled with pineapple juice. Strong, so sip slowly.
steps: Fill a hurricane glass with ice.
Add the overproof rum, coconut rum and pineapple juice.
Stir well and garnish with a pineapple wedge.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Mix pineapple juice with a splash of coconut water and coconut syrup over ice.

recipe.note: Overproof rum is flammable; keep it away from open flames.
tips: Overproof rum is very strong. For a milder drink, use regular white rum instead.
Shake it with ice instead of building it for a frothy top.
variations: Make it a punch: mix a bottle-sized batch in a jug and serve over ice.

recipe.title: Carnitas
recipe.description: Michoacán-style pulled pork: chunks of pork shoulder slowly braised with orange, garlic and spices in their own fat, then crisped until the edges are golden and crunchy.

ingredients.item: boneless pork shoulder, cut into 2-inch chunks
chopped onion, cilantro, lime wedges and salsa, to serve

steps: Heat the oven to 300°F. Toss the pork with the salt, cumin, oregano and pepper.
