Put the pork in a Dutch oven in a snug layer with the lard. Squeeze in the orange juice and add the squeezed halves, the onion, garlic, bay leaves, cinnamon stick, if using, and the water.
Bring to a simmer on the stove, cover and transfer to the oven. Cook for 3 hours, until the pork is very tender.
Remove the orange, onion, garlic, bay leaves and cinnamon. Lift out the pork and shred it into large pieces.

Skim off about 1/2 cup of the fat from the pot. Heat some of it in a large skillet over medium-high heat and fry the pork in batches, without stirring for 2 to 3 minutes, until crisp and golden on the bottom. Or spread it on a sheet pan, drizzle with the fat and broil for 5 minutes.
Drizzle with a little of the cooking juices and serve in warm tortillas with onion, cilantro, lime and salsa.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: The crisping step is what makes carnitas. Without it, you have pulled pork.
Choose a well-marbled shoulder. The fat renders out and does the frying for you.
recipe.make_ahead: Refrigerate the braised, shredded pork in its juices for up to 4 days. Crisp just before serving.
variations: Use the carnitas for burritos, tortas or rice bowls.

recipe.title: Carrot Cake
recipe.description: Moist spiced carrot layer cake with walnuts and cream cheese frosting.
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and grease two 9-inch cake pans.
Whisk the flour, baking soda, cinnamon and salt.
Beat the eggs, oil and both sugars, then stir in the dry ingredients, carrots and walnuts.
Divide between the pans and bake for 30 to 35 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool completely.
Beat the cream cheese and butter, then beat in the powdered sugar and vanilla until fluffy.
Fill and frost the cooled cake.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Casino
recipe.description: Old Tom gin with maraschino, orange bitters and lemon.
steps: Shake everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Chakhchoukha
recipe.description: An Algerian feast dish from the Aurès: thin semolina flatbread torn into pieces and soaked in marqa, a spiced tomato stew of lamb, chickpeas and vegetables.

ingredients.item: lamb shoulder, cut into large chunks
chickpeas, drained, or 1 cup dried, soaked overnight
rougag or thin semolina flatbread (or thin pita), torn into small pieces

steps: Brown the lamb in the oil in a large pot. Add the onion and garlic and cook 5 minutes, then stir in the tomato paste, tomatoes, ras el hanout, paprika, cayenne, pepper and salt for 2 minutes.
Add the water (and dried chickpeas if using). Bring to a boil, then simmer, covered, for 45 minutes.
Add the carrots (and canned chickpeas) and simmer 15 minutes, then the zucchini for 10 minutes more, until the lamb is tender and the sauce is rich and slightly reduced.
Meanwhile, steam the torn bread over the stew or in a steamer basket for 10 minutes, tossing once, until soft and pliable. Toss with the butter.
Pile the bread in a wide dish and ladle over plenty of the hot sauce, letting it soak in. Top with the lamb, chickpeas and vegetables and serve extra sauce on the side.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Steaming the bread first makes it soft enough to drink up the sauce without turning to mush.
The sauce should be plentiful and thin enough to soak in, more like a broth than a thick stew.
recipe.make_ahead: The marqa stew keeps 3 days in the fridge or 3 months frozen. Steam and soak the bread just before serving.
variations: Use chicken pieces instead of lamb and simmer 35 minutes.

vegetarian.title: Vegetarian Chakhchoukha
vegetarian.description: Torn semolina bread soaked in a spiced tomato broth with extra chickpeas, potatoes and vegetables.

ingredients.item: potatoes, peeled and cut in chunks
chickpeas, drained, or 1 cup dried, soaked overnight
rougag or thin semolina flatbread (or thin pita), torn into small pieces

steps: Heat the oil in a large pot. Add the onion and garlic and cook 5 minutes, then stir in the tomato paste, tomatoes, ras el hanout, paprika, cayenne, pepper and salt for 2 minutes.
Add the water (and dried chickpeas if using). Bring to a boil, add the potatoes, then simmer, covered, for 15 minutes (45 if using dried chickpeas).
Add the carrots (and canned chickpeas) and simmer 15 minutes, then the zucchini for 10 minutes more, until the vegetables are tender and the sauce is rich and slightly reduced.
Meanwhile, steam the torn bread over the stew or in a steamer basket for 10 minutes, tossing once, until soft and pliable. Toss with the butter.
Pile the bread in a wide dish and ladle over plenty of the hot sauce, letting it soak in. Top with the chickpeas and vegetables and serve extra sauce on the side.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Steaming the bread first makes it soft enough to drink up the sauce without turning to mush.
The sauce should be plentiful and thin enough to soak in, more like a broth than a thick stew.
vegetarian.make_ahead: The marqa stew keeps 3 days in the fridge or 3 months frozen. Steam and soak the bread just before serving.

vegan.title: Vegan Chakhchoukha
vegan.description: The vegetarian chakhchoukha finished with olive oil instead of butter.

ingredients.item: potatoes, peeled and cut in chunks
chickpeas, drained, or 1 cup dried, soaked overnight
rougag or thin semolina flatbread (or thin pita), torn into small pieces

steps: Heat the oil in a large pot. Add the onion and garlic and cook 5 minutes, then stir in the tomato paste, tomatoes, ras el hanout, paprika, cayenne, pepper and salt for 2 minutes.
Add the water (and dried chickpeas if using). Bring to a boil, add the potatoes, then simmer, covered, for 15 minutes (45 if using dried chickpeas).
Add the carrots (and canned chickpeas) and simmer 15 minutes, then the zucchini for 10 minutes more, until the vegetables are tender and the sauce is rich and slightly reduced.
Meanwhile, steam the torn bread over the stew or in a steamer basket for 10 minutes, tossing once, until soft and pliable. Toss with the olive oil.
Pile the bread in a wide dish and ladle over plenty of the hot sauce, letting it soak in. Top with the chickpeas and vegetables and serve extra sauce on the side.
vegan.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Steaming the bread first makes it soft enough to drink up the sauce without turning to mush.
The sauce should be plentiful and thin enough to soak in, more like a broth than a thick stew.
vegan.make_ahead: The marqa stew keeps 3 days in the fridge or 3 months frozen. Steam and soak the bread just before serving.

recipe.title: Champagne Cocktail
recipe.description: A bitters-soaked sugar cube in Champagne.

ingredients.item: vegan Champagne (such as Moët & Chandon Impérial)

steps: Soak the sugar cube with bitters and drop it into a flute.
Top slowly with Champagne.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Use alcohol-free sparkling wine.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Champs-Élysées
recipe.description: Cognac with yellow Chartreuse, lemon and bitters.
steps: Shake everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Chana Masala
recipe.description: Chickpeas simmered in a tangy, spiced tomato and onion gravy, a North Indian favorite.
steps: Heat the oil and fry the cumin seeds until they sizzle.
Add the onion and cook for 8 to 10 minutes until golden. Add the ginger, garlic and chile and cook 1 minute.
Stir in the tomatoes and the ground spices and cook until the oil starts to separate, about 8 minutes.
Add the chickpeas and 1 cup water, then simmer 15 minutes, mashing a few chickpeas to thicken.
Stir in the garam masala and lemon juice, season with salt and top with cilantro. Serve with rice or naan.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Chartreuse Swizzle
recipe.description: Green Chartreuse with pineapple, lime and falernum over crushed ice.
steps: Fill a tall glass with crushed ice and add everything.
Swizzle until the glass frosts, then top with more ice.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Classic Cheeseburger
recipe.description: Juicy griddled beef burgers with melted American cheese on toasted buns.
steps: Shape the beef into 4 patties slightly wider than the buns, with a dimple in the middle.
Heat a skillet or grill until very hot and season the patties.
Cook 3 to 4 minutes, flip, add the cheese and cook 2 to 3 minutes more, until 160°F in the center.
Serve on the toasted buns with your toppings.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: New York Cheesecake
recipe.description: The classic New York cheesecake: dense, rich and tangy with cream cheese and sour cream, baked slowly in a water bath on a buttery graham cracker crust.

ingredients.item: full-fat sour cream, at room temperature

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Wrap the outside of a 9-inch springform pan in two layers of wide heavy-duty foil.
Mix the graham cracker crumbs, 1/3 cup sugar and butter and press firmly into the bottom of the pan. Bake for 10 minutes, then cool. Lower the oven to 325°F and bring a kettle of water to a boil.
Beat the cream cheese, 1 1/4 cups sugar, flour and salt on medium speed until completely smooth, about 2 minutes, scraping the bowl.
Beat in the vanilla, lemon zest and juice. Add the eggs one at a time on low speed, mixing just until combined. Mix in the sour cream.
Pour the filling over the crust. Set the pan in a roasting pan and pour boiling water into the roasting pan to come 1 inch up the sides.
Bake for 75 to 85 minutes, until the edges are set and the center still jiggles slightly.
Turn off the oven, prop the door open and leave the cheesecake inside for 1 hour. Then cool on a rack and refrigerate for at least 6 hours, or overnight.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Have everything at room temperature. Cold cream cheese makes a lumpy batter.
Mix on low once the eggs go in. Beating in air causes cracks.
For clean slices, dip the knife in hot water and wipe it dry between cuts.
recipe.make_ahead: Refrigerate for up to 5 days, or freeze whole or in slices for up to 2 months.
variations: Top with strawberry or cherry sauce just before serving.

recipe.title: Cherry Cacao Rye Old Fashioned
recipe.description: Rye, tart cherry and cacao-nib syrup make a dark, gently sweet stirred drink.
steps: Loosen cherry preserves with water and cacao syrup in a mixing glass.
Add rye and ice, stir for 25 seconds, then fine-strain into a rocks glass over one large ice cube.
Express orange peel over the drink and add it with a pitted cherry.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Stir 2 oz cooled black tea, 1/4 oz cacao syrup, 1 tsp cherry preserves and 1/2 oz orange juice with ice; fine-strain over fresh ice.

recipe.note: An original Relish home cocktail. Please drink responsibly.
tips: For cacao syrup, steep 1 tbsp cacao nibs in 1/2 cup hot simple syrup for 15 minutes; strain and cool. Prep time assumes the syrup is ready.
recipe.make_ahead: Prepare to order. Keep juices and brewed teas refrigerated until needed.

recipe.title: Cherry Vanilla Bourbon Sour
recipe.description: Bourbon, cherry and lemon shaken with vanilla syrup.
steps: Shake bourbon, cherry juice, lemon and vanilla syrup with ice.
Strain into a rocks glass over fresh ice and garnish with a cherry.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake the cherry juice, lemon and vanilla syrup with ice and strain over ice with a splash of soda.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Chicago Cocktail
recipe.description: Brandy with orange curaçao and bitters, topped with Champagne.

ingredients.item: vegan Champagne (such as Moët & Chandon Impérial)

steps: Rim a coupe with sugar, if you like.
Stir the brandy, curaçao and bitters with ice, strain into the glass and top with Champagne.

cocktail.glass: coupe, rim sugared if you like

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Chicken Adobo
recipe.description: Filipino chicken braised in vinegar, soy sauce, garlic and bay leaves until glossy.
steps: Combine the chicken, soy sauce, vinegar, garlic, bay leaves and peppercorns and marinate 30 minutes.
Brown the chicken in the oil skin side down, then add the marinade and 1/2 cup water.
Simmer, covered, 30 minutes, then uncovered 10 minutes until the sauce reduces. Stir in the sugar.
Serve with steamed rice.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Chicken Alfredo
recipe.description: Fettuccine Alfredo topped with juicy seared chicken breast.
steps: Season the chicken with salt, pepper and Italian seasoning and sear in the oil 6 to 7 minutes per side, until 165°F inside. Rest and slice.
Cook the fettuccine and save some pasta water.
Melt the butter, cook the garlic 30 seconds, add the cream and simmer 4 minutes.
Stir in the Parmesan, then toss with the pasta, loosening with pasta water.
Top with the chicken and parsley.
recipe.note: Fresh egg fettuccine contains eggs; most dried fettuccine does not.

recipe.title: Chicken and Corn Enchilada Skillet
recipe.description: All the flavor of enchiladas without the rolling: chicken, corn, black beans and tortilla strips simmered in red sauce under melted Monterey Jack.

ingredients.item: small corn tortillas, cut into strips

steps: Cook pepper in oil in an oven-safe skillet for 4 minutes. Add corn, beans, chicken and sauce; simmer 5 minutes until hot.
Fold in tortilla strips. Top with cheese, cover and cook on low 3–5 minutes until melted and the filling is heated through to 165°F.
Scatter cilantro over the top.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Check the enchilada sauce label if you avoid wheat: some brands thicken it with flour.

recipe.title: Chicken and Ginger Rice Congee
recipe.description: A soothing rice porridge with shredded chicken, ginger and scallions.
steps: Bring rice, broth and ginger to a boil. Reduce to a gentle simmer and cook partially covered for 60–75 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the rice breaks down and the porridge is creamy. Add water as needed.
Stir in chicken and cook until heated to 165°F. Season with salt and white pepper.
Top with scallions.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Chicken Artichoke Sun-Dried Tomato Rice
recipe.description: Chicken thighs and rice cook together with artichokes, sun-dried tomatoes and spinach.

ingredients.item: artichoke hearts (14 oz), drained and quartered
oil-packed sun-dried tomatoes, drained and chopped

steps: Season chicken with half the salt and pepper. Brown in oil in a deep lidded skillet over medium-high heat for 3 minutes per side; set aside.
Soften onion for 5 minutes. Add garlic, oregano and rice and stir for 1 minute. Add water, artichokes, tomatoes and remaining salt.
Place chicken on top, bring to a simmer, cover tightly and cook over low heat for 20 minutes, until rice is tender and chicken reaches 165 F (74 C). Add a splash of water and cook longer if needed.
Rest covered off heat for 5 minutes, then fold spinach gently into the hot rice to wilt.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Use a skillet with a tight lid. Resist lifting it repeatedly while the rice cooks.
recipe.make_ahead: Refrigerate promptly in shallow containers for up to 3 days. Reheat leftovers to 165 F (74 C).

recipe.title: Chicken Cacciatore
recipe.description: Italian hunter-style chicken braised with tomatoes, peppers, mushrooms and herbs.
steps: Season and brown the chicken in the oil. Remove.
Cook the onion, pepper and mushrooms until soft, then add the garlic.
Add the wine and reduce, then the tomatoes and herbs.
Return the chicken, cover and simmer 35 to 40 minutes. Season and top with basil.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Chicken Cordon Bleu
recipe.description: Chicken breasts rolled around ham and Swiss cheese, breaded and baked.
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F.
Lay a slice of ham and cheese on each breast, roll up and secure with toothpicks.
Dredge in flour, dip in egg and coat in panko mixed with the butter.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes until golden and 165°F inside.
Remove the toothpicks and serve with Dijon.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Chicken Enchiladas
recipe.description: Corn tortillas rolled around chicken and cheese, baked in red enchilada sauce.
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F.
Mix the chicken, 1 1/2 cups cheese, sour cream and cumin.
Warm the tortillas so they bend, fill each with chicken and roll up.
Spread a little sauce in a baking dish, add the enchiladas seam side down and pour over the rest of the sauce. Top with the remaining cheese.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes until bubbling. Top with cilantro, green onions and avocado.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Check the enchilada sauce label if you avoid wheat: some brands thicken it with flour.

recipe.title: Chicken Fajitas
recipe.description: Sizzling strips of spiced chicken with peppers and onions, wrapped in warm tortillas.

ingredients.item: boneless chicken breasts, sliced into strips
salsa, guacamole and sour cream, to serve

steps: Toss the chicken with half the oil, the spices, salt and lime juice.
Heat a cast-iron skillet over high heat and cook the chicken 5 to 6 minutes until charred and cooked through (165°F). Remove.
Add the remaining oil, peppers and onion and cook 5 minutes until tender and charred.
Return the chicken to the pan and toss together.
Serve in warm tortillas with salsa, guacamole and sour cream.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Chicken Marsala
recipe.description: Golden chicken cutlets in a mushroom and Marsala wine pan sauce.

ingredients.item: large chicken breasts, halved and pounded thin

steps: Season the chicken and dredge in flour.
Brown in the oil and 1 tbsp butter 3 to 4 minutes per side, until 165°F inside. Remove.
Add 1 tbsp butter and the mushrooms and cook until browned, then the garlic.
Add the Marsala and broth and simmer until reduced by half. Swirl in the last of the butter.
Return the chicken to warm through and top with parsley.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Chicken Noodle Soup
recipe.description: Comforting chicken soup with vegetables and egg noodles.
steps: Cook the onion, carrots and celery in the oil for 6 minutes, then add the garlic.
Add the broth, chicken, thyme and bay leaf and simmer 25 minutes, until the chicken reaches 165°F.
Shred the chicken and return it to the pot.
Add the noodles and cook 6 to 8 minutes until tender. Season and add parsley.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Chicken Paprikash (Paprikás Csirke)
recipe.description: Hungary's comfort classic: bone-in chicken braised in a velvety sauce of onions, sweet Hungarian paprika and sour cream, served over little egg dumplings (nokedli).

ingredients.item: bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs and drumsticks
Hungarian wax or bell pepper, chopped
full-fat sour cream, at room temperature

steps: Season the chicken with 1 tsp salt. Brown it skin-side down in the lard in a wide pot for 5 to 6 minutes, then turn for 2 minutes. Lift out.
Cook the onions in the fat for 10 minutes until soft and golden. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in the paprika, so it doesn't burn. Add the pepper, tomato, broth and the rest of the salt, then return the chicken.
Cover and simmer gently for 30 to 35 minutes, until the chicken is tender.

Meanwhile, make the nokedli: mix the flour, eggs, water and a pinch of salt into a thick, sticky batter. Scrape small bits into simmering salted water with a spoon or spaetzle maker. When they float, cook 1 minute more, drain and toss with butter.
Whisk the sour cream and 1 tbsp flour, then whisk in a ladle of the hot sauce. Stir it into the pot and simmer gently 2 to 3 minutes until thickened. Serve over the nokedli.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Always add paprika off the heat. Scorched paprika turns bitter in seconds.
Real Hungarian sweet paprika makes the biggest difference; it's richer and redder than generic paprika.
Temper the sour cream with hot sauce first so it doesn't split.
recipe.make_ahead: The braise keeps 3 days; stir in the sour cream when reheating. Nokedli can be made a day ahead and warmed in butter.
variations: Serve with egg noodles, rice or mashed potatoes instead of nokedli.
Add 1/2 tsp hot paprika for a spicier version.

vegetarian.title: Mushroom Paprikash
vegetarian.description: Meaty mushrooms simmered in the same onion, paprika and sour cream sauce, served over buttered nokedli.

ingredients.item: mixed mushrooms (cremini, oyster, king oyster), thickly sliced
Hungarian wax or bell pepper, chopped
full-fat sour cream, at room temperature

steps: Brown the mushrooms in the oil in a wide pot over high heat, in batches, for 6 to 8 minutes. Season with 1 tsp salt and lift out.
Cook the onions in the fat for 10 minutes until soft and golden. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in the paprika, so it doesn't burn. Add the pepper, tomato, broth and the rest of the salt, then return the mushrooms.
Simmer gently, uncovered, for 10 minutes to blend the flavors.

Meanwhile, make the nokedli: mix the flour, eggs, water and a pinch of salt into a thick, sticky batter. Scrape small bits into simmering salted water with a spoon or spaetzle maker. When they float, cook 1 minute more, drain and toss with butter.
Whisk the sour cream and 1 tbsp flour, then whisk in a ladle of the hot sauce. Stir it into the pot and simmer gently 2 to 3 minutes until thickened. Serve over the nokedli.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Always add paprika off the heat. Scorched paprika turns bitter in seconds.
Real Hungarian sweet paprika makes the biggest difference; it's richer and redder than generic paprika.
Temper the sour cream with hot sauce first so it doesn't split.
vegetarian.make_ahead: The braise keeps 3 days; stir in the sour cream when reheating. Nokedli can be made a day ahead and warmed in butter.

vegan.title: Vegan Mushroom Paprikash
vegan.description: Mushrooms in a paprika and onion sauce made creamy with cashew cream, over egg-free dumplings tossed in olive oil.

ingredients.item: mixed mushrooms (cremini, oyster, king oyster), thickly sliced
Hungarian wax or bell pepper, chopped
cashew cream with 1 tsp lemon juice
tbsp olive oil, for the nokedli
water, plus 2 tbsp more, for the nokedli
olive oil, to toss the nokedli

steps: Brown the mushrooms in the oil in a wide pot over high heat, in batches, for 6 to 8 minutes. Season with 1 tsp salt and lift out.
Cook the onions in the fat for 10 minutes until soft and golden. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in the paprika, so it doesn't burn. Add the pepper, tomato, broth and the rest of the salt, then return the mushrooms.
Simmer gently, uncovered, for 10 minutes to blend the flavors.

Meanwhile, make the nokedli: mix the flour, olive oil, water and a pinch of salt into a thick, sticky batter. Scrape small bits into simmering salted water with a spoon or spaetzle maker. When they float, cook 1 minute more, drain and toss with olive oil.
Whisk the cashew cream and 1 tbsp flour, then whisk in a ladle of the hot sauce. Stir it into the pot and simmer gently 2 to 3 minutes until thickened. Serve over the nokedli.
vegan.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Always add paprika off the heat. Scorched paprika turns bitter in seconds.
Real Hungarian sweet paprika makes the biggest difference; it's richer and redder than generic paprika.
Cashew cream won't split, but stir it in at the end so it stays silky.
vegan.make_ahead: The braise keeps 3 days; stir in the cashew cream when reheating. Nokedli can be made a day ahead and warmed in olive oil.

recipe.title: Chicken Parmesan
recipe.description: Crisp breaded chicken cutlets baked with marinara and melted mozzarella.

ingredients.item: basil and cooked spaghetti, to serve

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Pound the chicken to an even 1/2 inch and season.
Dredge in flour, dip in egg, then press into the breadcrumbs mixed with half the Parmesan.
Fry in oil 3 minutes per side until golden.
Place in a baking dish, top with marinara, mozzarella and the remaining Parmesan.
Bake 10 to 15 minutes, until bubbling and the chicken reaches 165°F. Top with basil and serve with spaghetti.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Chicken Piccata
recipe.description: Thin chicken cutlets in a lemony butter and caper sauce.

ingredients.item: large chicken breasts, halved and pounded thin

steps: Season the chicken and dredge in flour.
Brown in the oil and 1 tbsp butter 3 minutes per side, until 165°F inside. Remove.
Add the broth, wine, lemon and capers and simmer until reduced by half.
Swirl in the remaining butter, return the chicken and top with parsley.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Chicken Poblano Corn Rice Bake
recipe.description: Ground chicken, mild poblano, corn and rice baked together under a light cheddar topping.
steps: Heat oven to 400 F (200 C). Heat oil in an ovenproof deep skillet and cook onion and poblano for 5 minutes.
Add chicken, cumin, salt and pepper. Break up the meat and cook for 6 to 8 minutes until it reaches 165 F (74 C).
Stir in rice, corn, drained tomatoes and water. Bring to a simmer, cover tightly and bake for 25 minutes, until rice is tender; add water and cook longer if necessary.
Sprinkle with cheddar and bake uncovered for 5 minutes, until melted and the center reaches 165 F (74 C). Rest for 5 minutes and add cilantro.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Poblano heat varies; remove seeds and ribs for a milder bake. Use a tight-fitting lid so the rice cooks evenly.
recipe.make_ahead: Refrigerate promptly in shallow containers for up to 3 days. Reheat leftovers to 165 F (74 C).

recipe.title: Chicken Pot Pie
recipe.description: Creamy chicken and vegetable filling under a golden, flaky crust.
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F.
Cook the onion, carrots and celery in the butter for 6 minutes, stir in the flour and cook 1 minute.
Whisk in the broth and milk and simmer until thick. Add the chicken, peas, thyme, salt and pepper.
Line a pie dish with one crust, add the filling, top with the second crust, crimp and cut vents.
Brush with egg and bake 30 to 35 minutes until golden.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Chicken Quesadilla
recipe.description: Crisp flour tortillas filled with melted cheese, shredded chicken and peppers.

ingredients.item: salsa and sour cream, to serve

steps: Toss the chicken with the chili powder.
Scatter cheese, chicken, pepper and green onions over half of each tortilla and fold over.
Cook in a buttered skillet over medium heat 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden and melted.
Cut into wedges and serve with salsa and sour cream.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Chicken Satay
recipe.description: Grilled turmeric-marinated chicken skewers with peanut sauce.

ingredients.item: boneless chicken thighs, cut into strips

steps: Marinate the chicken in the soy sauce, sugar, turmeric, coriander and 1/4 cup coconut milk for 1 hour.
Thread onto skewers.
Simmer the remaining coconut milk with the peanut butter, curry paste and lime juice until smooth.
Grill the skewers 3 to 4 minutes per side until charred and cooked through (165°F).
Serve with the peanut sauce.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Chicken Shawarma
recipe.description: Spiced, charred chicken thighs wrapped in pita with garlic sauce, pickles and vegetables.
steps: Marinate the chicken in the yogurt, lemon, spices, garlic and salt for at least 2 hours.
Roast at 425°F or grill 20 minutes until charred and cooked through (165°F). Rest and slice thinly.
Warm the pitas.
Fill with chicken, vegetables, pickles and sauce, and roll up.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Chicken Tacos
recipe.description: Spiced, charred chicken thighs in warm corn tortillas with onion, cilantro and lime.
steps: Toss the chicken with the oil, spices, salt and the juice of 1 lime.
Cook in a hot skillet or grill 5 to 6 minutes per side until charred and cooked through (165°F). Rest and chop.
Fill the tortillas with chicken, onion and cilantro.
Serve with lime wedges and salsa verde.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Chicken Teriyaki
recipe.description: Pan-seared chicken thighs glazed in a glossy homemade teriyaki sauce.
steps: Stir together the soy sauce, mirin, sake, brown sugar and ginger.
Heat the oil and cook the chicken skin side down for 6 to 7 minutes until crisp, then flip and cook 4 minutes, until 165°F inside.
Pour off the fat, add the sauce and simmer, turning the chicken, until the sauce is thick and glossy.
Slice and serve over rice, topped with sesame seeds and green onions.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Chicken Tikka Masala
recipe.description: Smoky, yogurt-marinated chicken charred under the broiler, then simmered in a silky, gently spiced tomato and cream masala.

ingredients.item: boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1 1/2 inch pieces
Kashmiri chili powder or sweet paprika, divided
chopped cilantro, basmati rice and naan, to serve

steps: Mix the yogurt, lemon juice, 1 tsp salt, half the garam masala, half the cumin, half the chili powder and the turmeric. Toss the chicken in it and marinate at least 1 hour, or overnight in the fridge.

Heat the broiler with a rack 4 inches from the heat. Thread the chicken on skewers or spread it on a foil-lined sheet with a little space between pieces. Broil 8 to 10 minutes, turning once, until charred in spots. It doesn't need to be cooked through yet.
Melt the butter in a wide pot over medium heat. Cook the onion with a pinch of salt for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring often, until deep golden. Don't rush this step; it sets the flavor of the sauce.

Add the garlic, ginger and chili and stir 1 minute until fragrant. Add the tomato paste and the rest of the garam masala, cumin and chili powder and stir 1 minute more, until the paste darkens and the spices smell toasty.
Add the tomatoes, sugar and 1/2 tsp salt. Simmer 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick and the oil starts to pool at the edges. For a smooth restaurant-style sauce, blend it now.

Stir in the cream and fenugreek, then add the chicken and any juices. Simmer 8 to 10 minutes until the chicken is cooked through (165°F) and tender. Taste and adjust the salt. Top with cilantro and serve with rice and naan.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Thighs stay juicy through both the broiling and the simmering; breast meat dries out. If you use breast, cut it bigger and simmer only 5 minutes.
Yogurt tenderizes the chicken and helps it char. Use whole-milk yogurt; low-fat yogurt makes the marinade watery.
The sauce is ready for the cream when oil separates at the edges. That means the water has cooked off and the tomatoes have sweetened.
Kashmiri chili gives deep red color with mild heat. For more heat, add cayenne a pinch at a time.
recipe.make_ahead: It tastes even better the next day. Keep it 4 days in the fridge or 3 months frozen. Reheat gently with a splash of water, as the sauce thickens when cold.
variations: Paneer tikka masala: use 14 oz paneer cubes instead of chicken. Broil them 5 minutes and simmer only 3.
Lighter: use half-and-half or coconut milk in place of the heavy cream.
On the grill: thread the marinated chicken on skewers and grill over high heat for extra smoke.

recipe.title: Chicken Tortilla Soup
recipe.description: Smoky tomato and chicken soup topped with crisp tortilla strips, avocado and cheese.

ingredients.item: tortilla strips, avocado, cheese and cilantro

steps: Cook the onion, garlic and jalapeño in oil until soft. Add the spices for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, broth and chicken and simmer 20 minutes, until the chicken reaches 165°F.
Shred the chicken and return it with the beans and corn. Simmer 5 minutes and add the lime juice.
Serve topped with tortilla strips, avocado, cheese and cilantro.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Chicken with Creamy Leeks and Mustard
recipe.description: Browned chicken breasts in a modest creamy leek and Dijon sauce.

ingredients.item: boneless skinless chicken breasts (5 oz each)
leeks, white and light-green parts sliced and washed

steps: Season chicken with half the salt and all the pepper. Heat oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and brown chicken for 3 minutes per side; set aside.
Lower heat, add butter and leeks, and soften for 6 minutes. Add water and scrape up browned bits.
Stir in cream, Dijon and remaining salt. Return chicken, cover partly and simmer gently for 8 to 12 minutes, until every breast reaches 165 F (74 C).
Rest for 5 minutes. Slice and serve with the leeks, sauce and parsley.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Wash between leek layers to remove grit. Keep the sauce at a gentle simmer so it does not split.
recipe.make_ahead: Refrigerate promptly in shallow containers for up to 3 days. Reheat leftovers to 165 F (74 C).

recipe.title: Chicken with Roasted Grapes and Shallots
recipe.description: Roast chicken thighs with sweet grapes, softened shallots and thyme pan juices.
steps: Heat oven to 425 F (220 C). Pat chicken dry and season with salt, pepper and thyme.
Toss grapes and shallots with oil in a roasting dish. Nestle chicken skin-side up among them and add water around the edges.
Roast for 35 to 45 minutes until shallots are tender and the thickest part of every thigh, away from bone, reaches at least 165 F (74 C).
Rest for 5 minutes. Stir vinegar into the pan juices and spoon around the chicken, keeping the skin crisp.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Use seedless grapes and keep chicken skin above the liquid. Start checking smaller thighs early.
recipe.make_ahead: Refrigerate promptly in shallow containers for up to 3 days. Reheat leftovers to 165 F (74 C).

recipe.title: Chicken Yassa
recipe.description: Senegal's beloved braise: chicken marinated in lemon, mustard and garlic, grilled, then simmered with a mountain of slowly caramelized onions, olives and a whole hot pepper.

ingredients.item: Scotch bonnet chili, left whole and pricked
white or broken rice, to serve

steps: Whisk the lemon juice, 2 tbsp mustard, garlic, vinegar, half the oil, salt and pepper. Toss the chicken and onions in it and marinate at least 3 hours, or overnight.
Lift the chicken out, shaking off the onions, and grill or broil it for 5 to 6 minutes a side, until well browned. It doesn't need to be cooked through.
Lift the onions from the marinade (keep the liquid). Cook them in the remaining oil in a wide pot over medium heat for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring often, until soft and golden.
Add the marinade, remaining mustard, chili, bay leaf, stock cube and water. Nestle in the chicken.
Cover and simmer gently for 30 minutes, until the chicken is tender. Add the olives for the last 5 minutes. Serve over rice with plenty of onion sauce.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: The onions are the star. Give them time to soften and turn sweet before the chicken goes back in.
Grilling the chicken first adds a smoky char, the way it's done in Senegal.
Keep the chili whole for flavor and gentle heat; break it open if you like it fiery.
recipe.make_ahead: Marinate up to a day ahead. The finished dish keeps 4 days and tastes even better reheated.
variations: Yassa poisson: use thick fish steaks and simmer only 10 minutes.

vegetarian.title: Tofu and Chickpea Yassa
vegetarian.description: Grilled tofu and chickpeas simmered in the same lemony mustard sauce with sweet caramelized onions and olives.

ingredients.item: extra-firm tofu, pressed and cut into thick slabs, plus 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained
Scotch bonnet chili, left whole and pricked
gluten-free vegetable stock cube (such as Herb-Ox)
white or broken rice, to serve

steps: Whisk the lemon juice, 2 tbsp mustard, garlic, vinegar, half the oil, salt and pepper. Toss the tofu and onions in it and marinate at least 1 hour, or overnight.
Lift the tofu out, shaking off the onions, and grill or broil it for 4 to 5 minutes a side, until well browned.
Lift the onions from the marinade (keep the liquid). Cook them in the remaining oil in a wide pot over medium heat for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring often, until soft and golden.
Add the marinade, remaining mustard, chili, bay leaf, vegetable stock cube and water. Nestle in the tofu and add the chickpeas.
Cover and simmer gently for 15 minutes so the tofu soaks up the sauce. Add the olives for the last 5 minutes. Serve over rice with plenty of onion sauce.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: The onions are the star. Give them time to soften and turn sweet before the tofu goes in.
Grilling the tofu first adds a smoky char and helps it hold together.
Keep the chili whole for flavor and gentle heat; break it open if you like it fiery.
vegetarian.make_ahead: Marinate up to a day ahead. The finished dish keeps 4 days and tastes even better reheated.

vegan.title: Tofu and Chickpea Yassa
vegan.description: Grilled tofu and chickpeas simmered in the same lemony mustard sauce with sweet caramelized onions and olives.

ingredients.item: extra-firm tofu, pressed and cut into thick slabs, plus 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained
Scotch bonnet chili, left whole and pricked
gluten-free vegetable stock cube (such as Herb-Ox)
white or broken rice, to serve

steps: Whisk the lemon juice, 2 tbsp mustard, garlic, vinegar, half the oil, salt and pepper. Toss the tofu and onions in it and marinate at least 1 hour, or overnight.
Lift the tofu out, shaking off the onions, and grill or broil it for 4 to 5 minutes a side, until well browned.
Lift the onions from the marinade (keep the liquid). Cook them in the remaining oil in a wide pot over medium heat for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring often, until soft and golden.
Add the marinade, remaining mustard, chili, bay leaf, vegetable stock cube and water. Nestle in the tofu and add the chickpeas.
Cover and simmer gently for 15 minutes so the tofu soaks up the sauce. Add the olives for the last 5 minutes. Serve over rice with plenty of onion sauce.
vegan.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: The onions are the star. Give them time to soften and turn sweet before the tofu goes in.
Grilling the tofu first adds a smoky char and helps it hold together.
Keep the chili whole for flavor and gentle heat; break it open if you like it fiery.
vegan.make_ahead: Marinate up to a day ahead. The finished dish keeps 4 days and tastes even better reheated.

recipe.title: Chickpea Spinach Shakshuka
recipe.description: A chickpea-and-spinach tomato skillet with fully set eggs and warm wheat pitas.
steps: Use a very wide lidded skillet, or divide between two pans. Soften onion and pepper in oil over medium heat for 6 minutes. Add garlic, cumin and paprika for 30 seconds.
Add tomatoes, chickpeas and salt and simmer for 10 minutes. Fold in spinach until wilted.
Make eight wells and crack an egg into each. Cover and cook gently for 8 to 12 minutes, until whites and yolks are set and the egg portion reaches 160 F (71 C).
Warm pitas according to the package and serve with the shakshuka and parsley, two eggs per person.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: This home variation adds chickpeas and spinach. Serve the eggs fully set rather than assuming runny yolks suit every diner.
recipe.make_ahead: Refrigerate leftovers promptly for up to 2 days. Reheat to 165 F (74 C); eggs may firm up further.

recipe.title: Chilaquiles Rojos
recipe.description: Tortilla chips simmered in red chile salsa, topped with eggs, crema and fresh cheese.
steps: Heat the salsa and broth in a wide skillet until simmering.
Add the chips and toss for 1 to 2 minutes until coated but still a little crisp.
Fry the eggs in the oil.
Divide the chilaquiles onto plates and top with eggs, queso fresco, crema, onion, cilantro and avocado.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Chilcano
recipe.description: Peru's favorite highball: pisco lengthened with ginger ale and fresh lime over ice, finished with a few drops of bitters. Light, spicy and refreshing.
steps: Fill a highball glass with ice and add the pisco and lime juice.
Top with ginger ale and stir gently.
Add the bitters on top and garnish with a lime wheel.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Pour lime juice over ice, top with ginger ale and add a few drops of bitters, or skip them for no alcohol at all.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Peruvian Quebranta pisco is traditional; any good pisco works.
Use a dry, spicy ginger ale rather than a sweet one.
variations: Chilcano de maracuyá: shake in 1 oz passion fruit pulp before topping with ginger ale.

recipe.title: Chili con Carne
recipe.description: Hearty beef and bean chili with chiles, cumin and tomatoes.

ingredients.item: salt, shredded cheese, sour cream and green onions

steps: Brown the beef in a large pot and drain most of the fat.
Add the onion, garlic and jalapeño and cook 5 minutes.
Stir in the spices, then the tomatoes, beans and broth.
Simmer, partly covered, for 1 to 1 1/2 hours, stirring now and then. Season with salt.
Serve with your toppings.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Char Siu
recipe.description: Cantonese barbecue pork with a sticky, sweet red glaze.

ingredients.item: pork shoulder, cut into long strips
red fermented bean curd or a few drops red food coloring (optional)

steps: Mix everything except the pork, then marinate the pork overnight.
Roast on a rack over a water-filled pan at 400°F for 25 minutes.
Flip, baste with marinade and roast 20 minutes more.
Brush with honey and broil 2 to 3 minutes until charred at the edges. Slice.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Mapo Tofu
recipe.description: Silky tofu and ground pork in a fiery, numbing Sichuan bean sauce.
steps: Simmer the tofu in salted water 2 minutes and drain.
Fry the pork in oil until cooked through (160°F) and crisp, then add the doubanjiang, black beans, garlic and ginger.
Add the stock and soy sauce, then slide in the tofu and simmer 5 minutes.
Thicken with the cornstarch mixture, shaking the pan gently.
Sprinkle with Sichuan pepper and green onions and serve with rice.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Peking Duck
recipe.description: Lacquered roast duck with crisp skin, wrapped in thin pancakes with hoisin, cucumber and green onion.

ingredients.item: green onions, cut into thin strips

steps: Pat the duck dry and rub the cavity with five-spice and salt.
Pour boiling water over the skin to tighten it, then dry.
Brush with the honey, vinegar and soy mixed together and refrigerate uncovered overnight.
Roast at 350°F for 1 1/2 hours on a rack, then at 425°F for 15 to 20 minutes until the skin is crisp and mahogany.
Carve and serve in pancakes with hoisin, cucumber and green onion.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Chocolate Layer Cake
recipe.description: Rich, moist chocolate cake with fudgy chocolate buttercream.
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and grease two 9-inch pans.
Whisk the flour, sugar, cocoa, baking soda, baking powder and salt.
Beat in the eggs, buttermilk and oil, then stir in the hot coffee. The batter will be thin.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes and cool completely.
Beat the butter, powdered sugar, cocoa, milk and vanilla until fluffy. Fill and frost the cake.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Chocolate Chip Cookies
recipe.description: Chewy, golden cookies with crisp edges and plenty of chocolate chips.
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F.
Whisk the flour, baking soda and salt.
Beat the butter and sugars until creamy, then beat in the eggs and vanilla.
Mix in the dry ingredients, then the chocolate chips.
Drop rounded tablespoons onto baking sheets and bake 9 to 11 minutes until golden at the edges. Cool on the sheet for 2 minutes.
recipe.note: Many chocolate chips contain soy lecithin; check your brand.

recipe.title: Choripán
recipe.description: Argentine grilled chorizo sandwiches with bright chimichurri.
steps: Mix the parsley, garlic, oregano, pepper flakes, vinegar and oil with a pinch of salt for the chimichurri.
Grill the chorizo over medium heat 12 to 15 minutes, turning, until cooked through.
Split the sausages lengthwise and grill the cut side briefly.
Toast the rolls, add the chorizo and spoon on chimichurri.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Chrysanthemum
recipe.description: Dry vermouth with Bénédictine and a touch of absinthe.

ingredients.item: vegan dry vermouth (such as Dolin Dry)

steps: Stir everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Churros with Chocolate Sauce
recipe.description: Crisp, ridged fritters of piped choux dough, fried golden, rolled in cinnamon sugar and dunked in a thick, warm chocolate sauce.

ingredients.item: vegetable or canola oil, for frying

steps: Make the sauce: heat the cream until steaming, pour it over the chocolate and let it sit for 2 minutes, then whisk until smooth. Keep warm.
Mix the 3/4 cup sugar and cinnamon in a shallow dish.

Bring the water, butter, 1 tablespoon sugar and salt to a boil in a saucepan. Add the flour all at once and stir hard with a wooden spoon for 1 to 2 minutes, until the dough forms a smooth ball and leaves a film on the pan.
Let the dough cool for 5 minutes, then beat in the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla, until smooth and glossy.
Spoon the dough into a piping bag fitted with a large open star tip.
Heat 2 inches of oil in a heavy pot to 360°F. Pipe 5-inch lengths straight into the oil, snipping them off with scissors. Fry 4 or 5 at a time for 3 to 4 minutes, turning, until deep golden.
Drain for a few seconds on paper towels, then roll in the cinnamon sugar while hot. Serve right away with the chocolate sauce.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Check the chocolate label if you avoid soy: many brands contain soy lecithin.
Use a star tip. The ridges help the churros cook evenly and stop them from bursting in the oil.
Keep the oil near 360°F. Too hot and they brown outside while staying raw inside.
recipe.make_ahead: Make the dough up to a day ahead and refrigerate it in the piping bag; let it warm slightly before piping.

recipe.title: New England Clam Chowder
recipe.description: Thick, creamy chowder with clams, potatoes and bacon.
steps: Cook the bacon until crisp, then add the onion and celery and cook until soft.
Stir in the flour, then whisk in the clam juice and the juice from the canned clams.
Add the potatoes and bay leaf and simmer 15 minutes until tender.
Add the clams and cream and heat through without boiling. Season and serve with crackers.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Clementine Thyme Vodka Sour
recipe.description: Fresh clementine, thyme and lemon make a pale orange vodka sour served up.
steps: Press thyme lightly with syrup in a shaker.
Add vodka, clementine juice, lemon and ice. Shake for 15 seconds and double-strain into a chilled coupe.
Express the clementine twist over the glass and add it.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake 3 oz clementine juice, 3/4 oz lemon juice, syrup and thyme with ice, then double-strain into a coupe.

recipe.note: An original Relish home cocktail. Please drink responsibly.
recipe.make_ahead: Prepare to order. Keep juices and brewed teas refrigerated until needed.

recipe.title: Clementine Vanilla Rum Fizz
recipe.description: Clementine juice and vanilla soften a bright white-rum fizz with fresh lime and soda.
steps: Shake rum, clementine juice, lime juice and vanilla syrup with ice for 12 seconds.
Strain into an ice-filled tall glass. Top with soda and stir once.
Garnish with the clementine wheel and serve immediately.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake 3 oz clementine juice, 1/2 oz lime juice and 1/4 oz vanilla syrup with ice; strain over ice and add 2 oz soda water.

recipe.note: An original Relish home cocktail. Please drink responsibly.
tips: For quick vanilla syrup, add 1/4 tsp vanilla extract to 1/2 cup plain simple syrup; measure the portion needed.
recipe.make_ahead: Juice clementines up to 1 day ahead and refrigerate. Add soda only when serving.

recipe.title: Clover Club
recipe.description: Gin with raspberry, lemon and a frothy egg white.

ingredients.item: vegan dry vermouth (such as Dolin Dry)

steps: Dry-shake everything without ice, then shake again with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake raspberry syrup, lemon and pasteurized egg white or aquafaba and top with sparkling lemonade.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: This drink uses raw egg white. Use pasteurized egg white if you prefer, and always for anyone pregnant, older or with a weakened immune system.

recipe.title: Turkey Club Sandwich
recipe.description: Triple-decker toast stacked with turkey, bacon, lettuce, tomato and mayo.
steps: Spread mayonnaise on the toast.
Layer turkey, lettuce and tomato on one slice, top with a second slice, then bacon, lettuce and tomato.
Finish with the third slice, secure with toothpicks and cut into quarters.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Cobb Salad
recipe.description: Rows of chicken, bacon, egg, avocado, tomato and blue cheese over greens.
steps: Spread the romaine on a platter.
Arrange the chicken, bacon, eggs, avocado, tomatoes and blue cheese in rows on top.
Drizzle with vinaigrette at the table and toss.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Cochinita Pibil
recipe.description: Yucatán slow-roasted pork marinated in achiote and citrus, with pickled red onions.

ingredients.item: pork shoulder, cut into large chunks
red onion, thinly sliced and soaked in lime juice with salt

steps: Blend the achiote, citrus juices, garlic, cumin, oregano and salt.
Coat the pork and marinate at least 4 hours or overnight.
Line a baking dish with banana leaves or foil, add the pork and marinade and wrap tightly.
Roast at 325°F for 3 1/2 to 4 hours until it shreds easily.
Shred and serve in tortillas with the pickled onions and salsa.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Coconut Lemongrass Rum Cooler
recipe.description: White rum, coconut water and lemongrass with lime and soda.
steps: Shake rum, coconut water, lime and syrup with ice.
Strain into a tall glass over fresh ice, top with soda and garnish.
For syrup, simmer 1/2 cup water, 1/2 cup sugar and one bruised lemongrass stalk for 5 minutes; cool and strain.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake the coconut water, lime and lemongrass syrup with ice, strain over ice and top with extra soda.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Coconut Lime Shrimp and Rice
recipe.description: Garlicky seared shrimp with lime and cilantro over fragrant jasmine rice cooked in coconut milk.
steps: Rinse rice. Bring rice, coconut milk, water and salt to a boil; cover and cook on low 15 minutes. Rest covered 10 minutes, then fluff.
Heat oil in a skillet over medium-high. Cook shrimp 2–3 minutes per side until opaque and cooked through; add garlic for the final 30 seconds.
Toss shrimp with lime zest and juice. Serve over rice with cilantro.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Coconut Pineapple Lime Cooler
recipe.description: Coconut rum with pineapple, lime and coconut water, topped with soda. Tropical and light.
steps: Shake rum, pineapple, lime and coconut water with ice.
Strain into a tall glass over fresh ice; top with soda.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: replace rum with 1 1/2 oz coconut water.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Coconut Red Lentil Spinach Dal
recipe.description: A home-style red lentil dal with coconut milk, tomato and spinach, served over basmati rice.
steps: Heat oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Soften onion for 5 minutes. Add garlic, ginger, cumin and turmeric and stir for 30 seconds.
Add lentils, tomatoes and water. Bring to a boil, then cover partly and simmer for 20 minutes, stirring often, until lentils collapse; add water if thickening too fast.
Stir in coconut milk and salt. Simmer for 5 minutes, then fold in spinach until wilted.
Serve over hot basmati rice and scatter with cilantro.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: This is a flexible home-style dal rather than a claim to one regional preparation. The lentils thicken as they cool.
recipe.make_ahead: Refrigerate dal and rice promptly in shallow containers and use within 3 days. Reheat once until steaming throughout, at least 165 F (74 C).

recipe.title: Cod in Coconut Tomato Broth
recipe.description: Cod gently poached in coconut milk, tomato, ginger and lime, served over rice.
steps: Heat oil in a deep skillet over medium heat. Soften onion for 5 minutes; add garlic and ginger for 30 seconds.
Add tomatoes, coconut milk, water and salt. Simmer for 8 minutes.
Nestle cod in the broth, cover and simmer gently for 7 to 10 minutes until every piece reaches 145 F (63 C).
Stir lime juice into the broth without breaking the fish. Serve over hot rice with cilantro.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: A gentle simmer keeps the fish in large moist flakes. Check that the coconut milk contains only the expected ingredients.
recipe.make_ahead: Refrigerate promptly in shallow containers and use within 2 days. Reheat leftovers gently to 165 F (74 C).

recipe.title: Creamy Coleslaw
recipe.description: Crunchy cabbage and carrot slaw in a tangy, creamy dressing.
steps: Whisk the mayonnaise, vinegar, sugar, mustard and celery seed.
Toss with the cabbage and carrot and season.
Chill 30 minutes before serving.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Commodore
recipe.description: Bourbon with crème de cacao, lemon and grenadine.
steps: Shake everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Continental Sour
recipe.description: A whiskey sour with egg white, finished with a float of red wine.

ingredients.item: vegan dry red wine (such as Yellow Tail Shiraz)

steps: Dry-shake the whiskey, lemon, syrup and egg white, then shake with ice.
Strain over ice and float the red wine on top.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: This drink uses raw egg white. Use pasteurized egg white if you prefer, and always for anyone pregnant, older or with a weakened immune system.

recipe.title: Coq au Vin
recipe.description: French chicken braised in red wine with mushrooms, bacon and onions.
steps: Cook the bacon and remove. Brown the seasoned chicken in the fat and remove.
Stir the flour into the fat, then add the wine, broth, tomato paste, garlic and herbs.
Return the chicken and bacon, cover and simmer 45 minutes.
Brown the mushrooms and onions in the butter, add to the pot and simmer 20 minutes more.
Season and serve with mashed potatoes or bread.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Corn 'n' Oil
recipe.description: Barbados rum and falernum with lime and bitters.
steps: Build in a rocks glass over ice and stir.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Corpse Reviver No. 2
recipe.description: Equal parts gin, Lillet, orange liqueur and lemon with an absinthe rinse.
steps: Rinse a chilled coupe with absinthe.
Shake the rest with ice and strain into the glass.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Cosmopolitan
recipe.description: Crisp and tart: citrus vodka, Cointreau, fresh lime and just enough cranberry for a pale pink color, shaken ice-cold and served up.
steps: Chill a coupe or martini glass with ice water while you mix.
Add the vodka, Cointreau, lime and cranberry to a shaker. Fill it two-thirds with ice.
Shake hard for 12 to 15 seconds, until the shaker is frosty and too cold to hold comfortably.
Dump the ice water from the glass and fine-strain the drink into it through a small sieve, so no ice chips cloud it.
Hold the orange peel skin-side down over the drink, squeeze to spray its oils across the top, then rub it on the rim and drop it in.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake 2 oz cranberry juice, 3/4 oz lime juice and 1/2 oz orange juice with ice and top with a splash of lemon-lime soda.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Fresh lime is the difference between a great Cosmo and a sour-mix one. Squeeze it within a few hours of using it.
It should be pale pink, not red. Too much cranberry turns it into a juice.
Cointreau is drier and stronger than generic triple sec, and keeps the drink balanced. If you use triple sec, cut the cranberry a little.
recipe.make_ahead: Make it to order. For a party, mix everything but the ice up to a day ahead, chill the bottle, and shake each drink with ice when serving.
variations: Use plain vodka with a dash of orange bitters if you don't have citrus vodka.
White Cosmo: use white cranberry juice and garnish with frozen cranberries.

recipe.title: Cou-Cou and Flying Fish
recipe.description: The national dish of Barbados: lime-marinated flying fish steamed in a tomato, onion and pepper creole sauce, served over cou-cou, a smooth, buttery cornmeal and okra mash.

ingredients.item: flying fish fillets, or 1 1/2 lb thin white fish fillets
Bajan seasoning (green onion, thyme, parsley, garlic and hot pepper blended)
hot pepper sauce, plus more to serve
fine yellow cornmeal, soaked in 1 1/2 cups cold water

steps: Rub the fish with lime juice and a pinch of salt, rinse, then coat with the Bajan seasoning. Marinate 30 minutes or up to overnight.
Make the sauce: melt the butter and cook the onion and pepper for 5 minutes. Add the garlic, tomatoes, tomato paste, thyme, stock, hot sauce and 1/2 tsp salt, and simmer 10 minutes.
Lay the fish in the sauce, roll it up if it's thin, cover and steam gently for 8 to 10 minutes, until it flakes.
Meanwhile, make the cou-cou: boil the okra in the 4 cups water with 1 tsp salt for 5 minutes. Scoop out the okra and keep the slimy cooking water.

Over low heat, stir the soaked cornmeal into half the okra water, then keep adding the rest a ladle at a time, stirring hard with a wooden spoon, for 10 to 12 minutes, until thick, smooth and pulling away from the pan.
Stir in the okra and butter. Press the cou-cou into a buttered bowl, then turn it out onto a plate.
Make a well in the top and spoon over the fish and plenty of sauce. Serve with extra pepper sauce and lime.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: The okra water is the secret: its natural thickness makes the cou-cou silky. Bajans stir it with a flat "cou-cou stick" to keep it lump-free.
Soaking the cornmeal in cold water first stops it from clumping when it hits the hot liquid.
Flying fish is delicate. Steam it gently in the sauce rather than boiling it.
recipe.make_ahead: The sauce keeps 3 days; cook the fish in it fresh. Cou-cou firms up as it cools; slice and fry leftovers in butter.
variations: Fried flying fish: dip the seasoned fillets in flour, egg and breadcrumbs and fry until golden, then serve the sauce on the side.

vegetarian.title: Vegetarian Cou-Cou with Creole Eggplant
vegetarian.description: Silky okra cou-cou topped with seasoned eggplant steamed in the same tomato and pepper creole sauce.

ingredients.item: small eggplants, sliced into thick rounds
Bajan seasoning (green onion, thyme, parsley, garlic and hot pepper blended)
hot pepper sauce, plus more to serve
fine yellow cornmeal, soaked in 1 1/2 cups cold water

steps: Salt the eggplant for 15 minutes and pat dry, then coat with the lime juice and Bajan seasoning. Brown it in a little oil for 3 minutes a side.
Make the sauce: melt the butter and cook the onion and pepper for 5 minutes. Add the garlic, tomatoes, tomato paste, thyme, stock, hot sauce and 1/2 tsp salt, and simmer 10 minutes.
Lay the eggplant in the sauce, cover and simmer gently for 12 to 15 minutes, until silky.
Meanwhile, make the cou-cou: boil the okra in the 4 cups water with 1 tsp salt for 5 minutes. Scoop out the okra and keep the slimy cooking water.

Over low heat, stir the soaked cornmeal into half the okra water, then keep adding the rest a ladle at a time, stirring hard with a wooden spoon, for 10 to 12 minutes, until thick, smooth and pulling away from the pan.
Stir in the okra and butter. Press the cou-cou into a buttered bowl, then turn it out onto a plate.
Make a well in the top and spoon over the eggplant and plenty of sauce. Serve with extra pepper sauce and lime.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: The okra water is the secret: its natural thickness makes the cou-cou silky. Bajans stir it with a flat "cou-cou stick" to keep it lump-free.
Soaking the cornmeal in cold water first stops it from clumping when it hits the hot liquid.
Browning the eggplant first helps it hold its shape in the sauce.
vegetarian.make_ahead: The sauce keeps 3 days; cook the eggplant in it fresh. Cou-cou firms up as it cools; slice and fry leftovers in butter.

vegan.title: Vegan Cou-Cou with Creole Eggplant
vegan.description: The vegetarian version made with olive oil in place of butter, in both the sauce and the cou-cou.

ingredients.item: small eggplants, sliced into thick rounds
Bajan seasoning (green onion, thyme, parsley, garlic and hot pepper blended)
hot pepper sauce, plus more to serve
fine yellow cornmeal, soaked in 1 1/2 cups cold water

steps: Salt the eggplant for 15 minutes and pat dry, then coat with the lime juice and Bajan seasoning. Brown it in a little oil for 3 minutes a side.
Make the sauce: heat the oil and cook the onion and pepper for 5 minutes. Add the garlic, tomatoes, tomato paste, thyme, stock, hot sauce and 1/2 tsp salt, and simmer 10 minutes.
Lay the eggplant in the sauce, cover and simmer gently for 12 to 15 minutes, until silky.
Meanwhile, make the cou-cou: boil the okra in the 4 cups water with 1 tsp salt for 5 minutes. Scoop out the okra and keep the slimy cooking water.

Over low heat, stir the soaked cornmeal into half the okra water, then keep adding the rest a ladle at a time, stirring hard with a wooden spoon, for 10 to 12 minutes, until thick, smooth and pulling away from the pan.
Stir in the okra and olive oil. Press the cou-cou into an oiled bowl, then turn it out onto a plate.
Make a well in the top and spoon over the eggplant and plenty of sauce. Serve with extra pepper sauce and lime.
vegan.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: The okra water is the secret: its natural thickness makes the cou-cou silky. Bajans stir it with a flat "cou-cou stick" to keep it lump-free.
Soaking the cornmeal in cold water first stops it from clumping when it hits the hot liquid.
Browning the eggplant first helps it hold its shape in the sauce.
vegan.make_ahead: The sauce keeps 3 days; cook the fish in it fresh. Cou-cou firms up as it cools; slice and fry leftovers in olive oil.

recipe.title: Maryland Crab Cakes
recipe.description: Golden, lightly bound lump crab cakes seasoned with Old Bay.
steps: Whisk the egg, mayonnaise, mustard, Worcestershire and Old Bay.
Gently fold in the crab, crackers and parsley without breaking up the lumps.
Shape into 8 cakes and chill 30 minutes.
Fry in butter over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes per side until golden.
Serve with lemon and tartar sauce.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Cracked Conch
recipe.description: The Bahamas' fish-fry favorite: conch pounded thin and tender, dipped in a seasoned egg and flour coating, and fried until golden. Served with lime, hot sauce and a tangy dip.

ingredients.item: limes, juiced, plus wedges to serve
mayonnaise mixed with 2 tbsp ketchup and hot sauce, for dipping
French fries, coleslaw or peas and rice, to serve

steps: Rinse the conch, rub it with the lime juice and trim off any tough orange skin.
Put each piece between sheets of plastic wrap and pound with a meat mallet until about 1/4 inch thick and noticeably softer. Cut large pieces in half.
Whisk the eggs and milk in one dish. In another, mix the flour, garlic powder, seasoned salt, cayenne, pepper and thyme.
Heat 2 inches of oil to 350°F. Dip the conch in flour, then egg, then flour again, pressing the coating on.
Fry 2 or 3 pieces at a time for 2 to 3 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp. Don't overcook or the conch toughens.
Drain on a rack and serve hot with lime wedges, the dipping sauce and fries, slaw or peas and rice.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: The name comes from "cracking", or pounding, the conch. Skip it and the meat is rubbery; overdo it and it falls apart.
Fry quickly and hot. Conch only needs a couple of minutes once it's been pounded thin.
Frozen cleaned conch from seafood or Caribbean markets works well; thaw it in the fridge.
recipe.make_ahead: Pound and coat the conch up to 2 hours ahead and chill on a tray; fry just before serving.
variations: Use thin calamari steaks or pounded shrimp if you can't find conch.

vegetarian.title: Cracked King Oyster Mushrooms
vegetarian.description: King oyster mushroom planks pressed flat, seasoned the Bahamian way and fried crisp in the same egg and flour coating.

ingredients.item: king oyster mushrooms, sliced lengthwise into 1/3-inch planks
limes, juiced, plus wedges to serve
mayonnaise mixed with 2 tbsp ketchup and hot sauce, for dipping
French fries, coleslaw or peas and rice, to serve

steps: Toss the mushroom planks with the lime juice and a pinch of salt.
Press each plank firmly with the flat of a knife or a heavy pan to flatten it slightly so it cooks evenly.
Whisk the eggs and milk in one dish. In another, mix the flour, garlic powder, seasoned salt, cayenne, pepper and thyme.
Heat 2 inches of oil to 350°F. Dip the mushrooms in flour, then egg, then flour again, pressing the coating on.
Fry 2 or 3 pieces at a time for 2 to 3 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp. The mushrooms should be tender inside.
Drain on a rack and serve hot with lime wedges, the dipping sauce and fries, slaw or peas and rice.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: King oyster stems have a firm, slightly chewy bite that's close to conch.
Fry quickly and hot so the coating crisps before the mushrooms turn soft.
Pat the mushrooms dry before coating or the crust will slip off.
vegetarian.make_ahead: Coat the mushrooms up to 1 hour ahead and chill on a tray; fry just before serving.

vegan.title: Vegan Cracked King Oyster Mushrooms
vegan.description: King oyster mushroom planks in a crisp seasoned coating made with soy milk instead of egg, with a vegan dipping sauce.

ingredients.item: king oyster mushrooms, sliced lengthwise into 1/3-inch planks
limes, juiced, plus wedges to serve
vegan mayo mixed with 2 tbsp ketchup and hot sauce, for dipping
French fries, vinegar slaw or peas and rice, to serve

steps: Toss the mushroom planks with the lime juice and a pinch of salt.
Press each plank firmly with the flat of a knife or a heavy pan to flatten it slightly so it cooks evenly.
Whisk the cornstarch and soy milk in one dish. In another, mix the flour, garlic powder, seasoned salt, cayenne, pepper and thyme.
Heat 2 inches of oil to 350°F. Dip the mushrooms in flour, then the soy milk mix, then flour again, pressing the coating on.
Fry 2 or 3 pieces at a time for 2 to 3 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp. The mushrooms should be tender inside.
Drain on a rack and serve hot with lime wedges, the dipping sauce and fries, slaw or peas and rice.
vegan.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: King oyster stems have a firm, slightly chewy bite that's close to conch.
Fry quickly and hot so the coating crisps before the mushrooms turn soft.
Pat the mushrooms dry before coating or the crust will slip off.
vegan.make_ahead: Coat the mushrooms up to 1 hour ahead and chill on a tray; fry just before serving.

recipe.title: Cranberry Ginger Gin Highball
recipe.description: Cranberry, ginger and lemon make a crisp ruby gin highball.
steps: Shake gin, cranberry juice, lemon and ginger syrup with ice for 12 seconds.
Strain into an ice-filled highball and add soda.
Stir gently and garnish with the lemon wheel.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake 3 oz cranberry juice, 1/2 oz lemon juice and 1/2 oz ginger syrup with ice; strain and top with 3 oz soda.

recipe.note: An original Relish home cocktail. Please drink responsibly.
tips: If using sweetened cranberry juice cocktail, start with half the syrup and taste before adding more.
recipe.make_ahead: Prepare to order. Keep juices and brewed teas refrigerated until needed.

recipe.title: Cranberry Orange Bourbon Sour
recipe.description: A bourbon sour with tart cranberry and orange, served over ice with an orange twist.
steps: Shake all liquid ingredients with ice and strain over fresh ice in a rocks glass.
Garnish with orange peel.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: use alcohol-free whiskey alternative.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Cranberry Sage Vodka Fizz
recipe.description: Tart cranberry, sage and lemon lift a sparkling vodka drink.
steps: Press the two sage leaves gently with syrup in a shaker.
Add vodka, cranberry juice, lemon juice and ice. Shake for 12 seconds and strain into an ice-filled highball.
Add soda, stir once and garnish with the small sage sprig.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake cranberry juice, lemon, syrup and sage without vodka; strain over ice and top with 3 oz soda.

recipe.note: An original Relish home cocktail. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Use unsweetened cranberry juice; sweetened cranberry cocktail needs less syrup.
recipe.make_ahead: Prepare to order. Keep juices and brewed teas refrigerated until needed.

recipe.title: Creamy Chicken and Wild Rice Soup
recipe.description: A creamy soup of chicken, wild rice, carrots and celery with thyme.
steps: Cook onion, carrots and celery in oil for 5 minutes. Add rice, broth and thyme; simmer covered according to the rice package, about 40–50 minutes, until tender.
Stir in chicken and cream. Simmer gently until the chicken is heated to 165°F; add water if the soup is too thick.
Season with salt and pepper.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Creamy Polenta with Mushroom Ragout
recipe.description: Soft polenta topped with mushrooms simmered in a thyme-tomato ragout.
steps: Bring milk and water just to a simmer in a heavy pan. Whisk in polenta and half the salt. Cook over low heat, stirring often, for 25 to 35 minutes or its package time until soft; add water if needed.
Meanwhile brown mushrooms in oil in a wide skillet over medium-high heat for 8 minutes. Add onion for 5 minutes, then garlic and thyme for 30 seconds.
Add tomatoes, remaining salt and pepper and simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir butter and cheese into polenta. Divide among bowls and spoon mushroom ragout over the top.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Use coarse cornmeal labeled polenta and follow its cooking time. Choose a hard cheese labeled vegetarian if needed.
recipe.make_ahead: Refrigerate promptly in shallow containers for up to 3 days. Reheat leftovers to 165 F (74 C).

recipe.title: Creamy Sun-Dried Tomato Gnocchi
recipe.description: Pillowy gnocchi in a garlicky sun-dried tomato cream sauce with spinach and Parmesan. Ready in 20 minutes.
steps: Cook gnocchi according to package directions and drain.
Cook garlic and sun-dried tomatoes in oil for 1 minute. Add cream and broth; simmer 3 minutes.
Stir in gnocchi and spinach until spinach wilts. Add Parmesan and season to taste.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Crème Brûlée
recipe.description: The French classic: a silky vanilla bean custard baked gently in a water bath, chilled, then topped with a glassy layer of caramelized sugar to crack with your spoon.

ingredients.item: vanilla bean, split and seeds scraped (or 2 tsp vanilla extract)
superfine or turbinado sugar, for the tops

steps: Heat the oven to 300°F and bring a kettle of water to a boil. Set six 6-ounce ramekins in a roasting pan.
Heat the cream with the vanilla seeds and pod until it just begins to steam. Turn off the heat and let it steep for 15 minutes, then remove the pod.
Whisk the yolks, 1/2 cup sugar and salt until pale. Slowly whisk in the warm cream, a little at a time.
