Strain the custard into a pitcher and pour it into the ramekins.
Pour boiling water into the roasting pan to come halfway up the sides of the ramekins.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes, until set at the edges but still wobbly in the center.
Cool the ramekins on a rack, then cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours.
Just before serving, sprinkle each with 1 teaspoon sugar and melt it with a kitchen torch until deep golden and bubbling. Let it harden for 1 minute.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Add the warm cream slowly. Pouring it in all at once can scramble the yolks.
No torch? Put the sugared custards under a very hot broiler for 1 to 2 minutes, watching closely.
recipe.make_ahead: Bake the custards up to 3 days ahead. Caramelize the tops just before serving.
variations: Add the zest of an orange or a spoonful of espresso powder to the cream.

recipe.title: French Crêpes
recipe.description: Thin, tender French pancakes made from a simple rested batter of flour, eggs, milk and melted butter. Serve them with lemon and sugar, jam or chocolate spread.

ingredients.item: unsalted butter, melted, plus more for the pan
lemon wedges and sugar, to serve

steps: Whisk the flour, sugar and salt in a bowl. Make a well, add the eggs and about half the milk and whisk to a smooth, thick batter.
Whisk in the rest of the milk, the water and the melted butter until the batter is as thin as heavy cream. Or blend everything in a blender for 15 seconds.
Cover and rest the batter for at least 30 minutes at room temperature, or overnight in the fridge.
Heat an 8- to 10-inch nonstick or crêpe pan over medium heat and brush it lightly with butter.
Pour in about 1/4 cup of batter and immediately tilt and swirl the pan to coat the bottom in a thin layer.
Cook for 1 minute, until the edges lift and the underside is lightly golden. Flip and cook for 20 to 30 seconds more.
Stack the crêpes on a plate. Serve folded into quarters with a squeeze of lemon and a sprinkle of sugar.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Resting the batter relaxes the gluten, which makes the crêpes softer and less likely to tear.
The first crêpe is often a test. Adjust the heat and the amount of batter after it.
If the batter thickens after resting, stir in a splash of milk.
recipe.make_ahead: Stack cooked crêpes with parchment between them and refrigerate for up to 3 days, or freeze for a month. Warm in a dry pan.
variations: Savory crêpes: leave out the sugar and fill with ham, Gruyère and a fried egg.
Crêpes Suzette: warm the crêpes in a sauce of butter, sugar, orange juice and orange liqueur.

recipe.title: Crispy Coconut Fish with Mango Salsa
recipe.description: Coconut and panko-crusted white fish served with fresh mango salsa.
steps: Heat oven to 425°F and oil a lined baking tray. Mix mango, onion, lime juice and cilantro for salsa.
Season fish with salt. Coat in flour, dip in egg, then press into the mixed coconut and panko. Place on the tray and brush or drizzle with oil.
Bake 15–20 minutes, until golden and fish reaches 145°F. Serve with mango salsa.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Crispy Halloumi Couscous Bowls
recipe.description: Golden halloumi slices over couscous with cucumber, tomato, mint and lemon.

ingredients.item: lemon, half juiced and half cut into wedges

steps: Put couscous in a heatproof bowl with salt and boiling water. Cover for 5 minutes, or follow package directions, then fluff.
Pat halloumi dry. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat and brown slices for 1 to 2 minutes per side.
Toss couscous with remaining oil, lemon juice, cucumber, tomatoes, mint and black pepper.
Divide among bowls and top each with two hot halloumi slices and a lemon wedge.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Halloumi is salty; season the couscous lightly. Select vegetarian-rennet halloumi if required.
recipe.make_ahead: Keep couscous salad refrigerated for up to 2 days. Halloumi is best cooked just before serving; refrigerate leftovers promptly.

recipe.title: Crispy Lentil Potato Patties with Cucumber Yogurt
recipe.description: Golden lentil-potato patties with a cool cucumber and yogurt sauce.

ingredients.item: green lentils (15 oz), drained, rinsed and patted dry

steps: Boil potatoes in water for 12 to 15 minutes until tender. Drain thoroughly, mash and let steam-dry for 5 minutes.
Mash lentils roughly and mix with potatoes, egg, flour, scallions, cumin, salt and pepper. Form eight firm patties.
Heat oil in a wide nonstick skillet over medium heat. Cook patties in two batches for 4 to 5 minutes per side, until crisp and the centers reach 160 F (71 C).
Mix yogurt with squeezed cucumber and lemon juice. Serve two patties per person with the sauce.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Dry potatoes and lentils thoroughly so the patties bind. Turn only after a crust forms.
recipe.make_ahead: Refrigerate patties and sauce separately promptly for up to 3 days. Reheat patties to 165 F (74 C); keep sauce cold.

recipe.title: Crispy Tofu Katsu Curry
recipe.description: Oven-crisp panko tofu with a mild vegetable curry and rice, inspired by Japanese katsu curry.
steps: Heat oven to 425 F (220 C). Cut tofu into four slabs and pat dry. Mix 1 tbsp flour with batter water; dip tofu in the mixture and press into panko. Place on a lined sheet pan, drizzle with 1 tbsp oil and bake for 25 minutes, turning halfway, until crisp.
Heat remaining oil in a saucepan. Soften onion and carrot for 6 minutes. Add potato, apple and spices and stir for 1 minute.
Stir in remaining flour for 1 minute, then gradually add curry water and soy sauce. Simmer for 20 minutes, stirring often, until vegetables are tender and sauce is thick; add water if needed.
Slice crispy tofu and serve with curry and hot rice.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Use plain panko whose label does not add milk or eggs; check tofu and sauce labels too. Start with ready-pressed tofu or allow an extra 15 minutes to press it.
recipe.make_ahead: Refrigerate promptly in shallow containers for up to 3 days. Reheat leftovers to 165 F (74 C).

recipe.title: Croque Monsieur
recipe.description: The Paris café classic: a ham and Gruyère sandwich with Dijon mustard, covered in creamy béchamel and more cheese, then baked and broiled until golden and bubbling.

ingredients.item: thick slices of white sandwich bread

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F and line a baking sheet with parchment.

Make the béchamel: melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat, whisk in the flour and cook for 1 minute. Slowly whisk in the warm milk and simmer, whisking, for 3 to 4 minutes, until thick. Stir in the nutmeg, salt and white pepper.
Toast the bread lightly on the baking sheet for 5 minutes.
Spread 4 slices with mustard and a thin layer of béchamel. Top with the ham and half the cheese, then the other slices of bread.
Spread the remaining béchamel thickly over the tops and sprinkle with the rest of the cheese.
Bake for 6 to 8 minutes, until the cheese melts, then broil for 2 to 3 minutes, watching closely, until golden brown and bubbling.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Make the béchamel thick, so it sits on top of the sandwich instead of running off.
Watch the broiler closely. The top goes from golden to burnt in under a minute.
recipe.make_ahead: Make the béchamel up to 2 days ahead and keep it covered in the fridge. Warm it gently before using.
variations: Croque madame: top each sandwich with a fried egg.

recipe.title: Cuba Libre
recipe.description: Rum and cola with plenty of lime.
steps: Fill a highball with ice and add the rum and lime.
Top with cola and stir.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Cola with lime.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Cucumber Green Tea Tequila Highball
recipe.description: Fresh cucumber, green tea and lime make a restrained sparkling tequila highball.
steps: Press cucumber slices gently with agave syrup in a shaker.
Add tequila, cooled tea, lime and ice; shake briefly and strain into an ice-filled highball.
Top with soda, stir gently and garnish with the cucumber ribbon.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake cucumber, 3 oz cooled green tea, 1/2 oz lime juice and 1/4 oz agave syrup with ice; strain and add 2 oz soda.

recipe.note: An original Relish home cocktail. Please drink responsibly.
recipe.make_ahead: Prepare to order. Keep juices and brewed teas refrigerated until needed.

recipe.title: Cucumber Lime Vodka Cooler
recipe.description: Vodka, lime and muddled cucumber topped with soda. Crisp and refreshing.
steps: Muddle cucumber and syrup in a shaker.
Add vodka, lime and ice; shake and strain into a tall ice-filled glass.
Top with soda and stir.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: replace vodka with cold water or alcohol-free vodka alternative.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Cucumber Melon Gin Cooler
recipe.description: Gin with honeydew, cucumber and lime, topped with soda.
steps: Muddle cucumber with syrup.
Shake with gin, melon, lime and ice.
Fine-strain into a tall glass over ice, top with soda and garnish with a cucumber ribbon.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Muddle the cucumber with syrup, shake with honeydew and lime, strain over ice and top with extra soda.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Cynar Julep
recipe.description: Buenos Aires' favorite modern classic: bittersweet artichoke amaro with mint, lemon and grapefruit over crushed ice. Low in alcohol and very refreshing.
steps: Gently muddle the mint with the syrup and lemon juice in a julep cup or rocks glass.
Add the Cynar and fill with crushed ice. Swizzle with a spoon until the glass frosts.
Top with grapefruit juice or soda and more crushed ice. Garnish with a big mint sprig.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Muddle mint with syrup and lemon, then top with grapefruit juice, grapefruit soda and crushed ice.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Cynar is bitter but not harsh; grapefruit and mint bring out its sweet, herbal side.
Swizzling over crushed ice chills and dilutes the drink quickly; that's what makes a julep.
variations: Add a splash of gin for a stronger version, as in the original Buenos Aires recipe.

recipe.title: Classic Daiquiri
recipe.description: White rum, lime and sugar, shaken and served up.
steps: Shake everything hard with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake lime and syrup with ice and top with lemon-lime soda.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Dal Makhani
recipe.description: Creamy, slow-simmered black lentils and kidney beans with butter, tomato and spices.

ingredients.item: whole black lentils (urad dal), soaked overnight

steps: Cook the lentils and beans in fresh water until completely soft, about 1 hour (or 30 minutes in a pressure cooker).
Melt the butter and cook the onion until golden, then the ginger-garlic paste.
Add the tomato and spices and cook until the butter separates.
Add the lentils with their liquid and simmer gently 45 minutes, mashing some, until creamy.
Stir in the cream and fenugreek and season.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Dan Dan Noodles
recipe.description: Sichuan's famous street noodles: springy wheat noodles in a numbing, spicy sesame and chili oil sauce, topped with crisp savory pork, preserved mustard greens and crushed peanuts.

ingredients.item: sui mi ya cai (Sichuan preserved mustard greens)
hot noodle water or chicken broth
roasted peanuts, crushed, and sliced green onions, to serve

steps: Heat the oil in a wok and stir-fry the pork over medium-high heat for 5 to 7 minutes, breaking it up, until browned, slightly crisp and cooked through (160°F).
Add the Shaoxing wine, sweet bean sauce and dark soy sauce and cook 1 minute. Push the pork aside, add the ya cai and stir for 30 seconds, then mix it in.
Whisk the sesame paste, light soy sauce, chili oil, vinegar, sugar, Sichuan pepper and garlic in a bowl, then loosen with the hot noodle water or broth.
Cook the noodles according to the package. Add the bok choy for the last minute, then drain.
Divide the sauce among four bowls, add the noodles and greens and top with the pork, peanuts and green onions. Toss everything together at the table.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Fry the pork until it's dry and slightly crispy; that's what gives dan dan its savory crunch.
Toast the Sichuan peppercorns in a dry pan before grinding for the full tingling, numbing effect.
Toss well before eating: the sauce sits at the bottom of the bowl.
recipe.make_ahead: The pork topping and sauce keep 4 days in the fridge. Cook the noodles fresh.
variations: Use ground chicken or turkey instead of pork.

vegetarian.title: Vegetarian Dan Dan Noodles
vegetarian.description: Crisp, savory chopped mushrooms and tofu in place of pork, over noodles in the same numbing sesame and chili sauce.

ingredients.item: mixed mushrooms and firm tofu, finely chopped
sui mi ya cai (Sichuan preserved mustard greens)
hot noodle water or vegetable broth
roasted peanuts, crushed, and sliced green onions, to serve

steps: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wok and stir-fry the mushrooms and tofu over medium-high heat for 8 to 10 minutes, until their liquid has cooked off and they are browned and crisp at the edges.
Add the Shaoxing wine, sweet bean sauce and dark soy sauce and cook 1 minute. Push the mushrooms aside, add the ya cai and stir for 30 seconds, then mix it in.
Whisk the sesame paste, light soy sauce, chili oil, vinegar, sugar, Sichuan pepper and garlic in a bowl, then loosen with the hot noodle water or broth.
Cook the noodles according to the package. Add the bok choy for the last minute, then drain.
Divide the sauce among four bowls, add the noodles and greens and top with the mushroom crumble, peanuts and green onions. Toss everything together at the table.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Fry the mushrooms until all their water is gone and they start to crisp; that's what gives dan dan its savory crunch.
Toast the Sichuan peppercorns in a dry pan before grinding for the full tingling, numbing effect.
Toss well before eating: the sauce sits at the bottom of the bowl.
vegetarian.make_ahead: The mushroom topping and sauce keep 4 days in the fridge. Cook the noodles fresh.

vegan.title: Vegan Dan Dan Noodles
vegan.description: Crisp, savory chopped mushrooms and tofu in place of pork, over noodles in the same numbing sesame and chili sauce.

ingredients.item: mixed mushrooms and firm tofu, finely chopped
sui mi ya cai (Sichuan preserved mustard greens)
hot noodle water or vegetable broth
roasted peanuts, crushed, and sliced green onions, to serve

steps: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wok and stir-fry the mushrooms and tofu over medium-high heat for 8 to 10 minutes, until their liquid has cooked off and they are browned and crisp at the edges.
Add the Shaoxing wine, sweet bean sauce and dark soy sauce and cook 1 minute. Push the mushrooms aside, add the ya cai and stir for 30 seconds, then mix it in.
Whisk the sesame paste, light soy sauce, chili oil, vinegar, sugar, Sichuan pepper and garlic in a bowl, then loosen with the hot noodle water or broth.
Cook the noodles according to the package. Add the bok choy for the last minute, then drain.
Divide the sauce among four bowls, add the noodles and greens and top with the mushroom crumble, peanuts and green onions. Toss everything together at the table.
vegan.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Fry the mushrooms until all their water is gone and they start to crisp; that's what gives dan dan its savory crunch.
Toast the Sichuan peppercorns in a dry pan before grinding for the full tingling, numbing effect.
Toss well before eating: the sauce sits at the bottom of the bowl.
vegan.make_ahead: The mushroom topping and sauce keep 4 days in the fridge. Cook the noodles fresh.

recipe.title: Dark 'n' Stormy
recipe.description: Dark rum floated over spicy ginger beer and lime.
steps: Fill a highball with ice and add the ginger beer and lime.
Float the rum on top.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Ginger beer with lime.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Date Orange Bourbon Sour
recipe.description: Soft dates, fresh orange and lemon give bourbon a rounded fruit-sour finish.
steps: Mash the chopped date with warm water in a shaker until loosened; stand for 2 minutes.
Add bourbon, orange juice, lemon juice and plenty of ice. Shake firmly for 15 seconds and double-strain into a rocks glass over fresh ice.
Express the orange twist over the drink and add it.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Mash the date with water; shake with 2 oz orange juice and 3/4 oz lemon juice and ice, then double-strain over fresh ice.

recipe.note: An original Relish home cocktail. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Remove the date stone completely before mixing. Fine-straining catches fibrous pieces.
recipe.make_ahead: Prepare to order. Keep juices and brewed teas refrigerated until needed.

recipe.title: Death Flip
recipe.description: A modern classic from Melbourne's Black Pearl bar: tequila, yellow Chartreuse and Jägermeister shaken with a whole egg into a rich, gingerbread-spiced flip.
steps: Shake the tequila, Chartreuse, Jägermeister, syrup and egg without ice for 15 seconds.
Add ice and shake hard for 10 seconds more.
Fine strain into a small chilled coupe or wine glass and grate nutmeg over the top.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake cold chai concentrate, a whole egg and a little vanilla syrup, and top with nutmeg.

recipe.note: Uses a raw egg; use a pasteurized egg if you prefer.
tips: The dry shake emulsifies the whole egg into a light, airy texture rather than a heavy one.
Grate the nutmeg fresh; its aroma is a big part of the drink.

vegan.title: Vegan Death Flip
vegan.description: The same tequila, Chartreuse and Jägermeister flip, made creamy with aquafaba and oat milk instead of a whole egg.

ingredients.item: oz aquafaba plus 1/2 oz oat milk

steps: Shake the tequila, Chartreuse, Jägermeister, syrup, aquafaba and oat milk without ice for 15 seconds.
Add ice and shake hard for 10 seconds more.
Fine strain into a small chilled coupe or wine glass and grate nutmeg over the top.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake cold chai concentrate, aquafaba, oat milk and a little vanilla syrup, and top with nutmeg.

vegan.note: Check that your spirits are vegan-friendly; most are.
tips: The dry shake whips the aquafaba into a light foam, while the oat milk adds body.
Grate the nutmeg fresh; its aroma is a big part of the drink.

recipe.title: Death in the Afternoon
recipe.description: Absinthe topped with Champagne until it clouds, Hemingway's creation.

ingredients.item: cold vegan Champagne (such as Moët & Chandon Impérial)

steps: Pour the absinthe into a coupe or flute.
Slowly add Champagne until it turns milky.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Derby
recipe.description: Bourbon, sweet vermouth, orange curaçao and lime.

ingredients.item: vegan sweet vermouth (such as Dolin Rouge)

steps: Shake everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Diamondback
recipe.description: Rye, applejack and yellow Chartreuse, strong and herbal.
steps: Stir everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Dirty Martini
recipe.description: A savory martini made with a splash of olive brine. Gin or vodka with dry vermouth, stirred ice-cold and garnished with olives.

ingredients.item: vegan dry vermouth (such as Dolin Dry)
green olive brine from the jar
green olives on a pick, to garnish

steps: Chill a martini glass in the freezer.
Add the gin or vodka, vermouth and olive brine to a mixing glass and fill it with ice.
Stir for 20 to 30 seconds, until very cold.
Strain into the chilled glass and add the olives.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Stir 3 oz non-alcoholic gin alternative with 1/2 oz olive brine over ice and strain.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Use the brine from a jar of olives you like eating. Good olives make good brine.
Want it dirtier? Add up to 1 oz of brine. Want it cleaner? Start with 1/4 oz.

recipe.title: Division Bell
recipe.description: Mezcal, Aperol, maraschino and lime.
steps: Shake everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Don's Special Daiquiri
recipe.description: Don the Beachcomber's tropical daiquiri: two rums, passion fruit and honey flash-blended with crushed ice.

ingredients.item: honey syrup (equal parts honey and hot water)
crushed ice, plus more to fill

steps: Add the rums, passion fruit syrup, lime juice, honey syrup and the cup of crushed ice to a blender.
Blend for just 3 to 5 seconds, until frothy but not slushy.
Pour into a footed glass and top up with more crushed ice.
Garnish with the passion fruit half.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Flash-blend 1 oz passion fruit syrup, 3/4 oz lime juice, 1/2 oz honey syrup and 2 oz pineapple juice with crushed ice.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: A quick flash-blend chills and froths the drink. Blend too long and it turns into a slushie.
No blender? Shake hard with crushed ice and pour everything into the glass unstrained.

recipe.title: Doro Wat
recipe.description: Ethiopian chicken stew slow-cooked in berbere and spiced butter, with hard-boiled eggs.

ingredients.item: large red onions, very finely chopped

steps: Rub the chicken with lemon juice and salt.
Cook the onions in a dry pot over low heat 20 minutes, stirring, until soft and reduced.
Add the niter kibbeh, berbere, garlic and ginger and cook 10 minutes.
Add the chicken and broth and simmer 40 minutes.
Add the eggs and simmer 10 minutes more. Serve with injera.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Dry Manhattan
recipe.description: A Manhattan made with dry vermouth instead of sweet.

ingredients.item: vegan dry vermouth (such as Dolin Dry)

steps: Stir everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Dubliner
recipe.description: Irish whiskey, sweet vermouth and Grand Marnier, stirred.

ingredients.item: vegan sweet vermouth (such as Dolin Rouge)

steps: Stir everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Pan-Fried Pork Dumplings
recipe.description: Juicy pork and cabbage dumplings with crisp, golden bottoms, served with a soy dipping sauce.

ingredients.item: soy sauce and 1 tbsp rice vinegar, for dipping

steps: Salt the cabbage, let stand 10 minutes, then squeeze out the water.
Mix the pork, cabbage, green onions, ginger, soy sauce, sesame oil and wine.
Place a teaspoon of filling on each wrapper, wet the edge, fold in half and pleat to seal.
Heat the oil in a nonstick skillet, add dumplings flat side down and fry 2 minutes until golden.
Add 1/2 cup water, cover and steam 6 to 8 minutes until the water is gone and the filling is cooked through (160°F).
Serve with the soy and vinegar dipping sauce.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Eastside
recipe.description: Gin, lime and sugar shaken with cucumber and mint.
steps: Muddle the cucumber and mint with the syrup and lime.
Add the gin, shake with ice and double-strain into a chilled coupe.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Muddle cucumber, mint, lime and syrup and top with tonic water.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Egg Fried Rice
recipe.description: The everyday Chinese fried rice: day-old rice tossed in a very hot pan with soft egg, peas, carrot and scallions. Ready in ten minutes.

ingredients.item: cold cooked jasmine rice, ideally a day old
large eggs, beaten with a pinch of salt
scallions, thinly sliced, whites and greens kept apart

steps: Break up any clumps of rice with your fingers so the grains are separate.

Heat a wok or large skillet over high heat until it just starts to smoke. Add 1 tablespoon of the oil, pour in the eggs and scramble for 30 seconds, until just set but still glossy. Slide them onto a plate.
Add the rest of the oil, then the garlic and scallion whites. Stir for 15 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the peas and carrots and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add the rice and spread it out. Let it sit for 30 seconds to toast, then toss. Repeat for 3 to 4 minutes, until every grain is hot and slightly chewy.
Add the soy sauce around the edge of the pan so it sizzles, then the sesame oil and white pepper. Toss well.
Return the egg, breaking it into pieces, add the scallion greens and toss once more. Taste for salt and serve right away.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Cold, day-old rice is drier, so it fries into separate grains. Fresh rice steams and turns mushy.
No leftover rice? Spread freshly cooked rice on a tray and refrigerate it uncovered for an hour.
Cook in two batches if your pan is small. A crowded pan can't stay hot enough to fry.
recipe.make_ahead: Keep leftovers in the fridge for up to 3 days and reheat in a hot pan with a splash of water.
variations: Yangzhou fried rice: add diced char siu and small shrimp with the peas.
Kimchi fried rice: add 1/2 cup chopped kimchi with the garlic and top with a fried egg.

vegan.title: Vegan Tofu Fried Rice
vegan.description: The everyday Chinese fried rice made with crumbled tofu instead of scrambled egg, plus peas, carrot and scallions, all tossed in a very hot pan.

ingredients.item: cold cooked jasmine rice, ideally a day old
firm tofu, patted dry and crumbled
scallions, thinly sliced, whites and greens kept apart

steps: Break up any clumps of rice with your fingers so the grains are separate.

Heat a wok or large skillet over high heat until it just starts to smoke. Add 1 tablespoon of the oil and the tofu, sprinkle with the turmeric and a pinch of salt, and stir-fry for 3 minutes, until golden. Slide it onto a plate.
Add the rest of the oil, then the garlic and scallion whites. Stir for 15 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the peas and carrots and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add the rice and spread it out. Let it sit for 30 seconds to toast, then toss. Repeat for 3 to 4 minutes, until every grain is hot and slightly chewy.
Add the soy sauce around the edge of the pan so it sizzles, then the sesame oil and white pepper. Toss well.
Return the tofu, add the scallion greens and toss once more. Taste for salt and serve right away.
vegan.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Cold, day-old rice is drier, so it fries into separate grains. Fresh rice steams and turns mushy.
The pinch of turmeric gives the tofu a golden color, and drying it well helps it brown.
Cook in two batches if your pan is small. A crowded pan can't stay hot enough to fry.
vegan.make_ahead: Keep leftovers in the fridge for up to 3 days and reheat in a hot pan with a splash of water.

recipe.title: Eggnog
recipe.description: Rich, nutmeg-spiced cooked custard with bourbon or rum.
steps: Whisk the yolks and sugar until pale.
Heat the milk, cream and nutmeg to a simmer, then slowly whisk into the yolks.
Cook gently, stirring, until it coats a spoon (160°F). Cool and stir in the vanilla and spirit.
Chill well and serve with more nutmeg.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Leave out the spirit for a family-friendly eggnog.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Eggplant Parmesan
recipe.description: Crisp breaded eggplant layered with marinara, mozzarella and Parmesan.
steps: Salt the eggplant, let stand 30 minutes and pat dry.
Dredge in flour, dip in egg and coat in breadcrumbs. Fry until golden on both sides.
Heat the oven to 375°F. Layer sauce, eggplant, mozzarella and Parmesan in a baking dish, repeating twice.
Bake 30 minutes until bubbling. Rest 10 minutes and top with basil.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Eggs Benedict
recipe.description: Poached eggs and Canadian bacon on English muffins under silky hollandaise.
steps: Blend the yolks and lemon juice, then with the blender running, slowly pour in the hot butter until thick. Season with salt and cayenne.
Warm the Canadian bacon in a skillet.
Bring water with the vinegar to a gentle simmer and poach the eggs 3 minutes.
Top each muffin half with bacon, an egg and hollandaise.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: The hollandaise yolks and the poached eggs are only lightly cooked. Use pasteurized eggs if you prefer, and always for anyone pregnant, older or with a weakened immune system.

recipe.title: Egyptian Koshari
recipe.description: Rice, lentils and pasta topped with spicy tomato sauce, chickpeas and crispy onions.
steps: Fry the onions in the oil until dark and crisp. Drain, keeping the oil.
Cook the lentils 15 minutes, add the rice, a spoon of onion oil and water to cover, and cook until both are tender.
Boil the macaroni.
Cook the garlic in a little oil, add the tomato sauce, cumin, chili and vinegar and simmer 10 minutes.
Layer rice and lentils, macaroni, chickpeas and sauce, and top with crispy onions.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: El Diablo
recipe.description: Tequila with crème de cassis, lime and ginger beer.
steps: Shake the tequila, cassis and lime with ice.
Strain into an ice-filled highball and top with ginger beer.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Blackcurrant syrup, lime and ginger beer.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: El Presidente
recipe.description: Cuban classic of white rum, blanc vermouth, orange curaçao and grenadine.

ingredients.item: vegan blanc vermouth (such as Dolin Blanc)

steps: Stir everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Elote (Mexican Street Corn)
recipe.description: Mexican street corn: ears of corn charred on the grill, slathered in mayonnaise and crema, rolled in salty cotija and finished with chile powder and lime.

ingredients.item: ancho or guajillo chile powder, plus more to serve

steps: Heat a grill or grill pan to medium-high. Brush the corn with oil and grill for 10 to 12 minutes, turning every couple of minutes, until tender and charred in spots.
Mix the mayonnaise and crema in a small bowl. Spread the cotija on a plate.
Brush each hot ear all over with the mayonnaise mixture, then roll it in the cotija, pressing so it sticks.
Sprinkle with chile powder and cilantro and serve with lime wedges for squeezing.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: No grill? Char the corn directly over a gas burner, or under a hot broiler, turning often.
Feta is a good stand-in if you can't find cotija.
variations: Esquites: cut the charred kernels off the cob and toss them with the same toppings to serve in cups.

vegetarian.title: Vegetarian Elote
vegetarian.description: Mexican street corn, charred and slathered in mayonnaise and crema, rolled in a salty cotija-style cheese made without animal rennet, with chile and lime.

ingredients.item: finely crumbled vegetarian cotija-style cheese (made with microbial rennet)
ancho or guajillo chile powder, plus more to serve

steps: Heat a grill or grill pan to medium-high. Brush the corn with oil and grill for 10 to 12 minutes, turning every couple of minutes, until tender and charred in spots.
Mix the mayonnaise and crema in a small bowl. Spread the cheese on a plate.
Brush each hot ear all over with the mayonnaise mixture, then roll it in the cheese, pressing so it sticks.
Sprinkle with chile powder and cilantro and serve with lime wedges for squeezing.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Traditional cotija is made with animal rennet. Look for one labeled vegetarian or made with microbial rennet, or use a vegetarian feta.

vegan.title: Vegan Elote
vegan.description: Mexican street corn, charred and slathered in a creamy lime-chile sauce, rolled in crumbled vegan feta.

ingredients.item: ancho or guajillo chile powder, plus more to serve

steps: Heat a grill or grill pan to medium-high. Brush the corn with oil and grill for 10 to 12 minutes, turning every couple of minutes, until tender and charred in spots.
Stir the vegan mayo and dairy-free sour cream together in a small bowl. Spread the crumbled vegan feta on a plate.
Brush each hot ear all over with the sauce, then roll it in the crumbles, pressing so they stick.
Sprinkle with chile powder and cilantro and serve with lime wedges for squeezing.
vegan.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Check labels: some vegan mayonnaise contains soy, and some vegan cheeses are made from cashews or almonds.

recipe.title: Encebollado (Ecuadorian Tuna and Yuca Soup)
recipe.description: Ecuador's beloved coastal soup: fresh tuna and tender yuca in a cumin-scented tomato broth, piled high with lime-pickled red onions. A famous hangover cure.

ingredients.item: fresh albacore or yellowfin tuna, in large pieces
yuca (cassava), fresh or frozen, peeled and cut in chunks
limes, juiced, plus wedges to serve
plantain chips (chifles), popcorn and hot sauce, to serve

steps: Make the curtido: soak the red onions in salted warm water for 5 minutes, drain, then toss with the diced tomatoes, lime juice, a pinch of salt and some cilantro. Let it sit while you cook.
Make a refrito: cook the white onion in the oil for 5 minutes, then add the chopped tomatoes, garlic, cumin and chili powder and cook 5 minutes more, until thick.
Add the water, salt and cilantro stems and bring to a boil. Add the tuna and simmer gently for 10 to 12 minutes, until just cooked. Lift it out and flake it into large chunks.
Add the yuca to the broth and simmer 25 to 30 minutes, until very tender. Remove the woody center strand from each piece, and mash a few pieces against the pot to thicken the broth.
Return the tuna, warm through and taste for salt. Serve in deep bowls, heaped with curtido, with chifles, lime wedges and hot sauce on the side.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Poaching the tuna first and returning it at the end keeps it moist instead of dry and stringy.
Frozen yuca is already peeled and cooks more evenly than fresh, and it works perfectly here.
The curtido is half the dish: the sharp, crunchy onions cut the rich broth.
recipe.make_ahead: The broth and yuca keep 3 days in the fridge; add the tuna when reheating if you can. The curtido keeps 3 days.
variations: Use swordfish or mahi-mahi if fresh tuna is hard to find.

vegetarian.title: Vegetarian Encebollado
vegetarian.description: The same cumin-tomato broth and tender yuca, with meaty hearts of palm and oyster mushrooms in place of the tuna.

ingredients.item: hearts of palm (2 cans) and oyster mushrooms, torn
yuca (cassava), fresh or frozen, peeled and cut in chunks
limes, juiced, plus wedges to serve
plantain chips (chifles), popcorn and hot sauce, to serve

steps: Make the curtido: soak the red onions in salted warm water for 5 minutes, drain, then toss with the diced tomatoes, lime juice, a pinch of salt and some cilantro. Let it sit while you cook.
Make a refrito: cook the white onion in the oil for 5 minutes, then add the chopped tomatoes, garlic, cumin and chili powder and cook 5 minutes more, until thick.
Add the water, salt and cilantro stems and bring to a boil. Add the mushrooms and simmer 5 minutes, then lift them out.
Add the yuca to the broth and simmer 25 to 30 minutes, until very tender. Remove the woody center strand from each piece, and mash a few pieces against the pot to thicken the broth.
Return the mushrooms, add the sliced hearts of palm, warm through and taste for salt. Serve in deep bowls, heaped with curtido, with chifles, lime wedges and hot sauce on the side.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Hearts of palm flake like fish and add the gentle sea-like flavor; add them at the end so they stay tender.
Frozen yuca is already peeled and cooks more evenly than fresh, and it works perfectly here.
The curtido is half the dish: the sharp, crunchy onions cut the rich broth.
vegetarian.make_ahead: The broth and yuca keep 3 days in the fridge; add the mushrooms and hearts of palm when reheating. The curtido keeps 3 days.

yuca (cassava), fresh or frozen, peeled and cut in chunks
limes, juiced, plus wedges to serve
plantain chips (chifles), popcorn and hot sauce, to serve

recipe.title: Enzoni
recipe.description: Gin and Campari shaken with muddled green grapes and lemon.
steps: Muddle the grapes with the syrup and lemon.
Add the gin and Campari, shake with ice and double-strain over ice in a rocks glass.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Espresso Martini
recipe.description: Silky, strong and lightly sweet: vodka, coffee liqueur and freshly pulled espresso, shaken hard to a thick, creamy foam.

ingredients.item: coffee liqueur (such as Kahlúa or Mr Black)

steps: Chill a coupe or martini glass with ice water.
Brew the espresso and let it cool for about 2 minutes, just until warm. Very hot coffee melts the ice too fast and makes a watery drink.
Add the vodka, espresso, coffee liqueur and syrup to a shaker and fill it to the top with ice.
Shake very hard for 15 to 20 seconds. This is what builds the foam, so put your arms into it.
Empty the chilled glass and double-strain the drink through a fine sieve into it. Wait a few seconds for the foam to settle, then float three coffee beans on top.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake 2 oz fresh espresso, 1/2 oz simple syrup and 1/2 oz cold brew concentrate very hard with ice; a splash of cream helps the foam.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Fresh espresso is what makes the foam. Its natural oils whip into a creamy head. Day-old or drip coffee gives a flat drink.
Full ice in the shaker gives the best foam. Too little ice and the drink gets too warm and too diluted.
Mr Black is drier and more coffee-forward; Kahlúa is sweeter. If you use Kahlúa, you may not need the syrup.
recipe.make_ahead: Best made to order. Cold brew concentrate makes a good batch-friendly swap: mix the drink without ice up to a day ahead, chill, then shake each one hard with ice.
variations: Salted caramel: use caramel syrup in place of simple syrup and add a pinch of salt.
Use tequila reposado instead of vodka for a richer, caramel note.
Stronger coffee flavor: replace the vodka with 3/4 oz vodka and 3/4 oz coffee liqueur.

recipe.title: Ethiopian Tibs
recipe.description: Sautéed beef cubes with onion, peppers, rosemary and spiced butter.
steps: Sear the beef in a very hot skillet with half the butter until browned. Remove.
Cook the onion, jalapeños, garlic and ginger in the remaining butter.
Return the beef with the berbere and rosemary and toss 2 to 3 minutes.
Season and serve with injera.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Fairy Belle
recipe.description: Gin, apricot brandy and grenadine with a frothy egg white.
steps: Dry-shake everything, then shake again with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: This drink uses raw egg white. Use pasteurized egg white if you prefer, and always for anyone pregnant, older or with a weakened immune system.

recipe.title: Falafel Plate
recipe.description: Crisp herb-packed chickpea falafel with tahini sauce, salad and pita.
steps: Drain the chickpeas well and pulse in a food processor with the onion, garlic, herbs, spices and salt until finely ground but not pasty.
Stir in the baking soda and shape into small balls or patties.
Fry at 350°F for 3 to 4 minutes until deep brown.
Whisk the tahini, lemon juice and water to a pourable sauce with a pinch of salt.
Serve with pita, salad, pickles and tahini sauce.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Fanciulli
recipe.description: Bourbon and sweet vermouth with a splash of Fernet-Branca.

ingredients.item: vegan sweet vermouth (such as Dolin Rouge)

steps: Stir everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Fancy Free
recipe.description: Bourbon with maraschino and bitters, stirred.
steps: Stir everything with ice.
Strain over a large cube in a rocks glass.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Fernandito
recipe.description: Argentina's Fernet-Branca and cola.
steps: Fill a highball with ice and add the Fernet.
Top with cola, tilting the glass to control the foam.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Fettuccine Alfredo
recipe.description: Fettuccine in a silky sauce of butter, cream and Parmesan.
steps: Cook the fettuccine in salted water. Save 1 cup of pasta water.
Melt the butter with the cream and simmer 3 minutes.
Off the heat, toss in the drained pasta and Parmesan, adding pasta water until silky.
Season with pepper and nutmeg and top with parsley.
recipe.note: Fresh egg fettuccine contains eggs; most dried fettuccine does not.

recipe.title: Fig Lemon Brandy Smash
recipe.description: Fresh fig and lemon bring a soft fruit texture to a brandy smash.

ingredients.item: ripe fig, stem removed and chopped

steps: Muddle chopped fig with syrup in a shaker.
Add brandy, lemon and ice, shake firmly for 15 seconds and fine-strain into a rocks glass over fresh ice.
Rest the fig half on a cocktail pick across the rim.

cocktail.garnish: fresh fig half on a pick
cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Muddle fig with syrup, shake with 3/4 oz lemon juice and 2 oz cooled black tea, then fine-strain over ice.

recipe.note: An original Relish home cocktail. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Choose a very ripe fig and fine-strain to remove most of its seeds and skin.
recipe.make_ahead: Prepare to order. Keep juices and brewed teas refrigerated until needed.

recipe.title: Fig Maple Bourbon Old Fashioned
recipe.description: Bourbon and a little maple syrup carry rich fig preserves in a gently stirred, spirit-forward drink.
steps: Stir fig preserves, maple syrup and water in a mixing glass until the preserves loosen.
Add bourbon and plenty of ice. Stir for 25 seconds, then fine-strain into a rocks glass over one large ice cube.
Squeeze orange peel over the drink to release its oils, then add it. Rest the fig half on a cocktail pick across the rim.

cocktail.garnish: fresh fig half and short orange peel
cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Stir 2 oz cooled strong black tea with 1 tsp fig preserves, 1 tsp maple syrup and 1/2 oz orange juice; fine-strain over ice.

recipe.note: An original Relish home cocktail. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Fine-straining removes most seeds while leaving the flavor of the fig.
recipe.make_ahead: Loosen preserves with maple syrup and water up to 1 day ahead; refrigerate. Stir with bourbon and ice to order.

recipe.title: Filipino Kare-Kare
recipe.description: Oxtail and vegetables in a rich peanut sauce, served with shrimp paste.

ingredients.item: annatto oil or 1 tsp annatto powder

steps: Simmer the oxtail in water for 2 1/2 to 3 hours until tender. Keep 4 cups of the broth.
Cook the onion and garlic, add the broth, peanut butter, ground rice and annatto and simmer until thick.
Add the oxtail, then the beans and eggplant, and cook until tender. Add the bok choy last.
Serve with rice and bagoong on the side.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Filipino Pancit Bihon
recipe.description: Thin rice noodles stir-fried with chicken, shrimp and vegetables, served with calamansi.
steps: Cook the garlic and onion in the oil, then the chicken until cooked through (165°F), then the shrimp.
Add the vegetables and cook 2 minutes.
Add the broth, soy sauce and oyster sauce and bring to a boil.
Add the noodles and toss until they absorb the liquid.
Serve with calamansi wedges.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Filipino Sinigang
recipe.description: Sour tamarind soup with pork and vegetables.

ingredients.item: pork spareribs or belly, in pieces

steps: Simmer the pork, onion and tomatoes in 10 cups water for 45 minutes, skimming.
Add the tamarind mix and daikon and simmer 5 minutes.
Add the beans, eggplant and chiles and cook until tender.
Add the greens and fish sauce and serve with rice.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Lohikeitto (Finnish Salmon Soup)
recipe.description: Finland's comforting salmon soup: tender chunks of salmon, potatoes, carrot and leek in a light, creamy broth, scented with allspice and lots of fresh dill.

ingredients.item: skinless salmon fillet, cut into 1-inch chunks
leek, white and light green parts, sliced
waxy potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
salt and white pepper, to taste
rye bread and butter, to serve

steps: Melt the butter in a pot and soften the leek for 5 minutes without browning.
Add the potatoes, carrots, stock, bay leaf, allspice and salt. Simmer 15 minutes, until the potatoes are just tender.
Turn the heat to low. Add the cream, salmon and most of the dill.
Cook very gently for 4 to 5 minutes, without boiling, until the salmon just turns opaque. Season with pepper and serve with the rest of the dill and rye bread.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Add the salmon at the end and keep the soup below a boil, so the fish stays tender and the cream doesn't split.
Fresh dill is essential; dried dill doesn't come close.
Use the salmon skin and trimmings to make a quick stock for extra flavor.
recipe.make_ahead: Best eaten fresh. Leftovers keep 2 days; reheat gently without boiling.
variations: Lighter: use half whole milk and half cream.

vegetarian.title: Creamy Dill Soup with Smoked Tofu
vegetarian.description: The same leek, potato and dill soup with allspice and cream, with smoked tofu in place of salmon.

ingredients.item: leek, white and light green parts, sliced
waxy potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
salt and white pepper, to taste
rye bread and butter, to serve

steps: Melt the butter in a pot and soften the leek for 5 minutes without browning.
Add the potatoes, carrots, stock, bay leaf, allspice and salt. Simmer 15 minutes, until the potatoes are just tender.
Turn the heat to low. Add the cream, smoked tofu and most of the dill.
Cook very gently for 4 to 5 minutes, without boiling, until warmed through. Season with pepper and serve with the rest of the dill and rye bread.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Keep the soup below a boil once the cream goes in so it doesn't split.
Fresh dill is essential; dried dill doesn't come close.
Smoked tofu gives the gentle smoky depth that salmon brings.
vegetarian.make_ahead: Best eaten fresh. Leftovers keep 2 days; reheat gently without boiling.

vegan.title: Vegan Creamy Dill Soup with Smoked Tofu
vegan.description: Leek, potato and smoked tofu in a dill and allspice broth made creamy with oat cream.

ingredients.item: leek, white and light green parts, sliced
waxy potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
salt and white pepper, to taste

steps: Heat the oil in a pot and soften the leek for 5 minutes without browning.
Add the potatoes, carrots, stock, bay leaf, allspice and salt. Simmer 15 minutes, until the potatoes are just tender.
Turn the heat to low. Add the oat cream, smoked tofu and most of the dill.
Cook very gently for 4 to 5 minutes, until warmed through. Season with pepper and serve with the rest of the dill and rye bread.
vegan.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Add the oat cream at the end and keep the soup at a gentle simmer.
Fresh dill is essential; dried dill doesn't come close.
Smoked tofu gives the gentle smoky depth that salmon brings.
vegan.make_ahead: Best eaten fresh. Leftovers keep 2 days; reheat gently without boiling.

recipe.title: Fish and Chips
recipe.description: Crisp beer-battered white fish with thick-cut fries, British style.

ingredients.item: russet potatoes, cut into thick fries
cod or haddock fillets, cut into 4 pieces
all-purpose flour, plus extra for dusting
malt vinegar, lemon wedges and tartar sauce, to serve

steps: Soak the cut potatoes in cold water for 15 minutes, then drain and pat very dry.
Heat oil to 325°F and fry the potatoes for 5 to 6 minutes until soft but pale. Drain.
Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt, then whisk in the cold beer until just smooth.
Raise the oil to 375°F. Pat the fish dry, dust with flour, dip in the batter and fry for 5 to 7 minutes until deep golden. Drain on a rack.
Fry the potatoes again for 2 to 3 minutes until crisp. Salt well.
Serve with malt vinegar, lemon and tartar sauce.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: British Fish Pie
recipe.description: The British family favorite: cod, smoked haddock, salmon and shrimp in a creamy parsley sauce under a thick blanket of buttery mashed potato, baked until golden.

ingredients.item: floury potatoes (such as russets), peeled and cut into chunks
salt and black pepper, to taste

steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 15 to 20 minutes, until tender. Drain well and mash with 3 tablespoons of the butter and 1/4 cup of the milk. Season with salt and pepper.

Meanwhile, put the cod, smoked haddock and salmon in a wide pan with the rest of the milk, the bay leaf and onion. Bring just to a simmer and poach gently for 5 minutes. Lift out the fish, strain the milk and keep it.

Heat the oven to 400°F. Melt the remaining 3 tablespoons butter in a saucepan, stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in the warm poaching milk and simmer, stirring, for 3 minutes, until thick and smooth.
Stir the mustard, lemon zest and parsley into the sauce and season with pepper. Taste before adding salt; smoked fish is salty.
Flake the fish into large chunks in a 2 1/2-quart baking dish and scatter over the raw shrimp and peas, if using. Pour the sauce over and stir very gently.
Spoon the mash over the top, spread it to the edges and rough up the surface with a fork.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, until the top is golden and the sauce bubbles at the edges. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Undercook the fish when poaching. It finishes cooking in the oven and stays in big, juicy flakes.
Let the sauce cool slightly before adding the mash, so the potato sits on top instead of sinking in.
recipe.make_ahead: Assemble up to a day ahead and refrigerate. Bake from cold for 40 to 45 minutes.
variations: Add halved hard-boiled eggs to the filling, the traditional way.
Stir 1/2 cup grated sharp cheddar into the mash for a cheesy top.

recipe.title: Baja Fish Tacos
recipe.description: Ensenada-style: light, crackly beer-battered fish tucked into warm corn tortillas with crunchy cabbage, lime crema and fresh pico de gallo.

ingredients.item: firm white fish (cod, halibut or mahi-mahi), cut into 4 x 1 inch strips
all-purpose flour, plus 1/4 cup for dusting
very cold Mexican lager or sparkling water
vegetable oil, for frying (about 2 inches deep)
limes, zested and juiced, plus wedges to serve
chopped cilantro, plus leaves to serve

steps: Make the crema: stir the mayonnaise, crema, lime zest, half the lime juice, the adobo and a pinch of salt. Chill until needed.
Make the pico de gallo: mix the tomatoes, onion, jalapeño, cilantro, a squeeze of lime and a pinch of salt. Toss the cabbage with the rest of the lime juice and a pinch of salt.
Pat the fish completely dry with paper towels and season with 1 tsp salt. Dry fish lets the batter stick and stay crisp.

Heat the oil in a heavy pot to 375°F. Meanwhile, whisk the flour, baking powder, garlic powder, cumin and 1/2 tsp salt. Add the cold beer and whisk just until smooth. A few small lumps are fine; overmixing makes it tough.

Dust each fish strip in the extra flour, shake off the excess, dip in the batter and let the extra drip off. Lower into the oil away from you. Fry 4 or 5 pieces at a time for 3 to 4 minutes, turning once, until deep golden and crisp.
Drain on a wire rack, not paper towels, which steam the bottom soft. Sprinkle with salt while hot. Let the oil come back to 375°F between batches.
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet 30 seconds per side until soft and spotted, then stack them in a towel. Use two tortillas per taco if they're thin.
Fill each tortilla with fish, cabbage, crema and pico de gallo. Top with cilantro and serve right away with lime wedges.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Keep the batter cold. Cold batter hitting hot oil puffs up into a lighter, crisper crust.
The flour dusting is what makes the batter cling. Skip it and the batter slides off in the oil.
Use a thermometer. Below 350°F the fish soaks up oil and turns greasy; above 400°F the outside burns before the fish cooks.
recipe.make_ahead: Make the crema, pico and cabbage up to 1 day ahead and keep them chilled. Fry the fish just before serving. Leftover fish re-crisps in a 400°F oven or air fryer for 5 minutes.
variations: Grilled: rub the fish with oil, chili powder, cumin and lime and grill 3 minutes per side instead of frying. This also skips the wheat and eggs in the batter.
Shrimp tacos: batter and fry large peeled shrimp for 2 to 3 minutes.
Add sliced avocado or pickled red onion.

recipe.title: Fitzgerald
recipe.description: A gin sour with Angostura bitters.
steps: Shake everything with ice.
Strain into a rocks glass over ice.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Five-Spice Pork with Bok Choy and Rice
recipe.description: Thin pork strips and bok choy in a glossy five-spice soy glaze over rice.

ingredients.item: baby bok choy, quartered and washed

steps: Whisk soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, cornstarch and water. Toss pork with five-spice powder.

Heat half the neutral oil in a wide skillet over high heat. Sear pork in batches until cooked through to at least 145 F (63 C), about 3 to 4 minutes per batch. Transfer to a clean plate and rest for at least 3 minutes.
Add remaining oil and bok choy to the pan. Stir-fry for 3 to 4 minutes until tender-crisp. Add sauce and simmer for 1 minute until glossy.
Return pork briefly to warm, finish with sesame oil and scallions, and serve over hot rice.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Use a plain five-spice blend and check its label. Rest the whole-cut pork before returning it to the hot sauce.
recipe.make_ahead: Refrigerate promptly in shallow containers for up to 3 days. Reheat leftovers to 165 F (74 C).

recipe.title: Flan
recipe.description: The Latin American caramel custard: a silky, vanilla-scented egg and milk custard baked in a water bath over a layer of caramel that becomes a golden sauce when you turn it out.
steps: Heat the oven to 325°F and bring a kettle of water to a boil. Set a 9-inch round cake pan or 8 1/2 x 4 1/2-inch loaf pan inside a larger roasting pan.
Make the caramel: stir the sugar and water in a small, heavy saucepan and cook over medium-high heat without stirring, swirling the pan now and then, until it turns a deep amber, 6 to 8 minutes.
Immediately pour the caramel into the cake pan and tilt to coat the bottom. It will harden; that's fine.
Whisk the condensed milk, evaporated milk, whole milk, eggs, yolks, vanilla and salt until smooth, without beating in air. Strain through a fine sieve over the caramel.
Cover the pan with foil. Pour boiling water into the roasting pan to come halfway up the sides.
Bake for 50 to 65 minutes, until the edges are set and the center jiggles slightly.
Cool in the water bath for 30 minutes, then refrigerate for at least 6 hours, or overnight.
To serve, run a thin knife around the edge, set a deep plate on top and flip quickly. Let the caramel pour over.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Watch the caramel closely. It goes from amber to burnt in seconds, and burnt caramel tastes bitter.
Straining the custard catches any bits of egg, so the flan is perfectly smooth.
recipe.make_ahead: Flan keeps covered in its pan in the fridge for up to 4 days. Unmold just before serving.
variations: Coconut flan: replace the whole milk with coconut milk and add 1/2 cup sweetened shredded coconut.

recipe.title: Floradora
recipe.description: Gin with raspberry, lime and ginger beer.
steps: Shake the gin, lime and syrup with ice.
Strain into an ice-filled highball and top with ginger beer.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Raspberry, lime and ginger beer.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Fog Cutter
recipe.description: A strong tiki drink of rum, brandy and gin with citrus and orgeat, topped with sherry.
steps: Shake everything except the sherry with ice.
Pour into a tall glass with ice and float the sherry on top.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: French 75
recipe.description: Gin, lemon and sugar shaken and topped with Champagne.

ingredients.item: vegan Champagne (such as Moët & Chandon Impérial)

steps: Shake the gin, lemon and syrup with ice.
Strain into a flute and top with Champagne.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Top lemon and syrup with sparkling grape juice or alcohol-free sparkling wine.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: French Connection
recipe.description: A smooth 1970s after-dinner sipper: cognac and nut-free amaretto stirred over ice. Warm, almond-scented and simple.
steps: Fill a rocks glass with ice, ideally one large cube.
Add the cognac and amaretto and stir for 15 seconds.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Stir cold black tea with a splash of almond (orgeat) syrup over ice.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Adjust the amaretto to taste; use less for a drier drink.
A large ice cube melts slowly, keeping the drink strong and cold.
variations: Godfather: use Scotch instead of cognac.

recipe.title: French Fries
recipe.description: Golden, crisp double-fried potatoes.

ingredients.item: peanut or vegetable oil, for frying

steps: Cut the potatoes into 1/4-inch sticks and soak in cold water for 30 minutes. Drain and dry thoroughly.
Fry at 325°F for 5 minutes until soft but pale. Drain and cool 10 minutes.
Fry again at 375°F for 3 to 4 minutes until golden and crisp.
Drain and toss with salt.
recipe.note: If you fry in peanut oil, highly refined peanut oil is usually not considered an allergen, but check with anyone who has a peanut allergy.

recipe.title: French Martini
recipe.description: Vodka, raspberry liqueur and pineapple, shaken to a frothy top.
steps: Shake everything hard with ice.
Strain into a chilled martini glass.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake pineapple juice and raspberry syrup until frothy.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: French Onion Soup
recipe.description: Deeply caramelized onions in rich beef broth, topped with a toasted baguette and melted Gruyère.
steps: Melt the butter, add the onions and a pinch of salt and cook over medium-low heat, stirring often, for 45 to 60 minutes until deep brown. Add the sugar halfway.
Add the wine and scrape the pan, then the broth, thyme and bay leaf. Simmer 20 minutes.
Ladle into ovenproof bowls, top with baguette and Gruyère.
Broil 2 to 3 minutes until bubbling and browned.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: French Toast
recipe.description: Thick slices of bread soaked in cinnamon custard and griddled until golden.
steps: Whisk the eggs, milk, sugar, cinnamon and vanilla.
Soak each slice for 20 seconds per side.
Cook in butter on a griddle over medium heat 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden.
Serve with syrup and powdered sugar.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Fuzzy Navel
recipe.description: The 1980s two-ingredient classic: peach schnapps and orange juice over ice. "Fuzzy" for the peach, "navel" for the orange.
steps: Fill a highball glass with ice.
Pour in the peach schnapps, then the orange juice.
Stir gently and garnish with the orange slice.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Build 4 oz orange juice and 2 oz peach nectar over ice.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Equal parts is the original, but it's very sweet. Two parts orange juice to one of schnapps is more balanced.
variations: Hairy Navel: add 1 oz vodka.

recipe.title: Garibaldi
recipe.description: Campari with fluffy, freshly juiced orange juice.

ingredients.item: freshly squeezed orange juice, whipped in a blender

steps: Fill a highball with ice and add the Campari.
Top with the fluffy orange juice.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Fluffy orange juice with a non-alcoholic bitter aperitivo.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Garlic Butter Shrimp
recipe.description: Juicy shrimp seared in garlic butter with lemon and parsley.
steps: Pat the shrimp dry and season with salt and pepper.
Melt 2 tbsp butter in a skillet over medium-high heat and cook the shrimp 1 to 2 minutes per side. Remove.
Add the remaining butter, garlic and pepper flakes and cook 30 seconds.
Return the shrimp with the lemon juice and parsley and toss to coat.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Garlic Shrimp with Lemony White Beans
recipe.description: Garlic shrimp, cannellini beans and cherry tomatoes simmer briefly in a bright olive-oil lemon sauce.

ingredients.item: cannellini beans (15 oz each), drained and rinsed

steps: Pat shrimp dry. Heat oil over medium heat in a wide skillet and soften garlic for 30 seconds without browning.
Add tomatoes and cook for 3 minutes. Add beans, water, lemon zest, salt and pepper; simmer for 5 minutes.
Nestle shrimp into the beans. Cover and cook for 4 to 6 minutes, turning once, until shrimp are opaque and fully cooked. Do not leave raw centers.
Stir in lemon juice and parsley. Serve immediately in shallow bowls.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Canned beans are already cooked; a short simmer warms them without breaking them apart. Add water if the pan becomes dry.
recipe.make_ahead: Refrigerate promptly and use within 2 days. Reheat gently to 165 F (74 C); shrimp may firm up as they reheat.

recipe.title: General Tso's Chicken
recipe.description: The Chinese-American takeout favorite: crisp fried chicken in a sticky, sweet, sour and gently spicy sauce with garlic, ginger and dried red chilies.

ingredients.item: boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
vegetable or canola oil, for frying

steps: Toss the chicken with 1 tablespoon soy sauce, the Shaoxing wine and egg white. Let it sit for 15 minutes.
Whisk the broth, 2 tablespoons soy sauce, dark soy sauce, rice vinegar, hoisin, sugar and 1 tablespoon cornstarch in a bowl.
Toss the chicken in the 3/4 cup cornstarch, pressing to coat.
Heat 2 inches of oil in a wok or heavy pot to 350°F. Fry the chicken in batches for 4 to 5 minutes, until golden and cooked through (165°F). Drain on a rack.
Pour off all but 1 tablespoon of oil. Over medium heat, add the dried chilies and fry for 10 seconds, then add the garlic and ginger and stir for 20 seconds.
Stir the sauce, pour it in and cook, stirring, until thick and glossy, about 1 minute.
Add the chicken and sesame oil and toss to coat. Top with the scallions and sesame seeds and serve with rice.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Fry the chilies only until they darken slightly. Burnt chilies turn bitter.
For extra-crisp chicken, fry it a second time at 375°F for 1 minute before tossing it in the sauce.
variations: Add steamed broccoli florets with the chicken.

recipe.title: Adjarian Khachapuri
recipe.description: Boat-shaped Georgian bread filled with molten cheese, topped with an egg and butter.
steps: Heat the oven to 475°F.
Divide the dough into 4 ovals. Roll the long sides in toward the middle and twist the ends to make boats.
Fill the centers with the mixed cheeses.
Bake 12 to 15 minutes until golden.
Drop an egg yolk and a pat of butter into each and bake 1 to 2 minutes more. Stir together at the table and tear off the crust to dip.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: The yolks stay runny. Use pasteurized eggs if you prefer, and always for anyone pregnant, older or with a weakened immune system.

recipe.title: Georgian Khinkali
recipe.description: Large twisted soup dumplings filled with spiced beef and pork in juice.

ingredients.item: salt and plenty of black pepper

steps: Knead the flour, warm water and salt into a firm dough. Rest 30 minutes.
Mix the meats, onion, herbs, spices and salt, then work in the cold water until loose.
Roll the dough and cut 4-inch circles. Add filling and gather the edge into many pleats, twisting the top into a knot.
Boil in salted water 10 to 12 minutes, until the filling is cooked through (160°F).
Dust with pepper. Bite a hole, sip the juice, and leave the knot.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Ghanaian Red Red
recipe.description: Black-eyed peas stewed in red palm oil and tomato, served with fried plantains.
steps: Heat the palm oil and cook the onion, garlic, ginger and pepper until soft.
Add the tomatoes and simmer 15 minutes.
Add the black-eyed peas and 1/2 cup water and simmer 15 minutes, mashing a few. Season.
Fry the plantains until caramelized and serve alongside.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Gimlet
recipe.description: Gin, fresh lime juice and simple syrup, shaken crisp.
steps: Shake everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake lime juice, syrup and a few cucumber slices and top with tonic water.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Gin and Tonic
recipe.description: Gin topped with tonic water over plenty of ice.
steps: Fill a highball or balloon glass with ice.
Add the gin and top with tonic.
Squeeze in the lime and stir gently.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Use a non-alcoholic gin alternative or just tonic with lime and cucumber.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Gin Basil Smash
recipe.description: Gin muddled with fresh basil, lemon and sugar.
steps: Muddle the basil with the lemon and syrup in a shaker.
Add the gin and ice and shake hard.
Double-strain into a rocks glass over ice.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Muddle basil, lemon and syrup and top with tonic water.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Gin Fizz
recipe.description: The original fizz: gin, lemon and a little sugar shaken hard, then lifted with a splash of soda. Served short and without ice, so it's crisp and bright from the first sip.
steps: Chill a small tumbler or fizz glass in the freezer.
Add the gin, lemon juice and simple syrup to a shaker, fill it with ice and shake hard for 15 seconds.
Strain into the chilled glass with no ice.
Top with the soda water and garnish with the lemon slice.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake 1 oz lemon juice and 3/4 oz simple syrup with ice, strain, and top with 3 oz soda water.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Shake longer than you think: the extra air and dilution give a fizz its light, almost frothy texture.
Keep the soda in the fridge. Cold soda holds its bubbles; warm soda goes flat on contact.
Too sharp? Add another teaspoon of syrup. Lemons vary a lot.
variations: Silver Fizz: add 1 egg white and dry-shake without ice first for a silky foam.
Sloe Gin Fizz: use sloe gin in place of London dry gin.

recipe.title: Gin-Gin Mule
recipe.description: Gin with mint, lime and ginger beer.
steps: Muddle the mint with the syrup and lime.
Add the gin, shake with ice and strain into an ice-filled highball. Top with ginger beer.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Muddle mint with lime and syrup and top with ginger beer.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Gin Rickey
recipe.description: The dry, unsweetened cooler from 1880s Washington: gin and fresh lime over ice, topped with soda.
steps: Fill a highball glass with ice.
Pour in the gin and lime juice.
Top with the soda water and stir gently.
Drop the squeezed lime shell into the glass.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Build 1 oz lime juice and 1/2 oz simple syrup over ice and top with 5 oz soda water.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: A Rickey has no sugar. That's what makes it different from a Collins.
variations: Joe Rickey: use bourbon in place of the gin, as the original did.

recipe.title: Ginger Beef and Bell Pepper Stir-Fry
recipe.description: Sliced beef and bell peppers in a ginger soy sauce, served over rice.

ingredients.item: flank steak, thinly sliced across the grain

steps: Stir soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, cornstarch and water together. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wide skillet; sear beef in batches until browned and cooked to preference. Transfer to a plate.
Add remaining oil and peppers; stir-fry 3–4 minutes. Add ginger and garlic for 30 seconds.
Return beef and any juices to the pan. Add sauce and simmer, stirring, until thickened and hot. Serve over rice.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Ginger-Lime Chicken Lettuce Cups
recipe.description: Ground chicken with ginger, lime and crisp vegetables spooned into butter lettuce leaves.

ingredients.item: large butter lettuce leaves, washed and dried

steps: Heat neutral oil in a wide skillet over medium-high heat. Cook chicken for 6 to 8 minutes, breaking it up, until fully cooked to 165 F (74 C).
Add ginger and garlic for 1 minute. Stir in soy sauce, maple syrup and sesame oil and cook for 1 minute more.
Take off the heat and stir in lime juice.
Spoon into lettuce leaves and top with carrot, cucumber and scallions; serve two filled leaves per person.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Butter lettuce is not dairy. Keep washed leaves dry so the cups remain crisp.
recipe.make_ahead: Refrigerate chicken and vegetables separately for up to 3 days. Reheat chicken to 165 F (74 C) before filling fresh lettuce leaves.

recipe.title: Ginger-Soy Glazed Tofu and Broccoli
recipe.description: Golden pan-browned tofu and crisp-tender broccoli in a glossy ginger-soy glaze, served over rice.
steps: Pat tofu dry. Brown in 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet, 8–10 minutes; transfer to a plate. Cook broccoli in remaining oil with a splash of water until crisp-tender, 5–6 minutes.
Mix soy sauce, maple syrup, vinegar, ginger, cornstarch and water. Return tofu to the skillet and add sauce; simmer 1–2 minutes until glossy.
Finish with sesame oil and serve over cooked rice.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Gochujang Beef Lettuce Wraps
recipe.description: Sweet, spicy gochujang beef with ginger and garlic, spooned into butter lettuce cups with cool cucumber and scallions.
steps: Brown beef in a skillet, breaking it up, until cooked through (160°F); drain excess fat. Add garlic and ginger and cook 30 seconds.
Stir in gochujang, soy sauce, sugar and sesame oil; cook 2 minutes until coated.
Spoon into washed lettuce leaves and top with cucumber and scallions.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Godfather
recipe.description: Scotch and amaretto over ice.
steps: Stir with ice.
Strain over a large cube in a rocks glass.
recipe.note: Amaretto is flavored with almonds or apricot kernels.

recipe.title: Gold Mine
recipe.description: Bourbon with honey, lemon and ginger, a golden sour.
steps: Shake everything with ice.
Strain over a large cube in a rocks glass.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Lemon, honey and ginger syrups topped with ginger beer.

recipe.note: Recipes for this drink vary between bars; this is one common version.

recipe.title: Gold Rush
recipe.description: Bourbon, lemon and honey syrup.

ingredients.item: honey syrup (equal parts honey and hot water)

steps: Shake everything with ice.
Strain into a rocks glass over a large cube.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake lemon and honey syrup with cold black tea.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Golden Cadillac
recipe.description: Galliano and white crème de cacao shaken with cream.
steps: Shake everything hard with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Golden Dream
recipe.description: Galliano and orange liqueur shaken with orange juice and cream.
steps: Shake everything hard with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
