recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Hungarian Goulash
recipe.description: Hearty Hungarian beef and paprika stew with peppers and potatoes.
steps: Brown the beef in the fat in batches. Remove.
Cook the onions slowly until golden, then off the heat stir in the paprika and caraway.
Add the garlic, tomato paste, beef and broth and simmer 1 1/2 hours.
Add the peppers and potatoes and simmer 30 minutes until tender. Season.
Serve with a dollop of sour cream if you like.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Grand Margarita
recipe.description: The top-shelf margarita: 100% agave tequila and Grand Marnier with lime, shaken and served on the rocks in a salt-rimmed glass.

ingredients.item: flaky sea salt, for the rim

steps: Run the lime wedge around the outer rim of a rocks glass and dip it in sea salt.
Fill the glass with ice.
Add the tequila, Grand Marnier and lime juice to a shaker with ice and shake hard for 10 seconds.
Strain into the glass and garnish with the lime slice.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake 1 oz lime juice, 1 oz orange juice and 1/2 oz agave syrup with ice and strain into a salt-rimmed glass of ice.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Salt only the outside of the rim, so the salt doesn't fall into the drink.
Grand Marnier is made with cognac, which makes this richer and rounder than a triple sec margarita.
variations: Use reposado tequila for a warmer, oakier drink.

recipe.title: Grape Basil Vodka Spritz
recipe.description: Red grape juice, basil and lemon make a sparkling vodka drink with a ruby-purple color.
steps: Gently press basil leaves with grape juice in a shaker. Add vodka, lemon juice and ice, then shake briefly.
Strain into an ice-filled balloon glass. Top with soda and stir gently.
Thread the three grapes on a cocktail pick. Add the pick and basil sprig.

cocktail.garnish: three red grapes on a pick and small basil sprig
cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Press basil with 3 oz red grape juice, add 1/2 oz lemon juice and ice, strain over fresh ice and top with 3 oz soda water.

recipe.note: An original Relish home cocktail. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Unsweetened grape juice provides enough sweetness; added syrup is not needed.
recipe.make_ahead: Chill grape juice and soda ahead. Add basil only when making the drink.

recipe.title: Grapefruit Cardamom Rum Highball
recipe.description: White rum, fresh grapefruit and a subtle cardamom syrup make a fragrant highball.
steps: Shake rum, grapefruit juice, lime juice and cardamom syrup with ice for 12 seconds.
Strain into an ice-filled highball glass and top with soda.
Stir gently and add the grapefruit half-wheel.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake 3 oz grapefruit juice, 1/2 oz lime juice and 1/4 oz cardamom syrup with ice; strain and top with 2 oz soda.

recipe.note: An original Relish home cocktail. Please drink responsibly.
tips: For syrup, warm 1/2 cup simple syrup with 3 cracked cardamom pods, cover off heat for 15 minutes, strain and cool. Preparation time assumes cooled syrup is ready.
recipe.make_ahead: Prepare to order. Keep juices and brewed teas refrigerated until needed.

recipe.title: Grapefruit Ginger Rye Sour
recipe.description: Rye whiskey, grapefruit, lemon and ginger syrup make a dry-spiced citrus sour.
steps: Shake rye, grapefruit juice, lemon and ginger syrup with ice for 15 seconds.
Double-strain into a chilled coupe.
Express grapefruit peel over the glass and add it.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake 2 oz cooled black tea, 1 1/2 oz grapefruit juice, 1/2 oz lemon juice and 1/2 oz ginger syrup with ice; strain into a coupe.

recipe.note: An original Relish home cocktail. Please drink responsibly.
recipe.make_ahead: Prepare to order. Keep juices and brewed teas refrigerated until needed.

recipe.title: Grapefruit Rosemary Gin Spritz
recipe.description: Gin with fresh grapefruit and rosemary syrup, lengthened with soda in a wine glass.
steps: Shake gin, grapefruit juice and syrup with ice.
Strain into an ice-filled wine glass, top with soda and garnish with rosemary.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: replace gin with alcohol-free gin alternative.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Rosemary syrup: simmer equal parts sugar and water with a rosemary sprig; cool, strain and refrigerate.

recipe.title: Grapefruit Thyme Tequila Cooler
recipe.description: Tequila with grapefruit, lime and thyme, topped with soda.
steps: Gently press thyme with syrup.
Shake with tequila, grapefruit, lime and ice; strain into a tall glass over ice.
Top with soda and garnish with thyme.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Press the thyme with syrup, shake with grapefruit and lime, strain over ice and top with extra soda.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Grasshopper
recipe.description: Mint-green and creamy, with crème de menthe and crème de cacao.
steps: Shake everything hard with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe and grate chocolate on top.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake cream, mint syrup and chocolate syrup.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Greek Salad
recipe.description: Tomatoes, cucumber, peppers, onion and olives with a slab of feta and oregano.
steps: Combine the tomatoes, cucumber, pepper, onion and olives in a bowl.
Season with salt and dress with the oil and vinegar.
Top with the feta and sprinkle with oregano.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Green Pea Spinach Risotto
recipe.description: Soft arborio rice, green peas and spinach finished with butter and vegetarian hard cheese.
steps: Keep broth hot in a small pan. Heat oil in a saucepan over medium heat and soften onion for 5 minutes.
Add rice and stir for 1 minute. Add hot broth a ladle at a time, stirring often and letting most absorb before adding more. Cook for 18 to 22 minutes, until tender with a slight bite.
Add peas with the last ladle of broth and cook for 3 minutes. Stir in spinach to wilt, then butter and cheese.
Season with pepper and salt to taste. Add a little hot water if needed so the risotto flows rather than standing in a mound.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Choose a hard cheese labeled vegetarian; traditional Parmesan uses animal rennet. Broth salt levels vary, so season at the end.
recipe.make_ahead: Refrigerate promptly in shallow containers for up to 3 days. Reheat leftovers to 165 F (74 C).

recipe.title: Greenpoint
recipe.description: Rye, sweet vermouth and yellow Chartreuse with two bitters.

ingredients.item: vegan sweet vermouth (such as Dolin Rouge)

steps: Stir everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Greyhound
recipe.description: Vodka and fresh grapefruit juice over ice. Tart, simple and very refreshing; add a salt rim and it becomes a Salty Dog.
steps: Fill a highball glass with ice.
Pour in the vodka and grapefruit juice.
Stir gently and garnish with the grapefruit wedge.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Build 4 oz grapefruit juice over ice and top with 2 oz tonic water.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Pink grapefruit is a little sweeter and gives the drink a pretty color.
variations: Use gin instead of vodka for a more herbal drink.

recipe.title: Grilled Cheese and Tomato Soup
recipe.description: Golden, buttery grilled cheese sandwiches, perfect with a bowl of tomato soup.
steps: Butter one side of each slice of bread.
Place two slices butter side down in a skillet over medium-low heat and top with the cheeses and the other slices, butter side up.
Cook 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden and melted.
Cut in half and serve with the soup.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Grilled Salmon with Asparagus
recipe.description: Lemon-garlic salmon fillets grilled with tender asparagus.
steps: Heat the grill to medium-high and oil the grates.
Mix the oil, garlic, lemon zest, salt and pepper. Brush over the salmon and asparagus.
Grill the salmon skin side down for 6 to 8 minutes, flip and cook 2 to 3 minutes more until it flakes.
Grill the asparagus for 5 to 6 minutes, turning, until tender and lightly charred.
Drizzle with lemon juice and scatter with herbs.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Guacamole and Chips
recipe.description: Chunky fresh avocado dip with lime, onion, jalapeño and cilantro, served with tortilla chips.
steps: Halve the avocados, remove the pits and scoop into a bowl.
Mash with a fork, leaving some chunks, and stir in the lime juice and salt.
Fold in the onion, jalapeño, tomato and cilantro. Taste and adjust.
Serve right away with tortilla chips.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Guava Ginger Vodka Collins
recipe.description: Guava nectar, ginger and lemon give a vodka Collins a soft pink color and warm finish.
steps: Shake vodka, guava nectar, lemon and ginger syrup with ice for 12 seconds.
Strain into an ice-filled Collins glass and top with soda.
Stir gently and garnish with the lemon wheel.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake 3 oz guava nectar, 1/2 oz lemon juice and 1/4 oz ginger syrup with ice; strain and add 3 oz soda water.

recipe.note: An original Relish home cocktail. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Guava nectar is sweet; keep the syrup small and adjust only after tasting.
recipe.make_ahead: Prepare to order. Keep juices and brewed teas refrigerated until needed.

recipe.title: Guava Lime Rum Cooler
recipe.description: Pink guava nectar, white rum and fresh lime make a softly tropical highball, lifted with soda.
steps: Shake rum, guava nectar and lime juice with ice for 12 seconds.
Strain into an ice-filled highball glass. Top with soda and stir gently.
Add the lime wheel and serve immediately.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Stir 3 oz guava nectar and 3/4 oz lime juice over ice; top with 3 oz soda water.

recipe.note: An original Relish home cocktail. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Guava nectar is already sweetened; taste before adding any extra sweetener.
recipe.make_ahead: Chill the nectar and soda in advance. Mix the finished cooler to order.

recipe.title: Chicken and Sausage Gumbo
recipe.description: Rich, dark-roux Cajun stew with chicken, andouille and the holy trinity, served over rice.

ingredients.item: gluten-free andouille sausage (such as Aidells Cajun Style), sliced
cooked white rice and filé powder

steps: Whisk the oil and flour in a heavy pot over medium heat, stirring constantly for 30 to 40 minutes until the roux is the color of dark chocolate.
Add the onion, pepper and celery and cook 5 minutes, then the garlic.
Slowly whisk in the stock, then add the chicken, sausage, seasoning and bay leaves.
Simmer 1 hour, skimming fat. Shred the chicken back into the pot.
Stir in the green onions and serve over rice with a pinch of filé.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Haitian Griot
recipe.description: Haiti's celebration pork: shoulder marinated in citrus and epis, braised until tender, then fried until crisp and caramelized. Served with fiery pikliz and fried plantains.

ingredients.item: sour orange juice, or half orange and half lime juice
epis (blend of parsley, green onion, peppers, garlic, thyme and oil)
pikliz, fried plantains and rice, to serve

steps: Rinse the pork with the lime juice and water, then toss it with the sour orange juice, epis, onion, garlic, thyme, cloves, salt and pepper. Marinate at least 2 hours, or overnight in the fridge.
Put the pork and marinade in a heavy pot with the whole Scotch bonnet and enough water to come halfway up. Simmer, covered, for 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes, until tender.
Uncover and boil off most of the liquid, then drain the pork and pat it dry. Remove the chili.
Heat 1 inch of oil to 350°F. Fry the pork in batches for 4 to 6 minutes, until deep golden and crisp at the edges.
Drain and serve hot with pikliz, fried plantains and rice, with a squeeze of sour orange on top.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Braising first, then frying, gives griot its tender center and crackly edges.
Dry the pork well before frying; wet meat spatters and won't crisp.
Keep the Scotch bonnet whole for flavor with gentle heat; slit it if you like it fiery.
recipe.make_ahead: Marinate and braise up to 2 days ahead, then fry just before serving.
variations: Air fryer: toss the braised pork with a little oil and air-fry at 400°F for 12 to 15 minutes, shaking twice.

vegetarian.title: Vegetarian Griot
vegetarian.description: Big oyster mushrooms and tofu soaked in the same sour orange and epis marinade, then fried until crisp, with pikliz and plantains.

ingredients.item: oyster or king oyster mushrooms, torn into large pieces
extra-firm tofu, pressed and cut in 1 1/2-inch cubes
sour orange juice, or half orange and half lime juice
epis (blend of parsley, green onion, peppers, garlic, thyme and oil)
pikliz, fried plantains and rice, to serve

steps: Toss the mushrooms and tofu with the sour orange juice, epis, garlic, chili, thyme, salt and pepper. Marinate 30 minutes to 2 hours.
Lift the pieces from the marinade, pat them dry and toss with the cornstarch.
Heat 1 inch of oil to 350°F and fry in batches for 4 to 5 minutes, until deep golden and crisp.
Drain and serve hot with pikliz, plantains and rice, with a squeeze of sour orange on top.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: A light coat of cornstarch gives the crackly crust that braised pork gets naturally.
vegetarian.make_ahead: Marinate up to a day ahead; fry just before serving.

vegan.title: Vegan Griot
vegan.description: Big oyster mushrooms and tofu soaked in the same sour orange and epis marinade, then fried until crisp, with pikliz and plantains.

ingredients.item: oyster or king oyster mushrooms, torn into large pieces
extra-firm tofu, pressed and cut in 1 1/2-inch cubes
sour orange juice, or half orange and half lime juice
epis (blend of parsley, green onion, peppers, garlic, thyme and oil)
pikliz, fried plantains and rice, to serve

steps: Toss the mushrooms and tofu with the sour orange juice, epis, garlic, chili, thyme, salt and pepper. Marinate 30 minutes to 2 hours.
Lift the pieces from the marinade, pat them dry and toss with the cornstarch.
Heat 1 inch of oil to 350°F and fry in batches for 4 to 5 minutes, until deep golden and crisp.
Drain and serve hot with pikliz, plantains and rice, with a squeeze of sour orange on top.
vegan.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: A light coat of cornstarch gives the crackly crust that braised pork gets naturally.
vegan.make_ahead: Marinate up to a day ahead; fry just before serving.

recipe.title: Hanky Panky
recipe.description: Gin and sweet vermouth with a touch of Fernet-Branca.

ingredients.item: vegan sweet vermouth (such as Dolin Rouge)

steps: Stir everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Harissa Chickpea and Sweet Potato Bowls
recipe.description: Sweet potatoes and chickpeas roasted with smoky harissa, served over couscous or rice with a lemony yogurt-tahini drizzle.
steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Toss sweet potatoes and chickpeas with oil, harissa and salt. Roast 25–30 minutes, turning once, until potatoes are tender.
Mix yogurt, tahini, lemon juice and water into a pourable sauce.
Serve the roasted mixture over cooked rice or couscous and drizzle with sauce. Couscous contains wheat; use rice for a wheat-free version.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Harissa-Roasted Vegetable Freekeh Bowls
recipe.description: Roasted cauliflower, carrots and chickpeas over freekeh with lemon tahini sauce.

ingredients.item: carrots, cut into thick diagonal slices

steps: Simmer freekeh in its water for 25 to 35 minutes, or its package time, until chewy and tender. Drain excess water.
Meanwhile heat oven to 425 F (220 C). Toss cauliflower, carrots and chickpeas with oil, harissa and salt. Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, turning once, until tender.
Whisk tahini, lemon juice and sauce water until smooth.
Divide freekeh among bowls, add roasted vegetables and chickpeas, and finish with tahini sauce and parsley.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Freekeh is roasted green wheat, not a gluten-free grain. Check harissa labels for added allergens.
recipe.make_ahead: Refrigerate promptly in shallow containers for up to 3 days. Reheat leftovers to 165 F (74 C).

recipe.title: Harissa Salmon with Cucumber Yogurt
recipe.description: Harissa-glazed salmon over rice with cool cucumber yogurt.
steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Mix harissa, oil and half the salt; brush over salmon on a lined baking tray.
Bake 12–15 minutes until salmon reaches 145°F.
Mix yogurt, cucumber, lemon juice and remaining salt. Serve salmon over hot rice with cucumber yogurt.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Harvey Wallbanger
recipe.description: The 1970s disco-era favorite: a vodka and fresh orange juice highball with a float of golden, vanilla-anise Galliano on top.
steps: Fill a highball glass with ice and add the vodka and orange juice. Stir.
Slowly pour the Galliano over the back of a bar spoon so it floats on top.
Garnish with an orange slice and cherry.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Top orange juice with a splash of vanilla syrup over ice.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Fresh-squeezed orange juice makes a huge difference here.
Float the Galliano last so the first sips are fragrant with vanilla.
variations: Freddy Fudpucker: use tequila instead of vodka.

recipe.title: Hemingway Daiquiri
recipe.description: A dry daiquiri with grapefruit and maraschino liqueur.
steps: Shake everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake grapefruit, lime and a little cherry syrup with ice.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Hibiscus Citrus Rum Punch
recipe.description: Aged rum with tart hibiscus tea, orange and lime. Deep ruby and refreshing.
steps: Shake all ingredients with ice and strain into a tall glass over fresh ice.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: omit rum and add 1 1/2 oz chilled hibiscus tea.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Hibiscus Grapefruit Vodka Sour
recipe.description: Ruby hibiscus tea and grapefruit make a tart vodka sour with a floral edge.
steps: Combine vodka, cooled hibiscus tea, grapefruit juice, lime and syrup in a shaker.
Shake with ice for 15 seconds and double-strain into a chilled coupe.
Express the grapefruit twist over the glass and add it.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake 2 oz cooled hibiscus tea, 1 1/2 oz grapefruit juice, 1/2 oz lime juice and 1/2 oz syrup with ice; strain into a coupe.

recipe.note: An original Relish home cocktail. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Brew tea from a plain food-grade hibiscus infusion and cool fully before mixing.
recipe.make_ahead: Prepare to order. Keep juices and brewed teas refrigerated until needed.

recipe.title: Honey Mustard Chicken with Roasted Carrots
recipe.description: Roasted chicken thighs brushed with honey mustard and served with tender carrots.

ingredients.item: carrots, peeled and cut into 2-inch pieces

steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Toss carrots with oil, half the salt and pepper; spread on a rimmed baking sheet.
Mix mustard, honey, garlic, thyme and remaining salt. Pat chicken dry, put skin-side up among carrots and brush with the mixture.
Roast 35–45 minutes, turning carrots halfway, until carrots are tender and chicken reaches 165°F. Rest chicken 5 minutes before serving.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Honeydew Basil Vodka Cooler
recipe.description: Pale green honeydew, basil and lime make a light vodka cooler.
steps: Muddle honeydew and basil with syrup until juicy.
Add vodka, lime and ice, shake for 15 seconds and fine-strain into an ice-filled highball.
Top with soda and add the basil sprig.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Muddle honeydew and basil with syrup; shake with 3/4 oz lime juice and ice, strain and top with 4 oz soda.

recipe.note: An original Relish home cocktail. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Choose sweet ripe honeydew; firm unripe melon makes a weak-flavored drink.
recipe.make_ahead: Prepare to order. Keep juices and brewed teas refrigerated until needed.

recipe.title: Horse's Neck
recipe.description: Brandy and ginger ale with a long spiral of lemon peel.
steps: Hang a long lemon spiral in a highball and fill with ice.
Add the brandy and bitters and top with ginger ale.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Ginger ale with a long lemon-peel spiral and no bitters (the original Horse's Neck).

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Hot Buttered Rum
recipe.description: Rum in hot water with a spiced brown-sugar butter.
steps: Mash the butter, sugar and spices together.
Put the spiced butter in a mug, add the rum and pour in the boiling water. Stir until melted.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Leave out the rum and use hot apple cider instead of water.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Hot Toddy
recipe.description: The classic winter warmer: whiskey, honey and lemon stirred into hot water, with a cinnamon stick and a clove-studded lemon slice.

ingredients.item: lemon slice, studded with 3 whole cloves

steps: Warm a heatproof mug by filling it with hot water, then pour that water out.
Add the honey and lemon juice to the mug.
Pour in the hot water and stir until the honey dissolves.
Stir in the whiskey, then add the clove-studded lemon slice and cinnamon stick.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Stir 1/2 oz honey and 1/2 oz lemon juice into 6 oz hot ginger or black tea.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Add the whiskey last, after the water, so it doesn't lose its aroma to the heat.
Swap the water for hot black or chamomile tea for a deeper flavor.
variations: Use brandy or dark rum in place of the whiskey.

recipe.title: Hotel Georgia
recipe.description: A 1940s classic from Vancouver's Hotel Georgia: gin, almond orgeat and lemon, shaken with egg white and perfumed with orange flower water.
steps: Shake the gin, orgeat, lemon juice, egg white and orange flower water without ice for 15 seconds.
Add ice and shake hard again.
Fine strain into a chilled coupe and grate a little nutmeg over the foam.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake orgeat, lemon, aquafaba and a drop of orange flower water with ice, strain and top with a splash of club soda.

recipe.note: Uses raw egg white; use pasteurized egg white if you prefer.
tips: Orange flower water is very strong; measure in dashes, not spoons.
Good orgeat makes the drink. Look for one made with real almonds.

vegan.title: Vegan Hotel Georgia
vegan.description: The same gin, orgeat and orange blossom sour, with aquafaba foam instead of egg white.

ingredients.item: aquafaba (liquid from a can of chickpeas)

steps: Shake the gin, orgeat, lemon juice, aquafaba and orange flower water without ice for 15 seconds.
Add ice and shake hard again.
Fine strain into a chilled coupe and grate a little nutmeg over the foam.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake orgeat, lemon, aquafaba and a drop of orange flower water with ice, strain and top with a splash of club soda.

vegan.note: Aquafaba foams like aquafaba (liquid from a can of chickpeas); give it a long, hard dry shake.
tips: Orange flower water is very strong; measure in dashes, not spoons.
Good orgeat makes the drink. Look for one made with real almonds.

recipe.title: Hotel Nacional
recipe.description: Havana classic of rum, apricot brandy, pineapple and lime.
steps: Shake everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Huevos Rancheros
recipe.description: Fried eggs on crisp corn tortillas with ranchero salsa, beans and fresh cheese.

ingredients.item: ranchero sauce or warm tomato salsa

steps: Fry the tortillas in oil until lightly crisp. Drain.
Fry the eggs to your liking.
Spread each tortilla with beans, top with an egg and spoon over the sauce.
Finish with queso fresco, avocado and cilantro.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Eggs fried with runny yolks aren't fully cooked. For anyone pregnant, older or with a weakened immune system, fry them until firm or use pasteurized eggs.

recipe.title: Hugo Spritz
recipe.description: Elderflower and mint with prosecco and soda.
steps: Gently press the mint in a wine glass and fill with ice.
Add the elderflower and prosecco, top with soda and squeeze in the lime.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Elderflower syrup, mint and lime topped with sparkling white grape juice.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Hummus
recipe.description: Silky, whipped chickpea and tahini dip with lemon and garlic, finished with olive oil. Cooking dried chickpeas until very soft is the secret to its smoothness.

ingredients.item: extra-virgin olive oil, paprika and chopped parsley, to serve

steps: The night before, cover the chickpeas with plenty of cold water, stir in 1/2 teaspoon of the baking soda, and soak overnight.
Drain and rinse the chickpeas, put them in a pot with the rest of the baking soda and cover them by 3 inches with fresh water.
Bring to a boil, skim off any foam and skins, then simmer for 45 to 60 minutes, until the chickpeas are very soft and fall apart when pressed. Drain well.
Blend the lemon juice, garlic and salt in a food processor and let it sit for 5 minutes to mellow the garlic.
Add the tahini and blend until thick, then pour in the ice water little by little with the machine running, until the mixture turns pale and smooth.
Add the warm chickpeas and the cumin, if using, and blend for 3 to 4 minutes, scraping down the sides, until completely smooth. Add more ice water if it's too thick.
Taste for salt and lemon. Spread in a shallow bowl, swirl a groove with the back of a spoon, and fill it with olive oil. Sprinkle with paprika and parsley and serve with warm pita.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Overcooking the chickpeas is the goal: soft chickpeas blend smooth, while firm ones stay grainy.
Ice water makes the tahini fluffy and lightens its color.
Good tahini matters most. It should taste nutty and pour easily, not bitter or stiff.
recipe.make_ahead: Keep it covered in the fridge for up to 5 days. Bring it to room temperature and stir in a spoonful of water before serving.
variations: Quick version: simmer 2 cans of drained chickpeas with 1/2 teaspoon baking soda for 20 minutes, then rinse and blend.
Hummus with meat: top with spiced ground lamb and toasted pine nuts.

recipe.title: Hurricane
recipe.description: New Orleans rum punch with passion fruit, citrus and grenadine.
steps: Shake everything with ice.
Strain into a hurricane glass filled with ice.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Passion fruit, orange and lime juice with grenadine, topped with lemon-lime soda.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: IBA Tiki
recipe.description: A modern Cuban tiki drink: two rums, amaretto and hazelnut liqueur with passion fruit, pineapple, lime and fresh ginger over pebble ice.

ingredients.item: aged rum (such as Havana Club Profundo)
smoky aged rum (such as Havana Club Smoky)
citrus wheels and a dried pineapple slice, to garnish

steps: Fill a tiki mug or tall glass with pebble ice.
Muddle the ginger slice in the bottom of a shaker.
Add all the remaining ingredients, fill with ice and shake hard for 15 seconds.
Strain into the mug and garnish with the citrus wheels and dried pineapple.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake 1 oz passion fruit purée, 3 oz pineapple juice, 1 oz lime juice, 1/2 oz simple syrup and a ginger slice with ice.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Frangelico is made from hazelnuts. Use 1 tsp more amaretto in its place for a nut-free drink.
Any good aged rum works. A dash of smoky mezcal can stand in for the smoky rum.

recipe.title: Illegal
recipe.description: A smoky mezcal sour with funky overproof Jamaican rum, falernum and a dash of maraschino. Strong, tropical and layered.
steps: Chill a coupe or cocktail glass.
Add everything to a shaker and fill it with ice.
Shake hard for 15 seconds.
Strain into the chilled glass, or over fresh ice in a clay cup.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake 1 oz lime juice, 1/2 oz falernum syrup and 1 oz pineapple juice with ice, strain, and add 2 drops of liquid smoke if you like.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: The small splash of egg white is only for texture. Leave it out and the drink is just as good.
Overproof rum is very strong. Measure it carefully.
This drink uses raw egg white. Use pasteurized egg white if you prefer, and always for anyone pregnant, older or with a weakened immune system.

vegan.title: Vegan Illegal
vegan.description: The same smoky mezcal sour, with aquafaba in place of the egg white.
steps: Chill a coupe or cocktail glass.
Add everything to a shaker and fill it with ice.
Shake hard for 15 seconds.
Strain into the chilled glass, or over fresh ice in a clay cup.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake 1 oz lime juice, 1/2 oz falernum syrup and 1 oz pineapple juice with ice, strain, and add 2 drops of liquid smoke if you like.

vegan.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: The small splash of aquafaba is only for texture. Leave it out and the drink is just as good.
Overproof rum is very strong. Measure it carefully.
Aquafaba foams like egg white and is safe to use raw.

recipe.title: Imam Bayildi (Turkish Stuffed Eggplant)
recipe.description: A classic Turkish olive oil dish: whole eggplants fried until silky, split and stuffed with sweet onions, tomatoes, peppers and garlic, then baked until meltingly soft. Best at room temperature.

ingredients.item: salt, plus more for the eggplants
green peppers (Turkish sivri or Anaheim), chopped
ripe tomatoes, grated or finely chopped

steps: Peel the eggplants in lengthwise stripes, leaving stripes of skin on. Soak them in salted water for 20 minutes, then pat very dry.
Fry the eggplants whole in 1/3 cup oil, turning, for 10 to 12 minutes, until golden and soft. Lay them in a baking dish.

In the same pan, cook the onions in the rest of the oil for 10 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and peppers for 3 minutes, then the tomatoes, tomato paste, sugar and salt. Cook 5 minutes, then stir in the parsley.
Split each eggplant down the middle without cutting through, and gently open it into a pocket. Fill generously with the onion mixture.
Mix the hot water and lemon juice and pour around the eggplants. Cover with foil and bake at 350°F for 40 minutes, until very tender.
Cool to room temperature before serving, drizzled with the pan juices.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Don't skimp on the olive oil. This is a zeytinyağlı dish: the oil carries all the flavor.
Imam bayildi tastes best the next day, served at room temperature.
Striping the skin helps the eggplant hold its shape while letting it soften evenly.
recipe.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge. Bring to room temperature before serving.
variations: Lighter: roast the oiled eggplants at 425°F for 30 minutes instead of frying.
Karnıyarık: add browned ground beef to the filling for the meaty version.

recipe.title: Improved Whiskey Cocktail
recipe.description: Rye with maraschino, absinthe and bitters, a 19th-century classic.
steps: Stir everything with ice.
Strain into a rocks glass over a large cube.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Income Tax
recipe.description: A Bronx cocktail with bitters: gin, both vermouths and orange juice.

ingredients.item: vegan sweet vermouth (such as Dolin Rouge)
vegan dry vermouth (such as Dolin Dry)

steps: Shake everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Aloo Gobi
recipe.description: Potatoes and cauliflower cooked with turmeric, cumin and ginger.
steps: Fry the cumin seeds in oil, add the onion and cook until soft, then the ginger and chile.
Add the tomato and spices for 2 minutes.
Add the potatoes and cauliflower with salt, cover and cook on low 15 to 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until tender.
Sprinkle with garam masala and cilantro.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Baingan Bharta
recipe.description: Smoky fire-roasted eggplant mashed with onion, tomato and spices.
steps: Roast the eggplants over a flame or under the broiler, turning, until charred and collapsed. Peel and mash.
Fry the cumin seeds in oil, add the onion until golden, then the ginger-garlic and chile.
Add the tomatoes and spices and cook until soft.
Stir in the eggplant and cook 5 minutes. Season and top with cilantro.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Idli Sambar
recipe.description: Soft steamed rice cakes with tangy lentil and vegetable stew.

ingredients.item: idli batter (fermented rice and urad dal)

steps: Grease the idli molds, fill with batter and steam 10 to 12 minutes until set.
Cook the toor dal until soft and mash.
Cook the vegetables, onion and tomato in water until tender, then add the tamarind, sambar powder, dal and salt and simmer 10 minutes.
Fry the mustard seeds and curry leaves in oil and pour over the sambar.
Serve the idli with the sambar and coconut chutney.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Check the sambar powder label if you avoid wheat: many contain asafoetida (hing) blended with wheat flour.

recipe.title: Pav Bhaji
recipe.description: Mumbai street food: buttery mashed spiced vegetables with toasted soft rolls.

ingredients.item: butter, plus more for the rolls
lemon wedges, chopped onion and cilantro

steps: Mash the potatoes, cauliflower and peas.
Cook the onion and pepper in butter, add the ginger-garlic paste, tomatoes and masala and cook until soft.
Add the mashed vegetables and 1 cup water and mash everything together. Simmer 10 minutes.
Split the rolls and toast in butter.
Serve the bhaji topped with butter, onion and cilantro, with lemon and the rolls.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Rajma Chawal
recipe.description: Punjabi kidney bean curry in a thick onion-tomato gravy, served with rice.

ingredients.item: each coriander, cumin and chile powder

steps: Fry the cumin seeds, then cook the onion until browned and add the ginger-garlic paste.
Add the tomatoes and spices and cook until the oil separates.
Add the beans and 2 cups water and simmer 25 minutes, mashing a few beans.
Stir in the garam masala and cilantro and serve over rice.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Indonesian Beef Rendang
recipe.description: Dry, deeply spiced beef curry slow-cooked in coconut milk until caramelized.
steps: Blend the shallots, garlic, ginger, galangal, chiles, 1 lemongrass and turmeric into a paste.
Fry the paste in oil 5 minutes, add the beef and coat.
Add the coconut milk, remaining lemongrass and lime leaves and simmer uncovered 2 1/2 to 3 hours, stirring more often as it thickens.
Stir in the kerisik and sugar and cook until the sauce is dark and clings to the beef. Season with salt.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Indonesian Gado-Gado
recipe.description: Vegetable salad with tofu, egg and potatoes under a sweet-spicy peanut dressing.

ingredients.item: wheat-free prawn crackers (check the label; optional)

steps: Blend the peanuts, garlic, chiles, kecap manis, lime juice and about 1 cup water into a thick sauce. Season with salt.
Arrange the vegetables, tofu and eggs on a platter.
Pour the peanut sauce over and serve with prawn crackers.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Kecap manis is usually brewed with wheat. Use a gluten-free sweet soy sauce if you avoid wheat.

recipe.title: Irish Coffee
recipe.description: Hot coffee with Irish whiskey and brown sugar under lightly whipped cream.
steps: Warm a glass mug with hot water, then empty it.
Stir the sugar into the coffee, then add the whiskey.
Float the cream on top over the back of a spoon.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Leave out the whiskey; add a drop of vanilla.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Irish Maid
recipe.description: Irish whiskey with elderflower liqueur, lemon and cucumber.
steps: Muddle the cucumber in a shaker.
Add the rest, shake with ice and strain over ice in a rocks glass.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Iskender Kebab
recipe.description: Turkish thin-sliced lamb over pide bread with tomato sauce, yogurt and browned butter.

ingredients.item: lamb or beef, very thinly sliced (or doner meat)

steps: Sear the meat in the oil until browned.
Simmer the tomato sauce with the pepper paste and a pinch of salt.
Toast the bread cubes and lay them on plates. Spoon some tomato sauce over.
Top with the meat and the rest of the sauce, with yogurt on the side.
Brown the butter with the paprika and pour over at the table.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Italian Arancini
recipe.description: Crisp fried risotto balls with a molten mozzarella center.

ingredients.item: oil for frying and marinara for dipping

steps: Mix the risotto with the Parmesan and 1 egg.
Shape into balls around a cube of mozzarella.
Roll in flour, dip in the remaining beaten eggs and coat in breadcrumbs.
Fry at 350°F for 4 to 5 minutes until golden. Serve with marinara.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Jabberwock
recipe.description: Gin, dry sherry and Lillet with orange bitters.

ingredients.item: vegan manzanilla sherry (such as La Gitana)

steps: Stir everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Jack Rose
recipe.description: Applejack, lemon and grenadine.
steps: Shake everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Apple cider with lemon and grenadine.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Ackee and Saltfish
recipe.description: Jamaica's national breakfast of salt cod sautéed with ackee, peppers and onions.
steps: Soak the salt cod overnight, changing the water, then boil 15 minutes and flake.
Cook the onion, peppers, tomatoes, green onions and thyme in the oil for 5 minutes.
Add the fish and toss.
Fold in the ackee gently and heat through. Season with pepper.
recipe.note: Use only canned or properly ripened ackee; unripe ackee is poisonous.

recipe.title: Jambalaya
recipe.description: Louisiana one-pot rice with andouille sausage, chicken and shrimp in a spicy Creole base.

ingredients.item: gluten-free andouille sausage (such as Aidells Cajun Style), sliced

steps: Brown the sausage and chicken in a heavy pot. Remove.
Cook the onion, pepper and celery until soft, then add the garlic.
Add the tomatoes, rice, broth, Creole seasoning, bay leaves, sausage and chicken. Bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer 20 to 25 minutes, until the rice is tender and the chicken reaches 165°F.
Stir in the shrimp, cover and cook 5 minutes until pink. Top with green onions.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Japanese Cocktail
recipe.description: Cognac with orgeat and bitters, a 19th-century classic.
steps: Stir everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Japanese Chicken Curry
recipe.description: Japan's favorite comfort food: chicken, potato and carrot simmered in a thick, mild, slightly sweet curry gravy made with a homemade roux. Served over rice.

ingredients.item: boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into bite-size pieces
Yukon Gold potatoes, cut into large chunks
hot cooked Japanese short-grain rice, to serve
pickled red ginger or fukujinzuke, to serve (optional)

steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onions with a pinch of salt and cook, stirring often, for 15 minutes, until soft and golden brown.
Add the ginger, garlic and chicken and cook for 3 minutes, until the chicken is no longer pink outside.
Add the carrots, potatoes, broth and grated apple. Bring to a boil, skim off any foam, then cover and simmer for 20 minutes, until the potatoes are tender and the chicken reaches 165°F.

Meanwhile, make the roux: melt the butter in a small pan over medium-low heat, stir in the flour and cook, stirring, for 8 to 10 minutes, until it smells nutty and turns light brown. Stir in the curry powder and garam masala and cook for 30 seconds more, then turn off the heat.
Ladle about 1 cup of the hot broth into the roux and whisk until smooth, then stir it back into the pot.
Add the soy sauce and ketchup and simmer gently, stirring, for 5 minutes, until the curry is thick and glossy. Taste for salt.
Serve over the rice, with pickles on the side if you like.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Browning the onions slowly gives the curry its deep, sweet flavor. Don't rush it.
Stir the curry often once the roux is in. The thick sauce can stick and scorch.
recipe.make_ahead: The curry tastes even better the next day. Refrigerate for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 2 months; the potatoes soften a little after freezing.
variations: Katsu curry: serve the curry with a crispy breaded pork or chicken cutlet.
For a spicier curry, add 1/2 to 1 tsp cayenne pepper with the curry powder.

recipe.title: Japanese Oyakodon
recipe.description: Chicken and onion simmered in sweet dashi and soy, set with egg over rice.
steps: Simmer the dashi, soy sauce, mirin and sugar with the onion for 3 minutes.
Add the chicken and cook 5 minutes, until cooked through (165°F).
Pour the eggs over, cover and cook 1 minute until softly set.
Slide over bowls of rice and top with herbs.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: The egg is served softly set. For anyone pregnant, older or with a weakened immune system, cook it until firm or use pasteurized eggs.

recipe.title: Cold Soba Noodles
recipe.description: Chilled buckwheat noodles with a savory dipping sauce, green onions and wasabi.
steps: Simmer the dashi, soy sauce and mirin for 1 minute, then chill.
Cook the soba as the package directs, rinse well in cold water and drain.
Top the noodles with nori.
Dip the noodles in the sauce mixed with green onions and wasabi.
recipe.note: Most soba contains wheat flour as well as buckwheat.
variations: Tenzaru soba: serve with shrimp and vegetable tempura on the side.

recipe.title: Japanese Unagi Don
recipe.description: Grilled eel glazed in sweet tare sauce over rice.
steps: Simmer the soy sauce, mirin, sugar and sake until syrupy to make the tare.
Brush the eel with tare and broil 3 to 4 minutes until bubbling.
Spoon a little tare over the rice, add the eel and drizzle with more.
Sprinkle with sansho pepper.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Japchae
recipe.description: Korean sweet potato glass noodles stir-fried with beef and vegetables in sesame-soy sauce.
steps: Cook the noodles 6 minutes, rinse and cut a few times with scissors.
Mix the soy sauce, sugar, sesame oil and garlic. Marinate the beef in 2 tbsp of it.
Stir-fry the vegetables one at a time until just tender, then the beef.
Toss everything with the noodles and the rest of the sauce. Sprinkle with sesame seeds.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Jasmine
recipe.description: Gin, Campari, orange liqueur and lemon. Tastes like grapefruit juice.
steps: Shake everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: John Collins
recipe.description: A tall, sparkling gin lemonade built right in the glass: London dry gin, lemon, sugar and soda over plenty of ice.
steps: Fill a highball glass with ice.
Pour in the gin, lemon juice and simple syrup.
Add the soda water and stir gently once or twice, just to mix.
Garnish with the lemon slice and cherry.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Build 1 oz lemon juice and 3/4 oz simple syrup over ice and top with 4 oz soda water.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Stir gently, just once or twice, after the soda goes in. Heavy stirring knocks out the fizz.
A John Collins uses London dry gin; a Tom Collins traditionally uses the sweeter Old Tom gin.
recipe.make_ahead: Mix a pitcher of gin, lemon and syrup up to 4 hours ahead and keep it cold. Pour over ice and top each glass with soda.
variations: Whiskey Collins: swap bourbon for the gin.
Juan Collins: swap blanco tequila for the gin.

recipe.title: Jollof Rice
recipe.description: West African rice cooked in a smoky, spiced tomato and pepper sauce.
steps: Blend the tomatoes, peppers, scotch bonnet and 1 onion until smooth.
Cook the other onion, sliced, in the oil, then fry the tomato paste 3 minutes.
Add the blended sauce, spices and bay leaves and cook 15 minutes until reduced.
Stir in the rice and stock, season, cover tightly and cook on low 30 minutes until tender.
Let the bottom toast slightly for a smoky flavor, then fluff and serve.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Serve it the classic way, with fried ripe plantain and grilled or fried chicken.

recipe.title: Jungle Bird
recipe.description: Dark rum, Campari, pineapple and lime, a bittersweet tiki drink.
steps: Shake everything with ice.
Strain into a rocks glass over ice.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Pineapple, lime and a non-alcoholic bitter aperitivo.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Chicken Kabsa
recipe.description: Saudi Arabia's national dish: chicken and basmati rice cooked together in a tomato broth scented with cardamom, cinnamon, cloves and dried lime, topped with toasted almonds and raisins.

ingredients.item: dried limes (loomi), pierced with a knife
basmati rice, rinsed and soaked for 20 minutes

steps: Heat the oil in a large, wide pot over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken on both sides in batches, about 8 minutes, and set it aside.
Add the onions to the pot and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, until golden. Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the tomato paste, tomatoes, carrot, dried limes, cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, bay leaves, spice mix and salt and cook for 2 minutes.
Return the chicken, add the water and bring to a boil. Cover and simmer for 30 minutes, until the chicken is tender.
Lift out the chicken. If you like, brown it under a hot broiler for 5 minutes while the rice cooks.
Drain the rice and stir it into the broth. Bring back to a boil, then cover tightly and cook over very low heat for 20 minutes, until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Rest for 5 minutes, then fluff the rice onto a large platter, set the chicken on top and scatter with almonds, raisins and parsley.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Dried limes give kabsa its tangy, slightly smoky flavor. Find them at Middle Eastern grocers; a strip of lime zest and a squeeze of juice is a rough stand-in.
Measure the broth after the chicken comes out: you want about 4 cups for the rice. Add water or boil it down as needed.
Nut allergy? Leave off the almonds; the dish is just as good.
recipe.make_ahead: Refrigerate leftovers for up to 3 days and reheat covered with a splash of water.
variations: Lamb kabsa: use 3 lb bone-in lamb shoulder pieces and simmer for 1 1/2 hours before adding the rice.

recipe.title: Kahlua and Cream
recipe.description: Coffee liqueur over ice with cream.
steps: Fill a rocks glass with ice and add the Kahlúa.
Pour the cream over and stir if you like.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Cold brew with coffee syrup and cream over ice.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Kamikaze
recipe.description: Equal parts vodka, triple sec and fresh lime, shaken hard. Like a vodka margarita, served up or as shots.
steps: Chill a cocktail glass, or two shot glasses.
Add the vodka, triple sec and lime juice to a shaker and fill it with ice.
Shake hard for 10 seconds.
Strain into the glass and garnish with the lime wedge.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake 1 oz lime juice, 1 oz orange juice and 1/2 oz simple syrup with ice and strain.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Fresh lime makes all the difference. Bottled lime juice makes it taste harsh.
variations: Blue Kamikaze: use blue curaçao instead of triple sec.

recipe.title: Katsudon
recipe.description: Japan's comforting rice bowl: a crisp panko pork cutlet simmered briefly with sweet onions in dashi, soy and mirin, then softly set with egg and served over steamed rice.

ingredients.item: boneless pork loin chops (about 5 oz each), 1/2 inch thick
salt and a pinch of pepper

steps: Make a few small cuts in the fat around each chop so it stays flat. Season, then coat in flour, beaten egg and panko.
Fry in 1/2 inch of oil at 340°F for 3 to 4 minutes a side, until golden and cooked through. Drain on a rack and slice into strips.
In a small frying pan, simmer the dashi, soy sauce, mirin and sugar with the onion for 3 to 4 minutes, until the onion is soft.
Lay one sliced cutlet on the onions. Pour half the beaten eggs around and over it, cover and cook 1 minute, until the egg is just barely set.
Slide it over a bowl of rice and top with green onion. Repeat for the second bowl.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Beat the eggs only lightly so you can still see streaks of white and yolk. That marbled look is the classic finish.
Pour the egg around the cutlet, not all over it, so part of the crust stays crisp.
Leftover tonkatsu is perfect here; the sauce brings it back to life.
The egg is served softly set. For anyone pregnant, older or with a weakened immune system, cook it until firm or use pasteurized eggs.
recipe.make_ahead: Fry the cutlets up to a day ahead and reheat in the oven. Cook the egg topping just before serving.
variations: Oyakodon: use sliced chicken thigh simmered in the sauce instead of the pork cutlet.

vegetarian.title: Tofu Katsudon
vegetarian.description: A crisp panko tofu cutlet simmered with onions in kombu dashi, soy and mirin, softly set with egg over rice.

ingredients.item: slabs of extra-firm tofu (about 5 oz each), pressed, 3/4 inch thick
salt and a pinch of pepper

steps: Pat the tofu very dry. Season, then coat in flour, beaten egg and panko.
Fry in 1/2 inch of oil at 350°F for 2 to 3 minutes a side, until golden and crisp. Drain on a rack and slice into strips.
In a small frying pan, simmer the kombu kombu dashi or mushroom broth, soy sauce, mirin and sugar with the onion for 3 to 4 minutes, until the onion is soft.
Lay one sliced cutlet on the onions. Pour half the beaten eggs around and over it, cover and cook 1 minute, until the egg is just barely set.
Slide it over a bowl of rice and top with green onion. Repeat for the second bowl.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Beat the eggs only lightly so you can still see streaks of white and yolk. That marbled look is the classic finish.
Pour the egg around the cutlet, not all over it, so part of the crust stays crisp.
Press the tofu for 20 minutes so the coating stays crisp.
The egg is served softly set. For anyone pregnant, older or with a weakened immune system, cook it until firm or use pasteurized eggs.
vegetarian.make_ahead: Fry the tofu cutlets up to a day ahead and reheat in the oven. Cook the egg topping just before serving.

vegan.title: Vegan Tofu Katsudon
vegan.description: A crisp tofu cutlet in sweet-savory kombu dashi with onions, topped with a soft-set silken tofu "egg" over rice.

ingredients.item: slabs of extra-firm tofu (about 5 oz each), pressed, 3/4 inch thick
salt and a pinch of pepper
silken tofu, blended with 1 tbsp cornstarch, a pinch of turmeric and a pinch of salt

steps: Pat the firm tofu very dry and season it. Whisk 1/4 cup flour with the water into a smooth batter. Coat the tofu in plain flour, then batter, then panko.
Fry in 1/2 inch of oil at 350°F for 2 to 3 minutes a side, until golden and crisp. Drain and slice into strips.
In a small frying pan, simmer the kombu dashi, soy sauce, mirin and sugar with the onion for 3 to 4 minutes, until the onion is soft.
Lay one sliced cutlet on the onions. Spoon half the silken tofu mixture around it, cover and cook 2 to 3 minutes, until softly set.
Slide it over a bowl of rice and top with green onion. Repeat for the second bowl.
vegan.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: The silken tofu, cornstarch and turmeric mixture sets softly like egg in the hot sauce.
Press the firm tofu for 20 minutes so the coating stays crisp.
vegan.make_ahead: Fry the tofu cutlets up to a day ahead and reheat in the oven.

recipe.title: Kentucky Mule
recipe.description: Bourbon, lime and ginger beer in a copper mug.
steps: Fill a copper mug with ice.
Add the bourbon and lime and top with ginger beer.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Ginger beer with lime.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Kimchi Jjigae (Kimchi Stew)
recipe.description: Korea's favorite everyday stew: sour, well-aged kimchi simmered with pork belly and tofu in a spicy, savory broth. Served bubbling hot with rice.

ingredients.item: pork belly, sliced 1/4 inch thick into bite-size pieces
anchovy-kelp stock or low-sodium chicken broth
firm or medium tofu, sliced 1/2 inch thick

steps: Put a heavy pot over medium heat and add the pork belly. Cook, stirring, for 4 to 5 minutes, until the fat renders and the edges brown.
Add the kimchi, onion and garlic and cook for 5 minutes, until the kimchi softens and smells toasty.
Stir in the gochugaru, gochujang, sugar and soy sauce, then add the kimchi juice and stock.
Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 15 minutes.
Lay the tofu on top, add the scallions and simmer for 5 minutes more, until the tofu is hot through.
Taste for salt, drizzle with sesame oil and serve hot with rice.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: The older and more sour the kimchi, the better the stew. Fresh kimchi tastes flat here; add 1 teaspoon rice vinegar if yours is young.
Most kimchi is made with fish sauce or salted shrimp. Check the jar if anyone has a fish or shellfish allergy.
recipe.make_ahead: The stew tastes even better reheated the next day. Keep it in the fridge for up to 3 days.
variations: Use canned tuna or Spam in place of the pork belly.

recipe.title: Kir
recipe.description: The classic Burgundy aperitif: crisp, dry white wine blushed pink with a splash of blackcurrant liqueur (crème de cassis).

ingredients.item: vegan dry white wine (such as Bonterra Sauvignon Blanc), well chilled

steps: Pour the crème de cassis into a chilled white wine glass.
Top with the cold wine; it mixes as you pour.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Add a splash of blackcurrant syrup to chilled sparkling white grape juice or non-alcoholic white wine.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Keep the cassis light; the drink should be pale pink, not purple.
Both the wine and glass should be very cold.
variations: Kir Royale: use Champagne instead of white wine, served in a flute.
Kir Pétillant: use any dry sparkling wine.

recipe.title: Kir Royale
recipe.description: Champagne with a splash of crème de cassis.

ingredients.item: vegan Champagne (such as Moët & Chandon Impérial)

steps: Pour the cassis into a flute.
Top slowly with Champagne.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Blackcurrant syrup topped with alcohol-free sparkling wine.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Kiwi Cucumber Tequila Cooler
recipe.description: Kiwi and cucumber bring a fresh green edge to a light tequila-lime highball.

ingredients.item: cucumber ribbon and kiwi half-slice, for garnish

steps: Gently muddle the chopped kiwi and cucumber slices with agave syrup in a shaker.
Add tequila, lime juice and ice. Shake for 12 seconds and strain into an ice-filled highball glass.
Top with soda, stir gently and garnish with the cucumber ribbon and kiwi half-slice.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Muddle kiwi and cucumber with 1/2 oz agave syrup, shake with 3/4 oz lime juice and ice, then strain and top with 4 oz soda water.

recipe.note: An original Relish home cocktail. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Use ripe kiwi for sweetness. A fine sieve removes most seeds if you prefer a smoother drink.
recipe.make_ahead: Prepare to order; kiwi and cucumber lose their fresh flavor after standing.

recipe.title: Kiwi Mint Rum Fizz
recipe.description: Kiwi and gently pressed mint make a fresh green rum fizz with lime.
steps: Muddle kiwi gently with mint and syrup in a shaker.
Add rum, lime and ice. Shake for 15 seconds and strain into an ice-filled highball.
Top with soda and garnish with the mint sprig and kiwi half-slice.

cocktail.garnish: small mint sprig and kiwi half-slice
cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Muddle kiwi and mint with syrup, shake with 3/4 oz lime juice and ice, strain and top with 4 oz soda.

recipe.note: An original Relish home cocktail. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Use a fine sieve if you prefer fewer kiwi seeds, and press mint lightly rather than pulverizing it.
recipe.make_ahead: Prepare to order. Keep juices and brewed teas refrigerated until needed.

recipe.title: Knickerbocker
recipe.description: Rum with orange curaçao, lime and raspberry over crushed ice.
steps: Shake everything with ice.
Strain over crushed ice in a rocks glass.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Korean Fried Chicken (Yangnyeom)
recipe.description: Twice-fried chicken with a thin, shatteringly crisp potato-starch crust, tossed in a sticky, sweet and spicy gochujang glaze.

ingredients.item: chicken wings and drumettes, or boneless thighs cut into 2-inch pieces
vegetable or canola oil, for frying
rice syrup or light corn syrup

steps: Pat the chicken dry and toss it with the salt, pepper and ginger.
Whisk the potato starch, flour, baking powder and ice water into a thin batter. Add the chicken and turn to coat.
Heat 2 inches of oil in a heavy pot to 325°F. Fry the chicken in batches for 8 to 10 minutes, until cooked through (165°F) and pale gold. Drain on a rack for 5 minutes.
Heat the oil to 375°F and fry the chicken again for 2 to 3 minutes, until deep golden and very crisp. Drain.

Meanwhile, make the glaze: warm 1 teaspoon of oil in a wide pan over medium heat and fry the garlic for 30 seconds. Add the gochujang, ketchup, syrup, soy sauce, brown sugar and vinegar and simmer for 2 minutes, until glossy and bubbling.
Turn off the heat, add the hot chicken and toss quickly to coat.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and scallions and serve right away.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: The second, hotter fry drives out moisture, so the crust stays crisp even under the sauce.
Potato starch makes the crust thin and light. Cornstarch works too, but flour alone turns heavy.
Toss the chicken in the glaze just before serving. If it sits, the crust softens.
recipe.make_ahead: Make the glaze up to 3 days ahead and keep it in the fridge.
variations: Soy garlic chicken: glaze with 1/4 cup soy sauce, 3 tbsp honey, 2 tbsp rice syrup and 4 cloves garlic instead.
Serve with cubes of pickled radish (chicken-mu) on the side.

recipe.title: Korean Sundubu Jjigae
recipe.description: Bubbling spicy soft tofu stew with seafood and an egg.
steps: Cook the pork in the oil, then add the gochugaru and garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the broth and soy sauce and bring to a boil.
Add the seafood and spoon in big pieces of tofu. Simmer 5 minutes.
Crack in the egg, add green onions and cook 1 minute. Serve bubbling with rice.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: The egg cooks only briefly in the stew. For anyone pregnant, older or with a weakened immune system, simmer until the egg is firm or use a pasteurized egg.

recipe.title: Korean Tteokbokki
recipe.description: Chewy rice cakes simmered in a sweet and spicy gochujang sauce with fish cakes.
steps: Soak the rice cakes in warm water if they are hard.
Bring the broth to a boil and stir in the gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce and sugar.
Add the rice cakes and simmer 8 to 10 minutes, stirring, until soft and the sauce thickens.
Add the fish cakes, green onions and eggs and cook 3 minutes more.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Kung Pao Chicken
recipe.description: Sichuan stir-fry of chicken, peanuts and dried chiles in a glossy, tingly, sweet-sour sauce.
steps: Toss the chicken with 1 tbsp soy sauce and 2 tsp cornstarch.
Stir together the 2 tbsp soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, 1 tsp cornstarch and 3 tbsp water.
Heat the oil in a wok, fry the chiles and peppercorns for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir-fry 4 to 5 minutes until cooked through (165°F). Add the garlic, ginger and green onions for 1 minute.
Pour in the sauce, toss until glossy and stir in the peanuts. Serve with rice.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: La Louisiane
recipe.description: Rye, sweet vermouth and Bénédictine with absinthe and Peychaud's.

ingredients.item: vegan sweet vermouth (such as Dolin Rouge)

steps: Stir everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: La Perla
recipe.description: Tequila, manzanilla sherry and pear liqueur.

ingredients.item: vegan manzanilla sherry (such as La Gitana)

steps: Stir everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Curry Laksa
recipe.description: Malaysian noodle soup in a spicy coconut curry broth with shrimp, tofu puffs and sprouts.

ingredients.item: cilantro, mint, lime wedges and sliced chiles

steps: Fry the laksa paste in the oil for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the stock and coconut milk and simmer 10 minutes. Season with fish sauce and sugar.
Add the shrimp and tofu puffs and cook 2 to 3 minutes.
Divide the noodles and sprouts among bowls and ladle the broth over.
Top with herbs, chiles and lime.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
variations: Top each bowl with a halved hard-boiled egg, the way many Malaysian stalls do.

recipe.title: Lamb Shish Kebab
recipe.description: Turkish grilled lamb skewers: chunks of leg of lamb marinated in onion juice, yogurt and red pepper paste, grilled with peppers and onion.

ingredients.item: boneless leg of lamb, cut into 1 1/2-inch cubes
Turkish red pepper paste (biber salçası) or tomato paste
Aleppo pepper or 1/2 tsp red pepper flakes
green bell peppers, cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
warm flatbread, sliced tomatoes and sumac onions, to serve

steps: Grate the large onion into a sieve set over a bowl and press hard to collect the juice. Discard the pulp.
Stir the yogurt, olive oil, pepper paste, garlic, Aleppo pepper, cumin, salt and black pepper into the onion juice. Add the lamb, toss well, cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or overnight.
Thread the lamb onto skewers, alternating with pieces of pepper and red onion.
Heat a grill to high. Grill the skewers for 10 to 12 minutes, turning every few minutes, until charred outside and still pink inside (135°F for medium-rare).
Rest for 5 minutes, then serve with flatbread, tomatoes and sliced onions sprinkled with sumac.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Only the onion juice goes into the marinade. Bits of onion would burn on the grill.
Leave a little space between pieces on the skewer so the heat can reach every side.
USDA's safe minimum for lamb is 145°F with a 3-minute rest. 135°F is the usual medium-rare.
variations: Chicken shish: use boneless chicken thighs and grill to 165°F.

recipe.title: Lamb Tagine
recipe.description: Moroccan lamb slow-cooked with warm spices, apricots and honey, finished with almonds.
steps: Brown the lamb in the oil. Remove.
Cook the onion, garlic and ginger, then the spices for 1 minute.
Return the lamb with the broth, cover and simmer 1 1/2 hours.
Add the apricots and honey and cook 30 minutes until the lamb is tender.
Top with almonds and serve with couscous.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Larb (Thai Minced Pork Salad)
recipe.description: The bright, punchy salad of northeastern Thailand and Laos: minced pork dressed with lime, fish sauce and chili, tossed with fresh herbs and nutty toasted rice powder.

ingredients.item: uncooked sticky or jasmine rice, for toasted rice powder
sticky rice, lettuce cups, cucumber and long beans, to serve

steps: Toast the rice in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring constantly, for 10 to 15 minutes, until deep golden and smelling like popcorn. Cool and grind to a coarse powder.
Cook the pork with the water in a pan over medium heat, breaking it up, for 5 to 7 minutes, just until cooked through (160°F). Don't brown it; it should stay moist.
Take the pan off the heat. Stir in the fish sauce, lime juice, sugar and chili flakes. Taste: it should be sour, salty and spicy all at once.
Add the shallots, green onions, most of the herbs and 2 tbsp of the toasted rice powder and toss.
Pile onto a plate, sprinkle with the rest of the herbs and rice powder, and serve with sticky rice and crisp vegetables to scoop it up.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Cooking the pork gently in a little water keeps it tender and juicy; larb isn't meant to be browned and crispy.
Season off the heat so the lime stays bright and fresh.
Toasted rice powder is essential: it adds a nutty crunch and soaks up the juices.
recipe.make_ahead: The toasted rice powder keeps 2 months in a sealed jar. Larb is best eaten right after mixing.
variations: Larb gai: make it with ground chicken instead of pork.

vegetarian.title: Vegetarian Larb
vegetarian.description: Crumbled tofu and mushrooms dressed with lime, soy sauce and chili, with fresh herbs and toasted rice powder.

ingredients.item: extra-firm tofu and mushrooms, finely chopped (about 1 lb total)
uncooked sticky or jasmine rice, for toasted rice powder
sticky rice, lettuce cups, cucumber and long beans, to serve

steps: Toast the rice in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring constantly, for 10 to 15 minutes, until deep golden and smelling like popcorn. Cool and grind to a coarse powder.
Cook the tofu and mushrooms in a lightly oiled pan over medium-high heat for 6 to 8 minutes, until the mushrooms have released their liquid and the tofu is lightly golden.
Take the pan off the heat. Stir in the soy sauce, lime juice, sugar and chili flakes. Taste: it should be sour, salty and spicy all at once.
Add the shallots, green onions, most of the herbs and 2 tbsp of the toasted rice powder and toss.
Pile onto a plate, sprinkle with the rest of the herbs and rice powder, and serve with sticky rice and crisp vegetables to scoop it up.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Crumble the tofu small so it holds the dressing like minced meat.
Season off the heat so the lime stays bright and fresh.
Toasted rice powder is essential: it adds a nutty crunch and soaks up the juices.
vegetarian.make_ahead: The toasted rice powder keeps 2 months in a sealed jar. Larb is best eaten right after mixing.

vegan.description: Crumbled tofu and mushrooms dressed with lime, soy sauce and chili, with fresh herbs and toasted rice powder.

ingredients.item: extra-firm tofu and mushrooms, finely chopped (about 1 lb total)
uncooked sticky or jasmine rice, for toasted rice powder
sticky rice, lettuce cups, cucumber and long beans, to serve

steps: Toast the rice in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring constantly, for 10 to 15 minutes, until deep golden and smelling like popcorn. Cool and grind to a coarse powder.
Cook the tofu and mushrooms in a lightly oiled pan over medium-high heat for 6 to 8 minutes, until the mushrooms have released their liquid and the tofu is lightly golden.

tips: Crumble the tofu small so it holds the dressing like minced meat.

Toasted rice powder is essential: it adds a nutty crunch and soaks up the juices.
vegan.make_ahead: The toasted rice powder keeps 2 months in a sealed jar. Larb is best eaten right after mixing.

recipe.title: Beef Lasagna
recipe.description: The classic Italian-American bake: a slow-simmered beef and sausage ragù, creamy herbed ricotta and three layers of melty mozzarella with crisp, browned edges.

ingredients.item: salt, plus more for the pasta water

steps: Make the ragù: heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown the beef and sausage, breaking them up, for 8 to 10 minutes. Let it really brown; those browned bits are flavor. Spoon off all but 2 tbsp of the fat.
Add the onion and cook 6 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and tomato paste and stir 2 minutes until the paste darkens. Pour in the wine and scrape up the browned bits from the bottom.

Add the crushed tomatoes, tomato sauce, oregano, sugar, salt and pepper. Simmer uncovered on low for 30 to 45 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick enough that a spoon dragged through leaves a trail. Stir in the basil. A thick sauce keeps the lasagna from being watery.
Meanwhile, heat the oven to 375°F. Boil the noodles in well-salted water for 2 minutes less than the package says. Drain, rinse with cool water and lay flat on an oiled sheet so they don't stick.
Mix the ricotta, egg, 1/2 cup Parmesan, parsley, nutmeg and a pinch of salt and pepper.

Assemble in a 9 x 13 inch dish: spread 1 cup ragù on the bottom. Then layer 3 noodles, a third of the ricotta, a quarter of the ragù and 1 cup mozzarella. Repeat twice. Finish with the last 3 noodles, the remaining ragù, the rest of the mozzarella and 1/2 cup Parmesan.

Cover with foil (spray it with oil so the cheese doesn't stick) and bake 25 minutes. Uncover and bake 25 to 30 minutes more, until bubbling at the edges and browned on top. For extra browning, broil 2 minutes at the end.
Let it rest at least 20 minutes before cutting. This lets the layers set so you get clean squares instead of a sloppy pile.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Undercooking the noodles is key. They finish softening in the oven by soaking up sauce; fully cooked noodles turn mushy.
Use whole-milk ricotta and low-moisture mozzarella. Skim ricotta and fresh mozzarella release water and make it soupy.
The egg in the ricotta binds it so it holds its shape as a layer instead of oozing out.
Resting is not optional. Cut it hot and it collapses; give it 20 minutes and it slices cleanly.
recipe.make_ahead: Assemble up to 2 days ahead, cover and chill; add 15 minutes to the covered bake. Or freeze it unbaked for 3 months, thaw overnight in the fridge and bake as usual. Leftovers keep 4 days and reheat well.
variations: No-boil noodles: use oven-ready noodles and add 1/2 cup water to the ragù, since they absorb more liquid.
Spinach: squeeze 10 oz thawed frozen spinach very dry and stir it into the ricotta.
Vegetarian: replace the meat with 1 1/2 lb chopped mushrooms and zucchini, browned well.

recipe.title: Last Word
recipe.description: Equal parts gin, green Chartreuse, maraschino and lime.
steps: Shake everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
