Char the tomatoes and chilies in a dry pan or under the broiler until blackened in spots. Blend them with the toasted sesame, lime juice, timur, the rest of the salt and a little water into a thick sauce.
Roll the dough into a log, cut into 30 pieces and roll each into a thin 3 1/2-inch circle, thinner at the edges.
Put a spoon of filling in the center and pleat the edges together into a round purse, twisting the top to seal.
Steam on oiled racks for 10 to 12 minutes, until the wrappers are glossy and tender (165°F). Serve hot with the achar.
vegan.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Roll the wrapper edges thinner than the center, so the pleated top isn't doughy.
Squeeze the salted cabbage well, or the filling will turn watery and tear the wrappers.
Charring the tomatoes gives the achar its smoky depth; don't skip it.
vegan.make_ahead: Freeze shaped momos on a tray, then bag them; steam from frozen for 15 minutes. The achar keeps 5 days.

recipe.title: Monkey Gland
recipe.description: Gin and orange juice with grenadine and an absinthe rinse.
steps: Rinse a chilled coupe with the absinthe and discard the excess.
Shake the gin, orange juice and grenadine with ice and strain into the glass.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Monte Carlo
recipe.description: A rye Old Fashioned sweetened with Bénédictine.
steps: Stir everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe or over a large cube.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Moqueca Baiana (Brazilian Fish Stew)
recipe.description: The coastal stew from Bahia, Brazil: firm white fish and shrimp simmered with peppers, tomatoes and onion in coconut milk, colored and flavored with red dendê palm oil.

ingredients.item: firm white fish fillets (such as cod, halibut or snapper), cut into 2-inch pieces
malagueta or other small hot chile, minced (optional)

steps: Toss the fish and shrimp with the lime juice, garlic and 1 teaspoon salt. Let them sit for 15 minutes.
Heat the olive oil in a wide, heavy pot over medium heat. Cook the onion and peppers for 5 minutes, until softened.
Add the tomatoes, chile, if using, and the remaining salt and cook for 5 minutes, until the tomatoes start to break down.
Nestle the fish into the vegetables and pour over the coconut milk and dendê oil. Bring to a gentle simmer, cover and cook for 8 minutes.
Add the shrimp and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes more, until the fish flakes and the shrimp are pink.
Stir in most of the cilantro, taste for salt and lime, and serve over rice with the rest of the cilantro on top.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Dendê oil gives moqueca baiana its deep orange color and flavor. Find it at Brazilian or West African grocers; 2 tablespoons of olive oil plus 1 teaspoon paprika is the closest stand-in.
Stir gently once the fish is in, so the pieces stay whole.
variations: Moqueca capixaba: the Espírito Santo version skips the coconut milk and dendê, using olive oil and annatto instead.

recipe.title: Moroccan Chicken Apricot Couscous
recipe.description: A Moroccan-inspired chicken and chickpea stew with dried apricots, served over couscous.

ingredients.item: boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into large pieces

steps: Heat oil in a deep skillet and brown chicken for 4 minutes. Add onion and cook for 5 minutes, then garlic and spices for 30 seconds.
Add tomatoes, chickpeas, apricots, stew water and salt. Cover and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes until chicken reaches 165 F (74 C).
Meanwhile cover couscous with boiling water in a heatproof bowl for 5 minutes, or follow its package; fluff with a fork.
Serve stew over couscous and finish with cilantro.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: This is a practical home adaptation using a skillet rather than a traditional tagine. Couscous contains wheat.
recipe.make_ahead: Refrigerate promptly in shallow containers for up to 3 days. Reheat leftovers to 165 F (74 C).

recipe.title: Moroccan Harira
recipe.description: Spiced tomato, lentil and chickpea soup, traditional for breaking the Ramadan fast.
steps: Brown the meat in the oil with the onion and celery, then add the spices.
Add the tomatoes, water and lentils and simmer 40 minutes.
Add the chickpeas and vermicelli and simmer 10 minutes.
Stir in the flour mixture to thicken and the herbs. Season and serve with lemon.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Moroccan-Spiced Carrot and Lentil Stew
recipe.description: A hearty red lentil and carrot stew warmed with cumin and coriander, brightened with lemon. Naturally vegan.
steps: Cook onion and carrots in oil for 5 minutes. Add garlic, cumin and coriander and stir 30 seconds.
Add lentils, tomatoes and broth; simmer 20–25 minutes until lentils and carrots are tender. Add water if needed.
Stir in lemon juice and season to taste.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Moscow Mule
recipe.description: Vodka, lime and spicy ginger beer, served in a copper mug.
steps: Fill a copper mug with ice.
Add the vodka and lime juice and top with ginger beer.
Stir gently.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Use extra lime and ginger beer and skip the vodka.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Moussaka
recipe.description: Greek baked layers of eggplant, spiced lamb sauce and creamy béchamel.
steps: Brush the eggplant with oil and roast at 425°F for 20 minutes until golden.
Brown the meat with the onion and garlic, add the tomatoes and spices and simmer 20 minutes.
Melt the butter, whisk in the flour, then the milk and cook until thick. Off the heat, whisk in the yolks and half the cheese.
Layer half the eggplant, the meat, then the rest of the eggplant in a dish. Pour over the béchamel and top with cheese.
Bake at 350°F for 45 minutes until golden. Rest 20 minutes before cutting.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Mudslide
recipe.description: Vodka, coffee liqueur and Irish cream, blended or over ice.

ingredients.item: gluten-free chocolate syrup (such as Hershey's), for the glass

steps: Swirl chocolate syrup inside a rocks glass.
Shake everything with ice and strain into the glass over ice.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Blend cold coffee, chocolate syrup, cream and ice.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Mulled Wine
recipe.description: Red wine gently warmed with orange, cinnamon, cloves and star anise, sweetened and finished with a splash of brandy.

ingredients.item: vegan dry red wine (such as Yellow Tail Shiraz)
cinnamon sticks, plus more to serve

steps: Peel a few wide strips of zest from the orange with a vegetable peeler, then juice the orange.
Put the wine, orange juice, zest, sugar, cinnamon, cloves and star anise in a saucepan.
Warm over low heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves, for about 20 minutes. Keep it steaming but never let it boil.
Turn off the heat and stir in the brandy.
Strain into heatproof glasses or mugs and serve with a cinnamon stick.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Warm 3 cups red grape juice, 1 cup apple juice, orange zest and the same spices gently for 15 minutes.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Don't let it boil. Boiling burns off the alcohol and makes the spices taste harsh.
Any inexpensive, fruity red works well. Save the good bottle.
recipe.make_ahead: Keep it warm on the lowest heat or in a slow cooker for up to 2 hours.

recipe.title: Mushroom and Spinach Orzo
recipe.description: Browned mushrooms and garlic simmered with orzo in broth until creamy, then finished with spinach and Parmesan. A cozy one-pot dinner.
steps: Brown mushrooms in oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat, 6–8 minutes. Add garlic and cook 30 seconds.
Stir in orzo and broth. Simmer uncovered, stirring frequently, 9–11 minutes until the orzo is tender; add a splash of water if needed.
Fold in spinach to wilt, then Parmesan. Season to taste.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Mushroom Barley Soup
recipe.description: A comforting soup of mushrooms, pearl barley and vegetables with thyme.
steps: Brown mushrooms in oil in a pot for 6–8 minutes. Add onion, carrots, celery and garlic; cook 5 minutes.
Stir in barley, broth and thyme. Simmer partially covered for 35–45 minutes, until barley is tender, adding water if needed.
Season to taste.
recipe.note: Barley contains gluten; check the broth label for allergens.

recipe.title: Mushroom Risotto
recipe.description: Creamy Arborio rice with sautéed mushrooms, white wine and Parmesan.

ingredients.item: chicken or vegetable stock, kept hot

steps: Brown the mushrooms in the oil and 1 tbsp butter and set aside.
Cook the shallot in 1 tbsp butter, add the rice and toast 2 minutes.
Add the wine and stir until absorbed, then add the stock a ladle at a time, stirring, for 18 to 20 minutes until creamy and just tender.
Stir in the mushrooms, remaining butter and Parmesan. Season and top with parsley.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Mushroom Walnut Lentil Lettuce Wraps
recipe.description: Chopped mushrooms, walnuts and lentils in a savory ginger glaze, wrapped in crisp lettuce.

ingredients.item: green lentils (15 oz), drained and rinsed
large butter lettuce leaves, washed and dried

steps: Heat oil in a wide skillet over medium-high heat. Cook onion and mushrooms for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring, until mushroom moisture evaporates and the mixture browns.
Add walnuts, garlic and ginger and cook for 2 minutes. Stir in lentils, soy sauce and maple syrup; cook for 3 minutes until hot.
Take off heat and add lime juice.
Divide among lettuce leaves and top with grated carrot and scallions, serving two filled leaves per person.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Walnuts are part of the filling and the recipe is not nut-free. Butter lettuce is a vegetable, not a dairy ingredient.
recipe.make_ahead: Refrigerate filling promptly for up to 3 days and keep lettuce and toppings separate. Reheat filling to 165 F (74 C) before assembling.

recipe.title: Loaded Beef Nachos
recipe.description: Tortilla chips layered with seasoned beef, beans, melted cheese and fresh toppings.

ingredients.item: gluten-free taco seasoning (such as McCormick Gluten Free)

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F.
Brown the beef until cooked through (160°F), then stir in the taco seasoning and a splash of water.
Spread the chips on a sheet pan and layer with beef, beans, cheese and jalapeños.
Bake 8 to 10 minutes until the cheese melts.
Top with pico de gallo, sour cream and guacamole.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Naked and Famous
recipe.description: Equal parts mezcal, yellow Chartreuse, Aperol and lime.
steps: Shake everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Nasi Goreng
recipe.description: Indonesian fried rice with sweet soy sauce and shrimp paste, topped with a fried egg.
steps: Fry the shallots, garlic, chile and shrimp paste in the oil until fragrant.
Add the chicken or shrimp and cook through (165°F for chicken).
Add the rice, kecap manis and soy sauce and toss over high heat until hot and lightly charred.
Serve topped with a fried egg, with cucumber, tomato and fried shallots.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Nasi Lemak
recipe.description: Malaysia's national dish: fragrant coconut and pandan rice served with a sweet-spicy sambal, crispy fried anchovies, roasted peanuts, a boiled egg and fresh cucumber.

ingredients.item: pandan leaves, tied in a knot
dried red chilies, soaked and seeded
dried anchovies (ikan bilis), rinsed and dried

steps: Put the rice, coconut milk, water, pandan, ginger and salt in a pot or rice cooker. Cook as you would plain rice, then rest 10 minutes and fluff.
Blend the chilies, shallots, garlic and belacan into a paste with a splash of water.
Fry the anchovies in 1/4 cup oil until crisp, about 3 minutes, then the peanuts for 2 to 3 minutes until golden. Drain both.

In the same oil, fry the chili paste over medium-low heat for 10 to 15 minutes, stirring, until dark red and the oil separates. Add the onion rings, tamarind water and sugar and simmer 5 minutes. Stir in a third of the anchovies.
Mound the rice on plates and serve with sambal, anchovies, peanuts, egg and cucumber around it.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Cook the sambal paste slowly until the oil splits away. Rushing it leaves a raw, harsh chili taste.
Fry the anchovies and peanuts separately; they cook at different speeds.
Serve on a banana leaf for the classic aroma.
recipe.make_ahead: The sambal keeps 2 weeks in the fridge and freezes well. Store the fried anchovies and peanuts airtight for 1 week.
variations: Add fried chicken (ayam goreng) or a squid sambal for a bigger meal.

vegetarian.title: Vegetarian Nasi Lemak
vegetarian.description: Coconut pandan rice with a belacan-free sambal, crisp fried tempeh in place of anchovies, peanuts, egg and cucumber.

ingredients.item: pandan leaves, tied in a knot
dried red chilies, soaked and seeded
white miso or a little extra salt

steps: Put the rice, coconut milk, water, pandan, ginger and salt in a pot or rice cooker. Cook as you would plain rice, then rest 10 minutes and fluff.
Blend the chilies, shallots, garlic and miso into a paste with a splash of water.
Fry the tempeh in 1/4 cup oil until crisp and golden, about 5 minutes, then the peanuts for 2 to 3 minutes until golden. Drain both.

In the same oil, fry the chili paste over medium-low heat for 10 to 15 minutes, stirring, until dark red and the oil separates. Add the onion rings, tamarind water and sugar and simmer 5 minutes. Stir in a third of the tempeh.
Mound the rice on plates and serve with sambal, tempeh, peanuts, egg and cucumber around it.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Cook the sambal paste slowly until the oil splits away. Rushing it leaves a raw, harsh chili taste.
Fry the tempeh and peanuts separately; they cook at different speeds.
Serve on a banana leaf for the classic aroma.
vegetarian.make_ahead: The sambal keeps 2 weeks in the fridge and freezes well. Store the fried tempeh and peanuts airtight for 1 week.

vegan.title: Vegan Nasi Lemak
vegan.description: Coconut pandan rice with belacan-free sambal, crisp tempeh, peanuts and cucumber, with fried tofu in place of the egg.

ingredients.item: pandan leaves, tied in a knot
dried red chilies, soaked and seeded
white miso or a little extra salt
slices of firm tofu, fried until golden

steps: Put the rice, coconut milk, water, pandan, ginger and salt in a pot or rice cooker. Cook as you would plain rice, then rest 10 minutes and fluff.
Blend the chilies, shallots, garlic and miso into a paste with a splash of water.
Fry the tempeh in 1/4 cup oil until crisp and golden, about 5 minutes, then the peanuts for 2 to 3 minutes until golden. Drain both.

In the same oil, fry the chili paste over medium-low heat for 10 to 15 minutes, stirring, until dark red and the oil separates. Add the onion rings, tamarind water and sugar and simmer 5 minutes. Stir in a third of the tempeh.
Mound the rice on plates and serve with sambal, tempeh, peanuts, tofu and cucumber around it.
vegan.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Cook the sambal paste slowly until the oil splits away. Rushing it leaves a raw, harsh chili taste.
Fry the tempeh and peanuts separately; they cook at different speeds.
Serve on a banana leaf for the classic aroma.
vegan.make_ahead: The sambal keeps 2 weeks in the fridge and freezes well. Store the fried tempeh and peanuts airtight for 1 week.

recipe.title: Navy Grog
recipe.description: Three rums with lime, grapefruit and honey over a cone of ice.
steps: Shake everything except the soda with ice.
Strain over crushed ice in a double rocks glass and top with soda.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Negroni
recipe.description: The Italian classic of equal parts gin, Campari and sweet vermouth. Bitter, sweet and herbal, stirred and served over one big cube.

ingredients.item: vegan sweet vermouth (such as Dolin Rouge)
ice, plus 1 large cube for serving

steps: Put a large ice cube in a rocks glass to chill it.
Add the gin, Campari and vermouth to a mixing glass and fill it with ice.
Stir smoothly for 20 to 30 seconds, until the outside of the glass is frosty. Stirring chills and dilutes it without adding air, so it stays silky.
Strain over the large cube.
Squeeze the orange peel over the top to spray its oils, rub the rim with it, and drop it in.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Stir 1 1/2 oz non-alcoholic bitter aperitivo with 1 1/2 oz alcohol-free red vermouth and garnish with orange.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Vermouth is wine, and it spoils. Refrigerate it after opening and use it within a month or two. Stale vermouth is the most common reason a Negroni tastes flat.
One big cube melts slowly, so the last sip tastes like the first.
Equal parts is the classic. If you find it too bitter, use 1 1/4 oz gin and 3/4 oz Campari.
recipe.make_ahead: Batch it: mix equal parts in a bottle, add 1/2 oz water per drink, and keep it in the fridge for up to a month. Pour over ice and garnish.
variations: Boulevardier: swap bourbon or rye for the gin for a warmer, richer drink.
Negroni Sbagliato: replace the gin with prosecco and serve in a wine glass.
White Negroni: use gin, Suze and Lillet Blanc.

recipe.title: New York Sour
recipe.description: A whiskey sour with a layer of red wine floated on top.

ingredients.item: vegan dry red wine (such as Yellow Tail Shiraz)

steps: Shake the whiskey, lemon and syrup with ice and strain over fresh ice.
Pour the wine slowly over the back of a spoon so it floats.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Nigerian Goat Meat Pepper Soup
recipe.description: A fiery, aromatic broth from southern Nigeria: tender goat meat simmered with Scotch bonnet and the warm, earthy pepper soup spice blend, finished with fresh herbs.

ingredients.item: bone-in goat meat, cut into chunks
pepper soup spice (ehuru, uda, uziza blend)
uziza, utazi or scent leaves (or basil), chopped
boiled yam, plantain or rice, to serve

steps: Put the goat meat in a pot with the onion, half the peppers, the stock cubes, ginger and salt. Cover and let it steam in its own juices over medium heat for 10 minutes, stirring once.
Add the water, bring to a boil, then simmer, partly covered, for 1 to 1 1/4 hours, until the goat is tender.
Stir in the pepper soup spice, crayfish and the rest of the peppers and simmer 10 minutes more.
Add the leaves, simmer 2 minutes and taste for salt and heat. Serve hot in bowls, with yam, plantain or rice.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Steaming the meat with the seasonings before adding water drives the flavor deep into it.
Pepper soup spice is sold ready-ground in African markets. A mix of ground nutmeg, cumin, coriander and black pepper is a rough stand-in.
It should be thin, clear and fiery, not thick like a stew.
recipe.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge or 3 months frozen. Add fresh leaves when reheating.
variations: Catfish pepper soup: use catfish steaks and simmer only 15 minutes so they don't fall apart.
Use bone-in chicken thighs and simmer 35 minutes.

vegetarian.title: Vegetarian Pepper Soup
vegetarian.description: The same fiery spiced broth with meaty mushrooms, plantain and yam simmered in it.

ingredients.item: oyster or king oyster mushrooms, torn into big pieces
green plantain, peeled and cut in chunks
yam or potato, peeled and cut in chunks
pepper soup spice (ehuru, uda, uziza blend)
uziza, utazi or scent leaves (or basil), chopped

steps: Brown the mushrooms in a little oil in a large pot for 5 minutes. Add the onion, half the peppers and the ginger for 2 minutes.
Add the water, stock cubes, salt, plantain and yam. Simmer, partly covered, for 25 minutes, until the yam is tender.
Stir in the pepper soup spice and the rest of the peppers and simmer 10 minutes.
Add the leaves, simmer 2 minutes and taste for salt and heat. Serve hot.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Browning the mushrooms first gives the broth a deeper, meatier taste.
vegetarian.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge; add fresh leaves when reheating.

vegan.title: Vegan Pepper Soup
vegan.description: The same fiery spiced broth with meaty mushrooms, plantain and yam simmered in it.

ingredients.item: oyster or king oyster mushrooms, torn into big pieces
green plantain, peeled and cut in chunks
yam or potato, peeled and cut in chunks
pepper soup spice (ehuru, uda, uziza blend)
uziza, utazi or scent leaves (or basil), chopped

steps: Brown the mushrooms in a little oil in a large pot for 5 minutes. Add the onion, half the peppers and the ginger for 2 minutes.
Add the water, stock cubes, salt, plantain and yam. Simmer, partly covered, for 25 minutes, until the yam is tender.
Stir in the pepper soup spice and the rest of the peppers and simmer 10 minutes.
Add the leaves, simmer 2 minutes and taste for salt and heat. Serve hot.
vegan.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Browning the mushrooms first gives the broth a deeper, meatier taste.
vegan.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge; add fresh leaves when reheating.

recipe.title: Nigerian Suya
recipe.description: Spicy grilled beef skewers coated in a peanut and chile spice blend.

ingredients.item: gluten-free bouillon cube (such as Herb-Ox), crushed
sliced red onion, tomatoes and cabbage

steps: Mix the ground peanuts, spices and bouillon to make yaji spice.
Toss the beef with the oil and most of the spice and marinate 1 hour.
Thread onto skewers and grill 5 to 6 minutes per side.
Dust with more spice and serve with onion, tomato and cabbage.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Oatmeal with Fruit
recipe.description: Creamy stovetop oats topped with fresh fruit, a drizzle of honey and a pinch of cinnamon.
steps: Bring the milk, water and salt to a simmer.
Stir in the oats and cook over medium-low heat for 5 to 7 minutes, stirring often, until creamy.
Stir in the cinnamon and let stand 1 minute.
Spoon into bowls and top with fruit and honey.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Oaxaca Old Fashioned
recipe.description: Reposado tequila and mezcal with agave and bitters.
steps: Stir everything with ice.
Strain over a large cube and flame an orange peel over it.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Okonomiyaki
recipe.description: Japanese savory cabbage pancake with pork belly, topped with sauce, mayo and bonito flakes.

ingredients.item: okonomiyaki sauce, Japanese mayo, bonito flakes and aonori

steps: Whisk the flour, dashi and eggs, then fold in the cabbage and green onions.
Spread half the batter in an oiled pan into a thick round and lay pork belly on top.
Cook 5 minutes over medium heat, flip and cook 5 minutes more until the pork is crisp.
Top with sauce, mayo, bonito flakes and aonori. Repeat with the rest.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Old Cuban
recipe.description: Aged rum, lime, mint and bitters shaken together and topped with Champagne. Like an elegant, sparkling mojito.

ingredients.item: fresh mint leaves, plus a sprig to garnish
chilled vegan brut Champagne (such as Moët & Chandon Impérial)

steps: Chill a coupe.
Add the mint, rum, lime juice, simple syrup and bitters to a shaker and fill it with ice.
Shake hard for 10 to 15 seconds.
Double strain through a fine strainer into the chilled coupe so no bits of mint get in.
Top with the Champagne and garnish with a mint sprig.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake 1 oz lime juice, 1 oz simple syrup and 6 mint leaves with ice, strain, and top with 3 oz chilled ginger ale.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Don't muddle the mint hard. Shaking with ice releases enough flavor without the bitter, grassy taste of crushed leaves.
A dry prosecco works if you don't have Champagne.
Slap the mint sprig between your palms before garnishing to wake up its aroma.
variations: Old Cuban Royale: double the Champagne and serve in a flute.

recipe.title: Old Fashioned
recipe.description: The original cocktail: good whiskey, a little sugar, bitters and an orange twist. Stirred until silky and served over one large cube.

ingredients.item: bourbon or rye (90 to 100 proof works best)
rich demerara syrup (2 parts demerara sugar to 1 part water)
ice, plus 1 large cube for serving

steps: Add the syrup and both bitters to a mixing glass, then the whiskey.
Fill with ice and stir 25 to 30 seconds, until very cold. Taste with a straw: it should be smooth, not harsh. Stir a little more if it bites.
Put the large cube in a rocks glass and strain the drink over it.
Squeeze the orange peel over the drink, skin side down, so the oils spray across the top. Rub it around the rim and drop it in with the cherry.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Stir 2 oz strong black tea or a non-alcoholic whiskey alternative with 1/4 oz demerara syrup and a few drops of bitters (bitters contain alcohol; use alcohol-free aromatic bitters for a fully alcohol-free drink).

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Rich syrup is the easiest way to sweeten it. A sugar cube is traditional, but it rarely dissolves fully in cold whiskey.
Higher-proof whiskey holds up to the dilution from stirring. Lower-proof bottles can taste watery.
Don't muddle fruit into it. That's a different, sweeter drink. The orange oils give all the citrus it needs.
recipe.make_ahead: Batch it: mix whiskey, syrup and bitters in a bottle; it keeps indefinitely. Add 1/2 oz water per drink, chill, then pour over a big cube.
variations: Rye gives a spicier, drier drink; bourbon gives a rounder, sweeter one.
Oaxaca Old Fashioned: 1 1/2 oz reposado tequila, 1/2 oz mezcal, agave syrup and mole bitters.
Maple Old Fashioned: use maple syrup in place of demerara and add a dash of walnut bitters.

recipe.title: Old Pal
recipe.description: Rye, dry vermouth and Campari, a drier relative of the Negroni.

ingredients.item: vegan dry vermouth (such as Dolin Dry)

steps: Stir everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe, or over fresh ice in a rocks glass.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Cheese and Herb Omelet
recipe.description: A soft, folded three-egg omelet with melted cheese and fresh herbs.
steps: Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Melt the butter in a nonstick pan over medium heat and add the eggs.
Stir gently, then let set, tilting the pan so the runny egg flows to the edges.
When nearly set, add the cheese and herbs to one half, fold over and slide onto a plate.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Orange Blossom Rum Sour

steps: Add rum, orange juice, lime, syrup and a single drop of orange blossom water to a shaker.
Shake with ice for 15 seconds and double-strain into a chilled coupe.
Express the orange twist over the glass and add it.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake 2 1/2 oz orange juice, 3/4 oz lime juice, syrup and one drop orange blossom water with ice, then strain into a coupe.

recipe.title: Orange Chicken

steps: Toss the chicken in the egg, then in the cornstarch and flour mixed together.
Fry in oil at 350°F in batches for 5 to 6 minutes until crisp and cooked through (165°F). Drain.
Simmer the orange juice, zest, sugar, soy sauce, vinegar, garlic and ginger for 3 minutes.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry and cook until glossy and thick.
Toss the chicken in the sauce and serve with rice and sliced green onion.

recipe.title: Osso Buco

steps: Tie each shank around the middle, season and dredge in flour. Brown well in the oil.
Cook the onion, carrot and celery until soft, add the wine and reduce by half.
Add the tomatoes and stock, return the shanks, cover and simmer 2 to 2 1/2 hours until very tender.
Mix the lemon zest, parsley and garlic for the gremolata.
Serve with saffron risotto or polenta, topped with gremolata.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Pad See Ew
recipe.description: Wide rice noodles wok-fried with chicken, Chinese broccoli and egg in sweet soy sauce.
steps: Separate the noodles and mix the sauces and sugar.
Stir-fry the garlic and chicken in hot oil until cooked through (165°F).
Add the gai lan stems, then the leaves.
Push aside, scramble the eggs, then add the noodles and sauce and fry without stirring too much so they char slightly.
Season with white pepper.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Shrimp Pad Thai
recipe.description: Stir-fried rice noodles with shrimp, egg and bean sprouts in a sweet, sour and savory tamarind sauce.

ingredients.item: flat rice noodles, soaked in warm water 30 minutes

steps: Stir the tamarind, fish sauce and sugar until dissolved.
Heat the oil in a wok, cook the garlic and shrimp 1 to 2 minutes and push aside.
Scramble the eggs in the space, then add the drained noodles and sauce and toss 2 to 3 minutes until soft.
Add the bean sprouts and green onions for 30 seconds.
Serve topped with peanuts, lime and chili flakes.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Seafood Paella
recipe.description: Valencian-style saffron rice with shrimp, mussels and squid, cooked in a wide pan until the grains are separate and a crisp, caramelized crust (socarrat) forms on the bottom.

ingredients.item: fish or chicken stock (or half of each)
ripe tomatoes, grated on a box grater (skins discarded)

steps: Peel the shrimp, leaving the tails on, and simmer the shells in the stock for 15 minutes. Strain the stock, crumble in the saffron and keep it hot. This adds a lot of seafood flavor.

Heat the oil in a 15 to 17 inch paella pan, or your widest skillet, over medium-high heat. Sear the shrimp 1 minute per side and the squid 1 minute, then set both aside. They'll finish cooking in the rice.

In the same oil, cook the onion and pepper over medium heat for 8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic for 1 minute, then the grated tomato and paprika. Cook 5 to 8 minutes, stirring, until it darkens into a thick paste (sofrito).

Add the rice and stir for 1 minute to coat each grain. Pour in 5 1/2 cups of the hot stock and the salt, stir once to spread the rice evenly, and then don't stir again. Stirring releases starch and makes it creamy like risotto.

Boil hard for 10 minutes, turning the pan over the burner so it cooks evenly. Then nestle the mussels (hinge down), shrimp, squid and peas into the rice and lower the heat to a gentle simmer for 8 to 10 minutes. Add the last 1/2 cup of stock if the rice looks dry before it's tender.
When the liquid is absorbed and the rice is just tender, raise the heat to high for 1 to 2 minutes. Listen for a crackle and smell for toasting, not burning. That's the socarrat forming.
Take it off the heat, cover loosely with a clean towel or foil and rest 5 minutes. Throw away any mussels that didn't open. Serve straight from the pan with lemon and parsley.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Bomba rice absorbs about three times its volume in liquid but stays firm and separate. Long-grain rice turns mushy, and arborio turns creamy.
The wider the pan, the better. A thin layer of rice cooks evenly and forms more crust. Aim for rice no deeper than 1/2 inch.
Once the stock is in, resist stirring. A paella is supposed to be dry and separate, not creamy.
Season the stock well: taste it before adding it. The rice absorbs all of it, and you can't fix bland rice later.
recipe.make_ahead: Paella is best eaten right away. The sofrito can be made 2 days ahead and the stock 3 days ahead. Leftovers keep 1 day; reheat with a splash of stock in a hot skillet, which re-crisps the bottom.
variations: Mixta: replace the squid with 1 lb chicken thighs, browned first, and add 4 oz sliced Spanish chorizo.
Paella de verduras: use vegetable stock, artichoke hearts, green beans and roasted red peppers instead of seafood.
On the grill: cook it over a charcoal fire for smoky flavor and an even socarrat.

steps: Shake everything with ice.

Serve with the ginger, chiles, cilantro and lemon, and naan.

Add the spinach puree and garam masala and simmer 5 minutes.

recipe.title: Paprika Pork Tenderloin with Apples
recipe.description: Paprika-crusted pork tenderloin roasted with apple wedges, onion and thyme.

ingredients.item: firm apples, cored and cut into wedges

steps: Heat oven to 400 F (200 C). Rub pork with paprika, half the salt and black pepper.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in an ovenproof skillet over medium-high heat. Brown pork on all sides for about 5 minutes; transfer briefly to a plate.
Add remaining oil, apples and onion to the skillet. Cook for 3 minutes, then add water, thyme and remaining salt. Place pork on top.
Roast for 15 to 20 minutes or until pork reaches 145 F (63 C). Rest for at least 3 minutes before slicing. Return apples to the oven if they need longer to soften.

recipe.title: Pasta alla Norma
recipe.description: Catania's famous pasta: silky fried eggplant in a garlicky tomato and basil sauce, finished with a snowfall of salty ricotta salata.

ingredients.item: medium eggplants (about 2 lb), cut into 1-inch cubes
salt, plus more for the pasta water
olive oil, for frying, plus 2 tbsp
whole peeled tomatoes, crushed by hand

steps: Toss the eggplant with 1 tsp salt and let it drain in a colander for 30 minutes. Pat very dry.
Fry the eggplant in the 1/2 cup oil in batches over medium-high heat for 6 to 8 minutes, until deep golden and creamy inside. Drain on paper towels.
In a clean pan, warm the 2 tbsp oil with the garlic and chili flakes until the garlic is pale gold. Add the tomatoes, 1/2 tsp salt and a few basil leaves. Simmer 15 minutes, until thickened.
Cook the pasta in well-salted water until al dente. Save a cup of the cooking water.
Stir two-thirds of the eggplant into the sauce, then toss in the pasta with a splash of pasta water.
Serve topped with the rest of the eggplant, torn basil and plenty of ricotta salata.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Salting the eggplant draws out water, so it fries up creamy instead of soaking up oil.
Ricotta salata is firm, salty and crumbly, nothing like fresh ricotta. Mild feta or pecorino is the best substitute.
Keep some eggplant aside for the top so it stays a little crisp.
recipe.make_ahead: The sauce keeps 4 days. Fried eggplant can be made a day ahead and warmed in the oven.
variations: Lighter: roast the oiled eggplant at 425°F for 25 to 30 minutes instead of frying.

steps: Toss the eggplant with 1 tsp salt and let it drain in a colander for 30 minutes. Pat very dry.

recipe.title: Pepperoni Pizza
recipe.description: Pizzeria-style at home: a blistered, crisp crust, a bright no-cook sauce, melty mozzarella and pepperoni that curls into crisp little cups.

ingredients.item: pizza dough, at room temperature for 1 hour
olive oil, plus more for drizzling
semolina or flour, for the peel
grated Parmesan, red pepper flakes and fresh basil, to serve

steps: Put a pizza steel or stone on the top third rack and heat the oven to its highest setting (500 to 550°F) for a full 45 minutes. The stone needs that long to get hot enough to crisp the base.
Make the sauce: crush the drained tomatoes by hand or pulse briefly, then stir in the garlic, olive oil, oregano and salt. Don't cook it; it bakes on the pizza.

Divide the dough in two. On a floured counter, press each from the center outward with your fingertips, leaving a 1/2 inch rim, then stretch it over your knuckles to 12 inches. Don't use a rolling pin; it presses out the air that makes the crust puffy.

Lay one round on a peel dusted with semolina. Spread a thin layer of sauce, about 1/4 cup, leaving the rim bare. Scatter half the mozzarella and half the pepperoni. Give the peel a little shake to make sure the pizza slides.

Slide the pizza onto the steel and bake 7 to 10 minutes, until the rim is puffed and charred in spots and the cheese is bubbling and browned. If your oven has a broiler, switch it on for the last minute.
Rest 1 minute on a rack so the bottom stays crisp. Finish with olive oil, Parmesan, pepper flakes and basil, then repeat with the second pizza.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Small, thick pepperoni curls into crisp cups and holds its fat in pools; wide, thin slices stay flat and greasy.
Use low-moisture mozzarella, not fresh, for this style. Fresh mozzarella releases water and makes a soggy center.
Less is more: too much sauce or cheese weighs the dough down and keeps the middle from cooking.
Cold dough is tight and springs back. Let it warm on the counter for an hour and it stretches easily.
recipe.make_ahead: Dough balls keep 3 days in the fridge in oiled containers, or 3 months frozen. Sauce keeps 5 days. Reheat leftover slices in a dry, covered skillet over medium heat to bring back the crisp bottom.
variations: Hot honey pepperoni: drizzle with honey warmed with chili flakes after baking.
Add sliced red onion, mushrooms or pickled jalapeños with the pepperoni.
No stone: heat an upside-down baking sheet the same way.

steps: Cook the onion and pepper in 1 tbsp oil until soft and golden. Remove.

recipe.title: Beef Pho
recipe.description: Northern-style Vietnamese beef noodle soup: a clear, deeply savory broth scented with charred onion, ginger and toasted spices, poured over rice noodles and paper-thin beef.

ingredients.item: beef bones (knuckle and marrow), plus 1 lb oxtail if you can find it
beef brisket or chuck, in one piece
fish sauce, plus more to taste
yellow rock sugar, or 1 tbsp sugar
beef eye of round or sirloin, partly frozen 30 minutes, sliced paper-thin
small onion, sliced paper-thin and soaked in cold water
bean sprouts, Thai basil, cilantro, sliced green onion, lime wedges and sliced chilies

steps: Parboil to keep the broth clear: cover the bones and oxtail with cold water, bring to a boil and boil hard 10 minutes. Drain, then rinse the bones and scrub out the pot to remove the gray scum.
While the bones boil, char the onions and ginger cut-side up under the broiler, or directly over a gas flame, until blackened in spots, about 10 minutes. Rinse off any loose burnt skin.
Toast the star anise, cinnamon, cloves, coriander, fennel and cardamom in a dry pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes, shaking, until fragrant. Tie them in a spice bag or cheesecloth.

Return the bones to the clean pot with the brisket, onions, ginger and 5 quarts of cold water. Bring slowly to a simmer and skim off any foam. Keep it at a gentle simmer, with just a few bubbles; boiling makes it cloudy.
After 1 1/2 hours, lift out the brisket, plunge it into cold water for 10 minutes so it doesn't darken, then chill and slice it thin. Add the spice bag, fish sauce, rock sugar and salt to the pot.

Simmer 1 1/2 to 2 hours more. Remove the spice bag after 45 minutes so the spices don't turn bitter. Strain the broth through a fine sieve and skim the fat, leaving a little on top for flavor. Taste: it should be well seasoned, a touch salty and slightly sweet. Keep it at a rolling boil for serving.
Soak the noodles in warm water 30 minutes, then dip portions in boiling water for 15 to 30 seconds until just tender. Divide among large warmed bowls.

Top the noodles with sliced brisket, raw beef slices and drained onion. Ladle the boiling broth straight over the raw beef to cook it pink. Serve right away with the herb plate, lime, chilies, hoisin and sriracha on the side.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Parboiling and rinsing the bones removes blood and impurities. It's the most important step for a clear, clean-tasting broth.
Charring the onion and ginger adds sweetness and smoky depth, and gives the broth its amber color.
Partly freezing the beef makes it firm enough to slice paper-thin, which lets the hot broth cook it in seconds.
The broth must be boiling, not just hot, when you pour it over the raw beef, or the beef stays raw.
Season in stages. Fish sauce varies by brand, so add the last splash at the end, to taste.
recipe.make_ahead: The broth is better made a day ahead: chill it overnight, lift off the solid fat, and reheat. It keeps 4 days in the fridge or 3 months frozen. Keep noodles, meat and herbs separate.
variations: Chicken pho (phở gà): use a whole chicken and chicken bones, simmer 1 1/2 hours, and shred the meat.
Pressure cooker: after parboiling and charring, cook everything on high pressure for 1 1/2 hours.

recipe.title: Potato and Cheese Pierogi
recipe.description: Polish dumplings filled with potato and cheddar, pan-fried with butter and onions.
steps: Mix the flour, egg, sour cream, water and a pinch of salt into a soft dough. Rest 30 minutes.
Mix the potatoes and cheese and season.
Roll the dough thin and cut 3-inch circles. Fill, fold and pinch tightly.
Boil in salted water until they float, plus 2 minutes.
Fry the onion in the butter until golden, add the pierogi and fry until crisp. Serve with sour cream.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Pimm's Cup
recipe.description: England's summer garden drink: Pimm's No. 1 over ice with sparkling lemonade, cucumber, strawberry, orange and mint.

ingredients.item: chilled sparkling lemonade (such as Sprite or 7UP)

steps: Fill a tall glass with ice, tucking the cucumber, strawberry and orange slices in between the cubes.
Pour in the Pimm's.
Top with the lemonade and stir gently.
Slap the mint sprig between your hands to wake it up and add it to the glass.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Build 1 1/2 oz cold black tea, 1 oz lemon juice and the fruit over ice and top with 4 oz ginger ale.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: The rule is one part Pimm's to three parts lemonade. Use the clear, fizzy kind, not American still lemonade.
For a drier drink, use half lemonade and half ginger ale.
recipe.make_ahead: For a crowd, fill a jug with ice and fruit, add the Pimm's, and top with lemonade just before serving.

recipe.title: Piña Colada
recipe.description: Rum blended with pineapple and cream of coconut.
steps: Blend everything until smooth.
Pour into a hurricane glass.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Blend without the rum for a virgin piña colada.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Piña Verde
recipe.description: A piña colada made with green Chartreuse.
steps: Shake everything with crushed ice.
Pour into a glass and top with more crushed ice.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Pineapple Basil Vodka Smash
recipe.description: Pineapple, basil and lemon give a juicy vodka smash a fresh herbal edge.
steps: Press the four basil leaves gently with the syrup in a shaker; do not grind them into a paste.
Add vodka, pineapple juice, lemon juice and ice. Shake for 12 seconds.
Strain into a rocks glass over fresh ice, allowing a few tiny basil flecks through. Garnish with the basil sprig.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Gently press basil with 1/4 oz syrup, add 3 oz pineapple juice and 1/2 oz lemon juice, shake with ice and strain over fresh ice.

recipe.note: An original Relish home cocktail. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Pressing rather than shredding the basil keeps its flavor fresh instead of bitter.
recipe.make_ahead: Keep juice chilled and prepare just before serving; muddled basil loses color as it stands.

recipe.title: Pineapple Coconut Water Tequila Cooler
recipe.description: Tequila, pineapple and coconut water make a bright, light-bodied tropical cooler.
steps: Shake tequila, pineapple juice, coconut water and lime with ice for 12 seconds.
Strain into an ice-filled highball glass.
Garnish with the pineapple triangle and serve immediately.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake 3 oz pineapple juice, 2 oz coconut water and 1/2 oz lime juice with ice, then strain over fresh ice.

recipe.note: An original Relish home cocktail. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Use coconut water, not coconut milk or cream; the finished drink is light and not creamy.
recipe.make_ahead: Prepare to order. Keep juices and brewed teas refrigerated until needed.

recipe.title: Pineapple Ginger Rum Highball
recipe.description: White rum with pineapple and lime, topped with spicy ginger beer.
steps: Add rum, pineapple and lime to a tall glass of ice.
Top with ginger beer, stir gently and garnish.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: replace rum with alcohol-free rum alternative.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Pineapple Jalapeño Tequila Highball
recipe.description: Tequila, pineapple and lime with a touch of jalapeño and soda.
steps: Gently muddle jalapeño in a shaker.
Add tequila, pineapple, lime and ice; shake and strain into a tall glass over ice.
Top with soda and garnish with a fresh jalapeño slice.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Muddle the jalapeño, shake with pineapple and lime, strain over ice and top with extra soda.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Pineapple Turmeric Rum Cooler
recipe.description: Pineapple, lime and a tiny measure of turmeric make a sunny rum cooler.
steps: Whisk the tiny measure of turmeric into pineapple juice in a shaker until dispersed.
Add rum, lime, syrup and ice. Shake for 15 seconds and fine-strain into an ice-filled highball.
Top with soda, stir gently and add the pineapple wedge.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake 4 oz pineapple juice, 1/2 oz lime juice, syrup and the measured turmeric with ice; strain and add 1 oz soda.

recipe.note: An original Relish home cocktail. Please drink responsibly.
tips: A small pinch, about 1/16 tsp, is enough; excess turmeric tastes earthy and settles out. This is a flavor ingredient, not a health claim.
recipe.make_ahead: Prepare to order. Keep juices and brewed teas refrigerated until needed.

recipe.title: Pink Squirrel
recipe.description: Creamy pink dessert drink of crème de noyaux, crème de cacao and cream.
steps: Shake everything hard with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
recipe.note: Crème de noyaux is flavored with apricot kernels or almonds.

recipe.title: Pisco Punch
recipe.description: San Francisco's Gold Rush-era favorite: pisco with pineapple, lemon and clove, finished with a splash of dry white wine.

ingredients.item: chilled vegan dry white wine (such as Bonterra Sauvignon Blanc)

steps: In a shaker, gently press the cloves into the simple syrup with a muddler to release their flavor.
Add the pisco, pineapple juice and lemon juice, then fill with ice.
Shake hard and double-strain into a large wine glass or goblet.
Pour the wine on top and stir gently.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake 2 oz pineapple juice, 1/2 oz lemon juice, 1/2 oz simple syrup and 2 cloves with ice, strain, and top with 1 oz white grape juice.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Press the cloves lightly. Crushing them hard makes the drink bitter.
Fresh pineapple juice gives a lovely foam; carton juice works but is flatter.

recipe.title: Pisco Sour
recipe.description: Peruvian pisco with lime, sugar and egg white, dotted with bitters.
steps: Dry-shake the pisco, lime, syrup and egg white, then shake again with ice.
Strain into a rocks glass or coupe and dot with bitters.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: This drink uses raw egg white. Use pasteurized egg white if you prefer, and always for anyone pregnant, older or with a weakened immune system.

recipe.title: Planter's Punch
recipe.description: Dark Jamaican rum with lime, sugar and a little grenadine.
steps: Shake everything except the soda with ice.
Strain into an ice-filled Collins glass and top with soda.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Lime, syrup, grenadine and pineapple juice topped with ginger ale.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Plum Basil Vodka Sour
recipe.description: Ripe red plum and basil make a fresh violet-red vodka sour.

ingredients.item: ripe red plum, pitted and chopped

steps: Muddle plum and basil gently with syrup in a shaker.
Add vodka, lemon and ice. Shake for 15 seconds and fine-strain into a chilled coupe.
Garnish with the plum slice and one small basil leaf.

cocktail.garnish: thin plum slice and small basil leaf
cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Muddle plum and basil with syrup; shake with 3/4 oz lemon juice and 2 oz cooled white tea, then double-strain into a coupe.

recipe.note: An original Relish home cocktail. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Remove the plum stone before muddling. Use just a few basil leaves to keep the fruit in balance.
recipe.make_ahead: Prepare to order. Keep juices and brewed teas refrigerated until needed.

recipe.title: Plum Ginger Brandy Sour
recipe.description: Ripe plum, lemon and ginger give brandy a tart, warming fruit-sour finish.

ingredients.item: ripe red plum, pitted and chopped

steps: Muddle chopped plum with ginger syrup in a shaker until juicy.
Add brandy, lemon juice and ice. Shake firmly for 15 seconds.
Double-strain into a rocks glass over a large ice cube. Garnish with the thin plum fan.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Muddle half a pitted plum with 1/2 oz ginger syrup; shake with 3/4 oz lemon juice and 2 oz cooled black tea, then double-strain over ice.

recipe.note: An original Relish home cocktail. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Remove the plum stone completely before muddling; fine-straining catches skin fragments.
recipe.make_ahead: Refrigerate cut plum for up to 1 day. Shake the drink just before serving.

recipe.title: Plum Rosemary Gin Fizz
recipe.description: Fresh plum, rosemary and lemon make a sparkling ruby gin drink.

ingredients.item: ripe red plum, pitted and chopped

steps: Muddle plum gently with syrup and rosemary in a shaker.
Add gin, lemon and ice, shake for 15 seconds and fine-strain into an ice-filled highball.
Top with soda, stir gently and garnish with the plum slice.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Muddle plum and rosemary with syrup; shake with 3/4 oz lemon juice and ice, strain and top with 4 oz soda.

recipe.note: An original Relish home cocktail. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Use only a small rosemary sprig; a little gives aroma without overwhelming the fruit.
recipe.make_ahead: Prepare to order. Keep juices and brewed teas refrigerated until needed.

recipe.title: Poet's Dream
recipe.description: Gin, dry vermouth and Bénédictine, stirred.

ingredients.item: vegan dry vermouth (such as Dolin Dry)

steps: Stir everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Pomegranate Black Tea Vodka Collins
recipe.description: A long vodka drink with tart pomegranate, black tea and a lemon-soda finish.
steps: Shake vodka, pomegranate juice, cooled tea, lemon juice and syrup with ice for 12 seconds.
Strain into an ice-filled Collins glass, top with soda and stir gently.
Garnish with the lemon wheel.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake 2 oz pomegranate juice, 2 oz cooled black tea, 1/2 oz lemon juice and 1/4 oz syrup with ice; strain and add 2 oz soda water.

recipe.note: An original Relish home cocktail. Please drink responsibly.
recipe.make_ahead: Prepare to order. Keep juices and brewed teas refrigerated until needed.

recipe.title: Pomegranate Lime Mezcal Sparkler
recipe.description: Smoky mezcal with pomegranate and lime, topped with soda.
steps: Shake mezcal, pomegranate, lime and agave with ice.
Strain into a tall glass over fresh ice, top with soda and garnish with lime.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake the pomegranate, lime and agave with ice, strain over ice and top with extra soda.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Pomegranate Rosemary Gin Fizz
recipe.description: Gin, pomegranate and lemon topped with soda and fragrant rosemary.
steps: Shake gin, pomegranate, lemon and syrup with ice.
Strain into an ice-filled tall glass, top with soda and garnish with rosemary.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake the pomegranate juice, lemon and syrup with ice, strain over ice and top with extra soda.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Pomegranate Vanilla Brandy Sour
recipe.description: Pomegranate and a little vanilla syrup bring a round tart-sweet balance to brandy.
steps: Shake brandy, pomegranate juice, lemon and vanilla syrup with ice for 15 seconds.
Double-strain into a chilled coupe.
Express lemon peel over the glass and add it.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake 2 1/2 oz pomegranate juice, 3/4 oz lemon juice and 1/2 oz vanilla syrup with ice; strain into a coupe.

recipe.note: An original Relish home cocktail. Please drink responsibly.
tips: For quick vanilla syrup, mix 1/4 tsp vanilla extract into 1/2 cup simple syrup and measure the portion needed.
recipe.make_ahead: Prepare to order. Keep juices and brewed teas refrigerated until needed.

recipe.title: Pork and Cabbage Rice Skillet
recipe.description: Ground pork, cabbage and carrot tossed with rice and a ginger-soy seasoning.
steps: Heat neutral oil in a wide skillet over medium-high heat. Brown pork for 6 to 8 minutes, breaking it up, until it reaches 160 F (71 C).
Add ginger and garlic for 30 seconds, then cabbage and carrots. Stir-fry for 6 to 8 minutes until tender.
Add rice, soy sauce and vinegar. Stir-fry for 4 to 5 minutes until the rice is steaming and reaches 165 F (74 C).
Finish with sesame oil and scallions. Divide among four bowls.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Chill cooked rice promptly, never overnight at room temperature. Break up cold rice clumps before adding to the pan.
recipe.make_ahead: Refrigerate promptly in shallow containers for up to 3 days. Reheat leftovers to 165 F (74 C).

recipe.title: Pork Katsu
recipe.description: Japanese panko-crusted pork cutlets with shredded cabbage and tonkatsu sauce.

ingredients.item: boneless pork loin chops, 1/2 inch thick

steps: Pound the pork slightly and season with salt and pepper.
Dredge in flour, dip in egg and press into the panko.
Fry at 340°F for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden and cooked. Drain on a rack.
Slice and serve with cabbage, rice, lemon and tonkatsu sauce.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Pork Meatballs with Ginger Broth
recipe.description: Tender pork meatballs, mushrooms and spinach in a light ginger broth with rice.
steps: Mix pork, egg, breadcrumbs, half the ginger, half the soy sauce and black pepper. Form 16 small meatballs.
Bring water, remaining ginger, remaining soy sauce and mushrooms to a gentle simmer in a wide saucepan. Cook for 5 minutes.
Lower meatballs into the broth. Cover partly and simmer gently for 12 to 15 minutes, until the center of every meatball reaches 160 F (71 C).
Stir in spinach to wilt. Divide hot rice among bowls and ladle meatballs and broth over it; scatter with scallions.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Keep the broth at a gentle simmer so the meatballs hold their shape. Check breadcrumbs for additional allergens.
recipe.make_ahead: Refrigerate promptly in shallow containers for up to 3 days. Reheat leftovers to 165 F (74 C).

recipe.title: Pork Schnitzel
recipe.description: Thin pork cutlets in a crisp, golden breadcrumb coating, served with lemon.

ingredients.item: boneless pork chops, pounded to 1/4 inch
large eggs, beaten with 1 tbsp water
vegetable oil or lard, for frying

steps: Season the pork with salt and pepper.
Dredge in flour, dip in egg and coat lightly in breadcrumbs without pressing.
Shallow-fry in 1/2 inch of hot oil, swirling the pan, 2 to 3 minutes per side until puffed and golden.
Drain and serve with lemon wedges.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Pork Souvlaki with Tzatziki
recipe.description: Greece's favorite street food: cubes of pork marinated in lemon, garlic, oregano and olive oil, grilled on skewers and tucked into warm pita with tzatziki, tomato and onion.

ingredients.item: boneless pork shoulder, cut into 1-inch cubes
English cucumber, grated and squeezed dry
fresh lemon juice, for the tzatziki

steps: Whisk the olive oil, 3 tablespoons lemon juice, vinegar, minced garlic, oregano, salt and pepper in a bowl. Add the pork, toss, cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or overnight.
Make the tzatziki: stir the yogurt, cucumber, grated garlic, dill and 1 teaspoon lemon juice together with a pinch of salt. Chill until needed.
Thread the pork onto the skewers.
Heat a grill or grill pan to medium-high. Grill the skewers for 10 to 12 minutes, turning every few minutes, until charred at the edges and cooked through (145°F).
Serve the pork on warm pita with tzatziki, tomato and onion, or on a plate with lemon wedges.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Pork shoulder stays juicy on the grill. Tenderloin works but cooks faster, so watch it.
Squeeze the grated cucumber well, or the tzatziki will turn watery.
recipe.make_ahead: Make the tzatziki up to 2 days ahead; it gets better as it sits.
variations: Chicken souvlaki: use boneless chicken thighs and grill for 10 minutes, to 165°F.
Add a few fries inside the pita, the way many Greek street stalls do.

recipe.title: Passion Fruit Martini
recipe.description: Vanilla vodka and passion fruit, served with a sidecar of prosecco.

ingredients.item: vegan prosecco (such as Mionetto Organic), on the side

steps: Shake everything except the prosecco with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe and float half a passion fruit on top.
Serve the prosecco in a shot glass alongside.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake passion fruit puree, lime and vanilla syrup and top with sparkling white grape juice.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Port of Spain
recipe.description: Trinidad-style rum sour with Angostura and lime.
steps: Shake everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
recipe.note: Recipes for this drink vary between bars; this is one common version.

recipe.title: Porto Flip
recipe.description: Ruby port and brandy shaken with a whole egg yolk, topped with nutmeg.

ingredients.item: vegan ruby port (such as Cockburn's Special Reserve)

steps: Dry-shake everything, then shake again with ice.
Strain into a small chilled glass and grate nutmeg on top.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: This drink uses a raw egg yolk. Use a pasteurized egg if you prefer, and always for anyone pregnant, older or with a weakened immune system.

recipe.title: Potato Gnocchi with Brown Butter and Sage
recipe.description: Light, pillowy Italian potato dumplings made from baked russets, a little flour and an egg, tossed in nutty brown butter with crisp sage leaves.

ingredients.item: kosher salt, plus more for the water
all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Prick the potatoes and bake them directly on the rack for 50 to 60 minutes, until very tender.
While they're still hot, peel the potatoes and press them through a ricer onto a clean counter. Spread them out and let them steam for 5 minutes.

Sprinkle the egg, salt and 3/4 cup of the flour over the potatoes. Gently fold and press together with a bench scraper or your hands, adding more flour only as needed, until a soft dough forms. Don't knead.
Divide the dough into 4 pieces. Roll each into a 3/4-inch rope on a floured counter and cut into 3/4-inch pieces. Roll each over a fork if you like, for ridges.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a gentle boil. Cook the gnocchi in batches until they float, then 30 seconds more, about 2 minutes. Lift them out with a slotted spoon.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat and cook, swirling, until it smells nutty and turns golden brown. Add the sage and fry for 30 seconds, until crisp.
Add the gnocchi to the brown butter, toss gently, season with pepper and serve.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Bake the potatoes instead of boiling them. Drier potatoes need less flour, and less flour means lighter gnocchi.
Use as little flour as you can. Too much makes gnocchi dense and chewy.
recipe.make_ahead: Freeze uncooked gnocchi on a floured tray, then bag them. Cook from frozen for 3 to 4 minutes.
variations: Serve with tomato sauce or pesto instead of brown butter.

recipe.title: Potato Salad
recipe.description: Classic creamy picnic potato salad with egg, celery and mustard.

ingredients.item: red or Yukon Gold potatoes, cubed

steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water 10 to 12 minutes until just tender. Drain and cool.
Mix the mayonnaise, mustard and vinegar.
Fold in the potatoes, eggs, celery, onion and relish. Season.
Chill and sprinkle with paprika.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Poutine
recipe.description: Quebec's late-night classic: crisp, twice-fried fries topped with squeaky fresh cheese curds and drowned in hot, savory brown gravy that just starts to melt them.

ingredients.item: vegetable or canola oil, for frying
fresh cheese curds, at room temperature

steps: Soak the cut potatoes in cold water for at least 30 minutes, then drain and dry them very well.

Make the gravy: melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat, whisk in the flour and cook, stirring, for 3 to 4 minutes, until golden brown. Gradually whisk in both broths, the vinegar and pepper. Simmer for 8 to 10 minutes, until it coats a spoon. Taste for salt and keep hot.
Heat 2 inches of oil in a heavy pot to 325°F. Fry the potatoes in batches for 5 to 6 minutes, until soft and pale but not browned. Drain on a rack.
Heat the oil to 375°F and fry the potatoes again for 2 to 3 minutes, until deep golden and crisp. Drain and salt right away.
Pile the hot fries into bowls, scatter over the cheese curds and pour the very hot gravy on top. Serve right away.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Fresh, squeaky cheese curds are the heart of poutine. Bring them to room temperature so the gravy softens them.
The gravy must be very hot, or the curds won't start to melt.
Short on time? Use crisp oven-baked frozen fries.
recipe.make_ahead: Make the gravy up to 3 days ahead and reheat until steaming.
variations: Add pulled pork, sautéed mushrooms or bacon on top.

recipe.title: Pozole Rojo
recipe.description: Mexican pork and hominy stew in a red chile broth, with crunchy toppings.

ingredients.item: shredded cabbage, radishes, onion, lime and tostadas

steps: Simmer the pork with the onion, half the garlic and salt in 3 quarts of water for 1 1/2 hours.
Soak the chiles in hot water, then blend with the remaining garlic, oregano and a cup of broth. Strain.
Add the chile puree and hominy to the pot and simmer 45 minutes.
Shred the pork and season.
Serve with the toppings.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Pulled Pork Sandwich
recipe.description: Slow-cooked, smoky pork shoulder tossed in barbecue sauce and piled onto buns with slaw.
steps: Mix the sugar and spices and rub all over the pork.
Put the onion in a slow cooker, add the pork and pour in the vinegar.
Cook on low for 8 hours until it pulls apart easily.
Shred the pork, discard excess fat, and toss with the barbecue sauce.
Pile onto buns and top with coleslaw.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Check the label if you need to avoid fish: some barbecue sauces contain Worcestershire sauce, which is made with anchovies. Creamy coleslaw is made with mayonnaise, which contains eggs.

recipe.title: Pupusas
recipe.description: Salvadoran stuffed corn cakes with cheese and beans, served with curtido slaw.
steps: Mix the cabbage, carrot, vinegar, oregano and salt for the curtido and chill.
Mix the masa, water and a pinch of salt into a soft dough.
With wet hands, flatten a ball of dough, fill with cheese and beans, close and pat into a 1/2-inch disk.
Cook on a hot griddle 3 to 4 minutes per side until spotted brown.
Serve with curtido and salsa.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Queen Elizabeth
recipe.description: The brandy Queen Elizabeth from The Savoy Cocktail Book era: cognac and sweet vermouth with a touch of orange curaçao, stirred and served up with a cherry. Like a rich, orange-scented Manhattan.

ingredients.item: vegan sweet vermouth (such as Dolin Rouge)

steps: Stir the cognac, vermouth and curaçao with ice for 20 to 30 seconds, until very cold.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
Garnish with a brandied or maraschino cherry on a pick.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Stir cold black tea with a splash of non-alcoholic red vermouth and orange syrup, and garnish with a cherry.

recipe.note: There is also a gin Queen Elizabeth (gin, dry vermouth and Bénédictine); this is the brandy version.
tips: Stir, don't shake; it keeps the drink clear and silky.
Use a fresh bottle of sweet vermouth, stored in the fridge once opened.
variations: Add 2 dashes of Angostura bitters for a drier, spicier drink.

recipe.title: Queen's Park Swizzle
recipe.description: Demerara rum swizzled with mint, lime and Angostura bitters in layers.
steps: Lightly press the mint in a Collins glass with the syrup and lime.
Add the rum, fill with crushed ice and swizzle until frosty.
Top with more ice and dash the bitters over the top.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Quiche Lorraine
recipe.description: The classic from Lorraine in eastern France: a crisp butter pastry shell filled with smoky bacon and a silky, nutmeg-scented egg and cream custard.

ingredients.item: all-purpose flour, plus more for rolling
kosher salt, plus 1/2 tsp for the custard
thick-cut smoked bacon, cut into 1/2-inch strips

steps: Make the pastry: mix the flour and salt, then rub in the butter with your fingertips until it looks like coarse crumbs with some pea-size pieces. Stir in just enough ice water for the dough to hold together. Flatten into a disk, wrap and chill for 1 hour.
Roll the dough out on a floured counter and line a 9-inch tart pan or deep pie dish. Prick the base with a fork and chill for 15 minutes. Heat the oven to 400°F.
Line the pastry with parchment and fill with pie weights or dried beans. Bake for 15 minutes, remove the weights and bake 8 to 10 minutes more, until pale golden. Lower the oven to 325°F.
Meanwhile, cook the bacon in a skillet over medium heat for 6 to 8 minutes, until golden but not crisp. Drain on paper towels.
Whisk the eggs, yolk, cream, milk, nutmeg, pepper and 1/2 teaspoon salt until smooth, without beating in air.
Scatter the bacon in the warm pastry shell and pour in the custard.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes, until the edges are set but the center still wobbles slightly. Cool for at least 20 minutes before slicing.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Blind-baking the crust first is what keeps the bottom crisp instead of soggy.
Take the quiche out while the center still jiggles. It keeps cooking as it cools, and an overbaked custard turns rubbery.
recipe.make_ahead: Bake up to a day ahead, refrigerate, and serve at room temperature or reheat at 325°F for 15 minutes.
variations: Add 1 cup grated Gruyère with the bacon, the way it's often made outside France.
Use a 9-inch store-bought pie crust to save time.

recipe.title: Rabo de Galo
recipe.description: Brazil's own bittersweet aperitif: cachaça stirred over ice with sweet vermouth and a touch of Cynar. The name means "rooster's tail".

ingredients.item: vegan sweet vermouth (such as Dolin Rouge)

steps: Fill a rocks glass with ice.
Pour in the cachaça, sweet vermouth, Cynar and bitters, if using.
Stir briefly to chill and mix.
Squeeze the orange twist over the drink and drop it in.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Stir 2 oz non-alcoholic red aperitivo with a splash of cold black tea and a dash of orange juice over ice.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Cynar is an Italian artichoke liqueur. It adds a gentle bitterness; Campari works if you can't find it.
Unaged (silver) cachaça gives a grassier drink; aged cachaça makes it rounder and warmer.

recipe.title: Chicken Ramen
recipe.description: Weeknight shoyu-style ramen: a rich chicken broth boosted with kombu, soy and aromatics, with jammy marinated eggs, tender poached thighs and chewy noodles.

ingredients.item: green onions, whites and greens separated
soy sauce, plus 2 tbsp for the eggs
mirin, plus 1 tbsp for the eggs
chili oil and toasted sesame seeds, to serve

steps: Marinate the eggs first: lower the eggs into boiling water and cook exactly 6 1/2 minutes, then plunge into ice water for 5 minutes and peel. Put them in a zip bag with 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp mirin and 2 tbsp water and chill while you make everything else.
Put the broth, kombu, garlic, ginger and green onion whites in a pot. Bring just to a simmer, then pull out the kombu before the broth boils (boiled kombu turns slimy and bitter).

Slip in the chicken thighs and keep the broth at a bare simmer, with small bubbles, not a rolling boil, for 15 to 18 minutes, until the thighs reach 175°F inside. Lift them out and rest 5 minutes, then slice.

Strain the broth and return it to the pot. Stir in 1/4 cup soy sauce, 3 tbsp mirin, sake and sugar. Taste: it should be slightly saltier than you'd want to sip, because the noodles dilute it. Keep it hot.

Warm the bowls with hot tap water. Boil the noodles in a large pot of unsalted water for about 30 seconds less than the package says, so they finish softening in the broth. Drain well and shake off the water.

Put 1/2 tsp sesame oil and a handful of spinach in each warm bowl, add the noodles and ladle the boiling broth over. Top with sliced chicken, a halved egg, green onion greens and nori. Serve right away with chili oil and sesame seeds.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Cook the eggs straight from room temperature into boiling water. Cold eggs crack and cook unevenly, and 6 1/2 minutes gives a set white with a jammy, custardy yolk.
A bare simmer keeps the broth clear and the chicken juicy. A hard boil clouds the broth and tightens the meat.
Warm bowls matter more than you'd think: noodles cool soup fast, and a cold bowl can drop it to lukewarm before the first bite.
Fresh noodles cook in 1 to 2 minutes. Cook them separately, never in the broth, or their starch makes the broth gummy.
recipe.make_ahead: The broth keeps 4 days in the fridge or 3 months frozen. The marinated eggs are best after 4 hours and keep 3 days. Store noodles and broth separately; leftover noodles go soft in the broth.
variations: Spicy miso: whisk 3 tbsp white miso and 1 tbsp chili bean paste into the hot broth instead of the 1/4 cup soy sauce.
Add corn, bamboo shoots, a pat of butter, or seared mushrooms as toppings.
Vegetarian: use vegetable broth with dried shiitake mushrooms in place of the chicken, and seared tofu on top.

recipe.title: Ramos Gin Fizz
recipe.description: New Orleans gin fizz shaken long with cream, egg white and orange flower water.
steps: Dry-shake everything except the soda for 30 seconds.
Add ice and shake hard for another minute.
Strain into a Collins glass and top with soda so the foam rises above the rim.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: This drink uses raw egg white. Use pasteurized egg white if you prefer, and always for anyone pregnant, older or with a weakened immune system.

recipe.title: Ranch Water
recipe.description: The West Texas porch drink: blanco tequila and lots of fresh lime topped with bubbly Topo Chico mineral water.

ingredients.item: chilled Topo Chico or other sparkling mineral water

steps: Fill a tall glass with ice.
Pour in the tequila and lime juice.
Top with the mineral water and stir gently.
Garnish with the lime wedge.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Build 1 oz lime juice and a pinch of salt over ice and top with 6 oz sparkling mineral water.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Topo Chico is very fizzy and a little salty. Any strongly carbonated mineral water works.
For a little extra orange flavor, add 1/4 oz orange liqueur.

recipe.title: Raspberry Beret
recipe.description: A ruby-red raspberry gin sour: fresh raspberries muddled with lemon and gin, shaken with raspberry liqueur and egg white into a silky pink foam.
steps: Muddle the raspberries in a shaker until completely crushed.
Add the gin, raspberry liqueur, lemon juice, syrup and egg white and shake without ice for 15 seconds.
Add ice and shake hard again.
Double strain into a chilled coupe and garnish with raspberries on a pick.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Muddle raspberries with lemon and syrup, shake with aquafaba and ice, strain into a coupe and top with a splash of sparkling lemonade.

recipe.note: Uses raw egg white; use pasteurized egg white if you prefer.
tips: Double strain through a fine sieve to catch the raspberry seeds.
Ripe, in-season raspberries give the brightest color and flavor.
variations: Use vodka instead of gin for a softer drink.

vegan.title: Vegan Raspberry Beret
vegan.description: The same raspberry gin sour, with aquafaba foam instead of egg white.

ingredients.item: aquafaba (liquid from a can of chickpeas)

steps: Muddle the raspberries in a shaker until completely crushed.
Add the gin, raspberry liqueur, lemon juice, syrup and aquafaba and shake without ice for 15 seconds.
Add ice and shake hard again.
Double strain into a chilled coupe and garnish with raspberries on a pick.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Muddle raspberries with lemon and syrup, shake with aquafaba and ice, strain into a coupe and top with a splash of sparkling lemonade.

vegan.note: Aquafaba foams like aquafaba (liquid from a can of chickpeas); dry shake it hard.
tips: Double strain through a fine sieve to catch the raspberry seeds.
