Ripe, in-season raspberries give the brightest color and flavor.

recipe.title: Raspberry Ginger Whiskey Smash
recipe.description: Raspberries, ginger and lemon shaken with whiskey over ice.
steps: Muddle raspberries with ginger syrup.
Shake with whiskey, lemon and ice; fine-strain into a rocks glass over fresh ice.
Garnish with a raspberry.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Muddle the raspberries with ginger syrup, shake with lemon and ice and strain over ice with a splash of soda.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Raspberry Mint Brandy Sour
recipe.description: Raspberries and gently pressed mint brighten a lemon-brandy sour.
steps: Press raspberries and mint gently with syrup in a shaker.
Add brandy, lemon and ice; shake for 15 seconds and fine-strain into a rocks glass over fresh ice.
Garnish with the mint sprig and two raspberries on a pick.

cocktail.garnish: small mint sprig and two raspberries
cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Muddle raspberries and mint with syrup; shake with 3/4 oz lemon juice and 2 oz cooled black tea, then strain over ice.

recipe.note: An original Relish home cocktail. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Use a gentle press for mint and a fine sieve for raspberry seeds.
recipe.make_ahead: Prepare to order. Keep juices and brewed teas refrigerated until needed.

recipe.title: Ratatouille
recipe.description: The Provençal summer vegetable stew: eggplant, zucchini, peppers and onion each browned in olive oil, then simmered gently with tomatoes, garlic and herbs.

ingredients.item: extra-virgin olive oil, divided, plus more to serve
red or yellow bell peppers, cut into 3/4-inch pieces
ripe tomatoes, chopped, or one 28-oz can whole tomatoes, crushed

steps: Toss the eggplant with 1 teaspoon salt in a colander and let it drain for 20 minutes. Pat it dry.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Brown the eggplant for 8 to 10 minutes, until golden and tender. Set it aside in a bowl.
Add 2 tablespoons oil and brown the zucchini for 5 minutes, until golden but still firm. Add it to the bowl.
Add 2 tablespoons oil, the onion and peppers and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic and tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, herbes de Provence, bay leaf and the remaining salt. Simmer for 10 minutes, until thickened.
Return the eggplant and zucchini, stir gently, cover and simmer over low heat for 15 minutes.
Remove the bay leaf, season with pepper, and serve warm or at room temperature with basil and a drizzle of olive oil.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Browning each vegetable on its own keeps them from turning to mush and gives them a deeper flavor.
Ratatouille is even better the next day, once the flavors have mingled.
recipe.make_ahead: Refrigerate for up to 4 days or freeze for up to 3 months.
variations: Serve over polenta or with a fried egg on top for a full meal.

recipe.title: Remember the Maine
recipe.description: Rye, sweet vermouth and cherry liqueur with an absinthe rinse.

ingredients.item: vegan sweet vermouth (such as Dolin Rouge)

steps: Rinse a chilled coupe with absinthe.
Stir the rest with ice and strain into the glass.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Revolver
recipe.description: Bourbon with coffee liqueur and orange bitters.
steps: Stir everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe and flame an orange peel over it.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Rhubarb Rose Gin Sour
recipe.description: A pale pink gin sour combining tart rhubarb, lemon and a single restrained drop of rosewater.
steps: Add gin, rhubarb syrup, lemon juice and one drop of rosewater to a shaker.
Shake with plenty of ice for 15 seconds. Double-strain into a chilled coupe.
Express the lemon twist over the glass and add it. This sour has no egg-white foam.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake 1 oz rhubarb syrup, 3/4 oz lemon juice, one drop rosewater and 2 oz cooled white tea with ice; strain into a coupe.

recipe.note: An original Relish home cocktail. Please drink responsibly. Use culinary rosewater, never fragrance or essential oil.
tips: For syrup, simmer 1 cup chopped rhubarb stalks with 1/2 cup each sugar and water for 8 minutes; strain and cool. Discard leaves; they are not edible. This preparation adds about 20 minutes if starting from scratch.
recipe.make_ahead: Refrigerate homemade rhubarb syrup for up to 5 days. Shake each drink to order.

recipe.title: Pan-Seared Ribeye Steak
recipe.description: A thick ribeye with a deep crust, basted with butter, garlic and thyme.
steps: Season the steaks with salt and pepper and leave at room temperature 30 minutes.
Heat the oil in a cast-iron skillet until smoking and sear the steaks 3 to 4 minutes per side.
Add the butter, garlic and thyme and baste for 1 to 2 minutes, until 130°F inside for medium-rare.
Rest 8 minutes before slicing.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: USDA's safe minimum for beef steaks is 145°F with a 3-minute rest. 130°F is the usual medium-rare.

recipe.title: Roast Chicken
recipe.description: Golden, crisp-skinned whole roast chicken with lemon, garlic and herbs.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F and pat the chicken very dry.
Rub with butter and season inside and out with salt and pepper.
Stuff with the lemon, garlic and herbs and tie the legs.
Roast 1 hour 10 minutes to 1 hour 20 minutes, until the thigh reads 165°F.
Rest 15 minutes before carving.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Roasted Beet Lentil Goat Cheese Salad
recipe.description: Sweet roasted beets, lentils and arugula with goat cheese, walnuts and lemon-mustard dressing.

ingredients.item: medium beets, peeled and cut into wedges
green lentils (15 oz each), drained and rinsed

steps: Heat oven to 400 F (200 C). Toss beets with 1 tbsp oil and half the salt. Roast for 35 to 40 minutes, turning halfway, until tender.
Toast walnuts in a dry skillet over medium-low heat for 3 minutes. Cool.
Whisk remaining oil, lemon juice, Dijon, remaining salt and pepper. Toss half the dressing with lentils.
Arrange arugula, lentils and warm beets in bowls. Add cheese and walnuts, then drizzle with remaining dressing.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Use goat cheese labeled suitable for vegetarians if that matters to you; rennet varies by producer.
recipe.make_ahead: Refrigerate beets and lentils promptly for up to 3 days. Keep arugula, cheese, walnuts and dressing separate and assemble just before serving.

recipe.title: Roasted Cauliflower Red Lentil Soup
recipe.description: Roasted cauliflower blended into a thick red lentil soup with lemon and cumin.

ingredients.item: large cauliflower, cut into small florets

steps: Heat oven to 425 F (220 C). Toss cauliflower with 1 tbsp oil and half the salt. Roast for 25 minutes, turning once, until golden and soft.
Meanwhile soften onion in remaining oil in a saucepan for 5 minutes. Add garlic, cumin and turmeric for 30 seconds.
Add lentils, water and remaining salt; simmer for 20 minutes until lentils collapse. Add most of the roasted cauliflower and blend carefully with an immersion blender until smooth.
Stir in lemon juice. Divide among bowls and top with reserved cauliflower and parsley.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Remove the pan from heat before blending hot soup. Add water to reach your preferred consistency.
recipe.make_ahead: Refrigerate promptly in shallow containers for up to 3 days. Reheat leftovers to 165 F (74 C).

recipe.title: Roasted Cauliflower Tacos with Lime Crema
recipe.description: Roasted spiced cauliflower in warm tortillas with lime crema and cilantro.
steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Toss cauliflower with oil, chili powder, cumin and salt. Roast 25–30 minutes, turning once, until tender and browned.
Mix sour cream with lime juice. Warm tortillas.
Fill tortillas with cauliflower; drizzle with crema and sprinkle with cilantro.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Roasted Red Pepper and White Bean Soup
recipe.description: A silky blended soup of roasted red peppers and cannellini beans with smoked paprika and a squeeze of lemon. Ready in 30 minutes.
steps: Cook onion in oil over medium heat for 5 minutes. Add garlic and paprika for 30 seconds.
Add peppers, beans and broth. Simmer 12 minutes. Blend until smooth, working carefully with hot soup.
Stir in lemon juice; season and warm through.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Roasted Red Pepper Turkey Chili
recipe.description: Ground turkey, kidney beans and white beans in a tomato chili with roasted red peppers.

ingredients.item: kidney beans (15 oz), drained and rinsed
cannellini beans (15 oz), drained and rinsed
roasted red peppers (12 oz), drained and chopped

steps: Heat oil in a saucepan and soften onion for 5 minutes. Add turkey and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, breaking it up, until it reaches 165 F (74 C).
Add garlic, cumin, paprika, chili and oregano and stir for 30 seconds.
Add beans, peppers, tomatoes, water and salt. Simmer partly covered for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thickened.
Taste, adjust salt if necessary and finish with cilantro.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Use canned kidney beans as specified; dry kidney beans require separate safe preparation and are not a direct substitute.
recipe.make_ahead: Refrigerate promptly in shallow containers for up to 3 days. Reheat leftovers to 165 F (74 C).

recipe.title: Roasted Tomato Eggplant Lentil Pasta
recipe.description: Roasted eggplant and tomatoes turn canned lentils into a hearty plant-based pasta sauce.

ingredients.item: green lentils (15 oz), drained and rinsed

steps: Heat oven to 425 F (220 C). Toss eggplant and tomatoes with oil, garlic, oregano, salt and pepper. Spread over two sheet pans and roast for 25 to 30 minutes, turning once, until eggplant is soft.
Meanwhile cook rigatoni according to the package. Reserve 1 cup pasta water and drain.
Tip roasted vegetables into the pasta pot, crush some tomatoes with a spoon and add lentils and 1/2 cup pasta water. Simmer for 3 minutes.
Toss in pasta and basil, adding more pasta water as needed for a loose sauce.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Roast eggplant until fully soft, not merely browned on the outside. No cheese is needed for this sauce.
recipe.make_ahead: Refrigerate promptly in shallow containers for up to 3 days. Reheat leftovers to 165 F (74 C).

recipe.title: Rob Roy
recipe.description: A Scotch Manhattan with sweet vermouth and bitters.

ingredients.item: vegan sweet vermouth (such as Dolin Rouge)

steps: Stir everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Roffignac
recipe.description: New Orleans highball of Cognac and raspberry syrup with soda.
steps: Fill a highball with ice and add the Cognac and syrup.
Top with soda and stir.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Raspberry syrup topped with ginger ale and a squeeze of lemon.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Ciorbă de Burtă (Romanian Tripe Soup)
recipe.description: Romania's beloved sour soup: tender strips of beef tripe in a rich broth, made silky with sour cream and egg yolk, and sharpened with vinegar and garlic. Served with hot peppers.

ingredients.item: celery root, peeled, or 2 celery stalks
garlic, crushed to a paste with a pinch of salt
white wine vinegar, plus more to taste
hot peppers and extra sour cream, to serve

steps: Rinse the tripe well, cover with cold water, boil 10 minutes, then drain and rinse. This removes strong odors.
Put the tripe, bones, bay leaves and 12 cups water in a large pot. Simmer gently, skimming often, for 2 1/2 to 3 hours, until the tripe is very tender.
Add the carrots, parsnip, celery root and onion for the last 45 minutes.
Lift out the tripe and vegetables. Strain the broth. Slice the tripe into thin strips and the carrot into matchsticks, and return them to the broth with the salt.

Whisk the sour cream and egg yolks in a bowl. Slowly whisk in 2 ladles of hot broth, then stir the mixture back into the pot over low heat. Heat gently until steaming (160°F) so the yolks cook through, but don't let it boil.
Stir in half the garlic paste and the vinegar. Taste and add more vinegar or salt until it's pleasantly sour. Serve with hot peppers, more garlic and sour cream on the side.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Temper the egg yolks with hot broth before adding them to the pot, and never boil afterward, or they'll curdle.
The soup should taste clearly sour. Add vinegar a spoonful at a time and taste as you go.
Cleaned, pre-cooked tripe from the butcher cuts the simmering time to about 1 1/2 hours.
recipe.make_ahead: The tripe and broth keep 4 days before adding the sour cream mixture. Reheat gently once thickened.
variations: Ciorbă de ciocănele: make it with pork shanks instead of tripe.

vegetarian.title: Romanian Sour Mushroom Soup
vegetarian.description: The tripe soup's silky sour cream, egg yolk, vinegar and garlic finish, made with strips of oyster mushrooms in a root vegetable broth.

ingredients.item: celery root, peeled, or 2 celery stalks
garlic, crushed to a paste with a pinch of salt
white wine vinegar, plus more to taste
hot peppers and extra sour cream, to serve

steps: Simmer the broth with the carrots, parsnip, celery root, onion and bay leaves for 30 minutes. Lift out the vegetables and cut the carrot into matchsticks.
Brown the mushroom strips in the oil over high heat for 6 to 8 minutes. Add them and the carrot to the broth with the salt and simmer 10 minutes.

Whisk the sour cream and egg yolks in a bowl. Slowly whisk in 2 ladles of hot broth, then stir the mixture back into the pot over low heat. Heat gently until steaming (160°F) so the yolks cook through, but don't let it boil.
Stir in half the garlic paste and the vinegar. Taste and add more vinegar or salt until it's pleasantly sour. Serve with hot peppers, more garlic and sour cream on the side.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Torn oyster mushrooms give the soft, ribbony texture of the sliced tripe.
vegetarian.make_ahead: The broth and mushrooms keep 4 days before adding the sour cream mixture.

vegan.title: Vegan Romanian Sour Mushroom Soup
vegan.description: Oyster mushrooms in a root vegetable broth, thickened with cashew cream and finished with vinegar and garlic.

ingredients.item: celery root, peeled, or 2 celery stalks
raw cashews, soaked 2 hours and drained
garlic, crushed to a paste with a pinch of salt
white wine vinegar, plus more to taste

steps: Simmer the broth with the carrots, parsnip, celery root, onion and bay leaves for 30 minutes. Lift out the vegetables and cut the carrot into matchsticks.
Brown the mushroom strips in the oil over high heat for 6 to 8 minutes. Add them and the carrot to the broth with the salt and simmer 10 minutes.
Blend the cashews and cornstarch with 1 1/2 cups of the hot broth until completely smooth. Stir it into the pot and simmer gently for 3 minutes, until silky.
Stir in half the garlic paste and the vinegar. Taste and add more vinegar or salt until it's pleasantly sour. Serve with hot peppers and more garlic on the side.
vegan.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Cashew cream blended with a little cornstarch gives the creamy body that sour cream and egg yolk give the original.
vegan.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge; reheat gently.

recipe.title: Ropa Vieja (Cuban Shredded Beef)
recipe.description: Cuba's national dish: flank steak braised until it falls into strands, then simmered in a sofrito of peppers, onion, tomato, cumin and olives. Serve with rice, black beans and sweet plantains.

ingredients.item: green bell pepper, sliced into strips
red bell pepper, sliced into strips
white rice, black beans and fried sweet plantains, to serve

steps: Put the steak, bay leaf, halved onion and salt in a pot and cover with water. Simmer, partly covered, for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, until very tender. Cool slightly in the liquid, then shred along the grain with two forks. Keep 1 cup of the broth.
In a wide pan, cook the sliced onion and peppers in the olive oil for 8 to 10 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic, cumin and oregano and stir for 1 minute.
Add the wine and let it bubble for 2 minutes, then the tomato sauce, reserved broth, shredded beef, olives and capers.
Simmer, uncovered, for 20 to 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sauce is thick and clings to the beef. Taste for salt.
Serve with white rice, black beans and fried sweet plantains.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Flank steak's long fibers are what give ropa vieja its "old clothes" strands. Shred along the grain, not across it.
Letting the beef cool in its broth keeps it juicy.
Simmering the shredded beef in the sauce at the end lets it soak up all the flavor.
recipe.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge and tastes even better the next day. Freezes well for 3 months.
variations: Pressure cooker: cook the steak for 45 minutes on high, then finish in the sofrito as written.

vegetarian.title: Vegetarian Ropa Vieja
vegetarian.description: Young jackfruit and shredded oyster mushrooms simmered in the classic sofrito with peppers, olives and cumin.

ingredients.item: young green jackfruit in brine, drained and rinsed
green bell pepper, sliced into strips
red bell pepper, sliced into strips
white rice, black beans and fried sweet plantains, to serve

steps: Pull the jackfruit pieces into shreds with your fingers, discarding any hard seeds.
Brown the mushrooms in 1 tbsp oil over high heat for 5 minutes. Add the remaining oil, onion and peppers and cook 8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic, cumin and oregano for 1 minute.
Add the wine for 2 minutes, then the tomato sauce, broth, bay leaf, jackfruit, olives, capers and salt.
Simmer, uncovered, for 20 to 25 minutes, mashing the jackfruit a little, until thick and saucy. Serve with rice, black beans and plantains.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Young green jackfruit in brine (not syrup) shreds into strands just like the beef.
vegetarian.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge or 3 months frozen.

vegan.title: Vegan Ropa Vieja
vegan.description: Young jackfruit and shredded oyster mushrooms simmered in the classic sofrito with peppers, olives and cumin.

ingredients.item: young green jackfruit in brine, drained and rinsed
green bell pepper, sliced into strips
red bell pepper, sliced into strips
white rice, black beans and fried sweet plantains, to serve

steps: Pull the jackfruit pieces into shreds with your fingers, discarding any hard seeds.
Brown the mushrooms in 1 tbsp oil over high heat for 5 minutes. Add the remaining oil, onion and peppers and cook 8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic, cumin and oregano for 1 minute.
Add the wine for 2 minutes, then the tomato sauce, broth, bay leaf, jackfruit, olives, capers and salt.
Simmer, uncovered, for 20 to 25 minutes, mashing the jackfruit a little, until thick and saucy. Serve with rice, black beans and plantains.
vegan.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Young green jackfruit in brine (not syrup) shreds into strands just like the beef.
vegan.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge or 3 months frozen.

recipe.title: Royal Bermuda Yacht Club
recipe.description: Barbados rum, lime, falernum and orange curaçao.
steps: Shake everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Rum Runner
recipe.description: Florida Keys tiki drink of rum, banana and blackberry liqueurs and juices.
steps: Shake everything with ice.
Strain into a hurricane glass with ice.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Pineapple juice, orange juice and banana nectar with grenadine.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Russian Spring Punch
recipe.description: Dick Bradsell's London party drink from the 1980s: vodka, lemon and blackcurrant shaken, then topped tall with sparkling wine.

ingredients.item: chilled vegan dry sparkling wine (such as Mionetto Organic Prosecco)

steps: Fill a highball glass with ice.
Add the vodka, lemon juice, crème de cassis and simple syrup to a shaker with ice and shake for 10 seconds.
Strain into the glass.
Top with the sparkling wine, stir once gently and garnish with the blackberries and lemon slice.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake 1 oz lemon juice and 1 oz blackcurrant syrup with ice, strain over ice and top with 4 oz sparkling white grape juice.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Add the sparkling wine last and stir only once, so it keeps its bubbles.
No cassis? Chambord or another berry liqueur makes a close substitute.
recipe.make_ahead: For a crowd, mix the vodka, lemon, cassis and syrup in a jug ahead of time and keep it in the fridge. Top each glass with wine as you serve.

recipe.title: Rusty Nail
recipe.description: Scotch and Drambuie over ice.
steps: Stir with ice.
Strain over a large cube in a rocks glass.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Salmon with Orange-Fennel Salad
recipe.description: Crisp-edged salmon with a cool salad of shaved fennel, orange, arugula and olives.

ingredients.item: fennel bulb, very thinly sliced, fronds reserved
oranges, peeled and cut into segments, juice reserved

steps: Pat salmon dry and season with half the salt and all the pepper. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat.
Cook salmon skin-side down for 5 minutes, then turn carefully and cook 3 to 5 minutes more, until the thickest part reaches 145 F (63 C). Rest while assembling the salad.
Whisk the remaining oil with lemon juice, reserved orange juice and remaining salt. Toss with fennel, orange segments, arugula and olives.
Serve each fillet beside the salad. Chop a few reserved fennel fronds and scatter over the plate.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Use a sharp knife or guarded mandoline for thin fennel. Cook fish fully rather than using color alone to judge doneness.
recipe.make_ahead: Keep salad and cooked fish separate, refrigerate promptly and use within 2 days. Dress salad just before serving.

recipe.title: Salty Dog
recipe.description: Gin or vodka with grapefruit juice in a salt-rimmed glass.
steps: Rim a highball with salt and fill with ice.
Add the spirit and grapefruit juice and stir.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Grapefruit juice topped with grapefruit soda in a salted glass.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Samgyetang (Korean Ginseng Chicken Soup)
recipe.description: Korea's restorative summer soup: a whole small chicken stuffed with sweet rice, ginseng, jujubes and garlic, simmered until falling-off-the-bone tender in a milky broth.

ingredients.item: fresh ginseng roots (or 2 tbsp dried ginseng)
salt and black pepper, at the table

steps: Rinse the hens inside and out and pat dry. Stuff each with soaked rice, 1 ginseng root, 1 jujube and 4 garlic cloves. Don't pack it too tightly.
Cross the legs and tie them, or tuck one leg through a small slit in the other, to keep the stuffing in.
Put the hens in a pot with the water, ginger, the rest of the garlic and jujubes, and any leftover rice.
Bring to a boil, skim, then simmer, covered, for 50 to 60 minutes, until the meat pulls easily from the bone and the rice is soft.
Serve each hen in a large bowl of broth, scattered with green onion. Season with salt and pepper at the table and eat with kimchi.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Leave room for the rice to swell or it will burst out of the hen.
Samgyetang is seasoned by each diner at the table, so the broth is cooked without salt.
Look for samgyetang kits at Korean markets; they bundle the rice, jujubes and dried ginseng.
recipe.make_ahead: Keeps 3 days in the fridge; reheat gently. Leftover broth makes a lovely rice porridge.
variations: Use a 3-lb whole chicken for 4 people and simmer 1 hour 15 minutes.

vegetarian.title: Ginseng Mushroom Soup with Sweet Rice
vegetarian.description: A vegetarian take on samgyetang: ginseng, jujubes, garlic and sweet rice simmered with shiitake, king oyster mushrooms and tofu into a soothing broth.

ingredients.item: firm tofu, cut in large cubes
fresh ginseng roots (or 2 tbsp dried ginseng)
salt and black pepper, at the table

steps: Simmer the water with the shiitake, kombu, ginseng, ginger, garlic and jujubes for 20 minutes. Remove the kombu.
Add the soaked rice and simmer 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until the rice is soft and the broth turns cloudy and silky.
Add the king oyster mushrooms and tofu and simmer 5 minutes more.
Serve in large bowls, scattered with green onion. Season with salt and pepper at the table and eat with kimchi.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: The shiitake and kombu build a deep, savory broth in place of the chicken.
vegetarian.make_ahead: Keeps 3 days in the fridge; add a splash of water when reheating, as the rice thickens it.

vegan.title: Ginseng Mushroom Soup with Sweet Rice
vegan.description: A vegan take on samgyetang: ginseng, jujubes, garlic and sweet rice simmered with shiitake, king oyster mushrooms and tofu into a soothing broth.

ingredients.item: firm tofu, cut in large cubes
fresh ginseng roots (or 2 tbsp dried ginseng)
salt and black pepper, at the table

steps: Simmer the water with the shiitake, kombu, ginseng, ginger, garlic and jujubes for 20 minutes. Remove the kombu.
Add the soaked rice and simmer 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until the rice is soft and the broth turns cloudy and silky.
Add the king oyster mushrooms and tofu and simmer 5 minutes more.
Serve in large bowls, scattered with green onion. Season with salt and pepper at the table and eat with kimchi.
vegan.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: The shiitake and kombu build a deep, savory broth in place of the chicken.
vegan.make_ahead: Keeps 3 days in the fridge; add a splash of water when reheating, as the rice thickens it.

recipe.title: Vegetable Samosas
recipe.description: Crisp, flaky pastries filled with spiced potatoes and peas, from India.

ingredients.item: vegetable oil, plus more for frying

steps: Mix the flour, carom seeds and a pinch of salt, rub in the 1/4 cup oil, then add water a little at a time to make a stiff dough. Cover and rest 30 minutes.
Heat 1 tbsp oil, fry the cumin seeds, then add the chile and ginger. Add the potatoes, peas, spices and salt, cook 3 minutes and stir in the cilantro. Cool.
Divide the dough into 6 balls, roll each into an oval and cut in half.
Form each half into a cone, sealing the seam with water, fill with potato mixture and pinch the top closed.
Fry in oil at 325°F for 10 to 12 minutes, turning, until golden and crisp. Serve with mint or tamarind chutney.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Red Wine Sangria
recipe.description: Spain's party punch: fruity red wine soaked overnight with orange, lemon, apple, brandy and a little orange liqueur, then poured over ice.

ingredients.item: chilled vegan dry red wine (such as Yellow Tail Shiraz)
apple, cored and cut into small cubes

steps: In a large pitcher, stir the sugar into the orange juice, brandy and orange liqueur until it dissolves.
Add the orange, lemon and apple and the cinnamon stick, if using.
Pour in the wine and stir.
Cover and chill for at least 4 hours, or overnight.
Just before serving, stir in the sparkling water, if using, and pour over ice with some of the fruit in each glass.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Mix 3 cups red grape juice, 1 cup orange juice, the sliced fruit and a cinnamon stick, chill, and top with lemon-lime soda.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Use a fruity, not-too-oaky red. Spanish Garnacha or Tempranillo is traditional.
Taste after chilling and add more sugar if needed. Cold drinks taste less sweet.
recipe.make_ahead: Make it the day before. The flavor gets better as the fruit soaks.
variations: White Sangria: use a dry white wine and add peaches or green grapes.

recipe.title: Saratoga
recipe.description: Equal parts rye and brandy with sweet vermouth and bitters.

ingredients.item: vegan sweet vermouth (such as Dolin Rouge)

steps: Stir everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Saturn
recipe.description: A 1967 award-winning tiki classic: gin with lemon, passion fruit, falernum and almond orgeat. Bright, tropical and floral, served up with a lemon twist.
steps: Shake the gin, lemon juice, passion fruit syrup, falernum and orgeat hard with ice.
Fine strain into a chilled coupe.
Garnish with a lemon twist curled around the rim, like the rings of Saturn.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake passion fruit syrup, lemon and a little orgeat with ice, strain over ice and top with ginger ale.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: The tiki-bar version is flash-blended with crushed ice and served in a tall glass; shaken and served up, it's crisper.
A juniper-forward London dry gin holds up well against the tropical syrups.
variations: Flash blend with 1 cup crushed ice and serve in a pilsner glass with a lemon peel ring.

recipe.title: Sauerbraten
recipe.description: German pot roast marinated for days in spiced vinegar, with a sweet-sour gingersnap gravy.
steps: Boil the vinegar, water, vegetables, spices and sugar with 1 tsp salt. Cool and pour over the beef.
Marinate in the fridge 3 days, turning daily.
Dry the beef and brown it in the oil, then add the strained marinade. Cover and simmer 2 1/2 to 3 hours.
Remove the beef. Stir the gingersnaps and raisins into the liquid and simmer until thick.
Slice the beef and serve with the gravy.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Sazerac
recipe.description: New Orleans rye with Peychaud's bitters in an absinthe-rinsed glass.

ingredients.item: sugar cube or 1/4 oz simple syrup

steps: Rinse a chilled rocks glass with absinthe and discard the excess.
Stir the rye, sugar and bitters with ice.
Strain into the glass with no ice and express a lemon peel over it.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Scofflaw
recipe.description: Rye and dry vermouth with lemon and grenadine.

ingredients.item: vegan dry vermouth (such as Dolin Dry)

steps: Shake everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Scorpion Bowl
recipe.description: A shareable tiki punch of rum, brandy, citrus and orgeat.
steps: Shake or blend everything with crushed ice.
Pour into a punch bowl over more crushed ice and serve with long straws.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Orange, lemon and orgeat topped with ginger ale.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Soft Scrambled Eggs
recipe.description: Creamy, slow-cooked scrambled eggs.
steps: Whisk the eggs with the milk and a pinch of salt.
Melt the butter in a nonstick pan over medium-low heat.
Add the eggs and stir slowly with a spatula, pushing them from the edges, until softly set, about 3 minutes.
Take off the heat while still glossy and top with pepper and chives.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Soft scrambled eggs are not fully firm. For anyone pregnant, older or with a weakened immune system, cook them until firm or use pasteurized eggs.

recipe.title: Screwdriver
recipe.description: Vodka and orange juice over ice.
steps: Fill a highball with ice.
Add the vodka and orange juice and stir.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Orange juice with a splash of lemon-lime soda.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Sea Breeze
recipe.description: Vodka with tart cranberry and a splash of grapefruit, poured over ice. Pink, easy and very refreshing.
steps: Fill a highball glass with ice.
Pour in the vodka, cranberry juice and grapefruit juice and stir briefly.
Garnish with the orange twist and cherry.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Build 4 oz cranberry juice and 2 oz grapefruit juice over ice and top with a splash of soda water.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Fresh grapefruit juice makes a big difference: it's sharper and less sweet than bottled.
For a foamy top, shake everything with ice and strain over fresh ice instead of building it.
variations: Bay Breeze: use pineapple juice in place of the grapefruit juice.
Cape Codder: leave out the grapefruit juice and garnish with lime.

recipe.title: Seared Tuna with Sesame Cucumber Rice
recipe.description: Fully cooked sesame-crusted tuna with cucumber rice and a soy-lime dressing.

ingredients.item: tuna steaks (4 to 5 oz each), about 3/4 inch thick

steps: Pat tuna dry and press sesame seeds onto both faces. Heat oil in a nonstick skillet over medium heat.
Cook steaks for about 4 to 6 minutes per side, lowering heat if seeds brown too fast, until the centers reach 145 F (63 C). This recipe serves tuna fully cooked, not rare.
Mix soy sauce, lime juice and vinegar. Toss hot rice with cucumber and scallions.
Slice the tuna and serve over rice with the dressing spooned on top.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Cooking time depends on thickness. Use a thermometer and avoid burning the sesame coating.
recipe.make_ahead: Refrigerate promptly and use within 2 days. Reheat leftovers to 165 F (74 C).

recipe.title: Seelbach
recipe.description: Bourbon, orange liqueur and lots of bitters, topped with Champagne.

ingredients.item: vegan Champagne (such as Moët & Chandon Impérial)

steps: Stir the bourbon, Cointreau and bitters in a flute.
Top with Champagne.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Thieboudienne
recipe.description: Senegal's national dish of fish and vegetables cooked in tomato, with the rice cooked in the broth.

ingredients.item: cassava or sweet potato, in chunks

steps: Cut slits in the fish and stuff with the rof. Brown the fish in the oil and remove.
Cook the onion, then the tomato paste for 5 minutes. Add 8 cups water and the bouillon.
Add the vegetables and fish and simmer until each is tender, lifting them out as they are done.
Measure about 4 1/2 cups of the broth into the pot, add the rice, cover and cook on low 25 minutes.
Serve the rice topped with the fish and vegetables.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Sesame Tofu with Snap Peas and Rice
recipe.description: Golden tofu and crisp snap peas in a sesame-soy glaze, served over rice.
steps: Whisk soy sauce, vinegar, maple syrup, ginger, cornstarch and water. Pat tofu dry.
Brown tofu in neutral oil over medium-high heat for 8 to 10 minutes, turning carefully.
Add snap peas and cook for 2 minutes. Add sauce and simmer for 1 to 2 minutes until glossy.
Finish with sesame oil and seeds. Serve over hot rice.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Press tofu for 15 minutes or use ready-pressed tofu. Soy sauce in this recipe contains wheat.
recipe.make_ahead: Refrigerate promptly in shallow containers for up to 3 days. Reheat leftovers to 165 F (74 C).

recipe.title: Sex on the Beach
recipe.description: Vodka, peach schnapps, orange and cranberry.
steps: Fill a highball with ice.
Add the vodka, schnapps and orange juice, then pour the cranberry over the top.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Orange and cranberry juice with peach nectar.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Shaft
recipe.description: Espresso, rum, coffee liqueur and cream, a creamy coffee cocktail.
steps: Shake everything hard with ice.
Strain into a chilled glass.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake espresso and syrup with a splash of cream.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Shakshuka
recipe.description: Eggs poached in a spiced tomato and pepper sauce, from North Africa and the Middle East.
steps: Cook the onion and pepper in the oil until soft, then add the garlic and spices.
Add the tomatoes, season and simmer 10 minutes until thick.
Make 6 wells and crack in the eggs.
Cover and cook 5 to 8 minutes until the whites set.
Top with feta and cilantro and serve with bread.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Shamrock
recipe.description: Irish whiskey and dry vermouth with green Chartreuse and crème de menthe.

ingredients.item: vegan dry vermouth (such as Dolin Dry)

steps: Stir everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Shawarma-Spiced Chickpea Pitas
recipe.description: Roasted spiced chickpeas in warm pitas with crisp vegetables and lemon tahini sauce.

ingredients.item: chickpeas (15 oz each), drained and rinsed

steps: Heat oven to 425 F (220 C). Pat chickpeas dry and toss with oil, cumin, coriander, paprika, cinnamon and salt. Roast for 20 to 25 minutes, shaking once.
Whisk tahini, lemon juice, water and garlic until smooth; add water a teaspoon at a time if too thick.
Warm pitas according to the package and split them to form pockets.
Fill with lettuce, cucumber, tomatoes and chickpeas, then drizzle with tahini sauce.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: These are chickpea-filled home pitas using a shawarma-inspired spice mix, rather than meat shawarma. Tahini contains sesame.
recipe.make_ahead: Refrigerate chickpeas and cut vegetables promptly for up to 3 days; store separately from pitas and sauce. Reheat chickpeas to 165 F (74 C).

recipe.title: Sheet-Pan Tofu Fajita Bowls
recipe.description: Roasted spiced tofu, bell peppers and red onion over rice with avocado, cilantro and lime.
steps: Heat oven to 425 F (220 C). Pat tofu dry and cut into 1-inch cubes.
Toss tofu, peppers and onion with oil, paprika, cumin, garlic powder and salt. Spread over two sheet pans in one layer.
Roast for 22 to 25 minutes, turning halfway, until tofu edges are golden and the vegetables are tender.
Divide hot rice among bowls. Add roasted tofu and vegetables, avocado, cilantro and lime wedges.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Start with tofu pressed for 15 minutes or ready-pressed tofu; pressing time is included in prep. Keep avocado fresh until serving.
recipe.make_ahead: Refrigerate tofu, vegetables and rice promptly for up to 3 days. Reheat to 165 F (74 C) and add fresh avocado afterward.

recipe.title: Shepherd's Pie
recipe.description: Savory ground lamb and vegetables in gravy, topped with golden mashed potatoes.
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F.
Brown the lamb with the onion and carrots, then add the garlic and tomato paste.
Stir in the flour, then the broth and Worcestershire, and simmer 10 minutes until thick. Add the peas.
Spread in a baking dish and top with the mashed potatoes, roughing up the top with a fork.
Sprinkle with cheese and bake 25 to 30 minutes until golden.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Sherry Cobbler
recipe.description: Amontillado sherry shaken with sugar and orange over crushed ice with berries.
steps: Shake the sherry, syrup and one orange slice with ice.
Strain into a glass packed with crushed ice.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Sherry Flip
recipe.description: Sherry shaken with a whole egg and sugar, topped with nutmeg.

ingredients.item: vegan oloroso sherry (such as Barbadillo Oloroso Seco)

steps: Dry-shake everything, then shake again with ice.
Strain into a small chilled glass and grate nutmeg on top.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: This drink uses a raw whole egg. Use a pasteurized egg if you prefer, and always for anyone pregnant, older or with a weakened immune system.

recipe.title: Sherry Sangaree
recipe.description: One of the oldest mixed drinks: rich oloroso sherry lightly sweetened, chilled and served with a dusting of nutmeg and a twist of lemon.

ingredients.item: vegan oloroso sherry (such as Barbadillo Oloroso Seco)

steps: Stir the sherry and syrup with ice until very cold.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
Grate nutmeg over the top and garnish with a lemon twist.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Stir cold black tea with a little prune or raisin syrup and top with nutmeg.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Oloroso is nutty and rich; amontillado gives a lighter, drier drink.
Fresh nutmeg is essential; its aroma is a big part of the drink.
variations: Port Sangaree: use ruby port instead of sherry.
Serve it long over ice with a splash of soda for a lighter aperitif.

recipe.title: Shrimp and Grits
recipe.description: Southern creamy cheese grits topped with shrimp in a bacon, garlic and lemon pan sauce.
steps: Bring the milk, water and a pinch of salt to a boil, whisk in the grits and simmer 20 to 25 minutes, stirring often.
Stir the cheese and butter into the grits.
Cook the bacon until crisp, then remove, leaving the fat.
Season the shrimp with Cajun seasoning and cook in the bacon fat 2 minutes per side with the garlic.
Add the lemon juice and bacon, spoon over the grits and top with green onions.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Shrimp Scampi
recipe.description: Linguine tossed with plump, garlicky shrimp in a glossy white wine, lemon and butter sauce. A restaurant favorite on the table in 30 minutes.

ingredients.item: large shrimp (16 to 20 per lb), peeled and deveined
salt, plus more for the pasta water
dry white wine (such as Pinot Grigio or Sauvignon Blanc)
cold unsalted butter, cut into cubes

steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and salt it until it tastes like the sea. Pat the shrimp very dry and season with 1 tsp salt and the pepper.
Drop in the pasta and set a timer for 2 minutes less than the package says.

Meanwhile, heat 2 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add the shrimp in one layer and cook 1 minute without moving, until pink underneath. Flip and cook 30 seconds more, then move to a plate. They should still be slightly translucent in the middle.
Lower the heat to medium. Add the remaining oil, the garlic and pepper flakes and cook about 1 minute, stirring, until the garlic is pale golden. Watch it closely; burnt garlic is bitter.
Pour in the wine and simmer 2 to 3 minutes until reduced by half. Scoop out 1 cup of the starchy pasta water before you drain the pasta.
Add the drained pasta, the lemon juice and zest and 1/2 cup pasta water to the skillet. Toss over the heat for 1 minute.

Turn off the heat. Add the cold butter a few cubes at a time, tossing constantly until it melts into a creamy, glossy sauce. Add the shrimp and parsley and toss 30 seconds to finish cooking the shrimp. Add more pasta water if it looks dry. Taste for salt, top with Parmesan and serve right away.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Pull the shrimp while they're still a little translucent. They finish cooking in the hot pasta and stay tender instead of rubbery.
Cold butter, added off the heat, blends with the starchy pasta water into a creamy sauce. Hot butter or high heat makes it separate and greasy.
Starchy pasta water is the glue of the sauce. Always save more than you think you'll need.
Dry shrimp sear; wet shrimp steam. Pat them dry with paper towels before seasoning.
recipe.make_ahead: Best eaten right away. Leftovers keep 2 days in the fridge; reheat gently in a skillet with a splash of water, or the shrimp will toughen.
variations: No wine: use 1/2 cup chicken broth plus an extra squeeze of lemon.
Add 2 cups baby spinach or halved cherry tomatoes with the pasta.
Lighter: serve the shrimp and sauce over zucchini noodles or with crusty bread instead of pasta.

recipe.title: Sidecar
recipe.description: Cognac, orange liqueur and lemon in a sugar-rimmed coupe.
steps: Rim a coupe with sugar.
Shake everything with ice and strain into the glass.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Siesta
recipe.description: Tequila, Campari, grapefruit and lime.
steps: Shake everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Silver Fizz
recipe.description: Gin, lemon and sugar with egg white, topped with soda.
steps: Dry-shake everything except the soda, then shake again with ice.
Strain into a highball without ice and top with soda.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: This drink uses raw egg white. Use pasteurized egg white if you prefer, and always for anyone pregnant, older or with a weakened immune system.

recipe.title: Singapore Sling
recipe.description: Gin with cherry, pineapple, lime and Bénédictine, the Raffles Hotel classic.
steps: Shake everything with ice.
Strain into a hurricane or Collins glass with ice.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Pineapple, lime, cherry juice and grenadine topped with ginger ale.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Sloe Gin Fizz
recipe.description: Ruby-red sloe gin shaken with lemon and a little sugar, then topped with soda. Fruity, tart and light.
steps: Fill a highball glass with ice.
Add the sloe gin, lemon juice and simple syrup to a shaker with ice and shake for 10 seconds.
Strain into the glass.
Top with the soda water, stir once and garnish with the lemon slice.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake 1 oz plum or blackcurrant syrup with 3/4 oz lemon juice, strain over ice and top with 4 oz soda water.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Sloe gin is sweeter and lower in alcohol than regular gin. Taste before adding the syrup.
variations: Swap half the sloe gin for London dry gin for a drier, stronger drink.

recipe.title: Smoky Black Bean and Quinoa Stuffed Peppers
recipe.description: Roasted pepper halves filled with black beans, quinoa, corn and smoky tomato, finished with cilantro.

ingredients.item: large red bell peppers, halved lengthwise and seeded
black beans (15 oz), drained and rinsed

steps: Heat oven to 400 F (200 C). Place peppers cut-side up in a baking dish. Cover loosely with foil and bake for 15 minutes.
Meanwhile bring quinoa and water to a boil. Cover and simmer gently for 15 minutes or until tender; stand off heat for 5 minutes and fluff.
Heat oil in a skillet over medium heat. Soften onion for 5 minutes, add garlic for 30 seconds, then add beans, corn, tomatoes, paprika, cumin and salt. Simmer for 5 minutes.

Fold quinoa into the filling. Divide among the pepper halves and bake uncovered for 20 to 25 minutes, until peppers are tender and the filling is piping hot. Scatter with cilantro; serve two halves per person.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Quinoa must be cooked before stuffing so the filling stays moist and the grains are tender.
recipe.make_ahead: Cool promptly and refrigerate for up to 3 days. Reheat covered until the center reaches 165 F (74 C).

recipe.title: Som Tam (Thai Green Papaya Salad)
recipe.description: Thailand's crunchy, fiery salad: shredded green papaya pounded with garlic, chilies, lime, fish sauce and palm sugar, with tomatoes, long beans, peanuts and dried shrimp.

ingredients.item: Thai bird's eye chilies, to taste
yard-long beans or 6 green beans, cut into 2-inch pieces

steps: In a large mortar, pound the garlic and chilies to a rough paste.
Add the palm sugar and pound until it softens.
Add the long beans, dried shrimp and peanuts and pound a few times, just to bruise the beans and break the peanuts.
Add the fish sauce, lime juice and tamarind paste, if using, and stir until the sugar dissolves.
Add the papaya and tomatoes. Pound lightly while turning everything with a spoon, for about 1 minute, until the papaya softens slightly and soaks up the dressing.
Taste: it should be sour, salty, sweet and spicy. Adjust with more lime, fish sauce or sugar and serve right away.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: No mortar? Mash the garlic, chilies and sugar in a large bowl with the end of a rolling pin, then toss everything together.
Use a julienne peeler for the papaya. Shreds that are too thick won't soak up the dressing.
Shredded carrot or cucumber can stand in for green papaya.
variations: Serve with sticky rice and grilled chicken for the classic Isaan meal.

vegetarian.title: Vegetarian Som Tam
vegetarian.description: Thailand's crunchy, fiery green papaya salad, seasoned with soy sauce and lime instead of fish sauce and dried shrimp.

ingredients.item: Thai bird's eye chilies, to taste
yard-long beans or 6 green beans, cut into 2-inch pieces

steps: In a large mortar, pound the garlic and chilies to a rough paste.
Add the palm sugar and pound until it softens.
Add the long beans and peanuts and pound a few times, just to bruise the beans and break the peanuts.
Add the soy sauce, lime juice and tamarind paste, if using, and stir until the sugar dissolves.
Add the papaya and tomatoes. Pound lightly while turning everything with a spoon, for about 1 minute, until the papaya softens slightly and soaks up the dressing.
Taste: it should be sour, salty, sweet and spicy. Adjust with more lime, soy sauce or sugar and serve right away.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: No mortar? Mash the garlic, chilies and sugar in a large bowl with the end of a rolling pin, then toss everything together.
Use a julienne peeler for the papaya. Shreds that are too thick won't soak up the dressing.
For a gluten-free version, use tamari instead of soy sauce.

vegan.title: Vegan Som Tam
vegan.description: Thailand's crunchy, fiery green papaya salad, seasoned with soy sauce and lime instead of fish sauce and dried shrimp.

ingredients.item: Thai bird's eye chilies, to taste
yard-long beans or 6 green beans, cut into 2-inch pieces

steps: In a large mortar, pound the garlic and chilies to a rough paste.
Add the palm sugar and pound until it softens.
Add the long beans and peanuts and pound a few times, just to bruise the beans and break the peanuts.
Add the soy sauce, lime juice and tamarind paste, if using, and stir until the sugar dissolves.
Add the papaya and tomatoes. Pound lightly while turning everything with a spoon, for about 1 minute, until the papaya softens slightly and soaks up the dressing.
Taste: it should be sour, salty, sweet and spicy. Adjust with more lime, soy sauce or sugar and serve right away.
vegan.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: No mortar? Mash the garlic, chilies and sugar in a large bowl with the end of a rolling pin, then toss everything together.
Use a julienne peeler for the papaya. Shreds that are too thick won't soak up the dressing.
For a gluten-free version, use tamari instead of soy sauce.

recipe.title: South African Bobotie
recipe.description: Curried, gently sweet minced beef baked under a savory egg custard.

ingredients.item: white bread, soaked in 1 cup milk

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F.
Cook the onion and garlic, add the beef and brown, then the spices for 1 minute.
Squeeze the bread, keeping the milk, and mix it into the beef with the jam, raisins, almonds and lemon juice.
Spread in a baking dish. Whisk the eggs with the saved milk, pour over and top with bay leaves.
Bake 35 to 40 minutes until the custard is set and golden.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Southern Fried Chicken
recipe.description: Bone-in chicken soaked in seasoned buttermilk, double-dredged in spiced flour and fried until deep golden and crackly. Juicy inside, crunchy outside.

ingredients.item: bone-in, skin-on chicken pieces (drumsticks, thighs and halved breasts)
kosher salt, plus 2 tsp for the flour
vegetable or canola oil, for frying

steps: Whisk the buttermilk, hot sauce and 1 tablespoon salt in a large bowl. Add the chicken, turn to coat, cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or up to 24.

Whisk the flour, cornstarch, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, black pepper, cayenne and 2 teaspoons salt in a wide dish. Drizzle in 3 tablespoons of the buttermilk marinade and rub it in with your fingers to make small, shaggy clumps.

Lift each piece of chicken out of the buttermilk, let the excess drip off, and press it firmly into the flour on all sides. Dip it back in the buttermilk for a second, then press it into the flour again. Set the pieces on a rack for 10 minutes while the oil heats.
Heat 2 inches of oil in a heavy Dutch oven to 350°F. Fry the chicken in batches without crowding, skin side down first. The oil temperature will drop: keep it around 300 to 325°F.
Fry for 15 to 18 minutes, turning every few minutes, until deep golden and the meat reaches 165°F in the breast and 175°F in the thighs and drumsticks.
Drain on a rack set over a sheet pan and season lightly with salt while hot. Let the oil come back to 350°F between batches.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: A clip-on thermometer is the most important tool here. Oil that's too hot burns the crust before the meat cooks; too cool, and the chicken turns greasy.
The flour clumps from the buttermilk are what make the craggy, extra-crunchy crust.
If the outside is done before the inside, finish the pieces on the rack in a 350°F oven.
recipe.make_ahead: Refrigerate leftovers for up to 3 days. Reheat on a rack in a 400°F oven for 15 minutes to re-crisp; the microwave makes the crust soggy.
variations: Nashville hot chicken: brush the hot chicken with 1/2 cup frying oil mixed with 2 tablespoons cayenne, 1 tablespoon brown sugar and 1 teaspoon paprika.
Boneless: use chicken thighs and fry for 6 to 8 minutes.

recipe.title: Southside
recipe.description: Gin, lime, sugar and fresh mint, shaken.
steps: Shake everything with ice.
Double-strain into a chilled coupe.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake lime, syrup and mint and top with lemon-lime soda.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Spaghett
recipe.description: A cult bar favorite: a cold bottle of light American lager, spiked with Aperol and fresh lemon right in the bottle. Bitter, bubbly and refreshing.

ingredients.item: vegan wheat-free lager (such as Miller High Life; check the label), ice-cold

steps: Drink or pour off about 2 oz of the beer to make room.
Add the Aperol and lemon juice straight into the bottle.
Tip gently once to mix and drink from the bottle.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Add a splash of non-alcoholic bitter orange aperitif and lemon to a non-alcoholic lager.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Start with 1 oz Aperol if you like it less bitter, and add more to taste.
Pour slowly to avoid it foaming over.
variations: Swap Campari for Aperol for a more bitter drink.

recipe.title: Spaghetti Bolognese
recipe.description: Slow-simmered beef and pork ragù with tomato and a splash of milk, tossed with spaghetti.
steps: Cook the onion, carrot and celery in the oil for 8 minutes until soft.
Add the beef and pork and brown, breaking it up. Season with salt and pepper.
Pour in the wine and let it bubble away, then add the milk and simmer until absorbed.
Stir in the tomatoes and tomato paste and simmer very gently, partly covered, for 1 to 1 1/2 hours.
Cook the spaghetti, toss with the sauce and a splash of pasta water, and serve with Parmesan.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Spaghetti Carbonara
recipe.description: Roman pasta with crisp guanciale, egg yolks and Pecorino, with no cream.
steps: Cook the guanciale in a skillet over medium heat until crisp. Turn off the heat.
Whisk the yolks, egg, Pecorino and pepper.
Cook the spaghetti in lightly salted water, saving 1 cup of pasta water.
Add the hot drained pasta to the skillet, then off the heat stir in the egg mixture with splashes of pasta water until creamy, not scrambled.
Serve at once with more Pecorino and pepper.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: The eggs are cooked only by the heat of the pasta. Use pasteurized eggs if you prefer, and always for anyone pregnant, older or with a weakened immune system.

recipe.title: Spiced Lamb and Chickpea Skillet
recipe.description: Ground lamb, chickpeas and tomato simmer with cumin and cinnamon in a quick dinner skillet.
steps: Heat oil in a wide skillet over medium heat. Soften onion for 5 minutes, then add garlic and spices for 30 seconds.
Add lamb and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, breaking it into small pieces, until browned and fully cooked to 160 F (71 C). Spoon off excess fat.
Add chickpeas, tomatoes, water, salt and pepper. Simmer uncovered for 10 minutes, until thickened.
Scatter parsley over the skillet and divide among four bowls.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Do not use the lower whole-cut temperature for ground lamb; ground meat needs 160 F (71 C).
recipe.make_ahead: Refrigerate promptly in shallow containers for up to 3 days. Reheat leftovers to 165 F (74 C).

recipe.title: Spicy Fifty
recipe.description: Salvatore Calabrese's modern classic: vanilla vodka, elderflower, lime and honey with a slow warmth from fresh red chili.

ingredients.item: honey syrup (equal parts honey and hot water)
thin slices of fresh red chili, seeds removed

steps: Chill a coupe or martini glass.
Add the chili slices to a shaker, then the vodka, elderflower cordial, lime juice and honey syrup.
Fill with ice and shake hard for 15 seconds.
Double-strain through a fine sieve into the chilled glass and hang the chili on the rim.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake 1 oz elderflower cordial, 1 oz lime juice and a chili slice with ice, strain, and top with 2 oz soda water.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Taste your chili first. Heat varies a lot; use one slice if it's fierce.
Double-straining catches the chili seeds and bits, so the drink stays smooth.

recipe.title: Spicy Peanut Chickpea Noodle Bowls
recipe.description: Wheat noodles, chickpeas and crisp vegetables with a creamy spicy peanut-lime dressing.
steps: Cook noodles according to the package and drain. Rinse briefly under cool water.
Whisk peanut butter, soy sauce, lime juice, maple syrup, sriracha and warm water into a smooth dressing. Add a spoonful more water if needed.
Toss noodles with chickpeas, cucumber, carrot and most of the dressing.
Divide among bowls and finish with remaining dressing, scallions and chopped peanuts.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: This dish intentionally contains peanuts; do not describe it as nut-free. Choose plain peanut butter and check sauce labels.
recipe.make_ahead: Refrigerate promptly for up to 2 days. Add a little water and lime juice to loosen the dressing before serving cold.

recipe.title: Spinach Ricotta Stuffed Portobello Mushrooms
recipe.description: Portobello caps filled with spinach, ricotta and Parmesan, baked until golden.
steps: Heat oven to 400°F. Brush mushroom caps with half the oil, place gill-side up on a lined tray and roast 8 minutes. Pour off any pooled liquid.
Wilt spinach with garlic in remaining oil, then squeeze out excess liquid. Mix with ricotta, half the Parmesan, salt and pepper.
Fill caps and sprinkle with remaining Parmesan. Bake 12–15 minutes until hot and lightly browned.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Fried Spring Rolls
recipe.description: Crisp rolls filled with cabbage, carrot, mushrooms and glass noodles, with sweet chili sauce.
steps: Stir-fry the garlic, cabbage, carrot and mushrooms for 3 minutes. Add the noodles, green onions, soy sauce and sugar. Cool completely.
Place 2 tbsp filling near one corner of a wrapper, fold the corner over, fold in the sides and roll up, sealing with the flour paste.
Fry at 350°F for 3 to 4 minutes until golden and crisp. Drain.
Serve hot with sweet chili sauce.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Sri Lankan Kottu Roti
recipe.description: Chopped flatbread stir-fried on a griddle with vegetables, egg, chicken and curry sauce.

ingredients.item: paratha or roti, cut into thin strips
cooked chicken curry, shredded, with 1/2 cup sauce

steps: Fry the onion, curry leaves and chiles in the oil, then the leek, carrot and cabbage for 3 minutes.
Push aside and scramble the eggs.
Add the chicken and roti strips and chop and toss everything together with two spatulas.
Add the curry sauce, season and toss until hot.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: St-Germain Cocktail
recipe.description: The elderflower spritz: floral St-Germain liqueur topped with dry sparkling wine and soda over ice, with a twist of lemon.

ingredients.item: vegan dry sparkling wine (such as Mionetto Organic Prosecco), chilled

steps: Pour the St-Germain into a chilled champagne flute.
Top with the sparkling wine, then the soda water.
Stir once gently and garnish with a lemon twist.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Mix elderflower cordial with sparkling white grape juice and a squeeze of lemon over ice.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Pour the bubbles gently down the side of the glass so they stay lively.
Squeeze the lemon twist over the drink first to release its oils.
variations: Hugo: add fresh mint and lime and use Prosecco.

recipe.title: Argentine Grilled Steak with Chimichurri
recipe.description: Asado-style grilled steak with Argentina's bright green sauce of finely chopped parsley, oregano and garlic in olive oil and red wine vinegar.

ingredients.item: finely chopped fresh oregano, or 2 tsp dried

steps: Make the chimichurri: stir the parsley, oregano, garlic, red pepper flakes, vinegar, olive oil and salt together in a bowl. Let it sit for at least 30 minutes, or up to 2 hours, so the flavors meld.
Pat the steak dry and season it all over with the coarse salt and pepper. Let it sit at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Heat a grill to high. Grill the steak for 3 to 5 minutes per side, depending on thickness, until well charred and medium-rare (130°F).
Rest the steak for 10 minutes, then slice thinly across the grain.
Serve with plenty of chimichurri spooned over.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Chop by hand. A food processor turns chimichurri into a paste; it should be a loose sauce of herbs in oil.
Slice skirt and flank steak across the grain, or it will be chewy.
USDA's safe minimum for beef steaks is 145°F with a 3-minute rest. 130°F is the usual medium-rare.
recipe.make_ahead: Chimichurri keeps in the fridge for up to 5 days and gets better on the second day. Bring it to room temperature before serving.
variations: Serve with grilled chorizo, provoleta (grilled provolone) or grilled vegetables, the way an Argentine asado would.

recipe.title: Stinger
recipe.description: Cognac and white crème de menthe, an after-dinner classic.
steps: Stir or shake with ice.
Strain into a coupe or over crushed ice.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Strawberry Balsamic Bourbon Smash
recipe.description: A splash of balsamic vinegar sharpens ripe strawberries in this bourbon smash.
steps: Muddle the chopped strawberries with syrup and balsamic vinegar in a shaker.
Add bourbon, lemon juice and ice. Shake for 15 seconds, then strain into a rocks glass over fresh ice.
Garnish with the strawberry half.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Muddle strawberries with syrup and vinegar; shake with 3/4 oz lemon juice and 2 oz cooled black tea, then strain over ice.

recipe.note: An original Relish home cocktail. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Use ordinary balsamic vinegar, not a thick sweet glaze.
recipe.make_ahead: Prepare to order. Keep juices and brewed teas refrigerated until needed.

recipe.title: Strawberry Basil Tequila Sour
recipe.description: Blanco tequila shaken with muddled strawberries, basil and lime. Fruity, fresh and tart.
steps: Muddle strawberries and basil with syrup.
Add tequila, lime and ice; shake and fine-strain into a rocks glass over ice.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: use an alcohol-free tequila alternative.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Strawberry Chamomile Gin Cooler
recipe.description: Strawberry and cooled chamomile tea soften a bright sparkling gin cooler.
steps: Muddle chopped strawberries with syrup in a shaker.
Add gin, cooled chamomile tea, lemon and ice. Shake for 12 seconds and fine-strain into an ice-filled highball.
Top with soda and add the strawberry half.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Muddle strawberries with syrup, shake with 3 oz cooled chamomile tea and 1/2 oz lemon juice, strain over ice and add 1 oz soda.

recipe.note: An original Relish home cocktail. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Use a plain food-grade chamomile infusion rather than a mixed herbal product with unspecified ingredients.
recipe.make_ahead: Prepare to order. Keep juices and brewed teas refrigerated until needed.

recipe.title: Strawberry Ginger Bourbon Fizz
recipe.description: Bourbon with strawberries, ginger and lemon, topped with soda.
steps: Muddle strawberries with ginger syrup.
Shake with bourbon, lemon and ice; fine-strain into a tall ice-filled glass.
Top with soda and garnish with strawberry.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Muddle the strawberries with ginger syrup, shake with lemon, strain over ice and top with extra soda.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Stuffed Bell Peppers
recipe.description: Bell peppers filled with beef, rice and tomato, baked under melted cheese.

ingredients.item: bell peppers, tops cut and seeded

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F.
Brown the beef with the onion and garlic, then stir in the rice, tomatoes, half the tomato sauce and seasoning.
Stand the peppers in a baking dish, fill them and top with the rest of the sauce.
Cover and bake 35 minutes, top with cheese and bake 10 minutes more.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Suffering Bastard
recipe.description: Gin and brandy with lime, bitters and ginger beer.
steps: Shake the gin, brandy, lime and bitters with ice.
Strain into an ice-filled highball and top with ginger beer.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Sweet and Sour Pork
recipe.description: The Cantonese classic: crisp, twice-fried pork tossed with pineapple, peppers and onion in a glossy, tangy ketchup and vinegar sauce.

ingredients.item: boneless pork shoulder, cut into 1-inch pieces
vegetable or canola oil, for frying
red bell pepper, cut into 1-inch pieces
green bell pepper, cut into 1-inch pieces
fresh or canned pineapple chunks, drained

steps: Toss the pork with the soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, white pepper and egg white and let it sit for 15 minutes.
Mix the ketchup, rice vinegar, sugar and water or pineapple juice in a bowl.
Mix the 1/2 cup cornstarch and the flour on a plate. Roll each piece of pork in it, pressing so the coating sticks.
Heat 2 inches of oil in a wok or heavy pot to 350°F. Fry the pork in two batches for 4 minutes, until lightly golden. Drain on a rack.
Heat the oil to 375°F and fry all the pork again for 1 to 2 minutes, until deep golden and very crisp. Drain.
Pour off all but 1 tablespoon of oil. Stir-fry the garlic, peppers and onion over high heat for 1 minute.
Add the sauce and bring to a boil, then stir in the cornstarch mixture until glossy. Add the pineapple.
Add the pork, toss quickly to coat and serve right away with rice.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: The second, hotter fry is what keeps the coating crisp under the sauce.
Taste the sauce before it goes in. It should be clearly sour as well as sweet; add a little more vinegar if needed.
variations: Sweet and sour chicken: use boneless chicken thighs and fry them for 1 minute less the first time.

recipe.title: Sweet Chili Salmon Noodle Salad
recipe.description: Fully cooked salmon, rice noodles and crisp vegetables with a sweet chili-lime dressing.
steps: Heat oven to 400 F (200 C). Brush salmon with half the oil and salt. Bake for 12 to 15 minutes until the thickest part reaches 145 F (63 C), then flake into large pieces.
Cook rice vermicelli according to the package; drain and rinse under cool water.
Whisk sweet chili sauce, lime juice, soy sauce, remaining oil and water. Toss noodles with cucumber, carrot, cabbage and most of the dressing.
Top with cooked salmon, cilantro and remaining dressing. Serve promptly.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Rice noodles do not remove the wheat in ordinary soy sauce. The stated allergen list includes wheat and soy for that sauce.
recipe.make_ahead: Refrigerate promptly and use within 2 days. Keep the salad cold and do not leave cooked fish at room temperature for more than 2 hours.

recipe.title: Sweet Potato Kale Black Bean Chili
recipe.description: Sweet potato, black beans and kale in a smoky tomato chili.

ingredients.item: medium sweet potatoes, peeled and diced
black beans (15 oz each), drained and rinsed

steps: Warm oil in a saucepan and soften onion for 5 minutes. Add garlic, cumin, paprika and chili for 30 seconds.
Add sweet potato, beans, tomatoes, water and salt. Simmer partly covered for 25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sweet potato is tender.
Stir in kale and simmer for 5 minutes more. Add water if too thick.
Serve in bowls with cilantro and lime wedges.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Use plain ground chili rather than an unspecified seasoning blend so the flavor and ingredients stay clear.
recipe.make_ahead: Refrigerate promptly in shallow containers for up to 3 days. Reheat leftovers to 165 F (74 C).

recipe.title: Tabbouleh
recipe.description: The Lebanese parsley salad: mostly finely chopped parsley and mint with tomato, scallion and a little fine bulgur, dressed with plenty of lemon and olive oil.

ingredients.item: finely chopped flat-leaf parsley (about 3 large bunches)
fresh lemon juice, plus more to taste

steps: Put the bulgur in a bowl, add the diced tomatoes and their juice and the lemon juice, and let it soak for 20 minutes, until tender.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the parsley and mint very well, then chop them finely with a sharp knife.
Add the parsley, mint, scallions, olive oil, salt and allspice, if using, to the bulgur and toss well.
Taste and add more lemon or salt. It should be bright and tangy.
Serve right away, with lettuce leaves for scooping.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Real tabbouleh is a parsley salad with a little bulgur, not a grain salad with herbs.
Dry the herbs completely before chopping. Wet herbs bruise and make the salad soggy.
Chop by hand. A food processor turns the parsley into a watery paste.
recipe.make_ahead: Chop the herbs and vegetables a few hours ahead and keep them in the fridge separately. Mix and dress just before serving.
variations: Gluten-free: use 1/2 cup cooked quinoa instead of bulgur.

recipe.title: Tacos al Pastor
recipe.description: Mexico City's favorite taco: thin slices of pork marinated in dried chiles, achiote and pineapple, seared until charred and tucked into warm corn tortillas with pineapple, onion and cilantro.

ingredients.item: dried guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded
dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
fresh or canned pineapple chunks, plus 6 thin rounds of fresh pineapple for grilling
white onion, plus 1/2 onion finely chopped, to serve
boneless pork shoulder, sliced 1/4 inch thick
lime wedges and salsa verde, to serve

steps: Toast the chiles in a dry skillet over medium heat for 20 to 30 seconds per side, until fragrant. Soak them in hot water for 15 minutes, then drain.
Blend the chiles, pineapple chunks, achiote paste, vinegar, the half onion, garlic, oregano, cumin and salt with 1/2 cup water until very smooth.
Toss the pork with the marinade, cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or overnight.

Heat a large cast-iron skillet or griddle over high heat with a little of the oil. Sear the pork in batches, without crowding, for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until cooked through and charred at the edges.
Sear the pineapple rounds for 2 minutes per side, until caramelized.
Chop the pork and pineapple into small pieces.
Pile into warm tortillas and top with chopped onion, cilantro, a squeeze of lime and salsa.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Partly freezing the pork for 30 minutes makes it much easier to slice thin.
Sear in batches. Crowding the pan steams the meat instead of charring it.
Wear gloves when mixing: achiote stains hands and counters.
