recipe.make_ahead: Marinate the pork up to 24 hours ahead.
variations: Grill the pork and pineapple over a hot grill instead of in a skillet.

recipe.title: Taiwanese Beef Noodle Soup
recipe.description: Braised beef shank in a spiced soy broth with thick wheat noodles and bok choy.
steps: Blanch the beef 5 minutes and rinse.
Fry the garlic, ginger and green onions in oil, add the doubanjiang and tomatoes.
Add the beef, soy sauce, wine, spices and 10 cups water. Simmer 2 to 2 1/2 hours until tender.
Cook the noodles and bok choy separately.
Serve the noodles in bowls with beef, bok choy and hot broth.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Takoyaki
recipe.description: Japanese octopus-filled batter balls topped with sauce, mayo, bonito flakes and seaweed.

ingredients.item: takoyaki sauce, Japanese mayo, bonito flakes and aonori

steps: Whisk the flour, eggs, dashi and soy sauce into a thin batter.
Heat an oiled takoyaki pan and fill the holes with batter.
Drop in octopus, green onion, ginger and tempura bits.
After 1 to 2 minutes, turn each ball with a skewer, tucking in the edges, and keep turning until round and golden.
Top with sauce, mayo, bonito flakes and aonori.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Pork Tamales
recipe.description: Steamed masa dough wrapped in corn husks around red chile pork.
steps: Beat the lard until fluffy, then beat in the masa, baking powder, salt and broth until a bit of dough floats in water.
Mix the pork with the chile sauce.
Spread a thin layer of masa on each husk, add a spoon of filling and fold the sides and bottom over.
Stand the tamales upright in a steamer and steam 1 to 1 1/2 hours until the masa pulls away from the husk.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Tangerine Ginger Bourbon Highball
recipe.description: Bourbon, tangerine and ginger make a bright, lightly sparkling highball.
steps: Shake bourbon, tangerine juice, lemon and ginger syrup with ice for 12 seconds.
Strain into an ice-filled highball glass and top with soda.
Stir gently and add the tangerine wheel.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake 3 oz tangerine juice, 1/2 oz lemon juice and 1/4 oz ginger syrup with ice; strain and add 3 oz soda.

recipe.note: An original Relish home cocktail. Please drink responsibly.
recipe.make_ahead: Prepare to order. Keep juices and brewed teas refrigerated until needed.

recipe.title: Tangerine Pink Pepper Gin Collins
recipe.description: Fresh tangerine and lemon brighten a sparkling gin Collins with a restrained pink-pepper aroma.
steps: Shake gin, tangerine juice, lemon juice and syrup with ice for 12 seconds.
Strain into an ice-filled Collins glass. Add soda and stir once gently.
Sprinkle the three lightly crushed peppercorns on the ice and garnish with the tangerine half-wheel.

cocktail.garnish: tangerine half-wheel and three pink peppercorns
cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake 2 oz tangerine juice, 1/2 oz lemon juice and 1/4 oz simple syrup with ice; strain into a tall glass and top with 3 oz soda water.

recipe.note: An original Relish home cocktail. Please drink responsibly. Pink peppercorns may cross-react with cashew or pistachio allergy. This drink is not verified nut-free; check product labels.
tips: Simple syrup here means equal parts sugar and water dissolved together and cooled. Keep the soda out of the shaker.
recipe.make_ahead: Juice citrus up to 1 day ahead and refrigerate. Build with soda just before serving.

recipe.title: Shrimp and Vegetable Tempura
recipe.description: Shrimp and vegetables in a lacy, ice-cold batter, fried until pale gold and shatteringly crisp. Served with a light soy and dashi dipping sauce.

ingredients.item: large shrimp, peeled with tails on, deveined
small sweet potato, cut into 1/4-inch rounds
small Japanese eggplant, cut into 1/4-inch slices
all-purpose flour, plus 1/4 cup for dusting
ice-cold water, plus a few ice cubes
vegetable or canola oil, for frying
finely grated daikon radish, to serve
finely grated fresh ginger, to serve

steps: Make the dipping sauce: bring the dashi, soy sauce and mirin to a simmer in a small pan, then turn off the heat and let it cool.
Make 3 or 4 shallow cuts across the underside of each shrimp and press them gently flat so they stay straight when fried. Pat the shrimp and vegetables very dry.
Heat 2 inches of oil in a heavy pot to 340°F for the vegetables.
Make the batter right before frying: whisk the egg and ice water in a bowl, add 1 cup flour all at once and stir just a few strokes with chopsticks. Lumps are fine.
Dust each piece lightly in the extra flour, dip it in the batter and let the excess drip off.
Fry the vegetables a few at a time for 2 to 3 minutes, turning once, until crisp and pale gold. Drain on a rack.
Raise the oil to 350°F and fry the shrimp for 1 to 2 minutes, until just cooked through.
Serve right away with the dipping sauce, grated daikon and ginger.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Keep the batter ice-cold and barely mixed. Stirring builds gluten, which makes the coating heavy and bready.
The dusting of flour helps the batter cling, especially to shrimp and smooth vegetables.
Skim floating bits of batter from the oil between batches so they don't burn.
variations: Add onion rings, green beans, kabocha squash or shiso leaves.

vegetarian.description: Sweet potato, eggplant, shiitake and zucchini in a light, ice-cold batter, fried crisp and served with a kombu and soy dipping sauce.

small Japanese eggplant, cut into 1/4-inch slices
all-purpose flour, plus 1/4 cup for dusting
ice-cold water, plus a few ice cubes
vegetable or canola oil, for frying
kombu broth (a 4-inch piece of kombu soaked in 1 cup water for 30 minutes)
finely grated daikon radish, to serve
finely grated fresh ginger, to serve

steps: Make the dipping sauce: bring the kombu broth, soy sauce and mirin to a simmer in a small pan, then turn off the heat and let it cool.
Pat the vegetables very dry.
Heat 2 inches of oil in a heavy pot to 340°F.
Make the batter right before frying: whisk the egg and ice water in a bowl, add 1 cup flour all at once and stir just a few strokes with chopsticks. Lumps are fine.
Dust each piece lightly in the extra flour, dip it in the batter and let the excess drip off.
Fry a few pieces at a time for 2 to 3 minutes, turning once, until crisp and pale gold. Drain on a rack.
Serve right away with the dipping sauce, grated daikon and ginger.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Keep the batter ice-cold and barely mixed. Stirring builds gluten, which makes the coating heavy and bready.
The dusting of flour helps the batter cling, especially to smooth vegetables.
Skim floating bits of batter from the oil between batches so they don't burn.

vegetable or canola oil, for frying
kombu broth (a 4-inch piece of kombu soaked in 1 cup water for 30 minutes)
finely grated daikon radish, to serve
finely grated fresh ginger, to serve

steps: Make the dipping sauce: bring the kombu broth, soy sauce and mirin to a simmer in a small pan, then turn off the heat and let it cool.
Pat the vegetables very dry.
Heat 2 inches of oil in a heavy pot to 340°F.
Make the batter right before frying: whisk 1 cup flour with the cornstarch in a bowl, pour in the ice-cold sparkling water all at once and stir just a few strokes with chopsticks. Lumps are fine.

recipe.title: Tequila Sunrise
recipe.description: Tequila and orange juice with grenadine sinking to make a sunrise.
steps: Fill a highball with ice and add the tequila and orange juice. Stir.
Slowly pour the grenadine down the side so it sinks.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Orange juice with grenadine poured in to sink.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Teriyaki Salmon Rice Bowls
recipe.description: Salmon glazed in homemade teriyaki over rice, with crunchy cucumber, edamame and toasted sesame seeds.
steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Mix soy sauce, mirin, sugar and ginger. Brush half over salmon on a lined tray; reserve the rest separately.
Bake 10–14 minutes until salmon reaches 145°F. Simmer the reserved sauce in a small pan for 2 minutes.
Serve salmon over rice with cucumber and edamame. Spoon on sauce and sprinkle with sesame.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Test Pilot
recipe.description: A 1941 Don the Beachcomber tiki classic: dark and light rums with lime, Cointreau, falernum, a dash of bitters and a whisper of anise, flash-blended over ice.
steps: Put all the ingredients in a blender with the crushed ice.
Flash blend for 5 seconds, just to chill and froth it.
Pour into a double rocks glass, adding more crushed ice if needed, and garnish with a lime wheel.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Flash blend lime juice, falernum syrup, orange juice and a dash of alcohol-free aromatic bitters (regular bitters contain alcohol) with crushed ice.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Flash blending for just a few seconds chills and dilutes it without turning it into a slushie.
Measure the anise in drops, not dashes; a little goes a long way.
variations: Jet Pilot: add 1/2 oz grapefruit juice and 1/2 oz cinnamon syrup and skip the Cointreau.

recipe.title: Texas-Style Smoked Brisket
recipe.description: Central Texas barbecue at its simplest: a whole brisket rubbed with just coarse salt and pepper, smoked low and slow over oak until it's tender, juicy and wrapped in a dark, peppery bark.

ingredients.item: whole packer beef brisket (12 to 14 lb)
oak or hickory wood, for smoking
pink butcher paper or heavy-duty foil, for wrapping
pickles and sliced onion, to serve (optional)

steps: Trim the hard fat on the fat side down to about 1/4 inch and remove any silver skin on the meat side.
Mix the salt and pepper and season the brisket generously on all sides. Let it sit while the smoker heats.
Heat a smoker to 250°F with oak or hickory. Put the brisket in fat side up, with the thicker end toward the hottest part of the smoker.
Smoke for 6 to 8 hours, until the bark is dark and set and the internal temperature reaches about 165°F. The temperature will stall for a while around this point; that's normal.
Wrap the brisket tightly in butcher paper or foil and return it to the smoker.
Keep cooking for 4 to 6 hours more, until the thickest part reaches 203°F and a probe slides in with almost no resistance.
Rest the wrapped brisket in an empty cooler or a 150°F oven for at least 1 hour, or up to 4.
Slice across the grain into pencil-thick slices, separating the lean flat from the fattier point, and serve with pickles and onion.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: In Texas it comes on butcher paper with slices of white bread on the side.
Plan on 10 to 14 hours of cooking plus the rest. Start early: a finished brisket stays hot for hours wrapped in a cooler, but a late one can't be rushed.
Cook to feel, not just temperature. Done brisket feels like a probe sliding into soft butter.
The flat and point grains run in different directions. Cut the two apart before slicing each one across its grain.
recipe.make_ahead: Wrap leftovers tightly and refrigerate for up to 4 days. Reheat slices wrapped in foil with a splash of broth at 300°F.
variations: No smoker? Season, then roast on a rack at 275°F for about 6 hours, wrap in foil and cook to 203°F. It won't be smoky, but it will be tender.

recipe.title: Thai Green Curry
recipe.description: Chicken and vegetables in a fragrant green curry with coconut milk and Thai basil.
steps: Fry the curry paste in the oil and a few spoonfuls of thick coconut cream until fragrant.
Add the chicken and cook 3 minutes.
Add the rest of the coconut milk, eggplant and lime leaves and simmer 10 minutes, until the chicken reaches 165°F.
Add the pepper and season with fish sauce and sugar.
Stir in the basil and serve with jasmine rice.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Thai Khao Soi
recipe.description: Northern Thai coconut curry noodle soup with chicken, topped with crispy noodles.

ingredients.item: pickled mustard greens, shallots, lime and chili oil

steps: Fry the curry paste and curry powder in some coconut cream until fragrant.
Add the chicken, the rest of the coconut milk and the broth, and simmer 30 minutes.
Season with fish sauce and sugar.
Fry a handful of the noodles until crisp. Boil the rest.
Serve the boiled noodles in the curry with chicken, topped with crispy noodles and the garnishes.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

vegan dry vermouth (such as Dolin Dry)

recipe.title: Three Dots and a Dash
recipe.description: Don the Beachcomber's WWII victory drink, named for the Morse code "V": rhum agricole and dark rum with lime, orange, honey, falernum and allspice, garnished with three cherries and a pineapple dash.

ingredients.item: honey syrup (equal parts honey and hot water)

steps: Put all the ingredients in a blender with the crushed ice.
Flash blend for 5 seconds.
Pour into a tulip or tiki glass. Garnish with three cherries and a pineapple spear on a pick: the three dots and the dash.

recipe.title: Tipperary
recipe.description: An Irish cousin of the Manhattan from the early 1900s: Irish whiskey and sweet vermouth with a measure of herbal green Chartreuse, stirred and served up.

steps: Stir the whiskey, vermouth, Chartreuse and bitters with ice for 20 to 30 seconds.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Green Chartreuse is intense; start with 1/2 oz and adjust to taste.
Stirring keeps it silky and clear.
variations: The 1916 original uses equal parts whiskey, vermouth and Chartreuse for a bolder herbal drink.

recipe.title: Tiramisù
recipe.description: The classic Italian no-bake dessert: espresso-dipped ladyfingers layered with a light mascarpone cream and dusted with cocoa. It sets overnight in the fridge.
steps: Beat the egg yolks with half the sugar for 3 to 4 minutes, until pale and thick.
Add the mascarpone and beat on low just until smooth.
In a clean bowl with clean beaters, whip the egg whites to soft peaks, then add the rest of the sugar and whip to firm, glossy peaks.
Fold the whites into the mascarpone mixture in three additions, gently, so the cream stays light.
Pour the espresso into a shallow dish. Dip each ladyfinger for 1 second per side and lay it in an 8-by-11-inch dish to make a single layer.
Spread half the cream over the ladyfingers. Repeat with a second layer of dipped ladyfingers and the rest of the cream.
Smooth the top, cover and refrigerate for at least 6 hours, or overnight.
Dust generously with cocoa through a fine sieve just before serving.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Dip the ladyfingers quickly. They keep soaking in the fridge, and too much coffee makes the dessert soggy.
This uses raw eggs. If you'd rather not, buy pasteurized eggs, which whip just as well.
Don't overbeat the mascarpone or it can turn grainy.
recipe.make_ahead: Make it a day ahead: it slices more cleanly. It keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days.
variations: Add 3 tablespoons of Marsala, dark rum or coffee liqueur to the espresso.
Make it in individual glasses, breaking the ladyfingers to fit.

recipe.title: Tom Collins
recipe.description: Sweet Old Tom gin, lemon and sugar, shaken and lengthened with soda water.
steps: Shake the gin, lemon and syrup with ice.
Strain into an ice-filled Collins glass and top with soda.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Lemon, syrup and soda water make fresh lemonade soda.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Old Tom gin is sweeter and softer than London dry. With London dry gin, built in the glass, it becomes a John Collins.

recipe.title: Tom Kha Gai (Thai Coconut Chicken Soup)
recipe.description: A creamy Thai soup of chicken and mushrooms simmered in coconut milk and broth with galangal, lemongrass and lime leaves, finished with lime and fish sauce.

ingredients.item: boneless, skinless chicken thighs, thinly sliced
lemongrass, bottom halves only, smashed and cut into 2-inch pieces
oyster or straw mushrooms, torn into bite-size pieces
fish sauce, plus more to taste
palm sugar or light brown sugar
fresh lime juice, plus more to taste

steps: Bring the broth to a simmer in a pot. Add the lemongrass, galangal, lime leaves and chilies and simmer for 5 minutes to release their flavor.
Add the coconut milk and chicken and bring back to a gentle simmer. Cook for 5 minutes.
Add the mushrooms, fish sauce and sugar and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes more, until the chicken is cooked through (165°F).
Turn off the heat and stir in the lime juice.
Taste: it should be sour and salty first, then creamy. Add more lime or fish sauce if needed. Serve topped with cilantro.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Keep it at a gentle simmer once the coconut milk is in. A hard boil can make it split.
The lemongrass, galangal and lime leaves are for flavor, not for eating. Leave them in the pot when you serve.
Galangal is not the same as ginger, but ginger will do in a pinch.
recipe.make_ahead: Refrigerate for up to 2 days. Reheat gently and add a fresh squeeze of lime.

recipe.title: Tom Yum Soup
recipe.description: Hot and sour Thai shrimp soup with lemongrass, galangal and lime leaves.

ingredients.item: lemongrass, smashed and cut into pieces

steps: Simmer the stock with the lemongrass, galangal, lime leaves and chiles for 10 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and chili paste and simmer 2 minutes.
Add the shrimp and cook 2 minutes until pink.
Off the heat, add the fish sauce and lime juice, taste and adjust, and top with cilantro.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Tomato-Basil Baked Chicken Meatballs
recipe.description: Tender Parmesan chicken meatballs baked, then simmered in marinara with fresh basil and served over spaghetti.
steps: Heat oven to 400°F. Gently combine chicken, breadcrumbs, egg, Parmesan, garlic and salt. Shape into 16 meatballs and place on a lined tray.
Bake 18–22 minutes until the centers reach 165°F. Meanwhile cook spaghetti according to package directions and warm marinara.
Add meatballs to sauce, toss with basil and serve over pasta.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Tomato Olive Chicken with Butter Beans
recipe.description: Chicken thighs, butter beans, tomatoes and olives in an oregano-scented skillet.

ingredients.item: large white lima beans (15 oz each), drained and rinsed

steps: Season chicken with half the salt and pepper. Heat oil in a deep skillet and brown chicken for 3 minutes per side; set aside.
Soften onion in the skillet for 5 minutes. Add garlic and oregano for 30 seconds.
Add tomatoes, water, beans, olives and remaining salt. Nestle chicken into the sauce, cover and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes until every thigh reaches 165 F (74 C).
Stand for 5 minutes and scatter with parsley.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Butter beans are a legume, not a dairy ingredient. Olives are salty, so taste the sauce before adding more salt.
recipe.make_ahead: Refrigerate promptly in shallow containers for up to 3 days. Reheat leftovers to 165 F (74 C).

recipe.title: Creamy Tomato Soup
recipe.description: Smooth tomato soup with garlic, basil and a splash of cream.
steps: Cook the onion in the butter until soft, then add the garlic.
Add the tomatoes, broth and sugar and simmer 20 minutes.
Add the basil and blend until smooth.
Stir in the cream and season.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Tommy's Margarita

steps: Shake everything with ice.

recipe.title: Tortilla Española (Spanish Omelette)
recipe.description: Spain's beloved tapa: thin slices of potato and onion slowly poached in olive oil, folded into beaten eggs and cooked into a thick, golden cake with a soft, juicy center.

ingredients.item: Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced

steps: Heat the oil in a 10-inch nonstick skillet over medium-low heat. Add the potatoes, onion and 1 tsp salt. The oil should almost cover them.
Cook gently for 20 to 25 minutes, turning now and then, until the potatoes are completely tender but not browned.
Drain the potatoes and onion in a colander set over a bowl, keeping the oil. Beat the eggs with the rest of the salt in a large bowl, then fold in the warm potatoes. Rest 10 minutes.
Wipe the pan, heat 2 tbsp of the reserved oil over medium heat and pour in the mixture. Cook 4 to 5 minutes, shaking the pan and tucking in the edges, until the bottom is golden.
Put a large plate over the pan and flip the tortilla onto it in one confident move. Slide it back into the pan and cook 2 to 3 minutes more.
Slide onto a plate and rest 5 minutes. Serve warm or at room temperature, cut in wedges.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: The potatoes should poach, not fry. Keep the heat low so they turn soft and creamy.
Resting the potatoes in the egg lets them soak it up for a juicy, cohesive tortilla.
Strain and keep the potato oil; it's wonderful for cooking.
recipe.make_ahead: Keeps 2 days in the fridge. Many Spaniards prefer it the next day, at room temperature.
variations: Leave the center runny (poco hecha) for the classic bar-style tortilla. Use pasteurized eggs if you do.
Add sliced chorizo or roasted peppers to the eggs.

vegan.title: Vegan Tortilla Española
vegan.description: Olive-oil-poached potatoes and onion folded into a chickpea flour batter and cooked into a golden, sliceable cake.

ingredients.item: Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced

steps: Heat the oil in a 10-inch nonstick skillet over medium-low heat. Add the potatoes, onion and 1 tsp salt. Cook gently for 20 to 25 minutes, turning now and then, until completely tender but not browned.
Whisk the chickpea flour, water, turmeric, baking powder and the rest of the salt into a smooth batter and rest it while the potatoes cook.
Drain the potatoes and onion, keeping the oil, and fold them into the batter.
Heat 2 tbsp of the reserved oil in the wiped pan over medium heat. Pour in the mixture and cook 6 to 8 minutes, until the bottom is golden and the edges are set.
Flip onto a plate, slide back into the pan and cook 5 to 6 minutes more, until set all the way through.
Rest 10 minutes before cutting into wedges. Serve warm or at room temperature.
vegan.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Chickpea flour needs a little longer than egg to set, so cook it a few minutes more on each side.
Resting before slicing lets it firm up into clean wedges.
vegan.make_ahead: Keeps 2 days in the fridge; it's great at room temperature.

recipe.title: Trinidadian Doubles
recipe.description: Two soft fried flatbreads (bara) filled with curried chickpeas and chutneys.

ingredients.item: tamarind sauce, mango chutney and pepper sauce

steps: Mix the flour, yeast, turmeric, cumin, a pinch of salt and water into a soft dough. Rise 1 hour.
Cook the onion and garlic in oil, fry the curry powder 1 minute, then add the chickpeas and 1 1/2 cups water. Simmer until very soft.
Pat small balls of dough into thin 4-inch rounds and fry 30 seconds per side until puffed.
Put two bara together, top with chickpeas and the sauces.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Tuna and Cucumber Maki Rolls
recipe.description: Classic thin sushi rolls of seasoned rice and nori, half filled with tuna and half with crisp cucumber. Served with soy sauce, wasabi and pickled ginger.

ingredients.item: Japanese or Persian cucumber, cut into thin sticks

steps: Rinse the rice in a bowl of cold water, swirling and draining, 4 or 5 times until the water runs almost clear. Drain for 15 minutes.
Cook the rice with the water in a rice cooker, or in a covered pot: boil, then simmer on low for 15 minutes and rest off the heat, still covered, for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, warm the vinegar, sugar and salt in a small pan, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Let it cool.

Spread the hot rice in a wide bowl. Drizzle the vinegar mixture over it and fold with a spatula, cutting through the rice rather than stirring, while fanning it to cool. Cover with a damp towel until it's at room temperature.

Lay a bamboo mat on the counter and place a half sheet of nori on it, shiny side down. Wet your hands and spread a thin, even layer of rice over the nori, leaving a 1/2-inch strip bare at the far edge.
Lay a line of tuna across the middle of the rice for 3 of the rolls, and cucumber for the other 3.
Lift the near edge of the mat and roll it over the filling, pressing gently, then keep rolling until the bare strip of nori seals the roll.
Cut each roll into 6 pieces with a sharp, wet knife, wiping the blade between cuts. Serve with wasabi, pickled ginger and soy sauce.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Keep a bowl of water with a splash of vinegar beside you. Wet hands stop the rice from sticking to your fingers.
Use less rice than you think. A thin layer keeps the roll neat and lets the filling stand out.
Cool the rice to room temperature before rolling: hot rice makes the nori go limp.

The fish is eaten raw. Buy fish sold for eating raw that has been frozen to kill parasites, keep it very cold, and serve only the cucumber rolls to anyone pregnant, older or with a weakened immune system.
recipe.make_ahead: Sushi is best eaten within a few hours. Don't refrigerate it, because cold makes the rice hard.
variations: Spicy tuna roll: chop the tuna and mix it with a little mayonnaise and sriracha before rolling.
Avocado roll: use thin slices of ripe avocado as the filling.

recipe.title: Tunisian Couscous
recipe.description: Couscous with lamb and vegetables in a spicy harissa and tomato broth.
steps: Brown the lamb and onion in the oil, then add the tomato paste, harissa and spices.
Add 6 cups water and simmer 45 minutes.
Add the carrots and potato, then the zucchini and chickpeas, and cook until tender.
Steam or soak the couscous in some of the broth with a little oil.
Mound the couscous, top with meat and vegetables and ladle over broth.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Turkey and Black Bean Stuffed Sweet Potatoes
recipe.description: Roasted sweet potatoes split open and filled with cumin-spiced turkey, black beans and salsa, topped with cilantro and a spoon of yogurt.
steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Pierce potatoes and bake on a tray 45–55 minutes until tender.
Brown turkey in a skillet until it reaches 165°F. Add beans, salsa, cumin and salt; simmer 5 minutes.
Split potatoes and fluff their centers. Fill with turkey mixture and top with cilantro and optional yogurt.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Turkey Zucchini Feta Burgers
recipe.description: Juicy turkey burgers with squeezed zucchini and feta, served with tomato, lettuce and dill yogurt in plain buns.
steps: Mix turkey, squeezed zucchini, breadcrumbs, egg, feta, salt and pepper gently. Form four equal patties about 3/4 inch thick.
Heat oil in a wide skillet over medium heat. Cook patties for 5 to 7 minutes per side, until every center reaches 165 F (74 C). Lower the heat if browning too quickly.
Mix yogurt with dill. Toast the buns if desired.
Spread yogurt sauce on buns and add lettuce, a cooked patty and tomato. Serve immediately.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Squeezing the zucchini prevents loose patties. Read bun and breadcrumb labels for additional ingredients and allergens.
recipe.make_ahead: Refrigerate cooked patties promptly for up to 3 days. Reheat to 165 F (74 C); assemble burgers only when serving.

recipe.title: Turkish Lahmacun
recipe.description: Thin, crisp flatbreads topped with spiced minced lamb, rolled up with herbs and lemon.

ingredients.item: lemon wedges, parsley and sliced onion, to serve

steps: Heat the oven with a baking stone to 500°F.
Pulse the onion, pepper, tomatoes, garlic and parsley finely, then mix with the lamb, pepper paste, spices and salt.
Roll the dough into very thin rounds and spread thinly with the topping.
Bake 6 to 8 minutes, until crisp at the edges and the lamb is cooked through (160°F).
Squeeze with lemon, scatter parsley and onion, and roll up to eat.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Tuxedo No. 2
recipe.description: Gin, dry vermouth, maraschino and orange bitters in an absinthe-rinsed glass.

ingredients.item: vegan dry vermouth (such as Dolin Dry)

steps: Rinse a chilled coupe with absinthe.
Stir the rest with ice and strain into the glass.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Uzbek Plov
recipe.description: Uzbekistan's national dish: rice steamed over a rich base of browned lamb, sweet carrots, onion and cumin, crowned with whole heads of soft, sweet garlic.

ingredients.item: large onions, sliced into half moons
yellow and orange carrots, cut into thick matchsticks
garlic, loose outer skin removed, left whole
medium-grain or basmati rice, rinsed until clear and soaked 30 minutes
sliced tomato and onion salad (achichuk), to serve

steps: Heat the oil in a heavy wide pot or Dutch oven until very hot. Brown the lamb in batches for 6 to 8 minutes, until deeply colored.
Add the onions and cook 5 to 8 minutes until golden, then the carrots. Cook 10 minutes without much stirring, until the carrots soften.
Make the zirvak: add half the cumin, the coriander, barberries, chili, 2 tsp salt, chickpeas and enough boiling water to just cover. Simmer, covered, for 40 minutes.
Drain the rice and spread it evenly over the zirvak. Don't stir. Pour boiling water gently over a spoon to come 1/2 inch above the rice. Add the remaining salt and cumin.
Boil, uncovered, until the water drops below the rice surface. Push the garlic heads into the rice, then gather the rice into a dome and poke 6 holes down to the bottom.
Cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 25 to 30 minutes, until the rice is tender. Rest 10 minutes.
Mix gently, mound on a platter with the meat and carrots on top and the garlic heads in the center. Serve with a fresh tomato and onion salad.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Never stir once the rice goes on. The rice steams in layers above the zirvak and soaks up its flavor.
Cut the carrots by hand into thick matchsticks; grated carrots turn to mush.
Squeeze the soft, sweet garlic cloves onto your rice as you eat.
recipe.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge. Reheat with a splash of water, covered, so it steams.
variations: Use beef chuck instead of lamb; the timing is the same.
Add a handful of quince or dried apricots to the zirvak for a sweeter plov.

vegetarian.title: Vegetarian Plov
vegetarian.description: The same golden carrot and cumin rice with whole garlic, built on a zirvak of chickpeas and browned mushrooms instead of lamb.

ingredients.item: cremini or king oyster mushrooms, halved
large onions, sliced into half moons
yellow and orange carrots, cut into thick matchsticks
garlic, loose outer skin removed, left whole
medium-grain or basmati rice, rinsed until clear and soaked 30 minutes
sliced tomato and onion salad (achichuk), to serve

steps: Heat the oil in a heavy wide pot or Dutch oven until very hot. Brown the mushrooms in batches for 6 to 8 minutes, until deeply colored.
Add the onions and cook 5 to 8 minutes until golden, then the carrots. Cook 10 minutes without much stirring, until the carrots soften.
Make the zirvak: add half the cumin, the coriander, barberries, chili, 2 tsp salt, chickpeas and enough boiling water to just cover. Simmer, covered, for 20 minutes.
Drain the rice and spread it evenly over the zirvak. Don't stir. Pour boiling water gently over a spoon to come 1/2 inch above the rice. Add the remaining salt and cumin.

Squeeze the soft, sweet garlic cloves onto your rice as you eat.

recipe.title: Vampiro
recipe.description: Tequila with spicy, savory sangrita, orange, lime and grapefruit soda.

ingredients.item: sangrita or tomato juice with orange and chile
pinch of salt and chili powder

steps: Rim a highball with chili salt and fill with ice.
Add the tequila and juices and top with grapefruit soda.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Leave out the tequila.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Pabellón Criollo
recipe.description: Venezuela's national plate of shredded beef, black beans, rice and fried plantains.
steps: Simmer the steak in salted water 1 1/2 hours until tender, then shred.
Cook the onion, pepper and garlic in oil, add the tomatoes, cumin and beef and simmer 15 minutes.
Simmer the beans with the sugar and a pinch of salt.
Fry the plantains until caramelized.
Serve the beef, beans, rice and plantains together.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Ve.n.to
recipe.description: Italy's grappa sour: smooth white grappa with lemon, chamomile honey and chamomile cordial, served over ice with white grapes.

ingredients.item: chamomile honey syrup (equal parts honey and hot chamomile tea)
strip of lemon zest, to garnish
white grapes on a pick, to garnish

steps: Fill a small tumbler with ice.
Add the grappa, lemon juice, chamomile honey syrup, chamomile cordial and egg white, if using, to a shaker.
Fill with ice and shake hard for 15 seconds.
Strain into the tumbler and garnish with the lemon zest and grapes.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake 1 oz lemon juice, 3/4 oz chamomile honey syrup and 2 oz white grape juice with ice and strain over ice.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Make the syrup by stirring honey into an equal amount of freshly brewed chamomile tea. It keeps in the fridge for two weeks.
Choose a soft, young grappa. Aged or very strong grappas overpower the chamomile.
This drink uses raw egg white. Use pasteurized egg white if you prefer, and always for anyone pregnant, older or with a weakened immune system.
recipe.make_ahead: Make the chamomile honey syrup up to two weeks ahead and keep it in the fridge.

recipe.title: Vesper
recipe.description: Gin, vodka and Lillet Blanc, shaken very cold.
steps: Shake everything with ice until very cold.
Strain into a chilled martini glass.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Vietnamese Bánh Xèo
recipe.description: Crisp turmeric rice-flour crepes filled with pork, shrimp and sprouts, wrapped in lettuce and herbs.

ingredients.item: oil, lettuce, mint, perilla and nuoc cham dipping sauce

steps: Whisk the rice flour, coconut milk, water, turmeric, green onions and a pinch of salt. Rest 30 minutes.
Fry a few slices of pork and some shrimp in an oiled hot skillet.
Pour in a thin layer of batter, swirling. Add sprouts, cover 2 minutes, then uncover until crisp.
Fold in half and slide out.
Wrap pieces in lettuce with herbs and dip in nuoc cham.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Vieux Carré
recipe.description: New Orleans classic of rye, Cognac, sweet vermouth and Bénédictine.

ingredients.item: vegan sweet vermouth (such as Dolin Rouge)

steps: Stir everything with ice.
Strain into a rocks glass over fresh ice.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Ward Eight
recipe.description: Boston classic of rye, lemon, orange and grenadine.
steps: Shake everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Warm Farro Squash Cranberry Salad
recipe.description: Chewy farro, roasted butternut squash, dried cranberries and pecans over arugula.

ingredients.item: small butternut squash (about 2 lb), peeled and cubed

steps: Heat oven to 425 F (220 C). Toss squash with 1 tbsp oil and half the salt. Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, turning once, until tender.
Simmer farro in water for 25 to 35 minutes, or according to its package, until tender but chewy. Drain.
Toast pecans in a dry skillet for 3 minutes. Whisk remaining oil with vinegar, maple syrup, remaining salt and pepper.
Toss warm farro and squash with dressing and cranberries. Serve over arugula with pecans.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Farro is wheat and is not gluten-free. Toast nuts gently and keep them moving to avoid scorching.
recipe.make_ahead: Refrigerate farro and squash promptly for up to 3 days. Store arugula and pecans separately and assemble just before serving.

recipe.title: Water Lily
recipe.description: Equal parts gin, orange liqueur, crème de violette and lemon.
steps: Shake everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Watermelon Mint Rum Cooler
recipe.description: White rum with fresh watermelon juice, lime and mint, topped with soda. Pure summer.
steps: Gently press mint in a shaker.
Add rum, watermelon, lime and ice; shake and strain into a tall glass over ice.
Top with soda.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: omit rum and add 1 1/2 oz soda water.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Egusi Soup
recipe.description: West African stew thickened with ground melon seeds, with greens and meat or fish.

ingredients.item: scotch bonnet peppers, blended with 2 tomatoes
beef or goat, cooked, with its stock

steps: Mix the egusi with a little water into a paste.
Heat the palm oil, cook the onion, then add the pepper and tomato blend and cook 10 minutes.
Add the egusi in spoonfuls and fry gently 10 minutes, stirring.
Add the meat with 3 cups stock, the fish, crayfish and bouillon and simmer 20 minutes.
Stir in the greens, cook 5 minutes and season. Serve with fufu or pounded yam.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

recipe.title: Whiskey on the Rocks
recipe.description: Good bourbon or rye poured over ice.
steps: Put a large ice cube in a rocks glass.
Pour in the whiskey and stir briefly.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Whiskey Sour
recipe.description: Bourbon, lemon and sugar with a silky egg-white foam.
steps: Shake the bourbon, lemon, syrup and egg white without ice for 15 seconds.
Add ice and shake hard again.
Strain into a rocks glass over ice and dot the foam with bitters.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake lemon, syrup, pasteurized egg white or aquafaba and cold black tea for a sour mocktail.

recipe.note: Uses raw egg white; leave it out or use pasteurized whites if you prefer.

recipe.title: White Bean Kale Pesto Soup
recipe.description: White beans and kale in a light vegetable soup finished with basil pesto containing cheese and pine nuts.

ingredients.item: cannellini beans (15 oz each), drained and rinsed
basil pesto made with vegetarian hard cheese and pine nuts

steps: Heat oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Soften onion and carrot for 6 minutes; add garlic for 30 seconds.
Add beans, water, salt and pepper. Simmer for 10 minutes, then mash a small scoop of beans against the pan to thicken the broth.
Stir in kale and cook for 4 minutes. Take off heat and stir in pesto and lemon juice.
Divide among bowls and serve hot.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Pesto here intentionally contains milk and tree nuts; do not use a generic unverified pesto while retaining these exact labels.
recipe.make_ahead: Refrigerate promptly in shallow containers for up to 3 days. Reheat leftovers to 165 F (74 C).

recipe.title: White Lady
recipe.description: Gin, orange liqueur and lemon, often with egg white.
steps: Dry-shake everything without ice, then shake again with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: This drink uses raw egg white. Use pasteurized egg white if you prefer, and always for anyone pregnant, older or with a weakened immune system.

recipe.title: White Russian
recipe.description: Vodka and coffee liqueur topped with cream.
steps: Fill a rocks glass with ice and add the vodka and coffee liqueur.
Float the cream on top and stir if you like.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Cold brew, coffee syrup and cream over ice.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Wonton Soup
recipe.description: Cantonese pork and shrimp wontons, silky and juicy, in a clear, gingery chicken broth with bok choy and scallions.

ingredients.item: raw shrimp, peeled, deveined and roughly chopped
toasted sesame oil, plus more to serve

steps: Put the pork, shrimp, soy sauce, sesame oil, egg white, grated ginger, salt, sugar and white pepper in a bowl. Stir hard in one direction for 2 minutes, until sticky.

Place 1 tablespoon of filling in the center of a wrapper. Wet the edges, fold it in half into a triangle and press out the air. Bring the two side corners together, overlapping, and press to seal. Keep the finished wontons under a damp towel.
Bring the broth and ginger slices to a simmer in a pot and season with salt.
Bring a separate large pot of water to a boil. Cook the wontons in batches for 3 to 4 minutes, until they float and the filling is cooked through (160°F).
Add the bok choy to the broth for the last 2 minutes.
Divide the wontons and bok choy between bowls, ladle the hot broth over and top with scallions and a few drops of sesame oil.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Cooking the wontons in plain water keeps the broth clear.
Stirring the filling in one direction makes it springy and juicy.
recipe.make_ahead: Freeze uncooked wontons on a floured tray, then bag them. Cook from frozen for 5 to 6 minutes.
variations: Wonton noodle soup: add thin egg noodles to each bowl.

recipe.title: Woo Woo
recipe.description: A fun, fruity 1980s highball: vodka and peach schnapps with cranberry juice over ice. Sweet, pink and easy.
steps: Fill a highball glass with ice.
Add the vodka, peach schnapps, cranberry juice and lime and stir well.
Garnish with a lime wedge.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Mix cranberry juice with a splash of peach nectar and lime over ice.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: A squeeze of lime keeps it from being too sweet.
variations: Woo Woo shots: shake with ice and strain into shot glasses.

recipe.title: Xiaolongbao (Soup Dumplings)
recipe.description: Shanghai's famous soup dumplings: thin pleated wrappers around a gingery pork filling and a burst of hot broth. Served with black vinegar and ginger.

ingredients.item: all-purpose flour, plus more for rolling
fresh ginger cut into fine matchsticks, to serve
napa cabbage leaves or parchment, for the steamer

steps: Make the aspic: sprinkle the gelatin over the cold broth in a small pan and let it soften for 5 minutes. Warm gently, stirring, until dissolved. Pour into a shallow dish and chill for at least 3 hours, until firm.
Make the dough: stir the flour and warm water together, then knead for 8 to 10 minutes, until smooth. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.

Mix the pork, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, sesame oil, sugar, salt, white pepper, minced ginger and scallions, stirring hard in one direction until sticky. Finely chop the aspic and fold it in. Keep the filling cold.
Roll the dough into a log and cut it into 32 pieces. Roll each into a 3 1/4-inch circle, thinner at the edges than in the center.
Put 1 tablespoon of filling in the center of a wrapper. Pleat the edge all the way around, about 16 to 18 small folds, then pinch and twist the top to seal.
Line a steamer with cabbage leaves or parchment and set the dumplings in it 1 inch apart.
Steam over boiling water for 8 minutes, until the filling is cooked through (160°F).
Serve right away with black vinegar and ginger matchsticks for dipping.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Lift each dumpling gently into a spoon, nibble a small hole, sip the soup, then eat the rest.
Keep the filling and aspic cold while you work. Warm aspic melts and makes the dumplings hard to seal.
recipe.make_ahead: Freeze uncooked dumplings on a floured tray, then bag them. Steam from frozen for 11 to 12 minutes.

recipe.title: Yakitori (Chicken and Scallion Skewers)
recipe.description: Japanese grilled chicken skewers, called negima: juicy thigh meat threaded with scallion and brushed with a sweet, glossy soy and mirin tare.

ingredients.item: boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
thick scallions, white and light green parts cut into 1-inch lengths, greens kept
6-inch bamboo skewers, soaked in water for 30 minutes

steps: Make the tare: put the soy sauce, mirin, sake, water, brown sugar and a few scallion greens in a small pan. Boil, then simmer for 10 to 15 minutes, until reduced by about a third and slightly syrupy. Discard the greens and let it cool a little.
Thread the chicken and scallion pieces onto the skewers, alternating them and pressing them snugly together.
Heat a grill, or a grill pan or broiler, to medium-high and brush the grates or pan with the oil.
Grill the skewers for 4 to 5 minutes, turning often, until lightly charred.
Brush with the tare and grill for 30 seconds per side. Repeat two or three times, until glossy and the chicken is cooked through (165°F).
Serve with a final brush of tare and a sprinkle of shichimi togarashi, if you like.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Pour some tare into a separate bowl for brushing so the leftover sauce stays clean for serving.
Thigh meat stays juicy on the grill. Breast meat dries out quickly.
recipe.make_ahead: Make the tare up to 2 weeks ahead and keep it in the fridge.
variations: Shio style: season the skewers with salt only and skip the tare.

recipe.title: Yellow Bird
recipe.description: White rum, Galliano, orange liqueur and lime.
steps: Shake everything with ice.
Strain into a chilled coupe.
recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Yuzu Honey Gin Sour
recipe.description: Floral honey rounds out the sharp citrus of yuzu in a gin sour served without egg foam.
steps: Combine gin, yuzu juice and honey syrup in a shaker.
Shake with ice for 15 seconds, then double-strain into a chilled coupe.
Express the lemon twist over the drink and add it.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake 2 oz cooled green tea, 3/4 oz yuzu juice and 1/2 oz honey syrup with ice; strain into a coupe.

recipe.note: An original Relish home cocktail. Please drink responsibly.
tips: For honey syrup, stir equal volumes honey and warm water until dissolved, then cool. Use food-grade yuzu juice rather than a sweetened concentrate.
recipe.make_ahead: Prepare to order. Keep juices and brewed teas refrigerated until needed.

vegan.title: Yuzu Agave Gin Sour
vegan.description: A yuzu gin sour sweetened with agave instead of honey.
steps: Combine gin, yuzu juice and agave syrup in a shaker.
Shake with ice for 15 seconds, then double-strain into a chilled coupe.
Express the lemon twist over the drink and add it.

vegan.note: An original Relish home cocktail. Please drink responsibly.

recipe.title: Za'atar Chicken and Cauliflower Traybake
recipe.description: Lemon-scented chicken, cauliflower and red onion roast together with a sesame-containing za'atar blend.

ingredients.item: large cauliflower, cut into bite-size florets
red onion, cut into thin wedges
lemon, half juiced and half cut into wedges

steps: Heat the oven to 425 F (220 C). Toss cauliflower and onion with 2 tbsp oil, half the za'atar, half the salt and the pepper. Spread on a large sheet pan.
Coat chicken with the remaining oil, za'atar and salt and the juice from half the lemon. Nestle among the vegetables in one layer.
Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, turning the vegetables once, until cauliflower is browned and the thickest part of every thigh reaches 165 F (74 C). Add a few extra minutes if needed.
Rest chicken for 5 minutes. Scatter over parsley and serve with the lemon wedges.
recipe.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Use two sheet pans if necessary; crowded vegetables steam instead of browning. Check the spice blend label for additional allergens.
recipe.make_ahead: Refrigerate leftovers promptly in shallow containers for up to 3 days. Reheat chicken to 165 F (74 C).

recipe.title: Zaza
recipe.description: A classic French café cocktail from the early 1900s: equal parts dry gin and Dubonnet Rouge, stirred cold with a twist of orange.
steps: Stir the gin, Dubonnet and bitters with ice for 20 to 30 seconds.
Strain into a chilled coupe or cocktail glass.
Express a lemon twist over the top and drop it in.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Stir cold red grape juice with a splash of tonic and a dash of orange syrup.

recipe.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Keep opened Dubonnet in the fridge; like vermouth, it fades after a few weeks.
Also known as the Dubonnet Cocktail, a favorite of Queen Elizabeth II, who preferred it over ice.
variations: Serve it on the rocks with a lemon slice, the royal way.

recipe.title: Zombie
recipe.description: A potent tiki blend of rums, lime, grapefruit, cinnamon and falernum.

ingredients.item: Don's Mix (grapefruit juice and cinnamon syrup)

steps: Blend or shake everything with crushed ice.
Pour into a tall tiki mug or Collins glass and add more ice.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake lime, grapefruit, cinnamon syrup and pineapple juice.

recipe.note: Very strong; limit to one.
tips: Don's Mix is 2 parts fresh grapefruit juice to 1 part cinnamon syrup. Make extra; it keeps 3 days in the fridge.
